plugins.name: housemate
plugins.author: RaYYeR220
plugins.does: Turns old phones, tablets and browsers into hands-free room speakers for Hermes with a LAN hub doing wake word and VAD, nearest-device arbitration, timers, intercom and spoken approvals.

why: Turns old phones and laptops into room speakers as a real Hermes gateway platform plus TTS provider with timers, intercom and spoken approvals, exactly Nous's own-hardware theme and deeply tested; setup is heavy, the audience is narrower, and anyone in earshot can talk to the agent. (Useful 3, Reliable 4, Polish 5, Creative 4, Beyond 5.)

Adds a whole new Hermes platform (a gateway adapter, a TTS provider, 7 tools, a Desktop Rooms page) that turns old phones and laptops into wake-word room speakers, matching Nous's push onto people's own hardware; it passed the catalog check, enable and doctor here, failed cleanly with 'hub not running' when called without the gateway, and 537 of its tests passed (28 failed, 4 errored on this machine), but setup is heavy and the wake phrase is 'Hey Jarvis'.

U5/R4/P5/C5/B5: A real gateway platform, paired browser satellites, room arbitration, persistent timers and actor-aware approvals most directly realize Hermes on users' own hardware, narrowly behind Canvas because audio hardware and model downloads add setup risk and live room audio remains unverified (pinned source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RaYYeR220/housemate/09c1a1d0a88bfa8762cee6b3ccf94271b0f172c5/README.md).

plugins.name: hermes-canvas
plugins.author: 0xbyt4
plugins.does: Connects an editable Desktop plan canvas to real tool writes, check exit codes and subagent activity, with mid-turn steering and removed-box write vetoes.

why: The agent's plan drawn as a live Desktop canvas whose boxes turn green only from real writes and exit codes and which the user can edit mid-build; fully implemented with 206 tests and a clean catalog check, though 'cannot fake' overstates since the model picks its own check commands. (Useful 4, Reliable 4, Polish 4, Creative 5, Beyond 5.)

The agent draws its plan as boxes bound to file globs and check commands and hooks set each box's status from real writes and exit codes, with a Desktop pane for steering; 306 tests passed here, the catalog check had no warnings and bad calls returned clear errors inside Hermes, but shell-write parsing is best effort and the value is mostly for Desktop coding sessions.

U5/R4/P5/C5/B5: Runtime-derived plan status, mid-turn user steering, subagent attribution and a finished Desktop canvas form the strongest broadly useful coding companion; the shell-write detector remains heuristic and live Desktop interaction was not independently exercised (pinned source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xbyt4/hermes-canvas/d6eeff0d6f7ec653262537bdd7bb001cc6d3c7f8/README.md).

reads.worst: Shell and execute_code write detection is explicitly best-effort, and the veto allows calls on unexpected hook errors, so removed-box enforcement is incomplete.

reads.best: It closes the loop between plans, real tool activity, checks, and user steering with rich Desktop UI, replay, demos, and a dedicated suite; earlier glob-matching concerns were fixed at this pin.
reads.worst: Its usefulness is strongest for software projects with well-defined files and checks, and user-authored checks still need careful setup.

plugins.name: hermes-ark
plugins.author: medomohamed22
plugins.does: Automatically checkpoints Hermes memory and skills and provides encrypted, versioned full-home backups with selective restore and off-site sync.

why: Encrypted, deduplicated backups of the Hermes home with item-level restore, secrets read from Hermes's secret store and a Desktop page; backup is a common category, its 'agent cannot switch it off' claim rests on regex matching, and ark_checkpoint was not offered to the model in my fresh-home run. (Useful 4, Reliable 4, Polish 4, Creative 3, Beyond 4.)

Encrypted, deduplicated, versioned backups of the Hermes home with item-level restore and a guard that snapshots before memory writes, which nearly every long-running user wants; 174 tests passed here and secrets go through Hermes's secret store, but backup is a familiar idea, the passphrase (and so encryption) is optional for a local repository, and its ark_checkpoint tool was not offered in my run.

U5/R4/P5/C4/B5: Automatic pre-write snapshots, authenticated encryption, credential exclusions and previewed item-level recovery protect a user's accumulated agent state more broadly than most specialist tools; local recovery code was checked but live S3 recovery remains unverified (pinned source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/medomohamed22/hermes-ark/a23e529c1f636aa49d974576cdc5cb15fc8242d3/README.md).

plugins.name: tenure
plugins.author: otsoa-dubief
plugins.does: Adds revocable per-action autonomy tiers, approval hooks, undo snapshots, model-specific evidence and a signed local audit passport.

why: Rebuilds Hermes's approvals as earned, revocable per-action trust with undo, a signed ledger, Desktop and dashboard pages and the field's biggest test suite; loses a Reliable point for three private core imports flagged by the catalog check, a heuristic shell classifier and an opt-in preset that can let high-stakes actions run unasked. (Useful 4, Reliable 4, Polish 5, Creative 5, Beyond 5.)

Per-action-type trust that asks first after a mistake and earns autonomy back, with file undo, a signed passport and the most polished Desktop page in the batch (five locales); 2,401 tests passed and 6 failed here, but it rests on a 5,200-line heuristic shell classifier, the catalog check raised a security-scan caution and private-import warnings, and its own README says the study behind its rule is pending.

U4/R4/P5/C5/B5: Per-action probation, evidence-based trust transitions, authenticated undo snapshots and an autonomy passport are an unusually complete change to agent oversight, although the large heuristic classifier and Hermes approval-mode semantics limit the strength of its always-ask language (pinned source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/otsoa-dubief/tenure/f4a62855e592b9e170ab0c54d9278aabef05f370/tenure/README.md).

demo.text:
Your agent makes one mistake.

Lose all your trust ? Or only for that kind of action ?

Tenure, my Hermes plugin: trust by default, taken back on a mistake, earned back on evidence, for each kind of action (files, commands, git…).

My entry for the @NousResearch hackathon 👀 https

reads.worst: Very large and complex (a 5,200-line classifier and an 8,000-line Desktop bundle), so its trust decisions rest on heuristics that are hard to audit.

plugins.name: trust-ladder
plugins.author: merdoks
plugins.does: Persists user corrections as tool guards, write checks, injected rules or approval requests, and tracks tasks against terminal verifiers.

why: Compiles a user's correction into the strongest enforceable rule (block, check, reminder or approval), compact and defensive with a clean catalog check and clear argument errors in my run; guards are best-effort regex, auto-learn is on by default, there is no UI and the install line still has an <owner> placeholder. (Useful 4, Reliable 4, Polish 3, Creative 4, Beyond 4.)

Turns a user's correction into an enforced guard, which is the plugin most Hermes users would install on day one: run inside Hermes it learned 'never push straight to main' and then blocked 'git push origin main' while letting 'echo hello' through; 95 of 96 tests passed here, there are no secrets or network code, but the 'minimal call' its own tool description promises (a bare command string) is refused by its schema, and it has no Desktop UI.

U5/R2/P4/C4/B5: Turning corrections into tool-boundary guards is broadly useful, but the pinned compiler accepts and example-verifies (a|aa)+$ with its full search window, then evaluate_match on 40 a characters followed by ! exceeds a three-second cutoff, so the claimed regex vetting can still stall the agent (pinned source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/merdoks/trust-ladder/fae4e9df58767e5e3832c8f65936b97868bc98fc/compiler.py).

plugins.does: Watches GitHub Actions and, on a red run, proposes a fix PR only after Hermes's own test runs prove red-then-green.

reads.best: Proof built from real repeated test runs, git push blocked, approval on first repo-code run, with Desktop pane, demo and CI.
reads.worst: Only pytest and go test are supported, and the automation prompt says to use 'whatever GitHub access you have', outside its token scope.

reads.best: It converts an agent coding loop into a rigorously gated product workflow, with explicit approval, proof ledger, protected-file checks, demo, Desktop UI, and tests.
reads.worst: It is deliberately limited to GitHub Actions projects using pytest or go test and cannot prove fixes requiring CI-only services or secrets.

reads.best: It builds a useful approval-aware CI repair workflow around observed terminal results, immutable source-state evidence, protected tests and a reviewable patch/PR (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kinnuworks/ci-red-to-green/83009f03e864264524b8c18bed4ec5423680ab4b/README.md).
reads.worst: Its full-suite gate can certify a regressing fix because environment-based pytest filtering passes command validation and tests missing from the later run are ignored (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kinnuworks/ci-red-to-green/83009f03e864264524b8c18bed4ec5423680ab4b/runners.py ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kinnuworks/ci-red-to-green/83009f03e864264524b8c18bed4ec5423680ab4b/ledger.py).
reads.validate: Passed: catalog validate --install-deps exit 0, security scan safe, declarations/no-core-override/Desktop checks passed; enable and doctor exit 0 (0 tools, 3 hooks).
reads.inside: Loaded /ci, pre_llm_call/pre_tool_call/post_tool_call hooks, its skill, automation blueprint and Desktop backend; no tool schemas. Five scripted terminal calls invoked the registered /ci handler through the real Hermes PluginManager: malformed watch returned usage; demo created the bundled humanize incident; status showed four failing tests; discard succeeded; watch without a GitHub token returned a clear error. The repository's real-Hermes integration test reproduced the failure twice, observed approval and push-block directives, repaired the source, recorded three passing runs and full-suite runs, and emitted a source-only local patch. No real GitHub PR was sent. An extra real-Hermes probe then demonstrated a false proof: after fixing the original bug but adding two new regressions, three runs with PYTEST_ADDOPTS=-ktest_args1 were accepted as full-suite evidence and emitted a patch; the genuine full suite still had 2 failed/15 passed. Code: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kinnuworks/ci-red-to-green/83009f03e864264524b8c18bed4ec5423680ab4b/runners.py ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kinnuworks/ci-red-to-green/83009f03e864264524b8c18bed4ec5423680ab4b/ledger.py
reads.tests: 96 passed, 0 failed in the supplied pytest suite, including test_hermes_e2e with HERMES_AGENT_DIR pointing to the real checkout. Additional regression probe exposed a product defect: status ready and proof accepted despite two actual full-suite failures; this is separate from the 96 passing repository tests. Integration test: https://github.com/kinnuworks/ci-red-to-green/blob/83009f03e864264524b8c18bed4ec5423680ab4b/tests/test_hermes_e2e.py

reads.best: Watches GitHub Actions and offers a fix PR only after Hermes's own test output proves the failing test failed twice before and passed three times after, with the token from the secret store and a human approval before any PR.
reads.worst: CI log text and commit titles from the repo go verbatim into the model's context while the agent runs that repo's code, and the pre_llm_call hook makes a GitHub call outside any try.
reads.validate: passed (all checks ok, exit 0)
reads.inside: Loaded; enable and doctor OK (0 tools, 3 hooks, /ci, skill, dashboard routes, Desktop pane). A chat with terminal + read_file calls completed with the hooks active and no errors; /ci demo and /ci watch are slash commands tryit cannot drive, and a GitHub token was not available, so the watch-and-PR path was judged by reading.
reads.tests: passed: 95 passed, 1 skipped (pytest; the Hermes e2e test skips without HERMES_AGENT_DIR)

reads.best: It proves a source-only fix against unchanged tests and asks the person before opening a PR, rather than merely suggesting a patch.
reads.worst: The supported path is limited to pytest/go test on GitHub Actions, and it still relies on the model and a compatible local environment to produce the fix.
reads.validate: Passed: validate --install-deps, enable and doctor exited 0; safe scan, 0 tools/3 hooks match, Desktop stays inside SDK. In-process notice is informational (gateway-bound post_message), not an admission failure. Pinned source: https://github.com/kinnuworks/ci-red-to-green/tree/83009f03e864264524b8c18bed4ec5423680ab4b.
reads.inside: Loaded in real Hermes; empty-plan conversation completed, adding /ci, 3 hooks, the fix-red-ci skill, morning-ci automation blueprint and Desktop proof surfaces, rather than a new model tool. Five real plugin-manager command calls: /ci status showed no watches, /ci watch malformed gave usage, /ci demo started the bundled incident, /ci status listed its four failing cases, /ci discard cleared it. Its real-Hermes E2E test additionally reproduced failing pytest output, applied the source fix, observed passing runs, verified first-code-execution approval and push blocking, and exported a source-only patch after proof. No live GitHub PR or polling account was exercised.
reads.tests: 96 passed with HERMES_AGENT_DIR set, including test_demo_through_the_real_plugin_manager (not skipped): 3 failing-before and 4 passing-after test invocations, proof ready, source-only patch. Unit tests cover log parsing, proof ledger, source/test guards, runners, API token/redirect handling and engine state.

plugins.name: neural-mesh
plugins.author: D0xedDevi0
plugins.does: Adds a local memory provider with fact supersession, point-in-time recall and filtered context injection.

reads.best: Bi-temporal memory changes what Hermes can recall, with a pure-Python store, relevant tests and reproducible evidence.
reads.worst: The large vendored engine broadens maintenance risk, and saved memory remains plaintext in the local SQLite store.

reads.best: Point-in-time recall with a measured ablation, demo video, evidence files and tests.
reads.worst: Huge vendored codebase with unused x402 payment/escrow modules widens review surface.

reads.best: A real local bitemporal memory provider (as-of recall, supersession) that plugs into Hermes's memory slot with no key or network and worked on the first call.
reads.worst: Doctor fails on hooks the manifest wrongly declares, the default recall is an MD5-hashed bag of words rather than the 'hybrid' the README claims, raw turn text is stored though the README says redacted, and ~50 vendored files (x402, bond escrow, OpenRouter) are imported but unused.
reads.validate: passed (exit 0); security scan 'caution' warning for destructive_root_rm patterns in a docs evidence text file, not code
reads.inside: enabled and loaded as a memory provider once memory.provider=neural-mesh; added mesh_remember, mesh_recall, mesh_asof, mesh_stats; all 4 planned calls ran: remember stored a fact, recall returned it, mesh_asof with as_of 'not-a-date' gave a clean 'needs a parseable as_of date' error, stats reported the SQLite store. Hermes plugins doctor exit 1: ERROR unknown hook 'on_pre_compress' and 'on_memory_write' in provides_hooks (manifest lists provider methods as hooks)
reads.tests: passed: 23 of 23 (pytest, tests/test_provider.py)

reads.best: Real Hermes retrieved different current and historical truths from the same local store, with no external service or embedding account.
reads.worst: The manifest misdeclares provider lifecycle names as runtime hooks and fails doctor, while its durable recalled-memory store is plaintext sensitive data.
reads.validate: Passed all 15 catalog checks; caution only for rm commands in recorded demo evidence. Runtime doctor FAILED: unknown on_pre_compress and on_memory_write hooks, plus declared hooks not registered. This did not prevent the documented memory-provider loading path from working.
reads.inside: Empty-plan install enabled successfully but added no tools until memory.provider was explicitly set to neural-mesh as documented. With that setting, real AIAgent exposed mesh_remember, mesh_recall, mesh_asof and mesh_stats. Four calls stored a 30-day rotation fact, recalled it, rejected an invalid as_of date and reported the pure-Python store. A second three-call conversation, with old/new facts prepared through the pinned provider API, returned current=30 days and March 2026=90 days, then cleanly rejected another bad date. Initial unconfigured mesh tool calls were unknown-tool errors, not plugin crashes. Pinned implementation: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/D0xedDevi0/hermes-neural-mesh/26abb610f3cbdd4215fbb898d4a2478317dfc5e5/__init__.py
reads.tests: Passed locally: python -m pytest tests -q, 23 passed. Covers temporal supersession, precision floor, prefetch, configuration, thread ownership and provider lifecycle; the broader vendored engine has no separately shipped test suite here.

reads.best: A fully local memory provider gives Hermes persistent recall and dated, superseding facts without a service or key.
reads.worst: The manifest fails runtime doctor on obsolete hook names, and dated recall returns unrelated valid memories because it has no relevance floor.
reads.validate: Passed catalog admission (15 checks; caution only for destructive commands in the historical demo transcript). Runtime doctor FAILED on unknown on_pre_compress/on_memory_write hooks and unregistered declared hooks; manifest metadata does not match current Hermes hook contracts.
reads.inside: Pinned 26abb610f3cbdd4215fbb898d4a2478317dfc5e5, repository D0xedDevi0/hermes-neural-mesh, root folder. Loaded as the selected memory.provider; four mesh tools were offered. All 5 planned calls ran inside AIAgent: empty stats, remember a dated deployment-cadence fact, recall it, dated recall, malformed date rejected with a clear message. Supplemental direct-provider probe confirmed unrelated dated query returns that deployment fact whereas ordinary recall correctly says no match.
reads.tests: 23/23 unittest tests passed offline. Supplemental relevance probe reproduced false-positive dated recall; no external service required.

plugins.name: look
plugins.author: SilentHacks
plugins.does: Lets a local Hermes session inspect pointed-at Chrome content, answer in browser cards, and carry out guarded browser actions with optional voice and gaze.

reads.best: It integrates browser context, consent-bound actions, local speech and gaze with extensive tests and detailed setup guidance.
reads.worst: Its supported path is a narrow Apple Silicon Chrome beta with large optional downloads and experimental eye tracking.

reads.best: Registers 14 tools, middleware, hooks and a Chrome extension, which is truly new for Hermes.
reads.worst: Apple-Silicon-only beta needing broad debugger permission and local debug port, a large attack surface; unverified elsewhere.

reads.best: Brings pointed-at browser evidence, private answer cards and guarded browser actions into Hermes through a substantial local multimodal stack.
reads.worst: The supported beta is Apple Silicon Mac, so this seat verified only synthetic resolution and safe refusal rather than the actual browser interaction loop.
reads.validate: Passed: catalog validate --install-deps, enable and doctor all exit 0; 14 tools, 7 hooks, request/tool middleware and CLI/chat commands. Catalog warns about private core imports in benchmark/probe_profile.py and runtime/native_input.py. Pin: https://github.com/SilentHacks/look/tree/7c01a94aa651adedaf27e5216598c6deef293050 (pinned README, implementation and tests in sources.json).
reads.inside: Loaded. Real-Hermes tool_describe found its deferred tools. gaze_benchmark completed 10 synthetic trials per noise level and returned baseline/fusion metrics; these are simulated reference-resolution results, not measured webcam accuracy. gaze_read and bad file-URL gaze_navigate both safely returned executed=false / No active browser task; the URL-validation branch was not reached. Real Chrome extension, pointing, speech, webcam and human confirmation could not be exercised on this Linux headless seat.
reads.tests: Full pytest after installing NumPy/HuggingFace prerequisites and normalizing the test umask: 366 passed, 15 failed, 393 subtests passed. Fourteen failures directly raise PermissionError on forbidden AF_UNIX socket creation; the extension-setup assertion also fails in that constrained setup. A previous private-directory assertion was only the restrictive test umask and passed on rerun. Actual Mac Chrome interaction remains untested.

reads.best: A genuinely new input channel for agents: point or look at a page element, speak, and Look resolves the target and drives Chrome through nonce-confirmed risky clicks, a closed shadow-DOM overlay and pinned model downloads.
reads.worst: Beta only on Apple Silicon Macs; the model can start microphone recording via gaze_resolve record_voice with an uncapped duration_s, fills and navigation need no human confirmation, and two of its own tests fail.
reads.validate: passed (ok; warning: private core imports hermes_yaml / hermes_cli.auth in benchmark/probe_profile.py and runtime/native_input.py, catalog rule 9)
reads.inside: Loaded (doctor OK: 14 tools, 7 hooks, 2 middleware); on load it starts a localhost HTTP server and a speech warmup (disclosed). gaze_benchmark returned a Monte Carlo accuracy table; gaze_calibrate returned settings with chrome_connected false; gaze_read with no browser returned a clean 'No active browser task' error; gaze_wait with seconds 9 was refused by the schema (max 2). The Chrome, webcam and voice paths need an Apple Silicon Mac with Chrome and were judged by reading.
reads.tests: partly failed: 381 tests (unittest discover, its documented runner, after installing numpy): 2 failures, 14 errors, all 14 errors from this sandbox refusing AF_UNIX sockets, 4 skipped

reads.best: Point-and-ask browser context, local speech and guarded page actions create a distinctive way to interact with Hermes that a text skill cannot reproduce.
reads.worst: The supported product is an Apple Silicon source beta with substantial browser/native setup, while this run could verify only offline logic and clean missing-browser errors, with 16 remaining test failures.
reads.validate: Passed: pinned source catalog validate --install-deps --json exit 0 with all checks passing and security scan safe; doctor/enable exit 0 (14 tools, 7 hooks, 2 middleware declarations). Warning for private core imports in benchmark/probe_profile.py and runtime/native_input.py. First empty validation also emitted a dependency-publication retry warning despite exit 0; subsequent full validation passed.
reads.inside: Loaded in real Hermes and exposed all 14 schemas when progressive disclosure was disabled. Four planned calls completed in both default and direct-schema runs: gaze_calibrate(mode=hover,reset_drift=true) returned ok=true, chrome_connected=false; gaze_read cleanly returned No active browser task; invalid gaze_choose(candidate_index=0) was rejected by default Hermes argument validation (direct-schema run returned simulated-only error); gaze_benchmark(trials_per_sigma=10) returned synthetic resolution metrics. Read README, manifest, tools, browser ownership/actions/extension code, speech/download handling, platform limitations and tests. No physical browser, microphone or eye-tracking acceptance test.

plugins.name: workgraph
plugins.author: aliiqbal24
plugins.does: Adds a local branching workspace that saves source, development SQLite state, context and browser evidence for continued agent work.

reads.best: Combines actual product-state restoration, independent protected-behavior replay and agent checkpoints into a visual workflow beyond ordinary Git history.
reads.worst: The developer preview requires Linux, bubblewrap and browser dependencies for its full workflow, and restores configured development state rather than hosted services or hidden conversation state.

reads.best: Native tool middleware checkpoints edits and avoids repeating uncertain side effects, while the visual history preserves executable product states.
reads.worst: It is a Linux developer preview requiring Git, bubblewrap and Chromium for its full workflow, and only supported foreground operations receive automatic capture.

reads.best: Its saved product-state tree, data-aware branching and automatic managed-edit checkpoints address real agent work recovery rather than merely describing a Git workflow.
reads.worst: The ordinary enable command failed, so even the successful manually enabled versioning path is not a dependable day-one installation; its documented Linux, Bubblewrap and browser prerequisites add setup work (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aliiqbal24/workgraph/37c7280a514d3fa23e7193f44b5123d1f9c90163/README.md).
reads.validate: Passed: plugins validate --install-deps --json exited 0, all 15 admission checks passed, security scan safe and zero warnings. Doctor --ci exited 0, with 1 tool and 3 hooks. Normal plugins enable failed twice: uv lock could not find the staged editable workgraph-agent distribution. Admission validation passing therefore did not mean successful activation.
reads.inside: The stock empty-plan and five-call runs could import/register the plugin for doctor but failed normal enablement; its workgraph tool was consequently unavailable in the chat. For diagnosis only, explicitly enabled it in a scratch profile configuration, without changing plugin source: all five calls then returned on a fresh scratch Git fixture (status, open attempt, checkpoint, history, bad version id). The checkpoint selected a revision, history listed one saved version, and the bad id returned NOT_FOUND. Code registers tool_request/tool_execution middleware for managed file/terminal routing in addition to its three hooks. This manual profile result does not erase the normal activation failure. No real browser gallery/protected-flow recording was exercised. Pinned adapter: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aliiqbal24/workgraph/37c7280a514d3fa23e7193f44b5123d1f9c90163/workgraph/hermes_adapter.py; tool contract: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aliiqbal24/workgraph/37c7280a514d3fa23e7193f44b5123d1f9c90163/workgraph/api.py
reads.tests: Failed: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v ran 69 tests in 1126.583 seconds: 56 passed, 7 failures, 6 errors. Errors were failed-candidate acceptance paths; several failure assertions depended on sandbox execution that returned a Bubblewrap initialization error in this run, and one concurrency check exceeded its 0.25-second bound. An isolated acceptance-test repeat also errored, and a separate minimal fixture check confirmed a Bubblewrap error rather than an application assertion. These sandbox-dependent results are not proof of an upstream source regression; normal Hermes activation nevertheless independently failed.

reads.best: It turns exploratory agent coding into a persistent, inspectable graph of snapshots, alternatives, verification, and landing rather than a chat-only workflow.
reads.worst: The core verification path depends on bubblewrap, which makes installation and use less portable and could not run under this sandbox.
reads.validate: passed: manifest, isolated load/capability probe, tool/hook/middleware/skill registrations, and security scan passed.
reads.inside: Hermes capability probe loaded the workgraph tool, hooks, middleware, and skill; the empty and planned tryit sessions could not complete against the sandboxed fake model, so no chat calls are reported.
reads.tests: failed in this sandbox: 9 failed and 9 passed; failures were checks running bubblewrap, which could not create a NETLINK_ROUTE socket under the sandbox.

reads.best: It gives agents a distinctive persistent product-state graph for branching, comparing, combining, and replaying development work.
reads.worst: Its core targeted tests had several failures, leaving the versioning workflow less trustworthy than its polished presentation suggests.
reads.validate: passed: manifest, schema, loadability, isolated capability probe, declared registrations, collision, security, and core-override checks all passed.
reads.inside: Not loaded into a completed Hermes chat: the shared tryit activation path could not finish isolated-runtime bootstrap in the 30-second executor window; the catalog capability probe loaded register() in isolation. No planned calls were observed.
reads.tests: 7 passed and 8 failed in targeted engine/interface tests; one interface test received 502 rather than 401 under the sandbox proxy, while several candidate-flow tests also failed.

reads.best: Isolated agent attempts, immutable Git checkpoints, explicit handoff state and evidence-bound candidate acceptance substantially improve Hermes coding workflows beyond what a skill can enforce.
reads.worst: The standard Hermes enable path failed locally before the tool became available, and this sandbox cannot exercise its required bubblewrap verification boundary, so the polished workspace is not a verified normal install here.
reads.validate: Passed: catalog admission, including capability probe and all declarations. Doctor passed (1 tool, 3 hooks). Standard enable FAILED twice: uv lock could not find the staged editable workgraph-agent distribution under plugin-sources; this is an observed Hermes dependency-preparation failure, not a failed catalog gate.
reads.inside: Pinned aliiqbal24/workgraph@37c7280a514d3fa23e7193f44b5123d1f9c90163. The required empty-plan and five-call tryit attempts were run: after enable refusal the tool was absent, two requests returned tool-not-found, and Hermes ended the conversation as an invalid tool call before the other three ran. For supplemental code assessment only, a separate scratch home manually enabled the unchanged pinned plugin and initialized a disposable Git project. Thus core snapshot/merge/acceptance logic is supported, but sandbox enforcement is not verified here. Browser galleries and Chromium acceptance were not run.

plugins.name: manyhands
plugins.author: PhiBao
plugins.does: Makes one Hermes bot safely multi-user: per-sender roles, tool allowlists, private memory, owner-DM approvals and per-person audit.

reads.best: Fails closed on unknown senders, only the owner can approve or edit the roster, and the operator's memory is hidden from others.
reads.worst: Tests are ad-hoc scripts with no CI, and owner DMs only fully work on Telegram.

reads.best: Acts on per-sender identity in hooks and middleware with an approval transport, and withholds the owner's memory from others; it adds a 68-test selftest and no dependencies.
reads.worst: Relies on platform event fields and a manifest workaround for an undocumented middleware key, and the tests are scripts rather than a standard runner.

reads.best: Human identity, per-person memory and owner-directed approvals make a shared Hermes gateway substantially more useful than a prompt could.
reads.worst: A live gateway is needed for owner DM approvals, and calls nested inside execute_code can lose identity and fail closed.
reads.validate: Passed: supplied tryit.py catalog validate exit 0, including isolated registration, declared tools/hooks/middleware and no core override; warning destructive_root_rm points to a README example. Initial enable and doctor both exit 0 (6 tools, 3 hooks).
reads.inside: Loaded at bc5ec1cb57bb26a133f7967bd06dee6441409544. Adds six person/memory/audit tools, identity/role hooks, memory-filtering middleware, /many and an owner approval transport. Final five-call Hermes plan searched/described deferred tools, dispatched whoami and people, rejected empty remember text cleanly, then dispatched recall and audit. It returned local operator/owner, an empty roster and recall, and an audit trail of tool decisions and scripted-model usage. Initial tool listing omitted the six deferred tools; discovery found all six. Gateway delivery of the owner DM was not exercised.
reads.tests: Passed: 68 stdlib self-tests (0 failures/errors) and repository live_integration.py against real Hermes PluginManager (LIVE INTEGRATION: PASS), covering human command authorization, role blocking, one-shot grants, private facts, identity spoofing and shared-session attribution. Final planned conversation completed all 5 calls.

reads.best: Gives a shared Hermes gateway per-human identities, private fact namespaces, owner approvals and an attributable local audit trail.
reads.worst: The permission-hook wrapper catches unexpected exceptions and returns None, so an audit-store failure can silently remove this plugin's block on a forbidden tool.
reads.validate: Passed: catalog validate --install-deps, enable and doctor all exit 0 (6 tools, 3 hooks, llm_request middleware, owner approval transport and /many command). Security-scan caution is a destructive-command example in README; not an executed command. Runtime warns that provides_middleware is an unknown manifest field but still registers the middleware. Pin: https://github.com/PhiBao/manyhands/tree/bc5ec1cb57bb26a133f7967bd06dee6441409544 (pinned README, implementation and tests in sources.json).
reads.inside: Loaded in real Hermes. whoami identified the local operator with owner permissions. remember with valid text reported no person attached; recall returned no-person/empty results; blank remember returned text is required. An additional replay using the local CLI subject had the same roster limitation. Included real-PluginManager live integration passed role blocking, one-use approvals, memory scoping and audit scenarios. A separate fault probe through the real get_pre_tool_call_directive gate normally blocked an unattributed terminal call, but returned (None, None), i.e. no permission directive, when Runtime.audit raised a simulated SQLite disk-full error. No terminal command was actually dispatched in the fault probe.
reads.tests: Selftest: 68 tests, 0 failures/errors, but logs an unhandled owner-denial-thread SQLite cannot commit - no transaction is active error. Live Hermes integration script: PASS. Supplemental fault probes reproduced the fail-open permission error both directly and through the real Hermes gate.

reads.best: Makes one Hermes gateway a real multi-user assistant with per-person roles, tool allowlists, private memory, token budgets and owner-approved risky calls.
reads.worst: Its 'fail closed' guard returns None (allow) on any exception in pre_tool_call, and an owner approval covers person plus tool rather than the exact arguments, so approving one terminal command lets the next run anything.
reads.validate: passed (all checks ok, exit 0); Hermes warns provides_middleware is an unknown manifest field
reads.inside: Loaded; enable and doctor OK (6 tools, 3 hooks, llm_request middleware, approval transport, /many). Via tool_call: manyhands_whoami returned the owner role; manyhands_remember refused cleanly ('no person attached to this conversation'); manyhands_recall returned an empty list; recall with limit='abc' was rejected by Hermes schema validation.
reads.tests: passed: 68 of 68 (tests/selftest.py, stdlib, stub host)

plugins.name: lumina
plugins.author: samirsawarkar
plugins.does: Adds on-device Apple Photos search, document privacy checks, verified redacted copies, and hooks intended to block raw ID-image exfiltration.

reads.best: It combines a memorable consumer workflow with native Photos access, on-device OCR rechecking, leak-guard hooks, media UI, tests, and a convincing demo.
reads.worst: It is macOS-only and its document detection and redaction assurance depend on OCR heuristics, so it can only protect what it recognizes.

reads.best: It combines an exceptionally polished macOS photo experience with plugin-enforced redaction and cross-tool leak checks that a prompt cannot provide.
reads.worst: It is macOS-only, and its outbound ID guard explicitly fails open if its inspection itself errors.

reads.best: On supported Macs, the code combines photo-library access with verified redacted copies and hooks that can stop raw-ID exports across other tools.
reads.worst: Apple-only dependencies prevented enablement here, so the reliability cap is 2 and the central Photos/OCR privacy workflow remains unverified; Leak Guard also explicitly fails open on OCR errors.
reads.validate: Passed: catalog validate --install-deps exited 0 and all 16 static/registration admission checks passed; doctor exited 0 with 10 tools and 4 hooks but warned that osxphotos, photoscript and Vision were not installed. Enable exited 1: PyObjC build requires macOS / sw_vers.
reads.inside: Pinned source https://github.com/samirsawarkar/lumina/tree/aaced5beb7bdb93cf7267060bb81fb49d4762c67. Not enabled in the real Linux Hermes conversation because its declared Apple-only dependencies could not build. The empty plan added no tools; planned library-info/search received unavailable-tool errors and the conversation stopped before invalid-export/expiry could execute. These are unavailable calls, not successful plugin executions. Source and portable tests cover the ten tool handlers, Privacy Check, verified redaction, outbound Leak Guard and Desktop integration; actual Photos/OCR/video/UI behavior was not verified.
reads.tests: 84 passed, 3 failed, 65 skipped (pytest). Failures were test_no_library_and_no_access, test_errors_never_leak_paths and test_status_no_library: osxphotos was absent on Linux. Library/macOS-dependent cases skipped; no Photos library or Apple Vision was available.

reads.best: Combines local Photos access, verified redacted copies and outbound-tool interception to protect documents the agent could otherwise leak.
reads.worst: Guardian accepts model-supplied allow_original=true without checking user approval, while the separate Leak Guard excludes lumina_* tools and fails open on OCR errors, weakening the advertised protection.
reads.validate: Catalog command returned exit 0 and all 16 static/probe checks passed, but --install-deps printed an actual dependency-preparation failure: macOS PyObjC build needs /usr/bin/sw_vers, unavailable on Linux. Enable was refused (exit 1); doctor could register 10 tools/4 hooks in a probe but warned osxphotos/photoscript/PyObjC were missing. Pin aaced5beb7bdb93cf7267060bb81fb49d4762c67.
reads.inside: Not enabled in this Linux Hermes. Both empty and four-call plans completed as conversations, but none of lumina_library_info, lumina_search, lumina_create_album or lumina_redact was available: Hermes returned unknown tool for each. This is a declared macOS-only entry, not evidence that the Mac Photos path is broken; nevertheless reliability is capped at 2 under the brief because it could not load here. Read the privacy, redaction and Leak Guard paths; no real Photos library or Apple Vision OCR was exercised.
reads.tests: 84 passed, 65 skipped, 3 failed. Failures are no-library/error-path tests needing missing osxphotos; skipped tests include the entire real Vision-based Leak Guard suite and Photos-library integration. Pure privacy classification, path/policy utilities, mocked tool registration and API tests ran; no actual OCR or redaction image verification ran.

plugins.name: hermes-regress

A second real-Hermes armed-fixture probe changed write_file content at the same path: the plugin blocked the actual write and preserved the sentinel, but supplied the original fixture anyway because args_key discards content. Both agents exited 0. This tested real capture and fixture interception, not a complete cross-model /regress run or its CLI preflight.

These defects are absent from the supplied passing tests.

reads.worst: Despite the README claiming captured text is redacted before disk, build_case redacts only tool results and persists synthetic passwords unchanged in prompts, answers and arguments (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harishkotra/hermes-regress/877c6dfdfd5e80bb1dca79a67b3081f9764545b5/rg_capture.py).

reads.worst: The plugin ships no engine and requires Linux, a separately attested binary, profiles, Claude Code, GitHub CLI, and sandbox tooling.

plugins.name: agent-security-guard

reads.worst: Plugin folder ships no tests itself and has a very large 42KB entry file; benchmark claims are outside the pinned plugin.

reads.best: Rule-based, no model decides, with a 1,920-attack benchmark and audit trail.
reads.worst: Rule-based pattern coverage is bounded, and similar guard ideas are common.

plugins.name: clotho

reads.best: Tool-execution and model middleware let it change Hermes's execution semantics, with effect review, dependency checks and a substantial test suite.
reads.worst: Its large and intricate interception surface has unavoidable edge cases, especially when commands or unknown effects cannot be previewed.

reads.best: Tool middleware, effect ledgers, drift checks and fork comparison create a substantive new way to review agent actions.
reads.worst: Apply relies on non-interactive tool dispatch that auto-approves dangerous-command prompts, and live rehearsal state disappears on gateway restart.

plugins.name: crowdcode

plugins.does: Gives Hermes a credential-store Base wallet to create, fund and operate CrowdCode cloud agents and withdraw earnings through guarded tools.

reads.best: It changes Hermes's capabilities substantially with wallet-signed agent orchestration while adding approval prompts, daily caps, reservations and receipts.
reads.worst: It can move real USDC and depends on a hosted beta service, so failures and the remaining financial trust assumptions are consequential.

reads.best: It opens a genuinely new agent economy capability with wallet signatures, task execution, receipts, and an explicit Hermes approval threshold.
reads.worst: It is intrinsically high-risk financial code: the default is not ask-before-every-call, transfers/withdrawals have special accounting, and correctness depends on a remote service and wallet key.

plugins.name: thumbs-fix

plugins.does: A thumbs-down on a Hermes Telegram reply finds the skill behind it, asks what was wrong, has the user's model draft a one-place edit, and patches the skill only after approval.

reads.best: A closed, human-approved loop from feedback to skill repair, with nonce-fenced prompts, stale-skill checks, backups, undo and about 2,500 lines of tests plus CI.
reads.worst: Works only in Telegram private chats, cannot repair a skill loaded in an earlier turn, and undo can bypass skill_manage with a direct file write.

reads.best: It connects feedback to the skill actually loaded and applies approved edits through Hermes tooling with stale-draft checks.
reads.worst: Message-range attribution can mistake unrelated bot messages for replies, and undo overwrites subsequent skill edits while staged writes are not tracked to final approval.

plugins.name: mcp-pin
plugins.author: yuzuru99
plugins.does: Fingerprints every MCP tool definition the first time it's seen and hides/blocks any tool whose description or parameters later change (a rug-pull/tool-poisoning attack) until an authorized owner reviews and approves the diff.

reads.best: Extraordinarily thorough test suite (482 lines, plus Hermes-integration and opt-in real-CLI end-to-end tests) covering concurrent writers, fail-closed behavior, and approval codes cryptographically bound to the exact reviewed diff.
reads.worst: No screenshots or visual assets; the README itself admits editing the pin-store file directly (rather than a definition) is a gap the plugin does not catch.

reads.best: Covers eager tools and deferred discovery with fail-closed pin storage, definition-bound review codes and real-agent-loop integration tests.
reads.worst: It cannot catch server behavior changes without definition changes, trusts first use by default, and does not cover Codex app-server MCP calls.

plugins.name: undo-effects
plugins.author: Moodtuner997

reads.best: Snapshots inside Hermes's tool path with conflict-safe restores and honest 'not covered' reporting, backed by unit and e2e tests.
reads.worst: Coverage of terminal commands rests on a hand-written shell parser and snapshots are stored unencrypted.

reads.best: It adds an automatic recovery layer even outside Git, preserves replaced content for redo, and explicitly reports commands its parser cannot cover.
reads.worst: Coverage depends on static command parsing, so several shell, scripting, and platform-specific mutation paths are deliberately outside its protection.

plugins.name: numogram
plugins.author: zblauser

reads.best: A real hardware feedback loop combines persistent serial watching, crash-triggered agent wakeups, deterministic decoding and code-enforced build/flash approval, with a no-board emulator demo and safety tests.
reads.worst: It supports one board at a time and ESP-IDF projects, with real-hardware coverage concentrated on ESP32-P4 and virtual ESP32-C3 rather than the full advertised chip family.

reads.best: A persistent hardware feedback loop can wake Hermes on a crash and complete debugging through guarded build and flash operations.
reads.worst: Only ESP32-P4 hardware and virtual ESP32-C3 have demonstrated full loops; other chip paths and older Xtensa crash decoding remain untested.

reads.worst: The board requires a hosted account and repairs require Pro; the shared bench follows the last board rather than isolating each chat session.

reads.best: It joins physical-board data, locally rendered PDFs, interactive cards and speech vocabulary into a coherent bench workflow with substantial offline tests. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Junkz3/hermes-wrenchboard/da468ace9e5c5cdfa118fe302eeda00de81f67cb/desktop/src/camera.js)
reads.worst: The pinned plugin is a client of a hosted board engine, repairs and plans require Pro, and one shared bench follows the last board rather than isolating each chat. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Junkz3/hermes-wrenchboard/da468ace9e5c5cdfa118fe302eeda00de81f67cb/README.md)

plugins.name: siemless
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Observes Hermes activity, correlates security events into evidence-labelled findings and exports them to local logs or opt-in SIEM destinations.

reads.best: A substantial observer pipeline combines redaction, session-aware correlation, replay isolation, bounded spooling, Desktop findings and extensive privacy/export tests.
reads.worst: Detection is heuristic and cannot prove exfiltration; pattern-based redaction can miss unknown secrets and bounded queues can drop events under load.

reads.best: Nonblocking observer hooks, evidence labels, bounded retry spools and Desktop findings make Hermes itself visible to existing security operations.
reads.worst: Detection and secret redaction are heuristic, and bounded queues or process shutdown can lose events, so this is neither complete surveillance nor a prevention layer.

plugins.name: hermes-wake
plugins.author: askclaw-vesper
plugins.does: Persists watches on systemd units, processes or output files and wakes the originating messaging chat through kanban completion.

reads.best: Solves the agent promising to report back on detached work with persisted, chat-scoped watches, atomic claims and retry tests.
reads.worst: Requires a running messaging gateway and kanban notifications; a crash after completion but before recording success can cause a duplicate wake.

reads.best: It closes a genuine agent-loop gap with durable SQLite state, compare-and-set completion, retry handling, and careful chat scoping.
reads.worst: Delivery relies on a running Hermes gateway and Kanban integration, so an offline gateway delays the wake.

plugins.name: fledge
plugins.author: 12burb
plugins.does: Gates Hermes's own skill-save/rewrite pipeline by scoring each turn's evidence (errors, corrections, denials) and blocking or requiring approval for skill writes that follow a bad run.

reads.best: 153 tests plus an unusually candid 'Limits, honestly' section in its own README admitting where its heuristics can fail.
reads.worst: No tools of its own and no screenshots/demo media, so its value is entirely invisible until a skill-write is actually blocked.

reads.best: Nine real lifecycle hooks govern Hermes's self-improvement loop using run evidence, human review and recoverable skill probation without another model.
reads.worst: Heuristic correction/error detection misses silent wrong answers, and private queue/curator imports plus deliberate fail-open behavior weaken protection when integration fails.

plugins.name: elcaro
plugins.author: udirobert
plugins.does: Runtime prompt-injection defense that scans every tool result through a transform_tool_result hook, quarantines or flags hits, taints the session to gate credential, network and destructive calls behind approval, and keeps a hash-chained verdict log.

reads.best: Changes how Hermes itself handles untrusted content: hooks on every tool result plus pre_tool_call taint gating, secrets from Hermes's secret store, LLM passes off by default, a Desktop pane/chip and 30 plugin tests.
reads.worst: After the log's first 512 KiB rotation, verify_chain will likely report it as TAMPERED, the rules are regexes that are easy to evade, and a configured api_url answering 'not quarantined' skips the local scan.

reads.best: Result replacement, inherited session taint and action-sequence policies protect the agent at boundaries a skill cannot enforce.
reads.worst: The default guard scans only the first 48,000 characters, skips error envelopes and fails open on scan errors, so the README promise that injection never reaches the model is too absolute.

plugins.name: corkboard
plugins.author: elijahboston
plugins.does: Collects owner tasks and decisions in a shared Desktop board, automatically pins blocked kanban cards, and routes answers back to those cards.

reads.best: The persistent owner-decision workflow spans profiles, Desktop and kanban, and keeps a pin open when delivering its answer fails.
reads.worst: Credential exclusion is incomplete: actions.pin checks titles and questions but persists choices, placeholders and check arguments without the token guard.

reads.best: The coherent owner decision flow spans agent tools, kanban hooks, shared storage, and a notably finished Desktop interface, with broad focused tests.
reads.worst: Owner-added shell checks run without an approval prompt when manually or cron-triggered; documentation clearly identifies this power, but safe operation depends on treating those commands like crontab entries.

plugins.name: check-please
plugins.author: itsLittleOdd
plugins.does: Matches each 'done' claim in a Hermes reply to the tool call that proves it and appends a backed/stale/not-backed line, with /check for detail and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: A new, deterministic claim-verification layer built on five hooks, with a big test suite, measured precision and recall, and candid limits.
reads.worst: Screenshots are placeholders and recall (0.768) is admittedly short, and a 35 KB __init__.py is heavy to review.

reads.best: Deterministic lifecycle hooks independently track evidence across turns and can request one recheck before a coding reply, without a second model or network service. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsLittleOdd/check-please/d9c370f09f7ae27b57047f74b235b60ddc7a6024/README.md)
reads.worst: English regex heuristics can count a successful no-op as proof and miss unsupported claims, while persisted command excerpts are not secret-redacted and screenshots remain placeholders. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsLittleOdd/check-please/d9c370f09f7ae27b57047f74b235b60ddc7a6024/README.md)

plugins.name: submission-desk
plugins.author: alfredbirkelund
plugins.does: Maintains a local application-readiness workspace linking requirements, exact instruction quotes, file hashes, human reviews and export snapshots.

reads.best: Human-only confirmations and hash-bound reviews are enforced across agent tools and the Desktop interface, with extensive adversarial regression tests.
reads.worst: Readiness depends on explicit rechecks and supported file formats; it does not watch folders continuously or verify the destination submission portal.

reads.best: Carefully separates agent proposals from human decisions and invalidates stale reviews when exact file bytes, rules or mappings change.
reads.worst: Its careful workflow is narrow: document-format recognition exceeds its actual page/word checking support, and users must finish the portal work themselves.

plugins.name: hermeneus
plugins.author: Bihruze
plugins.does: Live translation of audio playing on the Mac: Scribe STT, Hermes-model translation, floating subtitle strip, Desktop pane, optional speech.

reads.best: Ambitious native audio capture and overlay pipeline with very large tests, docs, screenshots and failure messages; key kept in secret store.
reads.worst: macOS-only (Windows preview) and needs a paid ElevenLabs key; some demo media still pending.

reads.best: Finished like a product, with driverless Core Audio capture, themed screenshots, a minimal child environment and heavy fakes-based tests.
reads.worst: macOS only (Windows a preview, Linux planned) and it needs an ElevenLabs key; the README still has a pending live capture.

plugins.name: phone-autopilot
plugins.author: jupist
plugins.does: Records phone tasks into routines that replay without the model, self-check with checkpoints, heal on app change and run daily.

reads.best: Model-free replay with checkpoints and healing, app guard hooks, Desktop pane and 13 test files.
reads.worst: Requires the phone-harness plugin and an Android setup, narrowing who can use it.

reads.best: Every routine save and every run of unapproved code goes through Hermes's approval prompt pinned to the script's sha256, and runs happen in a killable subprocess with checkpoints and failure screenshots.
reads.worst: Depends on a separate phone-harness plugin plus adb, and its system helpers work only on Android.

plugins.name: lights-out
plugins.author: JannetEkka
plugins.does: Prices AWS CLI creates for approval, ledgers every created resource with its delete command, posts a cost receipt, and /lights out deletes the unkept ones.

reads.best: Turns cloud-bill surprise into an approval step plus a cleanup ledger, with 140 offline tests and a benchmark against real Hermes and moto.
reads.worst: Sees only AWS CLI commands (not boto3, Terraform), prices are us-east-1 list only, and /lights out deletes from a ledger that could be wrong.

reads.best: A pre_tool_call price gate that fails closed with nobody to approve, a ledger matched from real CLI output, and a benchmark plus demo video recorded against a moto AWS stand-in.
reads.worst: Covers only the AWS CLI in one region's price table, so creates through SDKs, Terraform or other clouds go uncounted.

plugins.name: hype
plugins.author: asdugit
plugins.does: /hype turns the current session into a launch trailer rendered locally with headless Chromium, ffmpeg, composed music and optional Blender, with a Desktop studio.

reads.best: Ambitious, product-grade pipeline with a Desktop studio, consented SHA-pinned Blender download, network-off capture and over a thousand tests.
reads.worst: Heavy dependencies (Chromium, ffmpeg) and no cost cap or confirmation before a Directed film the README itself puts at several dollars of model usage.

reads.best: Finished product with seven presets, Desktop studio, and real session diffs as proof.
reads.worst: Heavy dependencies (Chromium, ffmpeg, optional Blender download) and AGPL licence; not run, so reliability is unverified.

plugins.name: workbench-link
plugins.author: dotmantissa
plugins.does: Routes native Hermes terminal, file and code tools to one explicitly bound Linux Docker project worker.

reads.best: Uses the terminal-environment provider rather than bypassing tool approvals, with authenticated transport, durable operation receipts and tested uncertainty fences.
reads.worst: Setup is substantial and supports only one foreground CLI environment per profile on Linux/Docker, excluding gateway multiplexing and delegated isolation.

reads.best: Changes where Hermes executes tools, with authentication, ledger and cleanup tests.
reads.worst: Pinned to Hermes 0.23.x, Linux and Docker, with complex setup and a narrow audience.

plugins.name: camel-guard
plugins.author: nativ3ai
plugins.does: Gates sensitive Hermes tool calls after untrusted output using capability categories classified solely from the current user request.

reads.best: Native hooks enforce a code-level authority boundary with fail-closed classification and tests covering direct, concurrent and sequential dispatch.
reads.worst: Authorization is only by broad effect category, so an already-authorized capability can still be misused for a different path, recipient or command.

reads.best: Hook-only guard with off/monitor/enforce modes, off by default, covers MCP tools conservatively.
reads.worst: Needs a structured-output classifier model; benefit is hard to see for users; tests live outside the plugin folder.

plugins.name: learnloop
plugins.author: huss-wrld
plugins.does: Turns Hermes into a structured tutor with graded questions, practice problems, persistent knowledge graphs and interactive Desktop learning views.

reads.best: Code enforces lesson phases and grading order while a substantial Desktop UI makes questions, practice and learned facts usable.
reads.worst: The composer middleware uses the focused chat rather than the sending chat, so an unusual multi-chat layout can submit text as the wrong question's answer.

reads.best: Enforces question and practice state in code and turns Hermes Desktop’s composer, transcript and sidebar into a coherent learning interface.
reads.worst: Teaching quality and graph accuracy still depend on the teacher model; the separate graph extraction and auditing pipeline has not been ported.

plugins.name: crash-recovery
plugins.author: sammy-XXIV
plugins.does: Journals protected tool execution and blocks further side effects after an uncertain outcome until an operator resolves it.

reads.best: Durable admission, integrity checks and cross-session blocking are backed by crash and concurrency tests.
reads.worst: One pending protected call blocks every other protected call in the profile, and resolution is manual.

reads.best: The execution middleware records intent before dispatch and explicitly blocks storage failures, with focused crash, cancellation, concurrency and corruption tests. [Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sammy-XXIV/hermes-crash-recovery/2d00ff5832a6a6d7aca0c09ef500a64a890efa14/recovery.py).
reads.worst: One protected call at a time and conservative error handling can halt ordinary or nested workflows until manual CLI reconciliation; history verification also grows with every event. [Limits and setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sammy-XXIV/hermes-crash-recovery/2d00ff5832a6a6d7aca0c09ef500a64a890efa14/README.md).

plugins.name: hermes-remote-hands
plugins.author: Vishnu-Aithal
plugins.does: Lets a server-hosted Hermes drive your own Mac over OpenSSH: shell, file edit/search, tmux processes and screen control through cua-driver, all behind the approval gate.

reads.best: Extends where Hermes runs onto the user's own machine with no agent on the Mac, approval-gated and credential-file aware, with a demo and offline CI.
reads.worst: Requires macOS plus SSH key setup and cua-driver, and the tests are few for such a powerful tool.

reads.best: Keeps one agent and memory across two machines, with separate approval scopes, resolved-path gates, real remote timeouts and offline/live test harnesses. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vishnu-Aithal/hermes-remote-hands/f807ba317cc55ff8b6cbf7668f243f98fb9218b4/__init__.py
reads.worst: Mac setup is lengthy, the bypass guard is explicitly best effort, and screen integration depends on private Hermes internals and an externally installed driver. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Vishnu-Aithal/hermes-remote-hands/f807ba317cc55ff8b6cbf7668f243f98fb9218b4/README.md

plugins.name: circuit-bench
plugins.author: juvenile454
plugins.does: An ESP32 workbench that checks pins against Espressif data, calculates parts, draws schematics, and builds, flashes, monitors and decodes crashes, with a Desktop bench and a simulated board.

reads.best: Hardware actions go through a pre_tool_call approval keyed to port, MAC and firmware SHA; allow_flash is off by default, it fails closed, and roughly 2,900 tests cover it.
reads.worst: Only ESP32 hobbyists will use it, real boards are tested on Linux only, and a /yolo session bypasses the approval prompts (disclosed).

reads.best: An unusually complete hardware workflow with deterministic engineering rules, explicit simulation, firmware-image hash checks, device identity checks and extensive regression fixtures.
reads.worst: Its audience is ESP32 builders, and the documented session /yolo and one-shot approval gap means users should retain allow_flash=false until deliberate hardware use.

plugins.name: rainbowomma
plugins.author: aviv27-dev
plugins.does: Separates each Hermes profile’s browser and leased resources on macOS and guards tool calls that could disrupt the human or another agent.

reads.best: The ownership registry, dedicated browser provider, leases, approval escalation, pre-tool guard, and cleanup solve cross-agent and human-resource collisions at the operating-system boundary.
reads.worst: It is a macOS-only system integration with many powerful process, document, and GUI actions; its guard is explicitly not a sandbox and its project exposes only two test modules.

reads.best: A browser provider plus fail-closed pre-tool guards and ownership-aware process/document cleanup directly improve agents running on the user's own hardware.
reads.worst: The guard inspects command text rather than confining programs, and macOS automation permissions and cooperative profile naming limit its guarantees.

plugins.name: hermes-line
plugins.author: uzay-eth
plugins.does: Gives Hermes a real Twilio phone line that, after approval, calls businesses, navigates menus, waits on hold and bridges the owner in.

reads.best: Ambitious new capability with approval gating and owner-consented SMS OTP release, secrets declared via requires_env.
reads.worst: Very large codebase (~900KB) that is hard to review, and setup needs a paid Twilio account plus a tunnel; tests (~1,400) sit at the repo root outside the plugin folder.

reads.best: Scoped single-use consent, restricted per-call Hermes sessions and extensive call/OTP tests support a real phone capability on the user's own account.
reads.worst: Twilio, a public tunnel and a separate call profile make setup substantial, while live detection of a real agent and successful bridging remain unproven in the documented trials.

plugins.name: night-shift
plugins.author: MuhammadMurtuzaHussain
plugins.does: Maintains incident runbooks and metrics context, diagnoses and proposes operational fixes, and requires explicit human approval before executing a fix, including Slack approval flows.

reads.best: The approval-code/fingerprint flow, Slack actions, runbook learning, and incident-oriented Desktop/demo material form a compelling agent operations product.
reads.worst: The implementation depends on substantial external deployment infrastructure and has only one repository test, leaving more integration risk than the documentation suggests.

reads.best: Human identity checks, expiring proposals, exact-command cards and recovery-before-learning form a useful complete on-call loop.
reads.worst: policy.py treats uniq as read-only without checking its output-file argument, so an incident command such as uniq input output can write before approval despite the read-only safety claim.

plugins.name: no-manual
plugins.author: cheedli
plugins.does: Helps assemble furniture with no instructions: finds the official manual, reverses disassembly photos into steps, or solves flat-pack carcass furniture from part photos via structured vision calls, then coaches step by step with photo checks and a Desktop 3D step viewer.

reads.best: A finished product: 14 tools, a deterministic solver and renderer with golden tests, a fail-closed safety gate for cribs and load-bearing furniture enforced in both handlers and a pre_tool_call hook, a 56-second demo video and a bundled three.js viewer.
reads.worst: It needs a vision-capable model and a gateway restart for the PDF renderer, and the solver only covers carcass furniture, so real-world coverage is narrower than the banner suggests.

reads.best: Real geometry solver, step-image renderer and Desktop 3D viewer behind vision calls via ctx.llm, with child and load-bearing furniture blocked twice in code (tool handlers and a pre_tool_call hook).
reads.worst: A home-furniture assembly helper is a niche use for most Hermes users, and its output is only as good as the vision model's reading of the photos.

plugins.name: solverforge-planner
plugins.author: blackopsrepl
plugins.does: Constraint-solves tasks into calendar availability and manages approved local plans plus cloud-calendar synchronization instructions.

reads.best: The actual Rust solver, stale-plan checks, scoped approvals, checksum-verified engine and calendar retry tests support a polished planning workflow.
reads.worst: Cloud calendar reads and writes still depend on the agent using another calendar tool and returning accurate pulls, rather than a direct transactional integration.

reads.best: Freshness checks, proposal fingerprints, scoped approvals and real-engine/calendar tests support an unusually complete planning workflow.
reads.worst: Cloud calendar reads and writes depend on Hermes coordinating a separate calendar tool, and first use requires a platform-specific engine download.

plugins.name: cacheguard
plugins.author: AIverflow
plugins.does: Uses Hermes request/execution middleware to warn or block costly context sends and report observed prompt-cache reuse ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AIverflow/hermes-cacheguard/4648bc056c28b9453d92089ffd9db09f11dc3392/README.md)).

reads.best: Directly improves the agent with configurable per-surface/model guards, single-call fail-open handling, bounded storage locks and extensive regression coverage.
reads.worst: Cache expiry cannot be known before sending; estimates and usage heuristics can misclassify risk, and private Hermes imports create ongoing compatibility work ([middleware](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AIverflow/hermes-cacheguard/4648bc056c28b9453d92089ffd9db09f11dc3392/guard.py)).

reads.best: The send guard, retry handling and usage journal improve the user’s own agent without extra model calls or stored message text.
reads.worst: Cache expiry cannot be known before sending, and cache accounting and unattended-mode detection depend on private Hermes helpers that may degrade across releases.

plugins.name: context-steward
plugins.author: jiangkoumo
plugins.does: Replaces context compression with checkpoint-or-fresh handoffs while preserving recent requests and searchable archived history.

reads.best: Directly improves long-running agent context with tool-pair closure, verbatim retention checks, redacted LLM calls and mechanical failure fallback.
reads.worst: Summary quality still depends on model judgment, and the plugin can return the original oversized transcript when its preservation and shrinkage checks cannot both pass.

reads.best: Directly improves the agent context lifecycle with guarded fresh-mode decisions, mechanical fallback, preservation checks and extensive boundary tests. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jiangkoumo/hermes-context-steward/ed2d16c1e97ad37c0821355b831ac3dc9181cd16/steward.py
reads.worst: Compaction still loses sampled facts and relies on model summaries; the README contains stale claims about using the host redactor and subclassing compressor helpers that differ from this implementation. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jiangkoumo/hermes-context-steward/ed2d16c1e97ad37c0821355b831ac3dc9181cd16/README.md

plugins.name: voice-unleashed
plugins.author: TacoTakumi
plugins.does: Serves a browser voice interface with streaming speech, interruption, spoken approvals, session attachment, and Desktop voice controls.

reads.best: It makes Hermes usable by voice from a phone or other browser and tests streaming, approvals, and session flows.
reads.worst: Setup needs a separate VoiceManager server and HTTPS for remote microphones; the page passes its access token in the URL.

reads.best: Implements a real interaction platform rather than an STT wrapper, with session continuation, reply routing, barge-in and browser/protocol regression tests. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TacoTakumi/hermes-voice-unleashed/f5573c909023be48dddb03fa36ad85dd80ca70ea/session.py
reads.worst: A separate VoiceManager speech stack and secure browser access make setup demanding; a shared URL token grants broad profile-session access, and approval integration uses private host APIs. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TacoTakumi/hermes-voice-unleashed/f5573c909023be48dddb03fa36ad85dd80ca70ea/README.md

plugins.name: hermes-vnc
plugins.author: YAN-XBT
plugins.does: Provides a VNC computer-use backend and optional Desktop live viewer for controlling another computer through Hermes.

reads.best: Native computer-use integration, scoped password lookup and scripted RFB fault tests make remote hardware control unusually complete.
reads.worst: A handshake timeout raises before retaining or closing the pending connection, and text input remains limited to ASCII or Latin-1 clipboard transfer.

reads.best: A real provider extension reaches remote machines through an existing protocol, with scoped credentials, explicit unsupported actions and scripted RFB fault tests. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YAN-XBT/hermes-vnc/2f1f8b906746dba670c526b06c87aa2859730d34/backend.py
reads.worst: Coordinate-only foreground input has no accessibility targeting and cannot type non-Latin-1 text; downscaled screenshots also require the model to convert coordinates. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YAN-XBT/hermes-vnc/2f1f8b906746dba670c526b06c87aa2859730d34/README.md

plugins.name: codecoach
plugins.author: heyitstony97-max
plugins.does: Builds small C or Python learning projects step by step, checking student code in a sandbox with visible and hidden tests and constrained hints.

reads.best: It turns Hermes into a real interactive programming tutor whose examples, progression, tests, hints, and Desktop UI are enforced by code.
reads.worst: Lesson quality and much of the project plan remain model-dependent, while sandbox, compiler, dependency, and long local-model setup requirements are substantial.

reads.best: Reference-solution, progression and hidden-output checks make the tutor materially more dependable than a teaching prompt.
reads.worst: Projects require a working Linux bubblewrap sandbox and can take minutes per step, while passing generated tests cannot establish teaching quality.

plugins.name: clack
plugins.author: adroidian
plugins.does: Adds end-to-end-encrypted agent-to-agent messaging over a relay, with identity enrollment, explicit acceptance, polling, reconciliation, and durable acknowledgements.

reads.best: This is a substantial new communication capability with encrypted messages, relay identity pinning, explicit human acceptance, and extensive offline adversarial/regression tests.
reads.worst: It requires a separate relay and peer enrollment, and its vendored pure-Python cryptography is explicitly not constant-time against a local timing adversary.

reads.best: End-to-end encrypted, signed messaging with explicit trust-on-first-contact avoidance and durable acknowledgements gives agents a distinct coordination channel.
reads.worst: It depends on an external relay and Linux, and initial setup requires independently verified relay and inviter keys, adding real onboarding friction.

plugins.name: patient-research
plugins.author: solo386
plugins.does: Searches and grades public trial and research evidence, stores local patient profiles, produces reports and handoffs, and schedules zero-model change watches.

reads.best: It backs a high-stakes workflow with deterministic evidence checks, exact-quote validation, privacy boundaries, confirmation gates, extensive fixtures, and code-rendered delivery.
reads.worst: Its clinical scope is inherently niche and the twenty-tool workflow asks users and agents to navigate substantial complexity.

plugins.name: screen-overlay
plugins.author: tuancookiez-hub
plugins.does: On Windows, draws click-through pointers, spotlights, step guides and sticky notes on the real desktop, using UI Automation targets.

reads.best: Gives Hermes a new ability on the user's own machine, with careful safety: no focus steal, expiry, a kill hotkey and an authenticated pipe.
reads.worst: Windows-only, the daemon has no automated tests, and the README screenshots are composites.

reads.best: Adds a tangible screen-level teaching capability with real UI targets, DPI handling, user-editable notes, expiry, an emergency clear shortcut, and focused client and shape tests.
reads.worst: At the pinned commit daemon_env copies the full Hermes environment into the PySide6/Qt child, unnecessarily exposing provider keys to that process.

plugins.name: skill-layers
plugins.author: tony-simons-aiowa
plugins.does: Preserves installed skill sources and publishes separately named derivatives after three-way merge review, with checkpoints, rollback and Desktop management.

reads.best: Directly improves Hermes skill maintenance with revision-bound publication, source preservation, profile isolation and unusually thorough failure-recovery tests.
reads.worst: V1 excludes plugin-registered skill bundles and never switches a running conversation to the preferred derivative, limiting seamless adoption.

reads.best: Revision and review-hash checks, immutable snapshots, no-replace publication and fault/path-boundary tests make source-preserving customization unusually careful.
reads.worst: It does not switch the running session to the preferred derivative, cannot accept plugin-bundled sources, and textual merges still need human behavioral review.

plugins.name: hermes-multiplayer
plugins.author: tyleramberry
plugins.does: Slack-like channels, DMs, threads and search inside Hermes Desktop, synced between up to five people's Hermes gateways directly or through a relay, where agents can post, read and be woken by @mentions.

reads.best: Turns single-user Hermes into a shared multi-human, multi-agent workspace using a platform handler, sync routes, four tools and a rich hand-written Desktop UI, with about 480 tests on sync, pairing, secret scope and wake injection.
reads.worst: Its disclosures say "No third-party services" while the default team-room flow sends unencrypted messages through an author-hosted workers.dev relay hard-coded in the code, a joined room's key is stored in plaintext SQLite, and there is no CI.

reads.best: The plugin makes agents and teammates participants in shared chat, with a polished Desktop experience and extensive coverage for sync, access, and thread behavior.
reads.worst: The pinned version defaults team-room traffic to a Cloudflare relay operated by the plugin author and also relies on a private Hermes session import, both concerns in the catalog review.

plugins.name: coolifybruecke
plugins.author: studioluftbruecke
plugins.does: A cockpit plugin for a self-hosted Coolify PaaS instance: reports what needs attention across the fleet, shows deployment history, diagnoses failed deploys from logs, and gates deploy/restart/stop/rollback actions behind human approval, with a Desktop dashboard pane.

reads.best: Tokens are declared as secrets and read only via Hermes's secret store; destructive actions require a human-approved one-time ticket and refuse unattended/cron contexts and protected environments by default; a dedicated prompt_injection.log fixture verifies the diagnose tool treats untrusted log text as data, never instructions.
reads.worst: Its value is tied to a specific self-hosting stack (Coolify), so it is strong but niche rather than broadly applicable to all Hermes users.

reads.best: Approval-gated actions, protected environments, secret-typed token, redaction patterns and a Desktop page with screenshots and many tests.
reads.worst: Useful only to Coolify users, and the failure diagnosis is plain pattern matching.

plugins.name: offgrid
plugins.author: emmaGH1
plugins.does: Platform adapter letting people with a basic phone and no data chat with Hermes over SMS/USSD via Africa's Talking.

reads.best: Scoped secret store, constant-time token check, phone allowlist and a command allowlist that refuses /yolo over SMS.
reads.worst: Only tested in the provider sandbox, and the question queue is in memory, so a restart can lose messages.

reads.best: A genuine new channel for people with no mobile data, with secrets read through Hermes's scoped secret store, constant-time callback token checks, an allowlist, rate limits and offline tests.
reads.worst: Sandbox-only by its own admission (no live carrier or handset tested) and it needs a public HTTPS endpoint the user must arrange.

plugins.name: phone-senses
plugins.author: LSUDOKO
plugins.does: Gives Hermes an Android phone's notifications, SMS, calls, location, money/bill/scam parsing and find-my-phone through a paired Termux:API helper.

reads.best: Puts Hermes onto the user's own phone with HMAC-paired helper, secret-store token and an approval prompt for every send, call, photo or OTP reveal.
reads.worst: No test suite in the plugin folder for ~2,900 lines handling SMS and money data, and setup needs a phone-side helper.

reads.best: Combines authenticated phone APIs, masked OTPs and native approval hooks with extensive tests and real-device demonstrations.
reads.worst: The default HTTP helper transport signs requests but does not encrypt sensitive phone responses; private networking requires care.

plugins.name: workspace
plugins.author: kaosjammo
plugins.does: Adds a local Desktop workspace for documents, databases, passage comments, scoped agent edits, and import/export.

reads.best: It pairs a finished document/database UI with narrowly revision-bound, user-reviewed agent editing and substantial source tests.
reads.worst: Its advanced native editing path depends on private same-process Hermes interfaces and is explicitly presented as a development preview.

reads.best: Revision-bound edits, explicit item grants and separate stop, restore and revert paths show serious attention to document integrity.
reads.worst: Finalization depends on private native-owner interfaces, while provider-positive editing and cancellation at this pin remain unqualified.

plugins.name: obol
plugins.author: UEddy
plugins.does: Creates and tracks Stripe or bank-transfer invoices through Hermes tools while putting every invoice write behind approval and deterministic risk checks.

reads.best: A remarkably product-complete money workflow with approval gating, injection and impersonation defenses, hash-chained logs, a dashboard, demo assets, and extensive adversarial tests.
reads.worst: Its protection is not absolute: pattern-based scam detection and an operator's approval remain critical to safe payment activity.
