reads.best: Combines scoped secrets, per-write approval requests, cron refusal, idempotency and tested invoice-specific scam checks into a practical cross-chat product.
reads.worst: Human approval still depends on Hermes policy: YOLO or approvals.mode off auto-approves its prompts; pattern-based scam checks and local hash chains have documented limits.

plugins.name: inset
plugins.author: winsznx
plugins.does: Measures rendered web-layout defects across viewports and gives Hermes evidence plus same-condition rechecks after edits.

reads.best: DOM measurements, section screenshots and conservative recheck classifications form a useful fix-and-verify loop backed by real-browser test cases.
reads.worst: Detection accuracy is established only on a controlled fixture, and external-scan DNS rebinding remains an acknowledged limitation.

reads.best: Recheck logic distinguishes genuine resolution from hidden or deleted targets and failed captures instead of accepting an edit as proof.
reads.worst: Accuracy on independent real-world sites is unmeasured, and Chromium installation adds setup overhead.

plugins.name: omlx
plugins.author: vitaliy-blprnt
plugins.does: Adds a managed Apple Silicon MLX runtime, public-model downloads, Desktop lifecycle controls and a native local inference provider.

reads.best: Makes local inference a first-class Hermes capability with checksum-pinned setup, scoped credentials, ownership-checked transport and tested cancellation and deletion boundaries.
reads.worst: It serves only macOS Apple Silicon, supports public Hugging Face models only, and requires in-process execution for its provider client.

reads.best: Registers a real provider and runs local models on user hardware, with checksum-pinned runtime and a scrubbed environment.
reads.worst: Apple Silicon and macOS only, and the provider needs in-process isolation.

plugins.name: proving-ground
plugins.author: dmustapha
plugins.does: A /provingground CLI that sends 24 harmless synthetic tool calls through the user's installed plugins in a throwaway child Hermes home, without calling the model, and reports what each plugin and the whole stack blocked, rewrote or let through.

reads.best: A genuinely new agent tool: it finds cross-plugin interactions (a rewriter slipping past a guard) through Hermes's real hook chain, isolated from the user's home, with dozens of test files and a hosted sample report.
reads.worst: Its audience is plugin authors and power users with large stacks, it can download about 650 MB of runtime on first use, and the pull request was still open when read.

reads.best: Baseline, solo and stack runs expose guard-versus-rewriter interactions through Hermes's actual dispatch path without calling a model, with rich reports and extensive fixtures. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dmustapha/hermes-proving-ground/11af83a569951bad96d62299c3e23cd7fc515ef4/proving_ground/census.py)
reads.worst: Child instrumentation replaces callbacks in private _hooks and _middleware registries, conflicting with catalog rule 9; its temporary homes also detect escaped rewrites only after execution. [Callback replacement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dmustapha/hermes-proving-ground/11af83a569951bad96d62299c3e23cd7fc515ef4/proving_ground/census.py) [Catalog rule 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/plugin-catalog/README.md)

plugins.name: rehearse
plugins.author: flamiinngo
plugins.does: Turns Hermes Desktop into an interview and presentation practice room with spoken questions, local speech and face analysis, scored replays, and model-written coaching.

reads.best: The integrated Desktop workflow combines live voice, local recording analysis, detailed replay, and tailored coaching, with seven focused test modules and clear privacy disclosure.
reads.worst: The experience depends on sizable platform-specific speech and vision dependencies, and Windows ARM loses full analysis.

reads.best: Combines camera and microphone capture, local speech and face analysis, live presence cues and scenario-specific coaching in a finished Desktop workflow.
reads.worst: Eye-contact scoring remains a head/pupil heuristic and filler detection is English-tuned; first-use speech and face models add setup weight.

plugins.name: saywhat
plugins.author: muhammadaus
plugins.does: Local faster-whisper STT provider that measures per-word confidence, asks the user to disambiguate, learns a personal dictionary and coaches pronunciation.

reads.best: Changes how Hermes hears voice input: confidence-aware confirmation before acting.
reads.worst: Depends on local Whisper models and hardware; v0.1.0.

reads.best: A useful change to Hermes voice input itself: uncertainty survives transcription, user corrections train future recognition, and tests exercise the learning loop.
reads.worst: confidence._readings materializes every candidate combination before keeping three, causing exponential memory/time growth on noisy or long dictation; confirmation is also model guidance rather than an enforced gate.

plugins.name: carnet
plugins.author: 404BugX
plugins.does: Provides local, layered long-term memory with bounded per-turn context, on-demand fact and document recall, optional embeddings, and a Desktop memory page.

reads.best: The native memory provider changes what Hermes remembers while keeping context bounded, profile-local data, and usable provenance and correction controls.
reads.worst: Automatic memory extraction and relevance recall can still miss or misclassify facts, and the pinned behavioral test suite is concentrated on storage and recall semantics.

reads.best: A native memory provider with addressable facts, lexical abstention, provenance and a substantial Desktop management surface.
reads.worst: dashboard/plugin_api.py writes custom endpoint keys to config.json and provider.py reads that file-backed fallback, violating the catalog secret-store rule; the advertised local embed_server.py is also absent.

plugins.name: sharewise
plugins.author: ardianreffa
plugins.does: Audits photo/video metadata and local visual privacy risks, lets the user review masks, and makes verified sanitized copies without changing originals.

reads.best: It combines local metadata checks, macOS Vision detection, human review, irreversible-looking redaction, and post-copy verification into a clear privacy workflow.
reads.worst: The macOS Vision path and several heavyweight imaging dependencies create platform-specific setup risk, while the visual detector cannot guarantee every sensitive feature is found.

reads.best: Its remove-only workflow preserves originals and re-reads outputs to verify redaction; on macOS it adds on-device detection and a visual review tool.
reads.worst: Automatic image detection depends on Apple Vision and is unavailable off macOS, leaving other systems to manual area selection.

plugins.name: docket
plugins.author: MKempler
plugins.does: Runs a trades-business workflow from voice or text job intake through deterministic price-book quotes, approval, customer acceptance, booking, follow-ups, and invoicing.

reads.best: It is an unusually complete product with Desktop, chat, customer web pages, PDFs, pricing tests, explicit approval before sending, and protections against unpriced extra work.
reads.worst: It has many stateful surfaces, email/web-server/payment-adjacent integrations, and a very broad codebase, so deployment and edge-case reliability remain substantial risks.

reads.best: Decimal pricing, unpriced-item blocking, approval gates and a tested quote lifecycle turn a concrete business workflow into a usable product.
reads.worst: Its audience is specialized, and external customer acceptance requires an owner-provided public URL or tunnel rather than working remotely out of the box.

plugins.name: hermes-notify
plugins.author: pkyanam
plugins.does: Links Hermes release workspaces to a phone through Notify, including progress, replies, signed receipts, a configurable Worker, and native approval transport.

reads.best: It makes remote release supervision and explicit phone approval a first-class Hermes workflow with durable state and careful disclosure.
reads.worst: Several headline capabilities—deployment, sign-in, deep links, and live progress—are explicitly unverified and require substantial external infrastructure.

reads.best: Uses Hermes’s native approval transport with exact action matching, bounded waits and durable replay prevention instead of treating ordinary phone replies as permission.
reads.worst: The complete live product path remains unfinished in verification: Worker deployment, App sign-in, deep links and live progress are explicitly unverified.

plugins.name: backfill
plugins.author: wth-amna
plugins.does: Replays old Hermes sessions into the active memory provider with dry-run, resume, deduplication and optional recall checks.

reads.best: It addresses a real migration pain through the standard memory hooks while preserving read-only history, redaction, confirmation and resumability.
reads.worst: It relies on some private Hermes internals and provider-specific behavior, so compatibility can change even with its careful fallbacks.

reads.best: A provider-independent migration path preserves the value of old chats while using Hermes memory redaction and ordinary provider hooks.
reads.worst: Original turn timestamps are lost, cloud providers remain untested, and resume bookkeeping is keyed by provider name rather than a particular destination store.

plugins.name: dreaming
plugins.author: hsyvy
plugins.does: A memory provider that records transcripts and notes and runs an offline dream pass that checks notes against transcripts, rewrites a linked wiki and keeps a capped index injected each session.

reads.best: It replaces Hermes's memory layer with consolidation that runs in the background, with real guard rails (path limits, size caps, backups, lock file) and an FTS5 store.
reads.worst: Relies heavily on the LLM dream pass, has no UI, and treats tool output as evidence, so fetched web text could be persisted into memory; its tests sit outside the plugin folder.

reads.best: Provider-level capture, automatic recall and bounded file-operation consolidation directly improve continuity across Hermes sessions.
reads.worst: Correction is still model judgment over retrieved excerpts; the reported gains come from small tests on one model and do not establish robust general memory accuracy.

plugins.name: tone-forge
plugins.author: efesn
plugins.does: Generates guitar-amp tone recipes from natural-language descriptions or reference-audio analysis, stores them as versioned presets, and can send real MIDI Control-Change messages to drive AmpliTube 5.

reads.best: Genuine hardware integration (ctypes bindings to winmm.dll for real MIDI I/O, a hand-rolled pure-Python FFT for reference-audio analysis) with careful safety design: MIDI never sent to an unselected port, sends labeled 'unverified' rather than claiming success, and SSRF-guarded URL/subprocess handling for reference-track fetches.
reads.worst: Niche audience (guitarists using AmpliTube 5 with MIDI gear) and the README itself admits no screenshots or recordings are committed yet and that actual AmpliTube receipt of MIDI messages hasn't been verified on the build machine.

reads.best: 162 passing tests, explicit SECURITY.md disclosing its only subprocess uses (fixed argv, no shell), and an honest 'what it does not do' section.
reads.worst: Windows-only and niche to AmpliTube 5 users with MIDI-mapped gear, limiting day-one install appeal.

plugins.name: pulse-rings
plugins.author: Stormxftw
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop monitoring pane of human-approved, automatically refreshed gauges and trends from public services, read-only MCP tools and local Hermes activity.

reads.best: Data-only definitions, explicit human activation, request budgets and a visual builder make persistent monitoring useful without repeated model calls.
reads.worst: Read-only MCP policy relies on private Hermes compatibility seams, and the documented minimum Hermes version was not verified by a clean install.

reads.best: Approval card lists every host and request rate, polling is data-only, and a deep test suite plus screenshots back it.
reads.worst: Version is 0.5.0-dev and the gallery is sample data, with a bulky 7,400-line pane.

plugins.name: data-lens
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Replaces eligible large local data-file reads with structural maps and adds bounded exact queries over CSV, JSON and JSONL.

reads.best: Read middleware preserves the built-in refusal path while adding full-record coverage, Decimal aggregates and extensive safety/runtime regression tests.
reads.worst: POSIX host-local only with a 16 MiB ceiling; it rereads files and offers cooperative time limits rather than hard resource isolation.

reads.best: Explicit secret/credential filename denylist (blocks reading files like 'secrets.json', 'client_secret.json', 'token.json') and a scrupulously honest README about scope limits.
reads.worst: Solves a fairly narrow pain point (oversized file reads) that a well-designed prompt/skill could partially mitigate with chunked reads.

plugins.name: proof-run
plugins.author: raffieeey
plugins.does: Records operator-demonstrated tool workflows as contracts, checks fresh read evidence at the tool boundary, and fail-closed blocks mutations that do not match the proven contract.

reads.best: It turns demonstrations into an enforceable, versioned action gate rather than a prompt promise, with bounded state, approval-aware capture, and extensive semantic tests.
reads.worst: The safety logic is subtle and host-API dependent; the catalog folder has a concise README and limited visible integration coverage compared with the complexity of the gate.

reads.best: Consumable read observations, durable unproven states and carefully tested atomic storage make a concrete fail-closed tool-boundary guard.
reads.worst: It permits only exact demonstrated actions, cannot enforce workflow ordering or stop alternate tool routes, and cannot undo a mutation whose result fails its evidence check.

plugins.name: skillcheck
plugins.author: neta-gym
plugins.does: Observes skill edits, snapshots revisions, generates reviewable regression cases, runs them in narrowed child sessions, reports verdicts, and offers reversible promote/revert commands.

reads.best: It creates a practical regression loop for self-modifying skills while explicitly distinguishing first runs, regressions, judge failures, snapshots, and human promotion.
reads.worst: The child sessions share the real environment and the LLM judge can be unavailable, so its safety and verdict quality depend on Hermes lifecycle behavior and careful review.

reads.best: Directly improves Hermes self-improvement with revision tracking, zero-tool child sessions, timeout cancellation and reversible user-invoked restores.
reads.worst: Its optional judge uses bool(payload["passed"]), so a JSON string "false" becomes a pass; tool-less, truncated skill replays also cannot verify real tool behavior.

plugins.name: secretshield
plugins.author: Whydiriki700
plugins.does: Scans tool arguments, tool results, and final replies for credential material and blocks or redacts leaks while keeping a metadata-only incident ledger.

reads.best: It addresses a high-value agent-specific failure mode at the exact pre-dispatch and pre-delivery boundaries, with fail-closed behavior and tests for secret non-persistence.
reads.worst: Pattern detection cannot guarantee semantic secret discovery, and blocking or rewriting every surface can create compatibility and false-positive costs.

plugins.name: freebusy
plugins.author: davidtsaidavid
plugins.does: Schedules meetings by email from free/busy data, holding offered slots, enforcing timezone and approval policy, and booking only through guarded paths.

reads.best: Its invariant-driven policy, hold ledger, timezone handling, owner approvals, reminders, fixture demo, and broad tests make a risky automation domain unusually careful.
reads.worst: The pinned release explicitly leaves the Google Workspace adapter unwired, so the impressive tested fixture path does not yet deliver the advertised real-calendar integration.

plugins.name: flightlog
plugins.author: piyushpradhan
plugins.does: Records agent runs locally, detects suspicious successful-looking behavior, and presents findings in CLI, dashboard, and Desktop views.

reads.best: It turns Hermes lifecycle data into practical run-quality checks, baselines, incident explanations, and a strong review UI with focused tests.
reads.worst: Several findings are necessarily heuristic from tool names, output text, and historical baselines, so they can miss failures or flag legitimate runs.

reads.best: Catches the unattended-cron failure mode with clear rules, a Desktop and dashboard view and screenshots.
reads.worst: The idea overlaps with generic observability and it edits the agent's answer with a note, with a single test file for 1,600 lines.

plugins.name: study-tree
plugins.author: IpastorSan
plugins.does: Branches side questions into separate Hermes sessions, resolves them back into the main thread, and renders requested research or time-change results as interactive widgets.

reads.best: It changes conversation topology and Desktop presentation, with explicit prompt policies, multiple tools/hooks, screenshots, and both Python and JavaScript tests.
reads.worst: The injected system-prompt directives are broad and unusually prescriptive, so prompt interactions and host surface compatibility remain meaningful risks.

plugins.name: leaveby
plugins.author: AloysJehwin
plugins.does: Uses Google Maps or TomTom to save places, calculate traffic-aware ETAs and leave-by plans, inject route context, and run no-agent background departure alerts.

reads.best: It combines real external-world routing, multi-stop planning, a pre-LLM context hook, and token-free cron alerts into a genuinely useful travel assistant.
reads.worst: Correctness and privacy depend on paid/limited map APIs and cron environment passthrough; the background watcher is an additional deployment surface with only one listed test file.

plugins.name: proveit-tests
plugins.author: jonathan-kellerai
plugins.does: Deterministically (AST + regex) flags an agent weakening tests to reach green, in observe/escalate/block modes, with a receipt ledger.

reads.best: Net-new-edit detection, human-approval escalation and a cheat/legit corpus with real-Hermes demo recording.
reads.worst: Python-strong only; JS/TS heuristic, and it admits it can be bypassed.

reads.best: Deterministic before/after detectors target agent test cheating directly, with net-new filtering and an adversarial corpus that also tests legitimate refactors. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KellerAI/proveit-tests-hermes/2412a18441611c988ec426b5c40b2b829ebb84d1/proveit_tests/hooks/runtime.py
reads.worst: Heuristics and inline waivers leave bypasses, while one shared runtime holds snapshots, pending warnings and nudge state without session keys, risking cross-session attribution under concurrency. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KellerAI/proveit-tests-hermes/2412a18441611c988ec426b5c40b2b829ebb84d1/proveit_tests/hooks/runtime.py

plugins.name: atomicmail
plugins.author: 7supersayin
plugins.does: Gives the agent its own @atomicmail.ai inbox as a gateway platform with DKIM-checked senders, mail tools and calendar invites.

reads.best: Email channel adapter that drops forged senders via DKIM and loop-guards, with tests.
reads.worst: Depends on a third-party mail service and sends mail from the agent, relying on prompt guidance for confirmation.

reads.best: Implements the channel as well as tools, including aligned-DKIM verification, loop rejection, scoped secrets, real signed-message tests, and invitation workflows.
reads.worst: Sign-ins repeatedly require CPU-intensive proof-of-work and initially delay listening, while unsigned senders and other Atomic Mail senders cannot use the secure default channel.

plugins.name: tinfoil-sandbox
plugins.author: counterposition
plugins.does: A terminal/execution backend that reroutes Hermes's terminal, code-execution and file tools to run inside a remote, attestation-verified confidential-computing enclave over an SSH tunnel.

reads.best: Reads its API key through Hermes's own secret_scope (not a plain file), explicitly strips admin/tunnel keys from any environment it passes along, and is tested with a stand-in CLI across many real failure scenarios.
reads.worst: Niche audience (users who already run a Tinfoil confidential-computing container) limits how many Hermes users would install it day one.

reads.best: It changes where Hermes runs and keeps the existing tool surface while stripping tunnel credentials and retaining dangerous-command approval.
reads.worst: The small plugin has no bundled tests and requires several separately installed Tinfoil, SSH, container, and key prerequisites.

plugins.name: test-drive
plugins.author: Xuefeng-Zhu
plugins.does: Detects capability gaps, recommends catalog plugins, and runs an approved pinned candidate in a temporary Hermes profile with before/after receipts.

reads.best: Combines conversational gap hooks, trust cards, approval-gated exact-SHA installs, bounded child runs and transcript-verified tool-use evidence.
reads.worst: The temporary profile is not OS isolation, and plugins requiring Desktop, hardware, existing user data or OAuth cannot demonstrate their normal value there.

plugins.name: hermes-sonic-ui
plugins.author: iKnz990
plugins.does: Adds local sound synthesis, opt-in Desktop event sounds, an eight-layer composition editor and reviewed model-generated patches.

reads.best: A complete local audio workspace combines composition/export with Desktop event integration, explicit audio consent and guarded, hash-bound source injection.
reads.worst: Native platform verification is concentrated on Windows, while automated Desktop/model integration uses SDK fixtures and Compose is limited to four bars.

plugins.name: radar
plugins.author: Naroh091
plugins.does: Watches mail, calendars, repositories and chats to maintain long-lived tasks, investigate developments and proactively deliver decisions to the owner.

reads.best: Implements persistent cross-source tasks, lifecycle observation, bounded background jobs, consent-bound operations and a Desktop/dashboard view with extensive tests.
reads.worst: The unattended-job firewall permits browser tools, terminal and execute_code; its own implementation admits scripts and SSH evade effect checks, weakening the external-action consent guarantee.

plugins.name: hermes-rescue
plugins.author: 0xNexuz
plugins.does: Guards Hermes's own files from destructive or unapproved agent edits, snapshots approved risky edits for undo, and explains actual model-provider failures.

reads.best: It addresses real self-damage and opaque-error failures through Hermes hooks, snapshots and a cross-surface Desktop control panel, with the human approval gate preserved.
reads.worst: The command/path guard must reason across many shells and platform path forms, and when it cannot resolve a relative path it deliberately permits the call.

plugins.name: headway
plugins.author: hanii090
plugins.does: Detects repeated local tool activity that changes neither workspace state nor observable evidence or read coverage, then gives recovery guidance and can block continued same-class loops.

reads.best: It adds a novel middleware-level progress signal across different commands, and tests exercise both warnings and actual pre-execution blocking.
reads.worst: It only fingerprints bounded local workspace samples, so remote effects and changes outside the selected workspace cannot count as progress; enforce mode is not an authorization boundary.

plugins.name: precedent-log
plugins.author: quotumorg
plugins.does: Stores board-scoped human rulings, injects applicable context for Kanban workers, and can veto repeated questions while exposing CLI and Desktop review.

reads.best: It turns prior human decisions into durable, scoped agent context with unusually strong audit, Desktop, recovery, and safety disclosures.
reads.worst: The cooperative veto can leave a worker card running, and matching text is not proof that the ruling was actually applied.

reads.best: Durable ruling records, bounded veto history and a Desktop retirement interface make human decisions reusable across workers.
reads.worst: Default enforcement can leave a worker card running indefinitely after a veto, and matching and compliance rely on word overlap and text markers.

plugins.name: cost-forecast
plugins.author: mr-jude-justin
plugins.does: Quotes a task's likely cost before it runs and pauses for approval when projected or actual spend exceeds budgets.

reads.best: Deep hook coverage and a large test suite enforcing spend caps the model cannot raise.
reads.worst: Estimates are heuristic and it serves API-key users only.

plugins.name: external-agents-agy
plugins.author: NomieC
plugins.does: Registers a custom Hermes model-provider that supervises the external AGY (Antigravity) CLI as a subprocess so Hermes's delegate_task can hand child tasks to that separate, already-authenticated agent instead of Hermes's native subagent loop.

reads.best: Unusually rigorous safety engineering for a high-impact capability: durable at-most-once job fencing, owner-only file permissions, explicit opt-in gating, non-bypassable shell-approval dialogs, and an honest limitations section backed by real unit tests.
reads.worst: Narrow applicability since it requires a specific external CLI already installed and authenticated, with only macOS arm64 actually live-tested.

plugins.name: hermes64
plugins.author: ark-qhantom
plugins.does: Lets Hermes plan, build, validate, playtest and export small late-1990s-style 3D adventure games in Godot.

reads.best: It makes Hermes itself a game-making system, with many native tools, skills, story checks, bot playtests, assets and a desktop surface.
reads.worst: The scope is ambitious and setup is heavy: Godot and Python dependencies are required, platform support is limited, and human playability is not proven.

plugins.name: restoreproof
plugins.author: Surajkumar5050
plugins.does: Restores backups in an isolated Docker network, boots the app, checks declared customer workflows and produces evidence-backed recovery verdicts.

reads.best: It tests the claim that a backup works against real data-linked workflows, with clear PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL/BLOCKED semantics, approvals, cleanup, reports and a polished Desktop view.
reads.worst: A safe useful drill still requires Docker, an app image, backup inputs and a carefully declared contract, so setup is substantial and operational edge cases remain.

plugins.name: agent-autocommit
plugins.author: gatoarmen
plugins.does: Automatically commits each agent turn's own hunks locally, isolates concurrent sessions, records task rationale and writes WHY.md summaries on completion.

reads.best: It changes Hermes's collaboration and accountability model with direct Git plumbing, profile identity, secret-name filtering, no-push defaults and a demo plus extensive tests.
reads.worst: It performs implicit repository writes on lifecycle hooks and has a complex concurrency and configuration surface where unusual Git states can still be difficult to reason about.

plugins.name: pwn-board
plugins.author: t4lus-sec
plugins.does: Adds an evidence-backed search board and operator review workflow for investigations, including goal tests and independent verifier subagents.

reads.best: It materially improves long-running agent work with a tested evidence ledger, immutable goal-test verdicts, review gates, Desktop UI, and independent verification.
reads.worst: The rich workflow and retained tool-output database add substantial complexity and are most valuable for investigations rather than routine chats.

reads.best: A structured evidence ledger and independent verification can make long investigations auditable and reduce unsupported agent conclusions.
reads.worst: The workflow is specialized and the goal test runs a configured command through Hermes terminal, so setup and execution policy require care.

plugins.name: smriti
plugins.author: vn-envy
plugins.does: Provides local MCP personal memory with scoped, dated facts, history, retrieval, and source evidence.

reads.best: Its local SQLite MCP server preserves corrections and temporal evidence while validating inputs and containing database access.
reads.worst: Memory capture remains explicit tool use, so it does not automatically retain a conversation the agent never sends to it.

reads.best: Its single-file SQLite design combines dated facts and raw episodes with lexical, semantic, entity, and temporal retrieval without a memory service.
reads.worst: The pinned plugin package contains no focused test suite, and its more capable fact extraction and consolidation mode requires configuring an external model.

plugins.name: hermes-tube
plugins.author: pedroberaldo87
plugins.does: Brings YouTube subscriptions into Hermes Desktop with folders, tabs, model-built topic tabs, cleanup and a browser extension.

reads.best: Full product: Desktop page, tools, RPC, extension, local DB, many tests and screenshots with sample data.
reads.worst: Huge surface incl. a 960KB bundled desktop plugin.js and browser extension that are hard to review; YouTube-specific.

plugins.name: talaria-bench
plugins.author: devorun
plugins.does: Builds and benchmarks servo-robot models in MuJoCo and gates robot motion on matching simulation preflights ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devorun/talaria-bench/511006ebe6ec8156b080f98e24698ef8ffa84660/README.md)).

reads.best: A complete local workflow combines randomized physics, exact-motion gates, generated firmware, virtual hardware, Desktop/dashboard replays and targeted safety tests.
reads.worst: The automatic return home is not simulated, and the README documents real moves that passed simulation but tipped the foam robot because friction was not modeled ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devorun/talaria-bench/511006ebe6ec8156b080f98e24698ef8ffa84660/hooks.py)).

reads.best: A novel simulation-gated path from agent to real hardware, with a dashboard, gallery, calibration and many test files.
reads.worst: Narrow audience (DIY servo robot builders) and it adds heavy dependencies (mujoco, numpy).

plugins.name: cron-budget
plugins.author: heirakug
plugins.does: A middleware/hook plugin that keeps a shared SQLite ledger of provider LLM-call counts across profiles and, in enforce mode, holds cron-triggered chat completions once usage passes a reserved threshold so interactive chat always keeps its quota.

reads.best: Structurally guaranteed to never block interactive chat, fails open on internal errors, and stores only call metadata with real unit and declared e2e tests covering edge cases.
reads.worst: Only the chat_completions API mode is actually enforced; other modes (Anthropic Messages, Codex Responses) are merely logged as 'would-block', so protection is partial.

reads.best: Enforces a real execution gate with observe-first setup, one notice per window and no model call for held jobs.
reads.worst: Anthropic/Codex API modes and delegated cron children are not blocked, while quota decisions and call recording are separate transactions that can race.

plugins.name: skilluminati
plugins.author: yxssxn
plugins.does: A plugin that empirically A/B-tests whether an installed Hermes skill helps: it replays past tasks once with and once without the skill, has a blind, order-swapped, hash-pinned-rubric LLM judge pick the better answer, and surfaces an Enlightened/Dead-weight/Hindrance/Unproven verdict via chat and a Desktop dashboard page.

reads.best: Genuinely novel idea executed with unusual rigor: PII redaction before any model call, frozen/hash-verified rubrics, blind order-swapped judging, and a self-test harness with deliberately poisoned fixtures to validate the judge itself; the plugin never holds credentials of its own.
reads.worst: No conventional pytest-style test directory (only its own selftest.py harness), and its own README discloses that repeated runs on the same skill can give unstable verdicts.

reads.best: Two-order blind judging, noise checks, model-consistency guards, call budgets and redaction turn skill evaluation into a practical Hermes workflow. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yxssxn/skilluminati/0affc46618f62d9b497f177178acefb83f63dd02/plugin/skilluminati/realrun.py)
reads.worst: The public pin omits its claimed unit suite, and replay offers no live tools, so costly text-answer comparisons cannot establish whether a skill improves real tool-using tasks. [Replay code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yxssxn/skilluminati/0affc46618f62d9b497f177178acefb83f63dd02/plugin/skilluminati/realrun.py) [Test disclosure](https://api.github.com/repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls/153804)

plugins.name: headroom
plugins.author: seongj-un
plugins.does: Guards heavy Hermes terminal jobs with reduced parallelism, shared queue slots, memory-capped systemd scopes and a pressure watchdog.

reads.best: Directly improves agents running on small personal hardware through enforceable resource controls and tests covering actual cgroup isolation and OOM handling.
reads.worst: Isolation is Linux/systemd-dependent and begins after process discovery, so early allocations and work performed by an external Docker daemon escape the memory cap.

plugins.name: sealed
plugins.author: kailashrajh
plugins.does: Provides an AES-256-GCM encrypted local secret store through Hermes's SecretSource interface and a management CLI.

reads.best: Its secret-source integration uses authenticated encryption, atomic 0600 writes, fail-closed errors, and focused crypto and permission tests.
reads.worst: The encryption key resides on the same host as the store, so it does not protect against a compromised user account.

plugins.name: stagehands
plugins.author: Peetbog69
plugins.does: Adds a delegation provider that routes subagent work to typed, token-budgeted worker roles and includes context-hygiene controls.

reads.best: It changes Hermes's delegation routing with a zero-config worker roster, bounded routes, fail-closed unknown-worker handling, and provider contract tests.
reads.worst: Its default worker routes depend on particular external model identifiers, so live provider availability and cost are outside its tested contract.

plugins.name: llmux
plugins.author: ivcained
plugins.does: Routes Hermes model requests across inference marketplaces by price or speed and exposes seller choices in Desktop.

reads.best: It combines a real model provider, authenticated local proxy, live offer routing and a Desktop seller switcher with extensive tests.
reads.worst: The pinned release lacks a paid end-to-end reply and installed Desktop seller-switch test, and operation needs a funded marketplace key.

plugins.name: rowverdict
plugins.author: demir-sama
plugins.does: Provides a local, approval-gated workflow for inspecting tabular files, defining contracts, quarantining bad rows, replaying corrections, and exporting audit receipts.

reads.best: Its source-bound contracts, separate host approvals, immutable exports, and unusually deep tests turn risky data imports into an auditable workflow.
reads.worst: The careful import-and-replay workflow is specialized rather than an everyday need for most Hermes users.

plugins.name: claim-receipts
plugins.author: gwelby
plugins.does: Captures observed session file mutations and commands, then emits a local receipt classifying recognized assistant claims as backed, unbacked, unverifiable, or contradicted.

reads.best: It makes an agent session externally auditable with an explicit evidence model and unusually candid, precise limits.
reads.worst: It fails open and the authors state it has not been run inside a live Hermes session; its pattern-based claim judge cannot assess many real claims.

plugins.name: quota-gauge
plugins.author: cynricantao
plugins.does: Adds a polished Hermes Desktop dashboard for subscription quota windows and persistent token-use charts across configured providers.

reads.best: It combines a real Desktop UI, guarded secret-store access, quota caching, and a durable local usage ledger into a product-quality operational view.
reads.worst: Several provider cards are necessarily limited by unavailable provider or Hermes usage APIs, and the full UI is not covered by end-to-end tests.

plugins.name: mnemos
plugins.author: bugnarokdev
plugins.does: Replaces Hermes memory with locally encrypted, portable memory checkpoints indexed on Sui and stored on Walrus testnet.

reads.best: It implements a real memory provider with local recall, client-side encryption, signed history, restore, and documented verification.
reads.worst: The durable path depends on external testnets and a multistep Sui setup, while the checked-in suite is comparatively small.

plugins.name: popquiz
plugins.author: 4n0nn43x
plugins.does: Turns a supplied document into a source-anchored live phone quiz, comparing the room with configured model players.

reads.best: It is an unusually complete, source-checked multiplayer product with local hosting, a demo, Desktop pane, and extensive tests.
reads.worst: Live model comparisons require Hermes model capabilities and can expose the document to the configured provider.

plugins.name: sieve
plugins.author: VGFreakXBL
plugins.does: Adds a user-configured notification policy that routes Hermes events through tiers, holds, digests, messaging, and optional phone alarms.

reads.best: Its policy matrix distinguishes desired urgency from the delivery arm and reports degraded escalation honestly.
reads.worst: High-priority delivery relies on external Hermes/mobile surfaces and an opt-in watcher, so it cannot guarantee detection or alarms.

plugins.name: foundry
plugins.author: aks-cmyk
plugins.does: Runs a creator workflow whose bots share a durable ledger of brand identity, sourced evidence, drafts, feedback, performance, and money, with dashboard and Desktop views.

reads.best: The shared ledger links sourced evidence and revisions to drafts and performance, while the dashboard and Desktop app make the state inspectable; approval and posting are disabled.
reads.worst: It is a narrowly targeted creator workflow, and its agent-supplied research has no live web-search surface in this Hermes version.

plugins.name: stave
plugins.author: Adolanium
plugins.does: A Hermes Desktop page where the agent writes checked ABC sheet music from a sentence, plays it with note highlighting, revises selected bars and exports PDF/SVG/MIDI/WAV.

reads.best: A real code checker (bar lengths, range, syntax) validates the model's notation, inside a finished Desktop page with GIFs, its own model slot and 48 Python/JS tests.
reads.worst: A niche audience, and stave_open casts tempo with int() without error handling.

plugins.name: patchsmith
plugins.author: icporcincula
plugins.does: Delegates a bounded coding task to a user-hosted local model through a restricted file/test tool loop and can return a reviewed, verified patch.

reads.best: It is unusually complete: path and test-file guards, budgets, rollback, isolated proposal mode, verified patch application, benchmarks, and extensive tests.
reads.worst: It is deliberately limited to bounded tasks and needs an owner-configured local model plus authorized test command.

reads.best: A local model can handle mechanical edits without sending project code to a hosted model; proposal mode, path protections, bounded budgets, and secret-minimal subprocess environments support safer use.
reads.worst: It requires a local tool-calling model and compatible endpoint; only Ollama is described as measured, and the entry’s effectiveness depends on the quality of that model and owner-configured checks.

plugins.name: proofly
plugins.author: 0xileri
plugins.does: Verifies claimed Base transfers against read-only chain evidence and corrects tool results or final replies when token, recipient or raw amount do not match.

reads.best: It addresses a distinctive agent failure mode with exact structured intent, chain-id and log checks, conservative verdicts, replay-safe correlation, tests and output correction.
reads.worst: It is limited to Base mainnet and allowlisted payment-tool conventions, so coverage must be configured and expanded for other chains and transaction shapes.

reads.best: Strict, read-only verifier (chain-id check, exact raw amounts, confirmations, time budget) wired into post_tool_call, transform_tool_result and transform_llm_output, tested against recorded real Base transactions.
reads.worst: Narrow scope (Base mainnet, simple transfers, only tools the user names) and no screenshots or video, so it serves few Hermes users.

plugins.name: butler
plugins.author: Intenzi
plugins.does: Follow-mode screen guide: the agent plans, a macOS overlay rings the real control and verifies each step via Accessibility.

reads.best: Novel desktop operator with native overlay, Desktop UI, many tests and checksummed helper download.
reads.worst: macOS only, and the repo is bloated with spike and planning files.

reads.best: The readable native companion makes the agent helpful inside existing apps without automating user clicks, backed by detailed guide and Desktop tests. [Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Intenzi/hermes-butler/a665eaed96adc6ceb54277616c1f7b9b5b817332/desktop/plugin.js).
reads.worst: Desktop code queries the core pet canvas and handles document pointer events outside SDK slots, conflicting with catalog rule 8; helper downloads also trust a checksum fetched alongside the release asset. [Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Intenzi/hermes-butler/a665eaed96adc6ceb54277616c1f7b9b5b817332/desktop/plugin.js). [Catalog rule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/plugin-catalog/README.md). [Limits and setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Intenzi/hermes-butler/a665eaed96adc6ceb54277616c1f7b9b5b817332/README.md).

plugins.name: baton
plugins.author: 4n0nn43x
plugins.does: Transfers a session and Git snapshot to another Hermes instance and retrieves a branch whose exact tree passed the agreed remote check.

reads.best: A substantive remote-workflow extension with resumable idempotent runs, blocking outgoing secret scans, fresh-tree verification, and tests for preserving the local working state.
reads.worst: It requires a shared Git remote and peer setup, and check execution falls back to the remote user's unsandboxed rights when bubblewrap is unavailable.

reads.best: Resumable git-ref handoffs, Runs API idempotency, secret scanning and tree-bound verification are backed by detailed failure-path tests and reproducible demos.
reads.worst: Remote checks run unsandboxed when bubblewrap is unavailable, and peers._secret falls back to process environment after a scoped lookup misses or fails.

plugins.name: egress-guard
plugins.author: moussetea315
plugins.does: Uses Hermes hooks to redact secrets, gate data-upload commands, and suppress sensitive small-cell or microdata disclosures in arguments, results, and replies.

reads.best: It turns practical data-loss prevention and statistical disclosure controls into a large, policy-driven, tested agent egress boundary.
reads.worst: Its parsers are deliberately heuristic and cannot certify safe disclosure or catch every network-exfiltration form.

reads.best: Brings research-data-centre output vetting to agents in code outside the model, including secondary suppression so a hidden cell cannot be recovered from totals, with a broad test suite.
reads.worst: Upload detection is pattern matching that a determined command can slip past, and fail_mode defaults to open on internal errors.

plugins.name: borealwork
plugins.author: raldblox
plugins.does: Hire verified humans for real-world tasks on boreal.work, with 12 tools, a spend-guard hook and a verdict digest.

reads.best: The spend guard enforces caps and approval before money moves.
reads.worst: Live PayPal money against an external service.

plugins.name: tinfoil-provider
plugins.author: counterposition
plugins.does: Model provider for Tinfoil enclave inference via an on-demand attested local proxy, plus a sandbox environment plugin.

reads.best: Changes where Hermes runs inference, with tests, e2e, install demo gif and secret-store key.
reads.worst: Needs a Tinfoil account and a separate proxy binary.

plugins.name: coffee-vram
plugins.author: jimmy77733
plugins.does: An llm_execution middleware that checks whether a local Ollama model fits in VRAM before each call, queues or evicts idle models, and shows a Desktop chip, pane and /vram.

reads.best: Changes how Hermes runs on the user's own GPU with a real fit estimator, a bounded queue (it times out and runs the call anyway) and many unit and e2e tests, plus measured research.
reads.worst: Only helps users of an external Ollama, and its many tuning settings (pool, KV type, overhead) take hardware knowledge to set correctly.

reads.best: Execution middleware and a FIFO scheduler manage local-model contention that a prompt cannot control, with tests for eviction and host-mode handoff.
reads.worst: Timeout or missing telemetry deliberately admits calls anyway, so memory safety is not guaranteed, and the install command still contains a placeholder repository.

plugins.name: mission-control
plugins.author: rohitdanda
plugins.does: A live, read-only observability dashboard for Hermes Desktop that streams tool calls, model calls, subagents, and approval events into a cost/token meter, call waterfall, and loop detector.

reads.best: Purely observer-based (8 lifecycle hooks, 'never written to: no tools, no middleware, no approval answers'), every hook fails open, no credentials or network calls at all, and ships a banner image and dashboard screenshot plus a Node-based UI smoke test under React 19.
reads.worst: It adds no new agent capability beyond observability — useful for operators but not something that changes what the agent itself can do (lower on 'beyond a prompt' than plugins that add real tools/providers).

plugins.name: conductor
plugins.author: capthvnsen
plugins.does: Orchestrates local and remote coding agents, monitors runs without model polling, and reports completion, errors, or approval needs to the asking chat.

reads.best: It gives Hermes real multi-agent execution, persistent monitoring, safe launch recipes, remote support, and polished progress reporting, with a large behavioral test suite and real-run demo.
reads.worst: It starts agents with the user's own permissions and imports a private Hermes session helper for routing, so the broad execution capability carries maintenance and operational risk.

reads.best: Real asynchronous supervision and resumable run records let Hermes coordinate existing coding-agent apps without spending model tokens while waiting.
reads.worst: At the field-pinned 0.4.2 code, arbitrary executable names are accepted and children inherit the process environment, with no explicit Hermes approval request before launch.

plugins.name: upstash
plugins.author: CahidArda
plugins.does: Memory provider that recalls Upstash Redis Search memories into each turn, stores searchable chat history, mirrors the built-in memory tool and adds four memory tools.

reads.best: A real MemoryProvider that changes Hermes's memory, reads its token through Hermes's get_secret, keeps writes to the primary agent only and has tests for the provider and Redis layout.
reads.worst: Needs a hosted Upstash database and the upstash-redis package, which a plain directory install of the catalog entry does not bring in by itself.

plugins.name: webgraft
plugins.author: ElSerda
plugins.does: Replaces web extraction with local page/PDF/Office reading, flags bot walls as errors, focuses long pages and appends a footer listing pages really opened.

reads.best: Web provider plus five hooks give small and local models verifiable sourcing, backed by roughly 110 tests and a very thorough README with a setup CLI.
reads.worst: Many behaviours (reminder injection, reply rewriting) interact with other plugins and optional Crawl4AI/OCR installs are heavy.

plugins.name: agenda-guardian
plugins.author: Moodtuner997
plugins.does: Deterministic day/week planner that schedules tasks around calendar events, corrects estimates by your median error and only writes to Google Calendar after opt-in and approval.

reads.best: Around 190 tests, CI, no model calls, and calendar writes gated behind an explicit switch and a yes.
reads.worst: Long, dense README; niche toward people who want rigid planning.

plugins.name: topoi
plugins.author: AlaisterLeung
plugins.does: Platform plugin that organizes Hermes chats into topics in Desktop/Dashboard and delivers cron results as replyable topic threads.

reads.best: Changes how Desktop organizes sessions, with a Desktop plugin, dashboard tab, screenshots and a mobile client.
reads.worst: Checks are ad-hoc check_ scripts rather than a pytest suite; requires gateway restart.

plugins.name: hermes-custodian
plugins.author: Cam-AcitveIce
plugins.does: Local security-posture monitor with baselines, evidence-backed findings, read-only agent tools and an authenticated local dashboard.

reads.best: 310 tests across Linux/macOS/Windows CI, scoped consent and fail-closed reporting.
reads.worst: Mostly a conventional file-integrity monitor; no hooks into the agent loop.

plugins.name: sightline
plugins.author: OutstandingVick
plugins.does: Gives Hermes a Solana wallet with preview, simulation, spend grants, hard payment blocks, and a decision log.

reads.best: The payment gate combines owner-issued limits, transaction simulation, one-use approvals, tests, and a Desktop audit view.
reads.worst: Setup persists the private key in Hermes’ .env, and standing grants permit unattended payments.

reads.best: Deterministic pre-sign checks, revocable budgets and approval escalation give agent payments meaningful controls beyond a wallet tool.
reads.worst: Its scope is Solana transfers and its safety model still trusts the configured RPC and the Hermes process holding the signing key.

plugins.name: chalkline
plugins.author: levi-lvjp
plugins.does: Turns dedicated business WhatsApp traffic into a tradesperson’s job ledger, reviewed quotes and invoices, approved sends, and scheduled follow-ups.

reads.best: Its code separates customer intake from agent turns and binds customer sends to owner-approved payloads and durable records.
reads.worst: Setup is substantial and the verified delivery path relies on an unofficial WhatsApp bridge and a dedicated profile.

reads.best: Payload hashes, owner-bound approval routes, attachment digests and claimed delivery rows turn business-message safety into tested code, with a substantial Desktop workflow. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/levi-lvjp/chalkline/e10ba31d612d07e529e757654574d89c63d92cca/chalkline/core/approvals.py
reads.worst: Installation takes over customer intake and setup restricts a dedicated business profile; the unofficial WhatsApp bridge and unverified Cloud/native Desktop operation limit deployment confidence. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/levi-lvjp/chalkline/e10ba31d612d07e529e757654574d89c63d92cca/README.md

plugins.name: secret-guard
plugins.author: ChasClogston
plugins.does: Accepts keys through a macOS keychain dialog and blocks or redacts common paths by which secrets could reach the model.

reads.best: It combines key intake, a secret source, pre-execution gates, inbound blocking, and fail-closed output transforms with extensive tests.
reads.worst: It is macOS-only and depends in part on non-public Hermes redaction internals, with documented bypass limits.

plugins.name: snare
plugins.author: mornslight
plugins.does: Plants per-install decoy credentials in local command environments and blocks their attempted exfiltration while producing an attack-chain report.

reads.best: Its canary-based tripwire, attack provenance ledger, lockdown, integration test, and human-facing incident reports address prompt injection as a runtime problem.
reads.worst: The environment trap is inactive on remote backends and error handling in the pre-tool hook intentionally fails open.

plugins.name: crash-test
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Injects bounded one-turn tool failures and rates how an agent retries, works around them, or reports uncertainty.

reads.best: Its per-session, one-turn harness blocks loud failures before execution and restricts silent corruption to eligible reads, backed by full-hook tests.
reads.worst: The final rating infers honesty from transparent reply-pattern heuristics, so unusual but honest wording can be scored incorrectly.

plugins.name: blindcouncil
plugins.author: sopskistar
plugins.does: Coordinates private two-account Telegram decisions with deterministic unanimity, persistent deadlines, delivery retries and a native Desktop operator page ([pinned source](https://github.com/sopskistar/blindcouncil/tree/2a7ceb4b75bfc24d9fa45349b08764eaeb082e48)).

reads.best: Transactional votes, account-and-message binding, revocation checks and a leased outbox are backed by substantive concurrency, rollback, restart and authorization tests.
reads.worst: The implemented workflow is limited to two-account decision coordination and has neither agent-facing request tools nor an executor that binds approval to a Hermes action ([README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sopskistar/blindcouncil/2a7ceb4b75bfc24d9fa45349b08764eaeb082e48/README.md)).

plugins.name: policy-backtester
plugins.author: noviceadam666
plugins.does: Replays Hermes tool-call history against YAML policies, reports affected jobs, proposes exemptions, and supports shadow logging and live enforcement.

reads.best: Uses the same evaluator for historical replay and a live pre_tool_call guard, making guardrail rollout measurable against the user's actual jobs.
reads.worst: Enforce checks for any recorded shadow promotion and historical job coverage, so it can activate immediately without observing a completed job under shadow.

plugins.name: idm-radio
plugins.author: discodirector
plugins.does: Turns Hermes tool activity into locally synthesized ambient music, Desktop visualizations and downloadable task soundtracks.

reads.best: Session hooks, a complete local audio engine and score-driven Desktop pictures create a distinctive ambient view of the agent at work without sending tool arguments or results.
reads.worst: Session.record retains counters and the start time after a failed turn, so the next successful turn can merge separate tasks into one exported track.

plugins.name: mapdesk
plugins.author: mackydubzz
plugins.does: Adds a persistent GIS workspace where chat tools and a Desktop map share geospatial imports, layers, selections, analysis, and exports ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mackydubzz/hermes-mapdesk/eaaea7102e5d6396840850ee968fe46aea025f41/mapdesk_runtime.py)).

reads.best: Local spatial operations and shared agent/Desktop state make the map a working analysis environment with meaningful geometry and integration tests ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mackydubzz/hermes-mapdesk/eaaea7102e5d6396840850ee968fe46aea025f41/README.md)).
reads.worst: The palette Open command clears the shared workspace through non-atomic writes, so failure or concurrent agent edits can leave a partial reset despite archiving ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mackydubzz/hermes-mapdesk/eaaea7102e5d6396840850ee968fe46aea025f41/README.md)).

plugins.name: shaderbruecke
plugins.author: studioluftbruecke
plugins.does: Gives Hermes a local GLSL render-check-fix loop, live Desktop shader cards and library, plus exports checked against rendered reference frames.

reads.best: A finished creative tool combines editable sliders, versioning, screenshots, export proofs and extensive safety and regression tests beyond what a skill supplies.
reads.worst: It needs host Chromium and uses a POSIX process launcher with --no-sandbox; export proofs sample frames, and TouchDesigner/ISF are checked in shims rather than their actual hosts.

plugins.name: worktree-sandbox
plugins.author: mahammadbakr
plugins.does: Adds a Git-worktree terminal backend, reversible promotion and parallel verification of competing implementations.

reads.best: Changes the actual execution backend and combines conflict-checked promotion, backups, verification hooks and a Desktop race leaderboard.
reads.worst: Commands retain access to absolute host paths, so the worktree and environment filtering do not enforce the README claim that the original checkout cannot be mutated.

reads.best: A real environment provider, diff UI, backups and deterministic candidate scoring improve the agent runtime beyond a skill.
reads.worst: Promotion writes target paths without resolving destination symlinks, and model-supplied race shell commands execute directly without a visible approval gate.

plugins.name: oneiros
plugins.author: noblebrown-69
plugins.does: Reviews session and memory facts into proposals for Hermes memory files, then applies accepted changes with snapshots, receipts, and rollback.

reads.best: Memory changes remain reviewable and gated, with evidence checks, secret scans, locking, atomic writes, snapshots, rollback, and a broad regression suite.
reads.worst: The feature is complex and depends on host hooks and session-log integration; the README says the Dashboard has no pinned screenshot URLs, and older hosts may warn on an unknown hook.

reads.best: Memory changes have locks, stale-evidence checks, secret scanning and receipts, with substantial tests for rollback and user requests not to save information. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noblebrown-69/hermes-oneiros/c9bd78835f6388f04b23a9171c331e6270ef2b73/README.md)
reads.worst: Extraction is a regex pass over labeled facts and user assertions, so it cannot deliver general semantic memory consolidation; naming and docs also retain the separate dream-cycle identity. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noblebrown-69/hermes-oneiros/c9bd78835f6388f04b23a9171c331e6270ef2b73/README.md)

plugins.name: model-kombat
plugins.author: DarkeTech
plugins.does: Runs structured head-to-head Hermes model evaluations, scores answers mechanically, tracks lane-specific Elo, and presents results in Desktop and kanban.

reads.best: It combines adaptive task selection, mechanical scoring, trend memory, capped pure-fight spend, and a polished live Desktop scoreboard, backed by extensive tests.
reads.worst: The optional code scorer runs model-written code as the user's account and explicitly is not a security sandbox; agentic billing is also uncapped.

reads.best: Deterministic checks, honest draws, usage accounting and a substantial visual interface turn model comparisons into usable evidence.
reads.worst: The scoring tool accepts allow_code_execution from tool arguments over the disabled configuration default, while execution remains only a best-effort Python subprocess boundary.

plugins.name: cardlake
plugins.author: cardleforall
plugins.does: Brings a Cardlake daily feed into Hermes chats with Telegram cards, human-operated action buttons, morning delivery, saving, snoozing, and undo.

reads.best: It feels like a finished cross-surface product, combining commands, tools, hooks, Telegram UI, undo behavior, secret redaction, screenshots, and real-Hermes tests.
reads.worst: Its richest experience is limited to private Telegram chats and requires a separate Cardlake account and MCP OAuth connection.

plugins.name: desktop-inbox
plugins.author: Nj07r
plugins.does: An Inbox pane for Hermes Desktop where cron jobs, scripts and webhooks file items as Hermes conversations, triaged by keyboard with snooze and undo, beside chats, kanban cards and cron jobs that need the user.

reads.best: A finished Desktop triage pane with a demo video, settings in the manifest, and a localhost-only webhook that refuses posts until a token or HMAC secret from Hermes's secret store is set.
reads.worst: Only about 300 lines of tests for roughly 2,000 lines of code, and the 991-line Desktop pane has no tests at all.

plugins.name: unified-inbox
plugins.author: krushna-sahu1
plugins.does: Reads, searches, triages and drafts replies across WhatsApp, Instagram and LinkedIn through the user's Unipile account, with digests, memory, scheduling, scam warnings and Desktop/dashboard views, sending only after per-message human approval.

reads.best: Sends go through a pre_tool_call approval hook that refuses to send when Hermes is in yolo mode, with hard-capped pacing limits, the API key as a secret config field, and around 340 tests.
reads.worst: Very large surface (22 tools, cloud sync, webhooks) that rests on a paid third-party bridge to WhatsApp, Instagram and LinkedIn, which carries account-restriction risk the plugin can only soften.

plugins.name: contagion
plugins.author: onchaindc
plugins.does: Marks a session tainted once it reads untrusted content and then runs its terminal, code and file tools in an OS jail (bubblewrap or sandbox-exec) with no network, hidden home and secrets, and approval-gated egress tools.

reads.best: A real terminal-environment provider that puts a prompt-injection wall at the OS layer rather than in prompts, with unit tests, an end-to-end jail check and an honest limits section.
reads.worst: Needs bubblewrap with unprivileged namespaces or deprecated macOS sandbox-exec, has no Windows support, detects taint only by tool-name patterns, and the README install line still says <owner>/contagion.

plugins.name: dropstation
plugins.author: satiricalguru
plugins.does: Gateway platform that turns private local folders into Hermes inboxes: each dropped file runs a fresh session under a lane's standing task and writes a Markdown report and SHA-256 receipt to an outbox.

reads.best: Carefully built spool: O_NOFOLLOW reads, symlink/FIFO refusal, a worker lease, dedup by content hash and crash recovery, all covered by eight tests.
reads.worst: Polling-based folder watcher with a one-job-at-a-time worker and only spool-level tests, nothing that exercises the adapter itself; the audience is people who already script file drops.

plugins.name: dial-a-hermes
plugins.author: ebohdarlington123-cmyk
plugins.does: Gateway platform that lets you use Hermes from any feature phone over USSD (Africa's Talking-compatible), with paged 182-char screens, keypad 1/2 exec approvals showing the full command, optional SMS replies, Pidgin menus and a local phone simulator.

reads.best: Puts the whole agent, including Hermes's own approval cards (once/deny only), behind a USSD short code with a phone-number allowlist, constant-time callback-token check and keys read through Hermes's scoped secret store.
reads.worst: Real use needs an Africa's Talking account, a public tunnel and a short code, and the 31 core tests plus e2e script sit outside the pinned plugin folder; the audience outside feature-phone regions is small.

plugins.name: zeromem
plugins.author: ptaranat
plugins.does: A Hermes memory provider backed by a Rust core that stores every message verbatim in one SQLite file and recalls it with local embeddings and lexical search, no LLM calls.

reads.best: Changes Hermes's memory through register_memory_provider with prefetch, background writes, recall/forget tools and a zero-token import of past sessions, all on the user's machine.
reads.worst: The Hermes wrapper has only a smoke script and no tests (the Rust core has eight pipeline tests), and it relies on a PyPI wheel plus a 130 MB model download at first run.

plugins.name: defuzz
plugins.author: defuzzr
plugins.does: Audits Hermes homes and organizes projects with templates, AGENTS.md rules, placement hooks, linting, and Desktop/dashboard surfaces.

reads.best: It materially improves project hygiene and agent write placement across CLI, hooks, Desktop, and dashboard, with clear disclosure of its broad scope.
reads.worst: Its breadth and optional code/lint execution create a large trust and compatibility surface, and it is Linux/Python-3.13-only.

reads.best: Changes real agent file placement through trust-aware hooks and includes extensive tests for write boundaries, redaction, audit uncertainty and creation workflows.
reads.worst: Linux/Python 3.13 requirements and a large lint toolchain narrow adoption; audits can read other profiles and checks execute project code without a sandbox.

plugins.name: perf-lab
plugins.author: Murali-lns
plugins.does: Benchmarks and profiles agent-edited programs, compares output fingerprints, and hooks Hermes to block unmeasured optimization claims.

reads.best: It makes performance claims an evidence-producing Hermes workflow with output equivalence, noise handling, hooks, and a polished Desktop view.
reads.worst: The hooks fail open and scripts still execute with the user’s permissions, so it is measurement discipline rather than a security sandbox.

reads.best: Connects reproducible before/after measurements and output checks to edit gates and a useful flame-graph Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Interpreter-only filtering still runs arbitrary scripts with user permissions without a native execution approval gate, and the measurement hooks fail open.

plugins.name: attest
plugins.author: pgreyy
plugins.does: Gives Hermes a paper-trading account whose locally stored ledger prices simulated orders from public quotes, enforces risk checks, and can flag contradictory financial figures in replies.

reads.best: It combines an authoritative Decimal/SQLite ledger, fresh-quote and loss/order limits, duplicate protection, optional fail-closed interception of one named order tool, and extensive isolated self-checks.
reads.worst: It is deliberately paper-only and its live marks depend on external public exchange endpoints; the output claim checker is heuristic and only adds a note.

reads.best: Balances come from transactional code with substantive arithmetic and failure-case checks, while the paper guard prevents its configured real order tool from executing. [Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgreyy/attest/0de5e1e49da1bb9bcd54ef28d224c2cc095e7ad6/intercept.py).
reads.worst: The simulator lacks depth and resting orders, its English claim checker is heuristic, and Guard.__call__ returns None if reading its target settings raises, weakening the claimed fail-closed boundary. [Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgreyy/attest/0de5e1e49da1bb9bcd54ef28d224c2cc095e7ad6/intercept.py). [Limits and setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgreyy/attest/0de5e1e49da1bb9bcd54ef28d224c2cc095e7ad6/README.md).

plugins.name: slopcannon
plugins.author: vincitamore
plugins.does: Drives a paid external video-generation SaaS from inside Hermes: uploads, scene/character generation and multi-stage rendering, with every credit spend gated by an exact-match human approval.

reads.best: Credits are only ever spent after approval that must match the exact quoted figure, the plugin never requests the OAuth scope needed to buy credits itself, and unattended spend defaults to zero.
reads.worst: Setup is relatively involved, requiring Node.js and an OAuth sign-in flow, and it depends entirely on a third-party paid SaaS staying available.

reads.best: The implementation binds rights and spending decisions to concrete productions and delivers a well-developed studio with scoped credentials and extensive gate tests. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vincitamore/hermes-slopcannon/b03e62386f85a13df42c34a63f87cf46618387b4/gate.py)
reads.worst: If Hermes approval-bypass detection is unavailable or raises, the gate treats calls as attended, allowing YOLO spending past the default unattended limit; the per-action ceiling is unlimited by default. [Gate code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vincitamore/hermes-slopcannon/b03e62386f85a13df42c34a63f87cf46618387b4/gate.py)

plugins.name: shiftrepair
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Repairs weekly staff schedules with minimum-change constraint optimization, independent validation, persistent revisions and a native Desktop board.

reads.best: A bounded solver, separate checker, exhaustive small-case oracle tests and revision/candidate checks support a reviewable proposal-to-Apply workflow.
reads.worst: The scheduling model is limited to one location and seven days, with no shift durations, fairness, payroll or rest rules, and OR-Tools adds installation/startup cost.

reads.best: Solver plus exact-oracle checker, 10 tools and a native Desktop board.
reads.worst: Niche audience, and the README says it is not yet a submitted entry.

plugins.name: hermes-screen
plugins.author: johaankjis
plugins.does: Controls Jellyfin and YouTube playback on Chromecast, saves and retrieves edition-specific scenes, and runs a phone-camera rock-paper-scissors game on the TV.

reads.best: Receiver-confirmed actions, scoped secrets, expiring single-item relay links and extensive failure-path tests turn the user's own TV and phone into agent surfaces.
reads.worst: Jellyfin playback requires a narrow direct-play codec profile without transcoding, while camera games need a separate HTTPS service and optional Custom Receiver registration.

reads.best: Real device control (Chromecast token-gated LAN capability URLs, Jellyfin watch-state logic) that only a plugin, not a prompt, could do, with 23 test files covering cast/scene/youtube paths.
reads.worst: Its own README labels it 'work in progress for the November 2026 hackathon', so parts of the scope are unfinished at the pinned commit.

plugins.name: epoch
plugins.author: simongonzalezdc
plugins.does: Uses Kanban claim and completion hooks to make calibrated time estimates, post them to the board, and record actual duration to a local Epoch ledger.

reads.best: It is a deeply engineered feedback loop with shared run bindings, replayable outbox work, scrubbed child environment, concurrency handling, tests, and clear visuals.
reads.worst: First use depends on downloading a pinned npm CLI through npx, so offline or restrictive npm policy delays estimation until a retry succeeds.

reads.best: Durable run bindings, retry outboxes and concurrency tests handle cross-profile and out-of-order completion instead of trusting comment markers.
reads.worst: The default execution path downloads a pinned npm CLI on first use and requires Node 22, adding a setup dependency before estimates can work.

plugins.name: reachmap
plugins.author: MindSproutStudios
plugins.does: Maps local browser sessions, services, CLIs, MCP configurations and drives, then flags replies that contradict that map.

reads.best: Cache-safe prompt sections, reply hooks and a persistent capability ledger directly improve the agent’s awareness of its own tools.
reads.worst: Browser access is inferred from tab URLs and local services from listener metadata, so apparent reachability does not prove authorization or a working operation.

plugins.name: rigforge
plugins.author: DECRUX9812
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop robotics design studio with deterministic geometry, sizing, bills of materials, firmware templates and printable exports.

reads.best: A substantial offline engine connects interactive 3D design, explicit engineering calculations, manufacturing exports and agent-to-studio handoff.
reads.worst: Generated gripper firmware declares US_OPEN=1200 and US_CLOSED=1800 as uint8_t, which overflows and makes the emitted servo pulse values wrong.

plugins.name: cutroom
plugins.author: KaanDRoid
plugins.does: Adds a local video editing studio with transcript and silence cuts, vision review, captions, background rendering and reviewed final exports.

reads.best: Revision-bound jobs, input hashes and stale-approval invalidation integrate a real local media pipeline with Desktop controls and agent tools.
reads.worst: Advanced editing requires optional native packages and separately acquired models, while the pinned status report leaves fresh-install and native Desktop-window acceptance open.

plugins.name: godseye
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a live globe for public geospatial queries, map control, annotations, saved investigations and area-watch alerts [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/EOH/9d433e49645df8ee549b58467876eb1e5daa0f34/gev/hermes_tools.py).

reads.best: Live map control, model-generated HUD captions and watch delivery are integrated into Hermes tools and its turn-state hook, making the globe part of the agent workflow [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/EOH/9d433e49645df8ee549b58467876eb1e5daa0f34/gev/hermes_tools.py).
reads.worst: Full functionality requires separately cloning, building and running a compatible globe fork, and its tool snapshots need refreshing when that external catalog changes [setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/EOH/9d433e49645df8ee549b58467876eb1e5daa0f34/README.md).

plugins.name: total-recall
plugins.author: dax8it
plugins.does: Provides durable local agent memory through a hash-chained ledger, signed checkpoints, cited retrieval, and lifecycle rehydration.

reads.best: A genuine memory-provider integration handles turn synchronization and compaction, backed by integrity checks, retrieval fallbacks, and extensive source tests.
reads.worst: Its prefetch buffer stores only context text without a query or session key, so a later request can consume context computed for an earlier request.

plugins.name: continuum
plugins.author: aidonerightcorp
plugins.does: Learns from local task outcomes to route Hermes turns to cheaper models, with consent-gated request shaping, recall and policy auditing. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aidonerightcorp/continuum/765aad799e520ce7f9cb60329b0d60675fa82c4b/README.md)

reads.best: Real request middleware, conservative evidence thresholds, per-sender recall isolation and extensive failure/privacy tests improve Hermes itself through public extension points.
reads.worst: The supplied live benchmark shows no clear savings, and effective routing needs repeated user marks plus a suitable cheaper model on the same provider.

plugins.name: reflexes
plugins.author: zahmed333
plugins.does: Starts Hermes turns in an existing chat when watched folders, connected drives or appended log lines trigger a saved rule.

reads.best: Local event sources, approval for arming rules, queued delivery and Desktop controls make Hermes useful between user messages.
reads.worst: Injection and delivery acknowledgement are separate operations, so a crash between them can replay an event despite the README's never-fires-twice claim.

plugins.name: unbl0ck
plugins.author: simongonzalezdc
plugins.does: Collects live prompts, pairing requests, blocked Kanban cards and unanswered chats into a Desktop queue with human-triggered responses.

reads.best: A single actionable queue addresses the practical bottleneck of supervising multiple Hermes runs while keeping decisions with the person.
reads.worst: Queue detection uses language heuristics and private Kanban/database interfaces, while automatic summaries send cross-profile item text to the configured model by default.

plugins.name: hermes-phone
plugins.author: winchxyz
plugins.does: Places user-approved outbound AI phone calls and relays mid-call questions, results and transcripts back to Hermes chat.

reads.best: One-use call approvals, signature-checked webhooks and a live question relay make the phone bridge a meaningful new agent capability.
reads.worst: Real provider behavior is mocked in the suite, setup requires a public bridge sharing SQLite with Hermes, and free-text privacy filtering covers fewer patterns than the blanket consent claims suggest.

plugins.name: boardloop
plugins.author: LSUDOKO
plugins.does: Gives Hermes an ESP32/Arduino workbench that compiles firmware, tests it in Wokwi, reports bounded repair steps and flashes approved real boards.

reads.best: Implemented compile/test feedback, approval-gated hardware writes, secret-isolated subprocesses, extensive targeted tests and a Desktop workbench form a polished hardware workflow ([implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LSUDOKO/BoardLoop/950586cd231d8f3d0905fdc53eecf8bba1319c3e/tools.py)).
reads.worst: Users must install two external toolchains and obtain Wokwi cloud access, and real-board checks cannot reproduce simulated inputs or verify GPIO expectations automatically ([setup and limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LSUDOKO/BoardLoop/950586cd231d8f3d0905fdc53eecf8bba1319c3e/README.md)).

plugins.name: forgebruecke
plugins.author: studioluftbruecke
plugins.does: Integrates self-hosted Forgejo through repository tools, a review desk, mention-driven conversations and gated automation flows. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/studioluftbruecke/hermes-forgebruecke/f01d5dae2b643ef2a2efffbdccaea7d9417632cf/README.md)

reads.best: One-use approval tickets, dry-run defaults and commit-pinned promotion checks provide unusually careful control over agent repository writes. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/studioluftbruecke/hermes-forgebruecke/f01d5dae2b643ef2a2efffbdccaea7d9417632cf/README.md)
reads.worst: Write availability depends on the private gateway.session_finite API and fails closed when that internal interface cannot be read. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/studioluftbruecke/hermes-forgebruecke/f01d5dae2b643ef2a2efffbdccaea7d9417632cf/approval.py)

plugins.name: spanwall
plugins.author: tuanpv47
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop Kanban wall across Hermes profiles with live session states, request approvals, inline replies, steering, and task creation.

reads.best: Makes several running agents manageable from one SDK-based Desktop surface while keeping approval decisions as explicit user actions routed to the owning gateway.
reads.worst: No automated tests are included for its large Desktop implementation, and polling every watched profile every three seconds can start additional backends.

plugins.name: blastradius
plugins.author: valenciayuna
plugins.does: Measures destructive terminal commands, adds policy-based blocking, and supplies checksummed filesystem snapshots and conflict-aware restore tools.

reads.best: Concrete impact reports and verified recovery directly improve the safety of an agent working on the user’s files, with parser and snapshot audit suites.
reads.worst: Protection covers terminal calls only, and strict-mode blast_allow measures in the process cwd while its grant is matched by command text alone, so a different workdir can consume a grant for the wrong snapshot.

plugins.name: whiteboard
plugins.author: Adolanium
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop planning whiteboard with agent-generated layouts, reviewable suggestions, parallel task sessions, route execution and chat-to-board tools. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Adolanium/hermes-whiteboard/9151ee902ae7008d1ab47f9398ea7667c569bf2f/desktop/plugin.js)

reads.best: The implemented route planner, editable board, reversible suggestions, result cards and export workflows make agent work tangible in a polished Desktop surface. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Adolanium/hermes-whiteboard/9151ee902ae7008d1ab47f9398ea7667c569bf2f/desktop/plugin.js)
reads.worst: Hidden sessions retain the user’s tools: prohibitions on file writes, commands and messaging are prompt instructions, while watched tool use is only flagged after it starts.
