[Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Adolanium/hermes-whiteboard/9151ee902ae7008d1ab47f9398ea7667c569bf2f/desktop/plugin.js)

plugins.name: mtg-deck-studio
plugins.author: GillesGaelBERNARD
plugins.does: Adds a shared Commander deck table to Hermes Desktop with conversational editing, Scryfall search, synergy links, statistics and strategy notes.

reads.best: Its human-and-agent editing loop has revision acknowledgments, conflict rejection, undo and browser tests around a complete visual deck workspace.
reads.worst: Editing requires a live Desktop pane to acknowledge commands, and the README reports manual UI testing on Windows 11 only.

plugins.name: siteform
plugins.author: duclucky
plugins.does: Turns reviewed planning PDFs into source-linked concept geometry with 3D chat cards, saved design alternatives, bounded studies and exports.

reads.best: The same measured, revision-linked geometry drives native tools, interactive chat previews and a full Desktop workspace, with meaningful storage and geometry tests.
reads.worst: It remains a specialist, operator-reviewed concept workflow: scale, outlines and heights must be supplied or confirmed, and advertised platform verification is Windows-focused.

plugins.name: ghostwriter
plugins.author: nevpit
plugins.does: Adds a screenplay workspace with scene-aware agent tools, reviewable revisions, undo, and PDF, Fountain and Final Draft import/export.

reads.best: A substantial document engine and Desktop editor combine immutable revisions, compare-and-swap writes, proposal validation and format-specific tests.
reads.worst: The audience is specialized and PDF import is best effort, with scanned and some CID-font documents unsupported.

plugins.name: local-fleet
plugins.author: humedini
plugins.does: Routes Hermes primary inference, auxiliary tasks, and subagents across registered local servers with cloud fallback, private mode, and a Desktop fleet console. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/humedini/local-fleet/94cd17d2477f9d1a6f39aeee153be1d25c5b57e2/README.md)

reads.best: It meaningfully changes where Hermes runs inference, with shared eligibility rules, reversible configuration, drift reporting, privacy controls, and substantial behavioral tests. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/humedini/local-fleet/94cd17d2477f9d1a6f39aeee153be1d25c5b57e2/health.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/humedini/local-fleet/94cd17d2477f9d1a6f39aeee153be1d25c5b57e2/README.md)
reads.worst: Health probes submit workers to ThreadPoolExecutor without copying context, yet resolve scoped secrets inside those workers, risking failed or incorrectly scoped authentication in multiplexed profiles. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/humedini/local-fleet/94cd17d2477f9d1a6f39aeee153be1d25c5b57e2/health.py)

plugins.name: the-millionaire-matrix
plugins.author: bufirstrepo
plugins.does: Runs competing model-generated code candidates through test and measured gates, blind peer scoring, a tournament, and a human approval gate, then records lessons for later sessions.

reads.best: The eight-family competition, hard evidence gates, explicit human merge approval, route holds for degraded judging, and broad test suite make an unusually ambitious agent coding workflow.
reads.worst: It executes operator-authored commands and generated candidates in the target worktree, while extensive adapters and runtime assumptions increase operational and maintenance risk.

plugins.name: tldr
plugins.author: ShawnCRMer
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop control that summarizes a selected span of the current chat into status, evidence labels, risks, and decisions users can review and insert.

reads.best: It reads actual session history and returns structured, revisable Desktop cards without consuming a chat turn, with user-controlled scope and opt-in capped automation.
reads.worst: Two private-core imports and the complex session-history projection create compatibility risk, and the PR reports no project-specific automated test count.

plugins.name: kin
plugins.author: vdimarco
plugins.does: Gives Hermes Desktop an animated avatar, lifecycle moods, task drawer, optional floating overlay, voice drafts, OCR actions, and local memory controls.

reads.best: It is a deeply integrated and unusually polished Desktop companion that makes Hermes activity legible and personable.
reads.worst: The optional overlay expands the attack and portability surface with OS capture, process/window integration, and external Electron dependencies.

plugins.name: hermes-reflex
plugins.author: arjunbagga-xyz
plugins.does: Compiles procedural skills into tested executable runners, rescues archived skills, transforms outputs into GenUI cards, and persists pinned widgets.

reads.best: The combination of skill compilation, archive recovery, output transformation, and native sticky-note UI is highly ambitious and Hermes-specific.
reads.worst: Generated code execution, subprocesses, multiple dependencies, and a narrow synthetic safety gate create a substantial reliability and security burden.

plugins.name: nachalo
plugins.author: RamsisDev
plugins.does: Pairs two Hermes agents (and their people) from six spoken words plus four safety words, then carries end-to-end encrypted messages over an ntfy relay, where the agent only drafts and a person sends.

reads.best: A new channel between agents with strong safety design: the inbox is untrusted (the model sees only counts), sending needs a human, there are about 33 MITM/revocation/leak tests, and it adds a Desktop page, a CLI and secrets through get_secret.
reads.worst: It needs Python 3.14 exactly and an external `nachalo` Rust wheel holding all the cryptography, so the post-quantum claims cannot be checked from this repo; the Desktop send route has no server-side confirmation.

reads.best: Novel pairing (PAKE plus safety words) where a person must send every message.
reads.worst: Unaudited draft crypto, a niche need and the public ntfy.sh relay by default.

plugins.name: hermes-voice-lab
plugins.author: Adolanium
plugins.does: Adds a local articulatory voice instrument with Desktop controls, speech and singing tools, WAV rendering and musical call-and-response with Hermes.

reads.best: A source-backed physical voice engine, interactive instrument and conversation-linked jam mode create a distinctive new Hermes Desktop capability.
reads.worst: Speech is English-only and less natural than neural TTS, gateway renders require Node, and bundled WASM provenance was not independently verified in this read.

reads.best: Genuinely novel idea (a playable articulatory voice instrument driven by the agent, no cloud TTS, no network calls) with real demo videos.
reads.worst: Niche appeal for day-one installs since it's a toy/performance instrument rather than a task the average Hermes user needs; only 6 test files for a complex DSP/UI engine.

plugins.name: hypruse
plugins.author: IlyasKhallouki
plugins.does: Computer-use provider that replaces Hermes's driver on Hyprland with the hypruse CLI using accessibility trees and agent-owned workspaces.

reads.best: Fixes a real Hermes gap (cua-driver failing on Wayland/Hyprland) by swapping the computer_use backend, backed by an extensively tested CLI.
reads.worst: Niche audience (Hyprland users only) and requires a separate hypruse install.

plugins.name: airlock-sandbox
plugins.author: justrunme
plugins.does: Terminal backend routing Hermes commands through an external Airlock policy engine and Docker sandbox with Ed25519-signed receipts.

reads.best: Fail-closed design with 41 tests, signed verifiable receipts and a demo video, via the terminal provider seam.
reads.worst: Depends on running the author's own Airlock service; few users will.

plugins.name: second-key
plugins.author: kamalbuilds
plugins.does: Two-person rule for dangerous commands: approvals go by Telegram to a roster, requester cannot self-approve, hash-chained ledger.

reads.best: Fail-closed approval transport that also detects tampering with approval settings and blocks /yolo.
reads.worst: Telegram-only, no screenshots or UI, and self-protection relies on command pattern matching.

plugins.name: hotwire
plugins.author: RohanGlitched
plugins.does: Lets Hermes design analog circuits from English, verifying netlists with its own ngspice-checked simulator and exporting BOM, stripboard and KiCad.

reads.best: A real simulator validated against ngspice with ~137 tests, plus a Desktop pane and many screenshots.
reads.worst: Its pre_llm_call hook injects a self-promoting hint on loose keyword matches, and the use case is niche.

plugins.name: hermes-issue-sync
plugins.author: elijahboston
plugins.does: Two-way sync of Hermes kanban cards with Linear and Jira issues, posting done summaries and routing blocked-question replies, with Desktop panel.

reads.best: Idempotent card links, secrets via profile secret scope, broad tests, screenshots.
reads.worst: Needs Linear/Jira setup, so it fits teams already on those trackers.

plugins.name: reliquary
plugins.author: Lokee86
plugins.does: Local memory provider with source provenance and a 3D relationship graph, backed by a Rust native host launched as a background process.

reads.best: Real exclusive memory provider with dashboard graph, local-only host and disclosure of data and processes.
reads.worst: Windows-only, needs a separate Rust build, ships a 1.1MB generated desktop bundle and host patches, so hard to set up and review.

plugins.name: ratcatcher
plugins.author: Truthgeng
plugins.does: Telegram group scam bouncer: detects drainer/airdrop/impersonator scams, deletes, mutes, bans, and reports to admins with Release/Ban buttons.

reads.best: Focused detector with a test corpus (43 tests), a watch mode for trial runs, and screenshots and a banner.
reads.worst: Automatic bans on heuristics can hit real members; the scope is crypto Telegram groups.

plugins.name: vape-coach
plugins.author: NeelM0906
plugins.does: Local webcam watcher detects vaping puffs, sets a taper schedule, and escalates playful nudges including camera-counted jumping jacks, with a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Polished, privacy-disclosed local CV with 66 tests, a demo video and a Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Niche health use, and the webcam and model downloads add setup weight.

plugins.name: ctx_handover
plugins.author: GottZ
plugins.does: Moves a live Hermes chat session and its project workspace (including uncommitted git state) between machines a user owns, via direct pull/push or an offline bundle file, with session locking so it isn't continued twice.

reads.best: Implements a real signed Ed25519 peer-pairing protocol with an explicit, documented environment allowlist for subprocess git calls so provider keys never reach the subprocess, backed by hundreds of unit/integration/e2e test files.
reads.worst: No Desktop UI of its own; everything is driven through a CLI slash command, so the polish is entirely in documentation rather than a visual surface.

plugins.name: receipt-printer
plugins.author: thedavidmurray
plugins.does: Observes Hermes tool calls and state history to render conservative text, PNG, Desktop, and optional thermal-printer receipts for agent claims.

reads.best: It gives Hermes an unusually original evidence and audit surface, backed by local-only data handling, substantial code, visual assets, and a broad test suite.
reads.worst: Its more ambitious v2 task and fleet judgments are explicitly experimental or unverified, while legacy hooks intentionally fail open on errors.

reads.best: Evidence scoping and mandatory verdict rendering distinguish supported outcomes from missing evidence, with local PNG, Desktop and optional USB output.
reads.worst: The pinned README labels v2 experimental with independent accuracy acceptance pending; the Desktop pane supplies only an unverified preview without a task manifest.

plugins.name: signaldesk
plugins.author: codeybot-labs
plugins.does: Scans public hiring/launch feeds and local-business listings, scores leads against a user ICP, drafts outreach, and only ever writes a local .eml file, never sending automatically.

reads.best: A pre_tool_call hook blocks any send-like tool call unless the matching lead is already approved, and unconditionally blocks sends during any cron/unattended execution — a host-enforced guardrail no prompt or skill could replicate.
reads.worst: The core idea (lead-gen scanning and scoring) is a familiar SaaS pattern; the novelty is mostly in the enforcement plumbing rather than the lead-gen concept itself.

plugins.name: swarm-studio
plugins.author: Pukujan
plugins.does: Uses a planner and parallel model agents to build multi-page websites, apps, games, promotional media, and deployable prototypes on an interactive Desktop canvas.

reads.best: It ships an unusually complete creative product with live multi-agent canvas, Desktop integration, publishing and game/app workflows, extensive docs, and a large test suite.
reads.worst: Its enormous vendored codebase, CAUTION install scan, external model and publishing services, and multi-gigabyte first app build create meaningful reliability and setup friction.

plugins.name: learning-workbench
plugins.author: alfredbirkelund
plugins.does: Runs tutoring sessions with frozen answer keys, quote-verified exercise assessment, and a Hermes Desktop study pane, storing attempts in an append-only SQLite schema.

reads.best: The deepest test suite in the batch: 7 test files, a dedicated mutation-check script claiming to break 22 invariants, and a live end-to-end harness, plus honest scope docs on what wasn't tested.
reads.worst: The README itself admits macOS and Windows paths were not tested, leaving real-world cross-platform reliability unverified.

plugins.name: hermes-openui
plugins.author: Revenue-Architect
plugins.does: Renders interactive OpenUI views and live MCP-backed dashboards in Hermes Desktop/Webapp chat through one tool, hooks and a desktop renderer.

reads.best: Changes what chat can show: clickable views and dashboards reading allowlisted MCP tools without passing data through the model, with Python and TS tests and validation.
reads.worst: A 5.7MB bundled desktop/plugin.js is hard for reviewers to read, and dashboards stay off until configured.

plugins.name: zerofactory
plugins.author: ntsd
plugins.does: Autonomous multi-agent software factory: Kanban dispatcher, git worktrees, spec audit, PR review loops and a dashboard, via four provisioned Hermes profiles.

reads.best: Large working system with dispatcher, SQLite kanban, dashboard and a big unit/e2e test suite.
reads.worst: Self-declared active beta with much code pre-dating the hackathon, and huge surface (shell, gh, PRs) that is hard to review and has no manifest env declaration.

plugins.name: tusk
plugins.author: Automationbot24x7
plugins.does: Memory provider that stores Hermes long-term memory encrypted on Walrus mainnet with proof links, plus dashboard.

reads.best: A real memory provider using Hermes's secret store, an outbox, and ~160 tests.
reads.worst: Depends on a crypto storage network and relayer; the ciphertext verify claim is only a heuristic.

plugins.name: photo-to-part
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Turns photos, measurements or a 3D scan into a validated, printable parametric part with six tools, hooks and a Desktop Part studio pane.

reads.best: Deep, finished pipeline with validation, renders, approval-gated builds, Desktop pane and 26 test files.
reads.worst: Runs user build scripts (approval can be switched off) and hook failures are silently swallowed.

plugins.name: exfilbar
plugins.author: quotumorg
plugins.does: Blocks recognized off-route file transfers before terminal or code tools run and shows route decisions in Desktop.

reads.best: User-defined file-to-host routes are enforced in a pre-tool hook with fail-closed errors and extensive tests.
reads.worst: Its static recognizer covers a bounded syntax subset and cannot enforce all network egress.

plugins.name: visual-workflow
plugins.author: Printaga
plugins.does: Adds Desktop and dashboard workflow canvases backed by a persistent sequential agent runner with conditions, approvals, retries, and scheduling.

reads.best: The [runner integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Printaga/Hermes-Workflow/3f7a6a185e489ff4d75a0e8c1a9050c300f602d5/visual_workflow_hermes/runtime.py) preserves run state and prevents the model from answering human gates or adding unapproved delivery targets while resuming.
reads.worst: The [documented limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Printaga/Hermes-Workflow/3f7a6a185e489ff4d75a0e8c1a9050c300f602d5/README.md) exclude parallel branches and loops, and selecting another bot does not bring that bot's tools, skills, or memory.

plugins.name: templeos
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Lets Hermes and its user operate a local TempleOS-family QEMU guest through shared video, keyboard, HolyC, and file-transfer tools.

reads.best: Its [input arbiter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/hermes-templeos/c61d00eb4d36c5e3c7cd57a2985985aed8db42f0/templeos/arbiter.py) serializes human and agent actions and gives the user explicit take-control and hand-back controls over the live guest.
reads.worst: The [documented workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/hermes-templeos/c61d00eb4d36c5e3c7cd57a2985985aed8db42f0/README.md) serves a narrow OS audience, requires separately installed QEMU, and still labels FAT file transfer experimental and macOS untested as a primary host.

plugins.name: autonoma
plugins.author: JoeisEvil
plugins.does: Adds action-class trust scoring, extra approval prompts, an activity dashboard and deterministic handoff notes for unfinished sessions.

reads.best: Combines real approval hooks, correction-driven grant revocation and tool-log handoffs with a documented dashboard and extensive focused tests.
reads.worst: The extra pre-tool gate catches internal exceptions and returns no directive, so its added protection can fail open; earned trust also rests on heuristic action classification.

plugins.name: whiplash
plugins.author: hejijunhao
plugins.does: Lets Hermes perform and shape live Digitakt II music through a clocked MIDI sequencer, optional audio analysis, and a local visualizer.

reads.best: Musical timing, bar-quantized changes, user-knob yielding, panic cleanup and MIDI message restrictions are implemented and covered by extensive fake-port tests.
reads.worst: Its main audience owns a specific synthesizer, and it cannot inspect or load the actual sample pool, so track roles need user labels and hardware sound is not established by fake-port tests.

plugins.name: retake
plugins.author: wevial
plugins.does: Provides a Desktop workspace for image generation, annotated revision briefs, immutable takes and side-by-side review.

reads.best: Durable single-use generation reservations, profile checks, bounded media handling and extensive boundary tests make paid image iteration unusually careful.
reads.worst: Generation requires extra Hermes tool-server setup and disabling tool search for the profile; the exact URL adapter and final UI lack a claimed full live end-to-end pass.

plugins.name: threejs-stage
plugins.author: tuancookiez-hub
plugins.does: Shows generated 3D scenes and local models in interactive chat cards, with hidden runtime checks and repair feedback.

reads.best: Integrates sandboxed live rendering, model import, GPU dry-run feedback and repair controls directly into Hermes chat.
reads.worst: No automated behavioral test suite is shipped for its sizable tool/backend; exported HTML runs model-written code without the Desktop sandbox CSP and loads a CDN at runtime.

plugins.name: skill-workshop
plugins.author: flabanabba8
plugins.does: Mines repeated Hermes session workflows into reviewed skills and adds skill-building, skill-loading checks and tool-call provenance guards.

reads.best: Session-history mining, content-hash skill decisions and runtime tool vetoes directly improve how a personal Hermes agent learns and uses skills.
reads.worst: Mining checks tool sequences rather than task success, while literal pattern and tool-name matching leave injection blind spots.

plugins.name: hermes-crm
plugins.author: gptnius
plugins.does: Provides a profile-scoped CRM with linked records, pipeline reports, reviewed research notes and bounded scheduled work shared by agent tools and a native Desktop pane.

reads.best: Version checks, idempotent writes, shared agent/UI storage and extensive workflow tests turn CRM records into a substantial native Hermes workspace.
reads.worst: It is explicitly a small-workspace prototype with bounded legacy lists, incomplete platform/accessibility coverage and no email or external CRM connectors.

plugins.name: assumption-ledger
plugins.author: itzebe
plugins.does: Persists operational assumptions and deterministic evidence, reinjects them into Hermes context, and holds verification when recorded decisions depend on contradictions.

reads.best: A durable evidence lifecycle distinguishes contradictions from outages and integrates capture, reinjection, session-scoped verification and explicit recovery.
reads.worst: Automatic capture covers a limited set of regex patterns, while useful blocking depends on the agent explicitly recording decision dependencies; live Hermes turn behavior is not tested end to end.

plugins.name: motion-studio
plugins.author: gregoryhorn
plugins.does: Adds Desktop workflows to collect, compare and retain generated media takes and assemble selected assets into exportable projects.

reads.best: Substantial scoped storage, output validation, minimal child environments and recovery tests back its native Desktop media workflow.
reads.worst: The current product cannot delete saved takes or projects, music generation is unavailable, and local sound effects require separately configured engines.

plugins.name: sluice
plugins.author: orjinameh
plugins.does: Runs terminal commands and file tools in a staged workspace copy and lets users review and selectively apply diff hunks.

reads.best: A real terminal backend stages both commands and file edits, with reviewed-diff freshness checks and conflict-aware atomic application.
reads.worst: It is path rewriting rather than OS isolation, so runtime-built paths can escape and its approval hook returns no restriction on internal errors.

plugins.name: hermes-action-bar
plugins.author: fquresh
plugins.does: Adds Desktop selection actions for annotated quote replies and private model-answer cards with follow-up questions.

reads.best: Native composer middleware and stateless answer cards improve reading and replying, with tests for per-chat scope, inert references, rendering safety and cleanup.
reads.worst: The answer card has no tools or web access, so its Fact-check action cannot verify sources, and busy-agent reply handling requires its separate Send button.

plugins.name: kestra-oncall
plugins.author: zkasuran
plugins.does: Diagnoses failed Kestra workflows, stores proposed fixes and applies approved repairs with replay verification and guarded rollback.

reads.best: Hash-bound approvals, fail-closed namespace policy and a durable replay journal turn workflow repair into a controlled Hermes capability.
reads.worst: Setup is involved and depends on a private approval-bypass API; Kestra lacks atomic flow updates, leaving a documented concurrent-edit window.

plugins.name: leitmotif
plugins.author: JustSteez
plugins.does: Sonifies tool calls, repeated calls, errors, approvals and turn endings with synthesized motifs and WAV/MIDI/SVG exports ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JustSteez/hermes-leitmotif/0d43079e3880a79750d87d07ce759769bd182acd/README.md)).

reads.best: Distinctive, local agent observability and accessibility, backed by deterministic composition tests and an included audio/visual demo.
reads.worst: A single registered Conductor owns the session timeline, composer and heartbeat, so concurrent sessions can overwrite or mix their state ([session state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JustSteez/hermes-leitmotif/0d43079e3880a79750d87d07ce759769bd182acd/conductor.py)).

plugins.name: coursebook
plugins.author: DeseretSaint
plugins.does: Turns Hermes Desktop into a resumable learning workspace with lesson generation, governed checks, evidence records and parent-led course packs.

reads.best: Transactional lesson transitions, nonce/revision fences and backend-only answer keys make learning progress enforceable beyond a tutoring prompt.
reads.worst: The README records incomplete live Desktop verification and partially exercised media/pronunciation surfaces, despite a large backend and UI test suite.

plugins.name: solverforge-routing
plugins.author: blackopsrepl
plugins.does: Plans and repairs multi-stop driving itineraries using a local Rust road-routing solver, a Desktop map and navigation handoff links.

reads.best: Revision-checked trip edits and independently revalidated route constraints are backed by Python, Rust and Desktop tests, with a polished map and QR handoff.
reads.worst: A new area still needs external geocoding/road-data services and a separate engine installation, and the result estimates driving without live traffic.

plugins.name: sluice-search
plugins.author: abhigyan-chatterjee
plugins.does: Replaces Hermes native web-search and extraction backends with a free-first multi-provider router, persistent health/cache state and a Desktop manager.

reads.best: Improves the existing native web tools across Hermes surfaces with cost-tier fallback, circuit breakers, scoped provider secrets and substantial routing/extraction tests.
reads.worst: Reliability still depends on changing public keyless endpoints and optional browser infrastructure, and the README retains stale rename examples and an incorrect API mount string.

plugins.name: atlas
plugins.author: zhaidarbek
plugins.does: Maintains cross-agent project records from local conversation stores and delivers actionable Telegram briefs with a dashboard and guarded agent tools.

reads.best: Cross-harness collection, evidence-grounded records and owner-message verification provide substantial persistent agent capability, backed by a broad scenario harness.
reads.worst: It keeps verbatim potentially secret-bearing transcripts and makes unattended model calls even while paused, and real-model and real-Telegram behavior remains untested.

plugins.name: hermes-ghost-call
plugins.author: winchxyz
plugins.does: Runs a live call copilot that transcribes conversation, offers private hints and earpiece speech, and produces a post-call summary.

reads.best: A working audio bridge, private whisper routing, bounded sessions and layered intervention gates go far beyond a conversational skill.
reads.worst: The README explicitly leaves live Twilio calls and use inside a running Hermes chat untested, and setup needs a separately reachable bridge.

plugins.name: hermes-superagent
plugins.author: AirKyzzZ
plugins.does: Adds a gated coordinator, isolated task workers, a progress watchdog and a persistent ledger fed by external task and session connectors.

reads.best: Role tool guards, stale-worker fencing, bounded repairs and completeness-aware ledger tests materially improve multi-agent supervision.
reads.worst: Real-model coverage is narrow: watchdog repairs have not run on real Hermes, and Gmail, Calendar and WhatsApp connectors have only synthetic-data coverage.

plugins.name: othigai
plugins.author: ramakrishnanhulk20
plugins.does: Runs consented prompt-injection drills against Hermes subagents using fake secrets, controlled tools and a local listener to measure attempted leaks.

reads.best: Paired clean controls, real-Hermes stub-model tests and lifecycle containment make agent safety measurable on the user’s own setup.
reads.worst: Known grading gaps can misclassify harmless payloads as failures or missed sends as resistance, undermining the central safety score.

plugins.name: hermes-helm
plugins.author: phucnht
plugins.does: Adds owner-only Discord and Telegram controls for Hermes tools, skills, MCP servers, lost-turn replay, long replies and daily spending limits.

reads.best: It brings practical control of a continuously running agent to the user’s phone, with tested owner gates and explicit replay permissions.
reads.worst: The spending gate counts only priced calls, so unknown model prices escape the limit unless the owner supplies rates.

plugins.name: hermes-pentest
plugins.author: WebisityStudio
plugins.does: Prepares and runs bounded local application security assessments with human approval, isolated runtimes, durable evidence and regression checks.

reads.best: Exact-scope one-use approval, default-deny unmanaged targets and controlled SQL/XSS tests make it a substantial extension of Hermes execution.
reads.worst: The guided workflow supports a limited Vite/Supabase recipe and needs prepared local Docker images and browser tooling rather than offering general application coverage.

plugins.name: why
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Records the requests behind agent file edits and explains the provenance of matching code lines through a tool, command and CLI.

reads.best: Lifecycle hooks capture provenance at edit time, with text fingerprints and neighbor matching that survive inserted lines.
reads.worst: Coverage is limited to write_file and patch; shell edits and renames lose provenance, and identical text can only be attributed heuristically.

plugins.name: pit-crew
plugins.author: trevornk
plugins.does: Monitors connected cars, plans charging readiness and executes policy-checked commands through Hermes approval integration.

reads.best: A simulator, proactive watcher, scoped credentials, fresh-motion checks and command readback form a substantial hardware integration.
reads.worst: Direct Tesla and non-Tesla profiles have limited live validation, and approval-class commands can run without a fresh human answer when Hermes approvals are disabled.

plugins.name: hermes-ui
plugins.author: Ilyassbm
plugins.does: Replaces Hermes Desktop and Webapp chat with a bot-oriented workspace, rich interactive replies and integrated approvals.

reads.best: A shipped Desktop bundle implements streaming conversations, per-bot models, attachments, shortcuts and structured interactive replies with extensive interface checks.
reads.worst: File-preview routes allow most files throughout the user home via a narrow secret-name denylist, and credential lookup falls back after scoped-secret errors.

plugins.name: tallyhand
plugins.author: RezaHarirchian
plugins.does: Adds a Twitch gateway platform with role-restricted chat tools, moderation approvals, viewer notes, and OBS control.

reads.best: Code-enforced roles, fail-closed memory protection, and extensive offline protocol tests make a public-chat agent unusually well defended.
reads.worst: Serving viewers safely requires a separate profile with memory disabled and careful context settings, while bot tokens need manual renewal.

plugins.name: second-hands
plugins.author: zaxcoraider
plugins.does: Uses a Desktop camera feed and Hermes models to track hands-on task steps and warn about visible mistakes.

reads.best: The camera pane, live chat card, staged warning pipeline, and no-cost demo form an original Hermes interaction.
reads.worst: There are no tests in the pinned tree, and model-generated guidance and visual judgments make missed hazards a substantial reliability risk.

plugins.name: film-suite
plugins.author: realartsbro
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop film workstation with shared script, media generation, audio analysis, timeline editing and queued rendering tools.

reads.best: The artist and agent edit the same durable project through revision-checked routes, with undo and exports to professional editing formats.
reads.worst: The pinned distribution excludes tests, relies on private Hermes authentication imports and direct Desktop bridge access, and documents Windows-only testing.

plugins.name: sharelet
plugins.author: TANGBUDU
plugins.does: Publishes explicitly selected Hermes or MCP tools as expiring, revocable browser links with bounded guest inputs and run quotas.

reads.best: Creator approvals bind the reviewed tool contract, and tests cover revocation during queued dispatch, changed grants, destructive-tool rejection and separate owner/guest listeners.
reads.worst: Optional image recipes store keys outside Hermes secrets, public links default to an author-operated relay, and cloudflared is fetched from mutable releases/latest with a digest supplied by that same response.

plugins.name: plugin-safehouse
plugins.author: LaithAskar
plugins.does: Trials a local Hermes plugin in a disposable macOS sandbox with planted canaries, invokes reachable handlers, and reports observed behavior and coverage.

reads.best: Behavioral execution with fake secrets, a jailed worker, handler coverage, and careful INCONCLUSIVE/REVIEW distinctions addresses a real gap left by static scanning; it includes extensive attack fixtures and tests.
reads.worst: Dynamic testing is macOS-only and supports only standalone and exclusive plugins; its real-loader integration relies on a disclosed private API seam.

reads.best: It combines OS containment, canary attribution, bounded invocation and adversarial fixtures while refusing to call an incomplete trial a safety clearance. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LaithAskar/hermes-plugin-safehouse/8e2e5ced6ece60b3c33a9ae36a0da5cf04a95fee/README.md)
reads.worst: Dynamic trials require macOS sandbox-exec, exclude most plugin kinds and dependencies, and cannot establish safety against a candidate that detects or tampers with the trial. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LaithAskar/hermes-plugin-safehouse/8e2e5ced6ece60b3c33a9ae36a0da5cf04a95fee/README.md)

plugins.name: draftroom
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Adds a Hermes Desktop Markdown workspace where the agent proposes selected-text rewrites and the editor user accepts or rejects them.

reads.best: Version-bound proposals, optimistic saves, atomic writes, revision history, native Desktop controls, and extensive backend and controller tests support a real co-writing loop.
reads.worst: It is an early release with known UX and accessibility work, and the backend requires Linux or macOS plus a compatible recent Desktop SDK.

plugins.name: leadpoet
plugins.author: gzaentz
plugins.does: Turns a seller's website into a sourced prospect brief, personalized outreach drafts, person-approved campaign launches, and reply drafting in chat.

reads.best: The workflow pairs evidence checks for personalized claims with cost disclosure, secret-store API access, code-bound human approval, and 213 focused tests.
reads.worst: The current PR text identifies v0.2.7 at a different SHA than this batch's v0.2.6 pin, so the reviewed tree is older than the PR description says.

plugins.name: prove-it
plugins.author: MikeGibbsOnyx
plugins.does: Checks an agent's completion claims (pushed, committed, file written, tests pass) with read-only local probes and appends verdicts to the reply.

reads.best: Catches false 'done' claims with no model calls, via transform_llm_output, with tests and a demo.
reads.worst: Regex claim extraction will miss many phrasings and can only verify a few claim types.

plugins.name: session-cassettes
plugins.author: eightyFJ
plugins.does: Records read-only session results and replays the same request against another model or prompt from a workspace snapshot, refusing live tool calls.

reads.best: Its middleware-level claimed replay, pins, explicit PASS/FAIL/DIVERGED/INVALID verdicts, and extensive security/test documentation make model comparison reproducible and safer.
reads.worst: The pinned code documents major untested platform limits, and replay can become INVALID or unsafe if the claim race or gateway conditions are not met.

reads.best: Tool interception and snapshot-backed synthesized reads make regression comparisons possible without a separate judge model.
reads.worst: An unclaimed replay can execute live tools before being graded INVALID, so the intended offline safety property is not guaranteed.

plugins.name: stmp
plugins.author: a7madgamal
plugins.does: Uses an approval-gated phone bridge as the trust boundary for Gmail, Calendar, Drive, contacts, notifications, secrets and SSH.

reads.best: Moving credentials and human approval onto a phone is a strong, concrete trust-boundary design with closed action contracts and path controls.
reads.worst: The bridge is a powerful remote dependency and HTTPS is only recommended, so deployment security still depends heavily on the phone setup.

plugins.name: hermes-whoop
plugins.author: solmonger
plugins.does: Adds WHOOP OAuth tools, commands, scheduled briefs and an opt-in hook for recovery, sleep, strain and readiness context.

reads.best: It is a polished, tested wearable integration with proper OAuth, bounded hook time, caching, demo mode and useful date/trend analysis.
reads.worst: Its usefulness is limited to WHOOP owners and the health interpretation remains necessarily advisory.

plugins.name: spine
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Tests whether the active model keeps correct answers after confident wrong pushback and reports a reproducible sycophancy score.

reads.best: Its deterministic, transcript-backed evaluation directly probes a meaningful agent failure mode without asking another model to grade it.
reads.worst: The fixed question bank and answer-line parser can make the score less representative of open-ended agent behavior.

plugins.name: rocketchat-team-gateway
plugins.author: csabatatrai-ulx
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Rocket.Chat rooms and DMs with per-person context, guarded commands, approval buttons, and durable delivery handling.

reads.best: A carefully built team gateway addresses shared-room identity, approvals, reconnects, setup, and live demonstration.
reads.worst: It still depends on a separately operated Rocket.Chat server and several bot credentials.

reads.best: The adapter covers difficult shared-room concerns including sender-scoped sessions, default-deny Hermes commands, duplicate suppression, and approval buttons.
reads.worst: At this pinned commit it registers the same `rocketchat` platform id as the existing catalog adapter, a collision the catalog reviewer flagged as a blocker.

plugins.name: show-your-work
plugins.author: kenpritchard
plugins.does: Builds an acceptance-criteria evidence board from JUnit results, file freshness, linked tests, and human accept/reject sign-off, with agent, CLI, slash, and Desktop surfaces.

reads.best: It separates coverage, test outcome, freshness, and human review instead of treating a green command as proof, and backs that model with tests and disclosure rules.
reads.worst: It is primarily an evidence workflow around existing test runners, so some value still depends on users maintaining meaningful criteria and links.

reads.best: Separates coverage, outcome, freshness and review rather than a single green check.
reads.worst: Audience is mainly developers who track requirements, and it only imports results.

plugins.name: claw-messenger
plugins.author: demegire
plugins.does: Gateway platform adapter that lets Hermes send and receive iMessage, RCS and SMS (including groups and attachments) through the paid Claw Messenger WebSocket service, plus a create-group tool.

reads.best: A full platform adapter with a sender allowlist, the API key declared as a password requires_env and read through Hermes's env helper, https/wss-only enforcement and eight test files.
reads.worst: Every message goes through a third-party paid relay on onrender.com, and the pip install path tells users to append the key to ~/.hermes/.env by hand.

plugins.name: steward
plugins.author: imprint-hash
plugins.does: Collects each department's weekly update in its own group chat, nudges only the teams that have not replied, builds a founder pack with a voice brief and publishes a staff version only after founder approval.

reads.best: A full multi-chat workflow on Hermes cron, gateway and TTS, with founder-only publishing, media-cache-confined file reads and 114 tests, including security suites.
reads.worst: Needs gateway setup across many group chats, has no screenshots or demo, and writes helper scripts into HERMES_HOME/scripts.

plugins.name: homework-coach
plugins.author: andrewjsoukup
plugins.does: Reads photos of a child's homework with a vision model and builds verified, adaptive daily practice PDFs plus a separate parent answer key that adjust to parent feedback.

reads.best: Answers are recomputed independently and the PDFs are checked before delivery, with 7 tools, a Desktop page whose source ships, a cron blueprint and about 190 tests.
reads.worst: A narrow audience (elementary math), and the author admits the 0.2 Desktop panel has not been tested live.

plugins.name: stoa
plugins.author: jarrett-del
plugins.does: A lightweight CRM run by talking to Hermes: market maps, a YAML-playbook SQLite pipeline, review-before-apply lead intake, Slack button cards, a dashboard tab and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Button clicks move the pipeline at once with no model involved, keys come from Hermes's secret scope, and the same data shows in Slack, the dashboard and Desktop with 11 screenshots and seeded demos.
reads.worst: A very broad surface tested in one file, and gtm_export writes a CSV to any path the agent supplies (desk.py:776), which can overwrite user files.

plugins.name: rung
plugins.author: pratham31012002
plugins.does: Connects Hermes completion verification to a code-bound ledger of project checks and exposes tools to plan, run, and inspect that verification. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CalQuity/rung/970be4f506c496586a7fec8b818491ceab602e4b/hermes-plugin/tools.py)

reads.best: Its pre_verify hook challenges stale passing results, bounds continuation attempts, and keeps feature-map approvals on human slash commands. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CalQuity/rung/970be4f506c496586a7fec8b818491ceab602e4b/hermes-plugin/tools.py)
reads.worst: Checks execute project-configured commands with the inherited environment, so users must trust rung.toml; the separate CLI dependency is version-ranged rather than fixed to the reviewed commit. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CalQuity/rung/970be4f506c496586a7fec8b818491ceab602e4b/hermes-plugin/README.md)

reads.best: Freshness is tied to checked inputs, and the completion hook asks for missing evidence with bounded continuations; plugin wiring and ledger behavior have tests. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CalQuity/rung/970be4f506c496586a7fec8b818491ceab602e4b/hermes-plugin/tools.py
reads.worst: The plugin is a thin wrapper around an independently installed CLI: unexpected hook failures let completion proceed, and configured check commands run with inherited environment without a per-command approval gate. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CalQuity/rung/970be4f506c496586a7fec8b818491ceab602e4b/hermes-plugin/tools.py

plugins.name: hermes-portals
plugins.author: ochikov
plugins.does: Creates persistent interactive tools that transfer between laptop and phone, with camera gestures and optional native Mac input control.

reads.best: Reviewable browser and Swift code combines stateful device handoff, local hand tracking and explicitly armed native input.
reads.worst: It remains a trusted-LAN HTTP prototype with one paired phone, substantial setup and limited hardware coverage.

reads.best: Transactional state, one-use pairing, revision conflict checks and local-only camera processing make the gesture-and-device handoff more than a visual mockup.
reads.worst: This remains a trusted-LAN HTTP prototype with one active artifact and one phone, a small fixed set of tool types and a separate multi-step companion/native setup.

plugins.name: data
plugins.author: Adolanium
plugins.does: Turns spreadsheets and pasted tables into editable Desktop reports with locally computed charts, reviewed suggestions and chat tools.

reads.best: Charts aggregate actual rows locally, numeric remarks use computed placeholders, and proposals wait for acceptance with undo.
reads.worst: Hidden Ask sessions can use the user’s tools; avoiding writes, commands and messages is prompt advice plus approval denial, not an enforced tool allowlist.

plugins.name: forgebox
plugins.author: nosliwhtes
plugins.does: Snapshots dirty Git checkouts into disposable worktrees, redirects supported Hermes tool paths, journals execution and lets users explicitly review, apply or discard changes.

reads.best: Preserves dirty work and the real index, with hook integration, conflict-aware staged application, rollback regressions and a Desktop review pane.
reads.worst: Redirection covers known file arguments and terminal working directories only; absolute shell paths and subprocess side effects escape it, and apply is not crash-atomic.

plugins.name: margin
plugins.author: pratikpoddar
plugins.does: Gateway platform that turns '@hermes' Google Docs/Slides/Sheets comments into Hermes chat threads and can apply suggested edits.

reads.best: A new platform adapter with OAuth through Hermes auth, tests and a demo gif.
reads.worst: Needs the user to create their own Google Cloud OAuth client; polling and niche audience.

plugins.name: alchemy-task
plugins.author: Darengb
plugins.does: Turns messy work from threads, meetings and notes into researched tasks with discovery, research and work-session tools plus Desktop/iOS views.

reads.best: Very large, heavily tested codebase (about 89 test files) with a demo, screenshots and Desktop UI.
reads.worst: Huge surface (~31k lines, 18+ tools) that is hard to review and reaches many sources.

plugins.name: cortive
plugins.author: KadenDevAi
plugins.does: Memory provider that recalls captures from the local Cortive knowledge base (SQLite FTS5) before each reply, with search/get/collections tools.

reads.best: Plugs into Hermes memory, read-only and local, with hooks that block other tools from Cortive's data and redact saved passwords, plus injection tests.
reads.worst: macOS only and useful only to users of the Cortive app.

plugins.name: protocol-chaos
plugins.author: chaos-xxl
plugins.does: Brings cross-assistant project context into Hermes turns and records and structures user updates on a self-hosted matters server.

reads.best: Lifecycle hooks, verbatim capture checks and version-aware updates provide durable shared context beyond a prompted memory workflow.
reads.worst: It requires a separately operated server and MCP setup, and capture starts a new background thread per eligible message without a concurrency cap.

plugins.name: cash-desk
plugins.author: miraklodowska
plugins.does: Reconciles invoice and bank CSVs, drafts overdue-payment reminders and delivers only text-bound, human-approved messages.

reads.best: Figure checks, ledger revalidation, exact-text approvals and extensive adversarial tests enforce safeguards a prompt cannot provide.
reads.worst: It needs manual CSV imports rather than live accounting integration, and its restricted financial prose still requires a person to catch semantic errors.

plugins.name: psychopomp
plugins.author: ponzgpt
plugins.does: Keeps approved weekly journal pages and sealed letters, then delivers them after prolonged silence and a witness code.

reads.best: The native journal cards, witness workflow and rehearsal using the real state machine on a virtual clock form an unusually coherent agent-native product.
reads.worst: Check-in state advances before send success and Book delivery has no persisted retry state, weakening its legacy-delivery promise; letters are also stored in plaintext.

plugins.name: adeptory
plugins.author: brefledev
plugins.does: Builds dedicated Hermes specialist profiles with searchable source libraries, procedures, tool capability records and retained verification evidence.

reads.best: Profile delivery is gated on revision-bound native task evidence, with source-passage checks, library freshness tracking and substantial mechanics and integration tests.
reads.worst: Specialist quality still depends on extensive model-directed research and host tool execution, while passage matching and receipts cannot establish the semantic correctness of professional advice.

plugins.name: herd
plugins.author: welliv
plugins.does: Synchronizes Hermes configuration, skills, memory and SOUL across paired machines through encrypted stores and per-key conflict-aware merging.

reads.best: Machine-specific settings and credential-bearing config sections are preserved locally, with encrypted objects, reversible pulls and substantial conflict and safety tests.
reads.worst: It requires a reachable shared folder or configured git store, and automatic interactive-session pulls can replace instruction-bearing files from a trusted peer without a fresh sync_now approval.

plugins.name: receipts
plugins.author: cirwel
plugins.does: Blocks supported terminal pushes and PR creation until the published Git tree has a passing verification receipt ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cirwel/hermes-receipts/0dd1a374cc70ce388040f99adc908c7054ed8fa9/README.md)).

reads.best: It binds actual command exit codes to Git content and rechecks the precise published commit, with real-repository behavioral tests.
reads.worst: The gate is inactive for remote terminal backends, multiplexed profiles and plugin-host isolation, and custom publishing scripts remain outside its bounded shell recognition ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cirwel/hermes-receipts/0dd1a374cc70ce388040f99adc908c7054ed8fa9/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: hermes-standing
plugins.author: percyhendrux123-prog
plugins.does: Tracks checked worker outcomes and applies earned trust levels and proof-before-completion gates to Hermes tool calls.

reads.best: Session-and-task-bound proof receipts, scoped checks and extensive adversarial tests make worker accountability concrete.
reads.worst: Repeated trivial checks can earn trust and an earlier passing receipt survives later failures, so the policy cannot establish task quality.

plugins.name: google-workspace
plugins.author: francoleff
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop workspace and forty tools for Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets and Contacts with cross-app workflows.

reads.best: Broad everyday utility comes with Hermes-managed OAuth, write-approval hooks, review dialogs, careful retry behavior and substantial Python and UI tests.
reads.worst: Google Cloud OAuth setup is demanding, and the README acknowledges that RSVP and actions inside a running Desktop have not been tested live.

plugins.name: hermes-audio-api
plugins.author: axAilotl
plugins.does: Serves authenticated OpenAI-compatible transcription and speech endpoints using the profile's configured Hermes voice providers.

reads.best: A gateway-managed listener makes Hermes voice providers reusable by other clients, with scoped credentials, streaming limits, codec checks and discovery tests.
reads.worst: Depends on private Hermes voice entry points and optional ffmpeg; concurrent listeners across multiplexed profiles are not covered by tests.

plugins.name: hermes-3d
plugins.author: PabloFMM
plugins.does: Mirrors Hermes activity, schedules and optional profile metadata into a local explorable 3D world embedded in Desktop.

reads.best: A distinctive Desktop experience has a real event bridge, sandboxed frame, verified engine download and queued approval-gated cron actions.
reads.worst: The separate Node engine and optional private database reads add setup and compatibility burden, while end-to-end first-run tests use a fake engine release.

plugins.name: apple-keychain
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Adds a macOS Keychain SecretSource plus operator commands for setup, diagnosis, secret rotation and recovery.

reads.best: Improves Hermes credential handling through its actual SecretSource interface, bounded noninteractive native reads and recovery-aware writes backed by discovery and disposable-Keychain tests.
reads.worst: macOS developer tools and service-identity Keychain authorization are required; helper rebuilds can require reauthorization and several Hermes imports are private.

plugins.name: harness2
plugins.author: shrinedogg
plugins.does: Runs isolated probe sessions to propose, test, compose, and adopt evidence-backed changes to an agent profile’s prompt, config, and skills.

reads.best: It makes self-improvement an actual measured loop with isolated profiles, budgets, structural gates, trajectories, and a reusable library.
reads.worst: There are no repository tests, and the central subprocess/profile orchestration has many failure and environment assumptions.

plugins.name: speckle
plugins.author: NikolaosArgy
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Speckle 3D/BIM models: 13 tools to query, diff, check and watch models, plus a live 3D viewer pane in Hermes Desktop.

reads.best: Tools, watcher service, hooks and an embedded Desktop 3D viewer make Hermes itself do something new, with get_secret, screenshots and tests.
reads.worst: Niche AEC audience, and a 3.8MB vendored viewer bundle is hard to review (build script and licenses are included).

reads.best: Model selection, element queries, visual diffs and saved version checks form a coherent specialist workflow beyond chat.
reads.worst: Issue creation immediately writes through the API; asking the user first is only a prompt/schema instruction, and tests focus on indexing, checks and redirects rather than the full viewer/watcher path.

plugins.name: household-fleet
plugins.author: rishiruben
plugins.does: Applies a deterministic message gate with caps, quiet hours, deduplication and audit history, and mirrors tasks into Home Assistant.

reads.best: The state-hash anti-repeat policy and pure, offline-testable decision function address a real multi-agent failure mode mechanically.
reads.worst: The plugin returns a delivery decision rather than delivering, and the Home Assistant mirror adds a live-service dependency.

plugins.name: wake
plugins.author: zzzubair
plugins.does: Queues notes and cron reports, waits for the bound chat, optionally prechecks relevance, and injects a turn into the user’s own agent conversation.

reads.best: It adds a genuinely Hermes-native proactive-agent loop across cron, platform delivery, CLI, hooks, and injected turns while defaulting to quiet skips.
reads.worst: It relies on a polling queue and gateway/session behavior, and retries can complicate operational diagnosis when a chat is unavailable.

plugins.name: flowlight
plugins.author: ayinmodeolarewaju-bot
plugins.does: A read-only wallet-watching plugin that tracks public NEAR/EVM/Solana addresses, summarizes inflows/outflows with USD pricing, and renders the flows as an animated visualization in a Desktop pane, dashboard tab and standalone page.

reads.best: Explicitly refuses seed phrases and signing keys in code (tested), every tool handler always returns read_only: true even on error, and it adds a genuine new Desktop UI surface (pane, route, sidebar row, status chip) via the plugin SDK.
reads.worst: Narrow audience of users who want to passively watch public on-chain addresses, rather than a broad day-one install.

reads.best: A shared Desktop, dashboard and loopback visualization makes multi-chain flows inspectable while keeping all transaction handling read-only.
reads.worst: The HTTP client can silently return an indefinitely old cached response after a failed read, weakening the freshness claim of its live view.

plugins.name: opensop
plugins.author: Chosen9115
plugins.does: Runs OpenSOP process files where scripts decide done and hooks re-anchor Hermes on its step and refuse self-approval.

reads.best: Hooks enforce a workflow, which a skill cannot do.
reads.worst: Depends on the OpenSOP ecosystem; niche.

plugins.name: hermes-sfx-forge
plugins.author: socraticblock
plugins.does: A deterministic procedural sound-effect synthesizer that generates short one-shot WAV files (hits, pickups, etc.) from named presets and an integer seed using real DSP, then verifies output against a fixed numeric QA gate.

reads.best: Strongest security posture reviewed: path-traversal and symlink-attack defenses (O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd-anchored opens, advisory locks) backed by a dedicated adversarial test file, plus fully deterministic, reproducible-by-seed audio generation with zero network/credential surface.
reads.worst: Narrow usefulness — only game-sound generation, Linux-only (explicitly unsupported on macOS/Windows because of an fcntl dependency), and no visual demo since audio output isn't screenshot-able.

plugins.name: quick-eval
plugins.author: shaunporwal
plugins.does: After an agent reply, sends the user's last question to other configured models (cloud or local) for a side-by-side second opinion, lets the user mark good answers, and logs results for a growing personal eval dataset.

reads.best: Requires explicit one-time user permission before calling other models, uses parameterized SQL with a read-only connection, and has a real end-to-end test that spins up an actual Hermes subprocess plus a fake model server.
reads.worst: No screenshots/visual assets found beyond demo-GIF test scaffolding, and 'comparing LLM outputs side-by-side' is a known pattern even if the zero-config chat-command UX is a thoughtful original touch.

plugins.name: kairos
plugins.author: Joe-Kneeland
plugins.does: Uses Hermes's own session history and sleep logs to offer wind-down nudges at clean stopping points, save your place, flag failing-tool streaks and report evidence-gated sleep/work correlations.

reads.best: A genuinely new agent-native idea (the agent was in the room at 3am) with careful statistics, honest copy, screenshots and a full Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Only the statistics are tested; the per-turn injection hooks, guard and sleep-file importers are untested, it reads Hermes's private state.db schema, and plugin.yaml (0.6.0) disagrees with __version__ (0.5.1).

plugins.name: hermes-body
plugins.author: Itsmetibo
plugins.does: A gateway platform that turns a phone browser into a Hermes channel with camera frames, push-to-talk voice and spoken replies over a token-gated WebSocket.

reads.best: A real platform adapter, so the phone gets the full agent loop with tools and memory, with constant-time token checks and capped, re-encoded uploads.
reads.worst: The phone page has no handler for the 'commentary' messages the adapter sends, so interim updates are silently dropped; voice uses the browser Web Speech API, which can send audio off-device, contrary to the privacy framing; only 3 script-style tests.

plugins.name: showreel
plugins.author: Duffey234
plugins.does: Records a session through six observer hooks into a secret-scrubbed SQLite log and cuts it into a captioned sub-90-second MP4 with SRT and poster via local ffmpeg.

reads.best: A complete, 50-test pipeline from hooks to deterministic storyboard to encoded video, with ElevenLabs keys via get_secret, host-locked requests and timeouts everywhere.
reads.worst: Screenshot images are drawn into the video unredacted, and the agent can pick paid ElevenLabs narration through the tool without the confirmation the Desktop asks for.

plugins.name: waiting-on-you-desktop
plugins.author: clientamp
plugins.does: A Desktop side panel that reads the end of every chat across profiles, uses Hermes's auxiliary model to extract what the agent is waiting on the user for, and lets the user answer in place from one prioritized list.

reads.best: It turns many parallel agent chats into one answerable queue: classification goes through Hermes's own model API, answers go into the chat composer after a five-second undo window, and it has screenshots, a changelog and a written list of known gaps.
reads.worst: The shipped desktop/plugin.js is a minified 260 KB bundle (source is in src/), it reads other profiles' state.db files straight from disk and leans on private Hermes internals, and its 36 JS and about 49 Python test files are run by no CI.

plugins.name: wiretap
plugins.author: aka-lacie
plugins.does: Records the exact request and response of every model API call into a local SQLite store and shows them in a dashboard tab, a Desktop page and a read-only CLI, including cache-miss analysis.

reads.best: Deep, honest engineering for debugging Hermes: wire capture beside the transcript, credential redaction, 0600 storage and about 229 Python tests plus browser tests.
reads.worst: Relies on fragile internals (frame inspection, a process-wide httpx patch, private Hermes imports), stores full conversation content by default, and its manifests still mention unshipped features.

plugins.name: hyperactive
plugins.author: justin06lee
plugins.does: Makes Hermes speak first: keeps a goal tree, promises and decisions in SQLite and uses Hermes cron jobs to send check-ins, a daily brief, stalled-goal nudges and tap cards that auto-apply only low-stakes choices.

reads.best: A coherent proactive layer built on public surfaces (six tools, /ha, CLI command, system-prompt section, three hooks, cron with a no-model pulse) where money, public and irreversible cards always wait for the person.
reads.worst: The Telegram reaction handler is marked UNTESTED in the code and guesses which card a reaction answers, there is no CI, and the CLI fallback parses `hermes cron list` text with regexes.

plugins.name: mulligan
plugins.author: onyebuchidaniel60
plugins.does: Records every LLM and tool step of a run through middleware, then replays the run in a child session from a chosen step with one edited tool argument, and diffs the two runs.

reads.best: A counterfactual record/rewind/edit/replay debugger built on Hermes's llm/tool middleware: something new for agents, that only a plugin can do.
reads.worst: The author's own notes say a real child replay is untested end-to-end; an edit before the branch point does nothing, and traces store unredacted prompts and tool results on disk.

plugins.name: hermes-strudel-studio
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Adds a local Strudel music workspace with agent-editable tracks, revisioned snapshots, and a sandboxed Desktop player requiring human playback.

reads.best: The native collaborative music pane combines real audio, scheduler highlights, revision conflict protection, and a carefully isolated authenticated sidecar.
reads.worst: Native Desktop worklets and remote gateway operation remain unverified, and a stale sidecar record requires deliberate recovery rather than automatic restart.

plugins.name: hermes-replicate
plugins.author: jacebenson
plugins.does: Registers native Replicate image, video, transcription, and speech providers with validated model schemas and guarded media handling.

reads.best: It is a broad, well-documented native provider integration with schema validation, secret-store use, and extensive mocked contract coverage.
reads.worst: It depends on a paid third-party service and live model schemas, so compatibility and cost remain outside the plugin's control.

plugins.name: telegram-app
plugins.author: aimanmalib
plugins.does: Provides an authenticated Telegram Mini App dashboard for Hermes sessions, status, cron, logs, knowledge, messaging, and alerts.

reads.best: It gives Hermes a substantial phone-first control surface through Telegram, with Telegram initData verification and an explicit allowlist-based login.
reads.worst: Its implementation reaches into private Hermes internals and runs a polling alert thread; the wide control surface increases compatibility and operational risk.

plugins.name: chess-coach
plugins.author: oppai
plugins.does: Adds a native Desktop chessboard for games and mate puzzles, backed by legal-move tools, local solving, and saved game state.

reads.best: Legal moves, puzzle validation, and replies are computed locally, with a polished board and Hermes opponent/review available when requested; it includes Python and UI tests.
reads.worst: It serves a niche audience, needs the python-chess dependency, and makes no claim to provide systematic strategy instruction or reliable evaluation of arbitrary positions.

plugins.name: ligis
plugins.author: udirobert
plugins.does: A read-only on-chain verification plugin (scoped to its hermes-plugin/ subfolder) that checks whether a payment destination holds a live, revocable credential on an EVM testnet registry, and gates/annotates payment-shaped tool calls via pre_tool_call/transform_tool_result hooks that escalate to Hermes's own approval prompt.

reads.best: Fails closed on any registry outage or unknown result, holds no keys and sends no transactions itself, and routes payment gating through Hermes's native approval prompt rather than auto-approving.
reads.worst: EVM-testnet-only in this release, and its payment-shaped-call detection relies on regex heuristics on tool names/args that the README itself admits can miss some payment shapes (e.g. wallet-server-settled payments).

plugins.name: agent-desktop-gnome
plugins.author: BruceBest
plugins.does: A Hermes computer_use provider that drives a real GNOME Linux desktop via AT-SPI accessibility APIs through a pinned, checksum-verified third-party binary, restricted to semantic element actions only (no screenshots, raw mouse/keyboard, or window focus).

reads.best: Careful security engineering: SHA256-pinned binary with no runtime network calls, argv-only subprocess execution, secret-field redaction, and explicit seat-isolation checks.
reads.worst: Its own README states catalog admission is pending on an unrelated upstream Hermes bug, and most of the action surface (coordinates, drag, scroll, screenshots) is deliberately refused, narrowing real-world usefulness.

plugins.name: reading
plugins.author: Nj07r
plugins.does: Builds a Gmail newsletter reader in Desktop and the dashboard, with native mail filters, unsubscribe controls, digest exports and newsletter context references ([pinned source](https://github.com/Nj07r/hermes-reading/tree/c739110797b0bcd0bad53d8f2a83b8ce1854430d)).

reads.best: The complete reading workflow joins a responsive keyboard-and-touch UI with Hermes-managed OAuth, sandboxed email rendering and direct newsletter-to-chat context.
reads.worst: sync() deletes existing Gmail filters before creating replacements and saves their IDs only after all creations succeed, so a partial API failure can break routing or leave untracked filters ([reading_core.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nj07r/hermes-reading/c739110797b0bcd0bad53d8f2a83b8ce1854430d/reading_core.py)).

plugins.name: ownmachine
plugins.author: rbur0425
plugins.does: Adds a native Hermes computer-use backend for a persistent macOS VM with capture-bound actions and shared human/agent control ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rbur0425/ownmachine/a93fbfec22281a01031a62629294e280fca4115b/plugin/ownmachine/provider.py)).

reads.best: The backend rejects stale targets and uncertain writes instead of replaying input, and integrates through Hermes's native provider contract ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rbur0425/ownmachine/a93fbfec22281a01031a62629294e280fca4115b/plugin/ownmachine/provider.py)).
reads.worst: Apple Silicon, separate relay/guest/viewer provisioning, a custom Lume build, and in-process configuration make onboarding demanding, while model-driven pixel-click acceptance remains deferred ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rbur0425/ownmachine/a93fbfec22281a01031a62629294e280fca4115b/plugin/README.md)).

plugins.name: flightdeck
plugins.author: freemanconsulting
plugins.does: Tracks Hermes model requests and local inference-server capacity in a Desktop fleet view, with optional capacity-aware subagent routing.

reads.best: Seven observer hooks, server adapters and an opt-in delegation provider turn local inference visibility into actionable routing, with detailed tests and a finished Desktop view.
reads.worst: At the field-pinned commit, config._read_yaml_config silently returns empty settings when undeclared PyYAML is unavailable, disabling normal server discovery and capacity routing; a later PR fix is outside this pin.

plugins.name: hermes-artifacts
plugins.author: MrSakal
plugins.does: Adds versioned Desktop artifacts with live document, spreadsheet and board editing, dashboards, design tools and local exports.

reads.best: A substantial collaborative workspace with revision conflict handling, sandboxed previews and broad tests materially expands Hermes Desktop.
reads.worst: Publishing a dashboard automatically approves all stored MCP calls by default, while dispatch checks MCP membership rather than read-only tool semantics; screenshots are still placeholders.

plugins.name: taint-sentry
plugins.author: YAN-XBT
plugins.does: Tracks untrusted tool-result provenance, sanitizes text and gates subsequent credential, egress and instruction-file actions with receipts and Desktop controls.

reads.best: Public hooks carry taint into subagents and enforce a configurable policy, with meaningful adversarial and false-positive tests.
reads.worst: Heuristic detectors miss memory/cron persistence and assembled payloads, taint expires in memory, and documented one-shot hook gaps leave some unattended runs unenforced.

plugins.name: ariadne-thread
plugins.author: benoit-dev
plugins.does: Desktop page that draws cron jobs, webhooks and skills as n8n-style step chains, with in-place editing, conflict checks, history/undo and change requests drafted into a new chat.

reads.best: A full Desktop UI over Hermes's own automation, with atomic writes, confined paths, credential redaction, 94 backend tests and screenshots.
reads.worst: Imports Hermes internals (cron.jobs), the conflict check on whole-skill saves is optional, and script editing through the dashboard API is effectively code execution.

plugins.name: hive
plugins.author: MFaiqKhan
plugins.does: Learns from exit codes which commands fixed a failing terminal command and appends a 'fixed before' hint to repeat errors, optionally sharing fixes between installs over Nostr.

reads.best: Evidence-based fix learning (flaky retries ignored) with egress redaction, signed events, peer quorums and 22 offline tests against a mock relay.
reads.worst: Peer hints go into tool output the agent reads, defended mainly by cheap proof-of-work and a regex blocklist, and the read-mode relay lookup runs synchronously under a lock on the hot path.

plugins.name: crashlab
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Injects lost-response and restart faults into a web app through a real Chromium, freezes the failing run as an experiment and re-runs it after Hermes repairs the app.

reads.best: Approvals bound to a digest of the exact plan, about 311 tests, and recorded before/after evidence on outside apps (Kist, Flaskr).
reads.worst: A dense, repetitive README and 14 tools aimed at a narrow web-reliability audience.

plugins.name: customs
plugins.author: pgreyy
plugins.does: Plants unique honeytoken credential files and blocks or flags any agent tool call that reaches for them, redacting the fake values from tool results and outgoing LLM requests.

reads.best: A new defence that catches an agent hunting for secrets inside the tool loop, with attack-chain correlation, session lockdown and a candid limitations section.
reads.worst: No pytest suite (only a 10-sample script and an in-plugin self-check) for about 4.3k lines, and every hook fails open by design.

plugins.name: ciphervault
plugins.author: samuel-1-avson
plugins.does: Wraps the CipherVault Rust CLI to give Hermes seven secret-vault tools (masked scan, approval-gated RAM-only run, encrypted push, recovery drill, redact, audit), leak-guard and result-scrubbing hooks, a Hermes secret source and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Deep, safety-first integration: every ciphervault_run goes through Hermes's approval gate, other tools' results are scrubbed before entering context, subprocesses get an allow-listed env, and the binary bootstrap is pinned to a SHA-256.
reads.worst: Depends on a separately built Rust binary (downloaded on a user-run setup step) and a large external project, so setup is heavy and the plugin's guarantees rest on code outside its folder.

plugins.name: clearance
plugins.author: yuzuru99
plugins.does: Enforces per-sender tool tiers, turn rate limits, and audit records for Hermes gateway users.

reads.best: Code-level, deny-by-default hooks use gateway sender identity, and an integration test exercises real tool dispatch.
reads.worst: Its security depends on Hermes propagating sender identity to every execution path; detached workers are treated as local sessions.

plugins.name: ghostrun
plugins.author: kdcyberdude
plugins.does: Builds a GPU-assisted pipeline for observing NES games, training a player, isolating a reference oracle, and validating editable recreations.

reads.best: It is an unusually complete plugin runtime with durable stages, reference/builder isolation, a black-box oracle, a CUDA training pipeline, and extensive adversarial tests.
reads.worst: It is an early-preview workflow for a very narrow audience that requires a user-supplied ROM, Linux, NVIDIA CUDA, and substantial local setup.

plugins.name: oathkeeper
plugins.author: Whydiriki700
plugins.does: Enforces owner-authored filesystem invariants and prerequisites at tool-call boundaries while logging and fingerprinting protected paths.

reads.best: It turns persistent owner constraints into deterministic hooks that can block unsafe actions instead of merely reminding the model.
reads.worst: Its bounded shell-command parser cannot understand inline scripts or every indirect mutation, leaving documented enforcement gaps.

plugins.name: parallax
plugins.author: kruschdev
plugins.does: Compares model framings and context-blinded code, records audits, and exports filtered DPO or SFT datasets through tools and a dashboard.

reads.best: It combines auxiliary-model calls, deterministic code analysis, durable audit data, dataset export, and a finished dashboard into a novel evaluation instrument.
reads.worst: The core framing and training-data workflow is specialized, and much of its confidence rests on one large test module and complex heuristics.

plugins.name: kindle-scribe
plugins.author: lEWFkRAD
plugins.does: Registers Kindle Scribe as a Hermes gateway platform so handwritten notebook messages reach the agent and replies return to the page.

reads.best: It puts Hermes on distinctive personal hardware through a real platform adapter with loopback-only binding, scoped secrets, bounded requests, and extensive integration tests.
reads.worst: It is useful only with a Kindle Scribe and a separately installed companion diary bridge, making onboarding more involved than the plugin alone suggests.

plugins.name: dirtside
plugins.author: the-ai-entrepreneur-ai-hub
plugins.does: Terminal backend that keeps Hermes's brain on the server while running terminal commands on a paired device chosen per conversation.

reads.best: Signed, key-pinned device pairing with policy caps, approvals kept, ~70 test files, CI and a Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Large, complex codebase (~13k lines) and remote shell execution increase setup and security surface.

reads.best: Its signed device protocol and terminal-environment-provider integration address a meaningful own-hardware agent use case.
reads.worst: At the pinned revision it has neither plugin manifest nor README nor tests, so the catalog entry is not a dependable installable product.

plugins.name: stock-runway
plugins.author: usegreymatter
plugins.does: Forecasts inventory run-out from recent sales, receipts, CSV or read-only Odoo data, with a chat tool, slash command and a native Desktop chart and quick view.

reads.best: It turns useful, appropriately qualified inventory forecasts into a polished multi-surface product with ERP-aware imports, a built-in sample and an interactive Desktop interface.
reads.worst: Forecast quality remains limited by sparse sales history and is explicitly a small historical check rather than a purchasing guarantee; Odoo behavior is tested against fakes rather than live servers.

reads.best: A finished inventory workflow with ERP column normalization, bounded arithmetic, detailed UI and read-only, secret-scoped Odoo access.
reads.worst: engine.py grades a three-month-average backtest even when the forecast uses seasonal factors, so the displayed grade does not validate that seasonal model.

plugins.name: multiverse
plugins.author: vdimarco
plugins.does: Runs alternative coding attempts in git worktrees, ranks them using common checks, and applies a chosen patch.

reads.best: Real subagent hooks, optional per-attempt models, terminal-dispatched checks and a Desktop race board make best-of-N coding operational.
reads.worst: Worktree pinning is textual path rewriting rather than containment: relative parent paths and shell navigation can escape it, and MCP writes are not rewritten.

plugins.name: openchi
plugins.author: imkieransmith
plugins.does: Offers illustrated stretching and breathing sessions in Hermes Desktop during long tasks, with local message-tension detection and user-controlled timers.

reads.best: Its carefully tested Desktop experience waits for a user click, handles cooldowns and sleep recovery, and keeps message text out of storage and network requests.
reads.worst: Its usefulness is concentrated in Desktop wellness breaks, with no additional capability for executing the agent's tasks.

plugins.name: archytan-lite
plugins.author: Hypgnosis
plugins.does: Gates Hermes tool calls through an external authorization service and redeems single-use capabilities before allowing execution [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/High-ArchyTech-Solutions/hermes-archytan-lite/38748165b089f776acf9d6119eaeafdb76eed83e/archytan-lite/gate.py).

reads.best: All checks must authorize before any capability is redeemed, and missing configuration, missing capabilities or failed redemption refuse execution [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/High-ArchyTech-Solutions/hermes-archytan-lite/38748165b089f776acf9d6119eaeafdb76eed83e/archytan-lite/gate.py).
reads.worst: The shell policy reduces executable paths to basenames, so a workspace executable named ls receives the same program identity as system ls, weakening executable restrictions [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/High-ArchyTech-Solutions/hermes-archytan-lite/38748165b089f776acf9d6119eaeafdb76eed83e/archytan-lite/shell.py).

plugins.name: hermes-detox
plugins.author: kellycryptos
plugins.does: Replaces large tool and terminal outputs with compact reports backed by locally stored evidence and retrieval tools [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kellycryptos/hermes-detox/6efe12bea00546d0e200c67c7afec5e1ac056ce7/__init__.py).

reads.best: It redacts output before persistence, skips its own retrieval tools, and preserves the original result when storage, extraction or compression fails [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kellycryptos/hermes-detox/6efe12bea00546d0e200c67c7afec5e1ac056ce7/__init__.py).
reads.worst: Neither transformation hook applies max_report_chars, so reports that satisfy the ratio gate can still exceed the advertised absolute character budget [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kellycryptos/hermes-detox/6efe12bea00546d0e200c67c7afec5e1ac056ce7/__init__.py).

plugins.name: freshness-sidecar
plugins.author: neweraXX
plugins.does: Binds notes to workspace file hashes and warns before each turn when their sources changed or disappeared.
