reads.best: Bounded, symlink-resistant hashing and superseding context snapshots address stale recall while leaving the existing memory provider available.
reads.worst: Tracks only explicitly registered small files, and unchanged bytes cannot establish that a saved fact was true in the first place.

plugins.name: hermis
plugins.author: gabogabucho
plugins.does: Adds a Windows Electron overlay with voice-oriented Autopilot mode, floating data and artifact surfaces, application launching and real window arrangement.

reads.best: The overlay, authenticated loopback bridge, local camera gestures and Win32 window controls form a distinctive new interface for Hermes.
reads.worst: Windows-only single-monitor support and a detached npm/Electron startup lifecycle leave substantial setup and process-recovery limits despite mocked bootstrap tests.

plugins.name: glance
plugins.author: Chinteyley
plugins.does: Captures and compares simulator screenshots around UI edits, nudges Hermes to check failures and displays before/after results.

reads.best: Bounded capture, persistent verification state and image fixtures support a useful feedback loop with an integrated Desktop comparison view.
reads.worst: The automatic baseline only watches write_file and patch on selected extensions, so terminal edits and UI changes in .ts or .js files escape it.

plugins.name: computer-view
plugins.author: bhoot1234567890
plugins.does: Provides an authenticated mobile desktop viewer with Telegram entry and coordinated human takeover, handback and fresh-observation enforcement.

reads.best: Real RFB input filtering and cross-process control fencing prevent supported agent actions during human control and require a fresh screenshot after handback.
reads.worst: Setup requires a dedicated Linux Xvnc desktop, private sockets, externally managed HTTPS and explicit in-process plugins; shell and direct desktop clients remain outside its cooperative fence.

plugins.name: emporia
plugins.author: wujitsana
plugins.does: Connects Hermes agents to a relay network for signed social interaction, games, collaborative labs and bounded agent payments.

reads.best: A gateway adapter, autonomous-turn tool restrictions, turn caps and integrated dashboard create a substantial new environment for Hermes agents.
reads.worst: Despite scoped secrets in the plugin, its required runtime supports direct private-key file reads and vendor-CLI key retrieval outside Hermes’s credential routes, conflicting with catalog rule 11.

plugins.name: hermes-gameshelf
plugins.author: KeyArgo
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop game center with local rule engines, human or agent seats, tutorials and opt-in online play. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KeyArgo/hermes-game-center/9359ba470168b527337a0677c1f911cc8c161129/README.md)

reads.best: Human-consent gates, legal-move checks and bounded model calls make agent opponents usable across a substantial game library. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KeyArgo/hermes-game-center/9359ba470168b527337a0677c1f911cc8c161129/README.md)
reads.worst: The Champions page is a placeholder and the bot ladder is hidden because rated bot-versus-bot play is not proven end to end. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KeyArgo/hermes-game-center/9359ba470168b527337a0677c1f911cc8c161129/README.md)

plugins.name: folio
plugins.author: okyssta
plugins.does: Indexes local documents for passage search, quotation verification, revision diffs and page-linked Desktop reading. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okyssta/hermes-folio/b101110c32b47b7c427204dfce19710d7f400c75/README.md)

reads.best: Local evidence tools combine source locators, content-hashed revisions and visible PDF highlights without requiring a hosted search service. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okyssta/hermes-folio/b101110c32b47b7c427204dfce19710d7f400c75/README.md)
reads.worst: Incremental folder scans skip files solely on unchanged modification time, so changed content with preserved timestamps can leave stale evidence until a forced scan. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okyssta/hermes-folio/b101110c32b47b7c427204dfce19710d7f400c75/indexer.py)

plugins.name: 1guy
plugins.author: jrezmo
plugins.does: Turns Hermes sessions, scheduled jobs and tasks into a Desktop work board with per-card conversation threads. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrezmo/1guy-plugin/2bb6728048388a419829af5ab8228f3bb977f03f/README.md)

reads.best: It reorganizes the user's existing Hermes work into actionable cards and resumes each card's own session through the Desktop SDK. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrezmo/1guy-plugin/2bb6728048388a419829af5ab8228f3bb977f03f/README.md)
reads.worst: The backend loads vendored modules under generic global names and explicitly fails if another board module is already loaded, making plugin coexistence fragile. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrezmo/1guy-plugin/2bb6728048388a419829af5ab8228f3bb977f03f/og_core/board.py)

plugins.name: idea-board
plugins.author: bmanturner
plugins.does: Mines the user’s chats and available Hermes capabilities into an evidence-backed Desktop board of suggested tasks and connectors, learning from dismissals.

reads.best: Capability-aware validation, durable dismissal rules and a careful Desktop setup turn agent suggestions into a usable personal workflow without automatically sending them.
reads.worst: A run can consume 70–80k tokens as disclosed, and capability discovery and duplicate checks depend partly on undocumented Hermes imports with fallbacks.

plugins.name: delegation-receipts
plugins.author: dacheah
plugins.does: Requires subagent receipts and checks their file claims and verification commands, delivering adverse verdicts to the parent and keeping a local ledger.

reads.best: Checks use the child’s own tool history, decline unproven working directories and keep host command execution off by default.
reads.worst: It cannot veto completion, file attribution remains heuristic, and proving test success requires opting into unsandboxed host execution of the child’s cited check.

plugins.name: multi-telegram
plugins.author: sergio-dev1-py
plugins.does: Runs multiple Telegram bot identities through one Hermes profile with per-bot authorization, shared or isolated transcripts, and reply routing.

reads.best: Implements a genuine gateway platform with profile-scoped token access, explicit transport routing, per-bot authorization, bounded startup, and tests for concurrent replies and session sharing.
reads.worst: Isolated transcripts still share profile memory and tools, and the validation report leaves live unauthorized-user, group, concurrency, and media checks pending.

plugins.name: ichor
plugins.author: mystiquemide
plugins.does: Captures user corrections, retries and undos as scrubbed preference pairs, with review cards, TRL/Atropos export and optional Hugging Face sharing.

reads.best: Turns ordinary agent corrections into user-reviewed training data through lifecycle hooks, local scrubbing and usable export formats without automatically retraining a model.
reads.worst: The live _windows.open call omits session_key, so replies.py permits another direct chat on the same platform to settle the sole open card; its chat-isolation tests supply a key the live path never supplies.

plugins.name: shared-memory-domains
plugins.author: DrFreeman001
plugins.does: Shares local SQLite memory across Hermes profiles with per-domain grants, human-verified facts, automatic recall and sticky revocation.

reads.best: Default-deny identity checks and transactional grants, verification and revocation are backed by adversarial and concurrency tests.
reads.worst: Access control is cooperative within one installation: shell-capable agents can bypass the path trip-wire, and revocation cannot retract facts already copied into conversation or external memory.

plugins.name: its-in-your-head
plugins.author: hi4c0ck
plugins.does: Observes Hermes work signals locally, visualizes activity and a six-axis portrait, and optionally adds bounded tool-selection guidance to later turns.

reads.best: Local persistence, interactive Desktop views and tested privacy/fallback paths make this a substantive agent extension.
reads.worst: Default perception uses character-ngram sketches and deterministic rules, so the portrait and advice remain heuristic rather than validated measures of better agent performance.

plugins.name: mdvault
plugins.author: kailashrajh
plugins.does: Uses a local Markdown vault as an automatic memory provider with multilingual lexical retrieval, note tools and built-in-memory mirroring.

reads.best: Automatic pre-turn recall and CJK-aware tokenization improve the agent itself while keeping notes local and human-readable.
reads.worst: Retrieval is lexical rather than semantic and bounded to Markdown, and indexing still scans file metadata during ongoing use.

plugins.name: smart-model-swap
plugins.author: CarmaOS-Dev
plugins.does: Manages local llama.cpp model processes so Hermes can swap models, release GPU memory, restore its primary model and edit launch settings in Desktop or dashboard.

reads.best: Real process management, request draining, measured per-GPU budgets and fallback loading improve what a user’s own local-model Hermes can do.
reads.worst: There are no shipped tests at this pin for the complex process, swap and GPU state machine, and managed operation is limited to llama.cpp on Linux or WSL NVIDIA setups.

plugins.name: ninsei
plugins.author: JustinPerea
plugins.does: Adds Nostr-backed social rooms, agent party games, reviewed shared web toys and a separate private Hermes messaging platform.

reads.best: A substantial platform and polished social UI enforce model budgets in code and separate tool-free room agents from the owner’s full Hermes agent.
reads.worst: Nostr signing secrets are generated and read from the plugin’s own unencrypted SQLite identity record instead of Hermes’s secret store, and shared toys retain disclosed network-isolation gaps.

plugins.name: signal-dog
plugins.author: scottleimroth
plugins.does: Listens for household knocks and beeps through a microphone and delivers alerts, ongoing-alarm updates and recent-event history into Hermes chat.

reads.best: An opt-in, local audio detector and resilient chat delivery make Hermes useful as an accessibility aid without sending or retaining microphone audio.
reads.worst: The disclosed measurements show substantial false knock alerts and missed sound patterns, while the history tool exposes household activity to anyone who can message the agent.

plugins.name: dynmem
plugins.author: ockentap
plugins.does: Enforces a keyword-to-Markdown memory index and audits model-reported retrieval through hooks and output transforms.

reads.best: Enforces memory-format and header integrity in both tool hooks and memory middleware, with tests for stock-store and batch-operation edge cases.
reads.worst: Installation also needs a separately copied skill and manual memory restructuring; retrieval remains model-dependent and the index grows with topic count.

plugins.name: doubt
plugins.author: PinnacleCryptNG
plugins.does: Uses token log probabilities to display uncertainty and request approval for uncertain re-derived tool arguments.

reads.best: Middleware exposes provider-level signals a skill cannot access, with heat maps and native human approval rather than automatic execution.
reads.worst: Requires non-streaming compatible providers, adds a model request per guarded call, and lets calls through when scoring fails or re-derivations disagree too much.

plugins.name: vibe-relay
plugins.author: trenthalden
plugins.does: Routes coding delegation by quota, checks changed paths and test receipts, and parks work for a scheduled resume after reset.

reads.best: A real delegation provider combines quota-aware routing, native cron continuation and regression tests for child environments and path confinement.
reads.worst: Acceptance hashes untracked filenames without their contents and accepts PASS-like terminal output without checking it matches the required gate command, weakening its central freshness guarantee.

plugins.name: coldstart
plugins.author: zvporter-ops
plugins.does: Retrieves tiered document evidence and uses Hermes input and held-output hooks to flag or withhold unsupported quotations, figures, and identifiers. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zvporter-ops/coldstart/2f8d036e070f7a4bc593ab9fa5b60dcdd820cab3/README.md)

reads.best: The output-transform hook can prevent unchecked text from streaming, and the implementation distinguishes internal from public evidence with locality checks on model access. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zvporter-ops/coldstart/2f8d036e070f7a4bc593ab9fa5b60dcdd820cab3/__init__.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zvporter-ops/coldstart/2f8d036e070f7a4bc593ab9fa5b60dcdd820cab3/README.md)
reads.worst: Strict mode still allows unsupported prose when it lacks a checked quote, figure, date, URL, or identifier, so the opening promise that every answer is grounded or refused is broader than the mechanical gate. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zvporter-ops/coldstart/2f8d036e070f7a4bc593ab9fa5b60dcdd820cab3/__init__.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zvporter-ops/coldstart/2f8d036e070f7a4bc593ab9fa5b60dcdd820cab3/README.md)

plugins.name: pixel-hq
plugins.author: W4-NERF
plugins.does: Desktop page that shows a fleet of Hermes profiles as a pixel-art office with XP/HP from a review ledger, live session activity, Kanban blocked-card triage with confirmed actions and a GPU/vLLM reactor panel, plus a pixelhq_review tool.

reads.best: Highly polished and creative: demo GIF and video, four screenshots, about 200 tests, and writes limited to confirmed Kanban actions and reviews.
reads.worst: Its value needs a multi-profile fleet, a Kanban practice and a quality ledger most users do not have; for a single agent it is mostly decoration.

plugins.name: hermes-ride
plugins.author: martyllmaccs-hash
plugins.does: A new Hermes gateway platform: a phone web app mounted on a motorcycle streams voice (ElevenLabs Scribe or offline on-host STT) plus GPS and motion to the agent and speaks replies back.

reads.best: Genuinely new: a register_platform adapter that puts Hermes on a moving vehicle, with keys read through get_scoped_secret, constant-time access-key checks with lockout, and about 170 tests.
reads.worst: Heavy, partly unverified setup: the README admits the locked-phone and Ride Summary paths are untested, the wake word needs a local Emscripten build, the README's ride_character tool is not registered, and the STT helper inherits the full environment.

plugins.name: brainvault
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: A Hermes memory provider that remembers locally and syncs cards minted by the user (via their own Wave wallet) on Theta, decrypting private cards with a paired decrypt-only agent key, with a Desktop/dashboard page.

reads.best: It replaces Hermes's memory provider with portable memory the owner controls; the plugin never signs or mints, chain reads are keccak-checked, recalled text is labelled as data, and secrets are refused at capture.
reads.worst: It is tied to one vendor's wallet and chain, the agent key falls back to a 0600 file instead of Hermes's secret store when keyring is absent, install is a manual git clone and copy, and there are only 38 tests.

plugins.name: habit
plugins.author: scottleimroth
plugins.does: Watches Hermes's command-approval prompts, learns which commands you always approve, proposes a narrow command_allowlist pattern, and writes it only after /habit accept.

reads.best: It improves Hermes's own approval system safely: 49 tests cover over-broad globs against Hermes's matching logic, an owner lock on gateways, and the rule that nothing is written without /habit accept.
reads.worst: README:61 promises it never proposes `docker kill`, but that is only excluded from glob forms; never_auto.py builds its strings 'from parts' so the security scanner skips the file; and config writes are not atomic.

plugins.name: sabbath
plugins.author: ponzgpt
plugins.does: Gives Hermes a weekly day of rest: it messages goodnight, pauses its cron jobs (exempting the ones you list), steers every turn away from work through pre_llm_call, keeps a basket of set-aside tasks, and sends a digest at the end.

reads.best: A fresh, well-made idea that uses Hermes's own cron, hooks, gateway and Desktop, resumes only the jobs it paused itself, and discloses every risky behaviour.
reads.worst: Few users will want it; it imports fcntl, so it is Unix-only; it shells out to `hermes send`; and it has only 13 tests.

plugins.name: sql-dryrun
plugins.author: aoyamari
plugins.does: A pre_tool_call hook that counts the rows a DELETE/UPDATE/DROP/TRUNCATE would touch, read-only, and asks for approval above a threshold.

reads.best: It catches whole-table writes (WHERE 1=1, no WHERE) that Hermes's shape-based detector lets run, with a concrete comparison table.
reads.worst: Only helps users whose agent runs SQL through the shell; it needs to parse each client's commands.

plugins.name: safe-swap
plugins.author: itsolaph
plugins.does: pre_tool_call hook that rewrites destructive shell/git commands into reversible twins (quarantine, force-with-lease, snapshots) with receipts and /unswap.

reads.best: Rewrites the command itself rather than blocking, tells the agent what really ran, and is backed by 13 test files.
reads.worst: Shell-string rewriting can miss variants, which it admits by telling the agent when a command was not swapped.

plugins.name: precog
plugins.author: 0xNomind
plugins.does: Learns failed-terminal-command to fixing-command pairs and rewrites or briefs future commands across sessions.

reads.best: Measured live session shows 8 tool calls dropping to 1, with a dashboard tab and Desktop plugin.
reads.worst: Silently rewriting commands from learned lessons can misapply a fix in a different context; only four test files.

plugins.name: pocketbook
plugins.author: MaanavD
plugins.does: Personal finance in Hermes: Plaid sync, budgets, net worth, alerts, CSV imports and a Finance tab for Desktop and dashboard.

reads.best: Product-grade finance tab with screenshots, and Plaid tokens kept in Hermes's secret store.
reads.worst: Requires the user's own Plaid developer keys, a real setup hurdle; a familiar budgeting-app idea.

plugins.name: secret-vault
plugins.author: jimmy77733
plugins.does: Replaces secrets in gateway chat with {{SECRET:name}} placeholders, substitutes them at tool time and redacts them from outputs and replies.

reads.best: Uses hooks that rewrite messages, tool arguments and results, which a skill cannot do, and its README honestly lists coverage gaps.
reads.worst: Does not cover CLI/TUI/Desktop input, uses its own vault rather than Hermes's secret store, and on non-Windows falls back to a dev-only key file.

plugins.name: dxmt
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Memory provider backed by a DXMT server with hybrid recall, fact extraction at session end and compression, and supersede/forget tools.

reads.best: A real MemoryProvider that reads its key via the secret scope, with offline and live tests and a shared store across agents.
reads.worst: Requires the user to run a separate DXMT server and embedding model, which limits day-one adoption.

plugins.name: clearing
plugins.author: Dgardenhire
plugins.does: The Clearing: a Desktop writing editor in which the user's own Hermes model returns notes anchored to exact quotes, the writer accepts each by click, and a built-in check and WordNet thesaurus work without a model.

reads.best: Product-grade Desktop page with readable source in desktop/src, redaction forced before model calls, no keys, about 216 Python and 110 JS tests, and many screenshots.
reads.worst: Niche audience (prose writers); the 670KB built bundle includes a UI kit not in the repo, it is tested on macOS only, and STATUS.md is partly stale.

plugins.name: timeline-replay
plugins.author: firetussin
plugins.does: Records metadata-only Hermes activity via hooks and renders animated HTML/MP4 replays across profiles, with a Desktop/dashboard view.

reads.best: Highly polished with screenshots, ten visual styles, a dashboard and metadata-only capture.
reads.worst: Mostly eye candy; usefulness beyond show-and-tell is modest.

plugins.name: aura
plugins.author: KeyArgo
plugins.does: Docks a film/YouTube theatre pane in Hermes Desktop and drives a MilkDrop-style visualiser from system loopback audio with agent-mood hooks.

reads.best: Unusually finished Desktop experience with ~370 tests and local-only audio analysis.
reads.worst: Mostly ambience, not agent capability; Linux-first, large 29k-line codebase.

plugins.name: household-tiers
plugins.author: chevlume
plugins.does: Per-person owner/user/guest tool tiers for a shared gateway bot, with family curfew, parent alert and owner memory withheld from others.

reads.best: Adds real per-user permissions to Hermes gateway via dispatch hooks and llm_request middleware.
reads.worst: Config is a hand-edited JSON file and catalog install does not resolve yet.

plugins.name: melange
plugins.author: lEWFkRAD
plugins.does: Records terminal sessions as hash-chained timelines and lets Hermes scrub, explain provenance, fork what-ifs, clamp inputs, recompute dependents, and preserve original recordings.

reads.best: The local, append-only replay/what-if engine gives Hermes provenance and counterfactual computation over real terminal work, with a substantial demo and product-quality surfaces.
reads.worst: It is a very large and ambitious codebase with PTY execution and many moving parts, so the integration and fidelity failure surface is high even with bundled tests.

reads.best: Character provenance and forward-checked counterfactual edits are an unusual, locally implemented debugging direction.
reads.worst: The bundled bridge rebuilds computations through the tax flagship or coding demo; a generic recorded shell command does not become a recomputable What-if, and a fork only records intent.

plugins.name: injection-shield
plugins.author: MOTHR
plugins.does: Tags untrusted tool output and uses hooks to audit or enforce against prompt injection, dangerous tool calls, and leaked credentials.

reads.best: It covers multiple actual hook points, ships a Desktop control surface, and has broad detector, integration, and privacy/retention tests.
reads.worst: Its regex- and injected-firewall-based detection cannot reliably decide all prompt-injection cases and enforcement can create false positives.

plugins.name: trade-preflight
plugins.author: Mohamedhazeem
plugins.does: A pre_tool_call/post_tool_call policy firewall that normalizes two simulated ('paper') equity order tools into a canonical form and blocks any order that violates an operator-edited JSON policy, logging an audit trail to local SQLite.

reads.best: By design it needs no broker account, API key, or network access at all, and is fail-closed and deterministic, with an ADR, architecture docs and ~780 lines of edge-case tests.
reads.worst: Because it only simulates paper trades against two mock adapters, it never actually touches a real brokerage, so its real-world usefulness is mostly as a policy-firewall pattern/demo rather than a deployable trading safeguard.

plugins.name: omp-sessions
plugins.author: mbaradad
plugins.does: Delegates coding tasks to local omp sessions with queues, scheduling, kanban integration, notifications and a Desktop/dashboard supervision page.

reads.best: Approval-aware delegation, persistent card/session links and extensive integration tests make it a substantive extension of Hermes workflows.
reads.worst: Requires separately installed omp and omp-sessions runtimes and relies on undocumented Hermes kanban internals, making setup and compatibility more fragile.

reads.best: Deep integration ties persistent external coding sessions to Hermes chats and kanban cards, with readable code, extensive tests and a finished supervision UI.
reads.worst: At the pinned commit, Tools.start passes the model-selected mode directly to omp.new, including auto, without the agent_approvals guard used by Tools.mode; external omp setup is also required.

plugins.name: hermes-parallel
plugins.author: kOs-tile
plugins.does: Creates three isolated file futures, verifies and previews their diffs, and permits only an explicit human slash command to apply one.

reads.best: The bounded operations, hash rechecks, fail-closed proof gate, and human-only apply path make multi-outcome agent editing concrete and inspectable.
reads.worst: Its filesystem isolation is not an OS security boundary, and model-backed planning is unverified unless the operator opts in.

reads.best: Checks source and candidate hashes, serializes mutations, and tests fail-closed recovery while reserving apply and rollback for slash commands.
reads.worst: The README manual install omits proof.py and worktree_review.py used by registered features; planning is sequential and constrained to move/write operations, not parallel agents.

plugins.name: hermes-watchdog
plugins.author: 33hodl
plugins.does: Watches Hermes's own cron incidents, matches them against a JSON playbook, and runs a bounded rerun/pause/check repair cycle, verifying success only against Hermes's own incident records.

reads.best: A runnable proof script reproduces the README's example output end-to-end, and the README candidly discloses an upstream Hermes gap it has to work around.
reads.worst: Value only materializes for users who already run cron jobs through Hermes, a narrower audience than a general-purpose plugin.

reads.best: Repairs are checked against actual cron incident or execution state and exposed through tools and a Desktop health view.
reads.worst: The agent can save arbitrary check-command argv through watchdog_runbooks and run it directly via repair, with no plugin-side human approval; calling these user-authored checks understates that reach.

plugins.name: hermes-crux
plugins.author: tony-simons-aiowa
plugins.does: Builds decision models and finds the exact assumption thresholds and constraint conflicts that change the best option, with a Desktop atlas.

reads.best: Exact analytic thresholds and a minimal conflict set, with a polished Desktop atlas, screenshots and tests.
reads.worst: Users must define formal decision models, so day-one appeal is narrow.

plugins.name: neuron-steer
plugins.author: mrfentmen
plugins.does: Finds contrastive sparse MLP-neuron circuits in a local model, stores them, and scales or ablates them during generation with dose scans.

reads.best: It exposes a genuinely novel model-level capability based on forward-pass neuron attribution, with lazy loading, download gates, and substantial unit tests.
reads.worst: The audience is limited to users with compatible local Transformer models and substantial compute, and the large dependency/runtime path remains harder to operate than ordinary plugins.

plugins.name: briq
plugins.author: goums
plugins.does: Terminal backend that runs Hermes's terminal, file and code tools in a briq cloud microVM sandbox.

reads.best: Changes where Hermes runs via a backend provider, with tests, CI and the key declared as a secret env var.
reads.worst: Depends on a paid third-party service; the plugin is mostly a client for it.

plugins.name: scope-recall
plugins.does: Memory provider giving Hermes local, source-backed long-term memory with history-preserving revisions shared across agents.

reads.best: Plugs in as Hermes's memory provider, with recall-with-sources and versioned corrections.
reads.worst: The catalog folder is an 18-line shim; the real code comes from a pip package outside the pinned folder.

plugins.name: hyperliquid-desk
plugins.author: KevinM0001
plugins.does: A read-only Hyperliquid market dashboard tab, collector and twelve agent tools (market, flow, wallets, candles, node book and stops) with a commentary skill, on Hyperliquid's public data and an optional node relay.

reads.best: A large, finished dashboard with screenshots, about 13,000 lines of tests with recorded fixtures, no order or signing code, and its one optional key read only through Hermes's secret scope.
reads.worst: Node panels call the author's hosted relay (relay.perpdepth.com) by default, a third-party network call that is on unless the user turns it off, and the audience is a trading niche.

plugins.name: charrette
plugins.author: GuideboardLabs
plugins.does: A shared whiteboard pane beside the chat where the user draws and the agent reads, points at, annotates and asks about the user's own strokes through eleven board tools, with replay and headless PNG rendering.

reads.best: A fresh human-ink-first contract: the agent can annotate and point at the user's own marks through vision-grounded tools but can never edit them, and each object keeps its provenance and can be replayed.
reads.worst: Setup needs three separate switches, the repo carries an archive of old engine versions, and it runs a local token-guarded web server that can be exposed past loopback.

plugins.name: look-at-this
plugins.author: Elshayib
plugins.does: A hotkey, /look or composer menu captures the window you were just in (screenshot, accessibility tree, URL, selection, title) as one redactable packet attached to your next turn and discarded after 300 seconds.

reads.best: User-initiated, consent-first desktop context capture on Windows, macOS and Linux with a fail-closed password-manager exclude list, secret redaction, a companion token via the secret route, and 61 tests.
reads.worst: Depends on the cua-driver binary and OS accessibility grants, with an 1,800-line core module and a separate companion process that make setup and review harder.

plugins.name: hermes-shortcuts
plugins.author: mjneuroart
plugins.does: Lets the agent write Cherri source for Apple Shortcuts, compile it in a network-less bubblewrap sandbox, sign it via RoutineHub on explicit consent, deliver it to the phone, and audit any .shortcut or iCloud link before install.

reads.best: Opens the iPhone's Shortcuts surface to Hermes from Linux with no Mac, verifying compiled output, decoding LZFSE/AEA in pure Python and refusing builds without a sandbox.
reads.worst: Linux-only, needs an external Cherri compiler, and signing uploads the shortcut to a third-party service (RoutineHub), so it rests on tools it does not control.

plugins.name: permission-tiers
plugins.author: imperator-clawdius
plugins.does: Enforces allow, ask, and block rules on Hermes tool calls and records a local SQLite audit ledger through pre/post tool hooks.

reads.best: It converts per-tool safety policy into host-enforced behavior that prompts cannot reliably guarantee, while retaining an audit trail.
reads.worst: The small package has no Desktop surface and its fail-open hook-error behavior weakens the safety promise in damaged configurations.

plugins.name: storage-utility
plugins.author: ShawnCRMer
plugins.does: Tune-up: a Desktop/dashboard panel that shows what Hermes stores, does review-first cleanup with a restorable Trash, checks service health and stops leftover processes.

reads.best: Finished like a product: many screenshots, a large Desktop and dashboard UI, and a safety design where nothing is deleted without a frozen, re-checked review list and a 30-day Trash.
reads.worst: About 9,000 lines of code that deletes files, prunes sessions and stops processes, and not one test is in the repository.

plugins.name: weft
plugins.author: celador
plugins.does: Edit-time coordination for coding agents: hooks report every edit to a Weft gateway and put other agents' conflicting changes into the agent's tool results, with an enforce mode that blocks stale edits, two tools, /weft and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: A genuinely new idea for multi-agent coding, built on pre/post tool-call and transform hooks, with the token read only through get_secret, a trusted-gateway rule so a cloned repo cannot redirect edits, and a large test suite.
reads.worst: Setup is long (npx gateway, paste a token, set an agent id, open both sessions first), it serves only people running several coding agents on one repo, and the hosted option sends edit diffs off the machine.

plugins.name: patch-sentinel
plugins.author: thebangarang
plugins.does: Audits Linux patch posture, running kernels, package integrity, containers and language dependencies, then prepares plans and gated upgrades.

reads.best: Evidence-based clean/finding/unknown states, broad fixture tests and an integrated Desktop pane turn a host audit into an actionable workflow.
reads.worst: Coverage remains uneven across Linux families, excludes image-layer CVEs, and offers no macOS or Windows support.

plugins.name: blind-accessibility-reader
plugins.author: ella0333
plugins.does: Uses a Chrome extension and Hermes vision calls to describe images and narrate videos through screen readers or speech. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ella0333/hermes-blind-accessibility-reader/04891de3962644b0666c29b5b85b981645762432/README.md)

reads.best: Scene-change detection and recent-narration chat context turn browser media into an ongoing accessibility workflow. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ella0333/hermes-blind-accessibility-reader/04891de3962644b0666c29b5b85b981645762432/service.py)
reads.worst: The service checks estimated spending before a call and records usage afterward without reserving in-flight costs, so concurrent descriptions can overshoot the advertised ceiling. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ella0333/hermes-blind-accessibility-reader/04891de3962644b0666c29b5b85b981645762432/service.py)

plugins.name: tiled-sessions
plugins.author: strnadchristopher
plugins.does: Adds keyboard-controlled session tiling, multiple layouts and saved workspaces to Hermes Desktop.

reads.best: A substantial pure layout engine, geometry tests, configurable shortcuts and illustrated UI make multi-session work much easier.
reads.worst: Its defining tiling features depend on the proposed upstream session-layout SDK; without that seam it falls back to ordinary tabs, with no manifest release floor.

plugins.name: ballast
plugins.author: 1momoh
plugins.does: Plans and performs human-approved cleanup of macOS developer and AI caches using estimated regeneration regret, signed plans and a durable ledger.

reads.best: Closed cache roots, snapshot revalidation, fresh approval receipts, Desktop planning and extensive safety tests make destructive cleanup unusually deliberate.
reads.worst: macOS-only cleanup remains irreversible and nontransactional; regeneration costs are estimates and concurrent cache activity can interrupt execution.

plugins.name: signal-atlas
plugins.author: RahmelJackson
plugins.does: Builds source-linked visual investigations in Hermes Desktop, with a persistent evidence ledger, feed ingestion, charts, claim dossiers and saved follow-up answers.

reads.best: A shared revisioned evidence store and interactive Desktop workspace preserve citations and follow-up research beyond a chat response.
reads.worst: Claim extraction and verification depend on heuristics or the host model; direct ingestion accepts only bounded uncompressed RSS/Atom feeds, and social connectors remain future work.

plugins.name: ghost-run
plugins.author: tnvolman
plugins.does: Redirects selected Hermes file and terminal operations into a project copy for diff review, optional verification and selective human apply.

reads.best: Lifecycle middleware makes reversible coding tangible, with multi-file patch remapping, token-protected local review, selective apply and security regression tests.
reads.worst: A copied working directory and command denylist do not confine terminal code: paths outside the project remain executable and arbitrary scripts can reach the network, undermining the README promise that real disk stays untouched.

plugins.name: memrack
plugins.author: Kesuek
plugins.does: Replaces Hermes’s single memory-provider slot with dockable backends, routed writes and merged searches over facts, wiki pages and session history.

reads.best: A real MemoryProvider implementation combines local SQLite retrieval, backend conformance checks, visible degradation and regression tests for prior data-loss bugs.
reads.worst: Automatic recall is absent because the built-in prefetch paths return empty strings; users depend on the agent choosing memrack_search, and installation remains marked experimental.

plugins.name: hermes-spendguard
plugins.author: Blackleets
plugins.does: Tracks model-call costs in SQLite and enforces human-configured daily and monthly budgets through lifecycle hooks.

reads.best: Accounting and pre-inference blocking directly improve the agent, with read-only agent tools and budget controls exposed through a slash command.
reads.worst: Enforcement explicitly lets calls proceed on exceptions, and unpriced calls contribute no dollars to the cap despite the strong wallet-guard claims.

plugins.name: cooldown
plugins.author: Savage27z
plugins.does: Intercepts package-install terminal calls to block known malicious releases and request approval for fresh or unverifiable packages.

reads.best: Adds an automatic supply-chain checkpoint through Hermes’s approval hook with keyless registry lookups and offline policy tests.
reads.worst: Version ranges are checked as latest rather than resolved, and packages beyond the first twelve or unsupported install paths can pass unchecked without a notice when all checked findings are OK.

plugins.name: overhead
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Measures vegetation, burn and water changes from Sentinel-2 imagery and delivers comparison images, timelapses and interactive Desktop cards.

reads.best: A substantive geospatial engine computes pixel-based measurements with provenance, cloud handling and tests, then presents them through polished Hermes media surfaces.
reads.worst: Spectral thresholds can confuse seasonal change or land clearing with damage, and the image cache grows without automatic pruning.

plugins.name: redgreen
plugins.author: shahaman098
plugins.does: Rechecks fixes on current and pre-change Git trees and gates completion on a discriminating negative-control test.

reads.best: Automatic baseline capture, test overlay, tamper checks, and completion hooks directly improve coding-agent verification.
reads.worst: Test-runner recognition is an unanchored regex, and shell metacharacters trigger shell execution from tools or hooks without a separate approval gate.

plugins.name: deja-fix
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Fingerprints edited file versions and blocks one attempt to restore a version previously associated with a failed check.

reads.best: A small dependency-free lifecycle guard catches repeated failed code reached through different edit calls.
reads.worst: It only tracks write_file and patch, attributes a failed check to every dirty file, and lets the same failed version through on retry.

plugins.name: docs-drift
plugins.author: vigohan95
plugins.does: Checks documentation against code after Hermes edits and reports new mismatches with source lines in the same tool result.

reads.best: Deterministic session baselines, bounded hooks, hardened git children, and targeted regression tests make documentation checks automatic without another model call.
reads.worst: It checks syntactic names rather than meaning, misses unsupported documentation formats, and its own evidence reports poor precision for whole-repository scans.

plugins.name: rh-preflight
plugins.author: quotumorg
plugins.does: Checks public Robinhood Chain builder and ecosystem records before detected tool actions, applies user rules through Hermes approvals, and records local evidence cards.

reads.best: A real approval hook uses fresh check keys, blocks unattended execution by default and fails closed on check or ledger errors, with extensive capture-backed tests and Desktop history.
reads.worst: Detection covers only chain 4663 and recognized tool/argument patterns; its private Hermes approval-presence imports are a compatibility weakness and a requested catalog fix at this pin.

plugins.name: so101-arm
plugins.author: jamesEmerson112
plugins.does: Gives Hermes named robot-arm operations, simulated vision and rehearsal, plus fault detection and repair through a local SO-101 host.

reads.best: Simulation rehearsal and a deterministic watchdog produce a distinctive inspect-correct-repair loop with integration tests and visual demonstrations.
reads.worst: The real-arm driver is only mock-tested, and the freeze boundary can be bypassed by other same-user tools that access the host socket.

plugins.name: board-insights
plugins.author: kwpings
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop List and Dashboard for current Kanban work and historical flow, trends, run times, and assignee workload across local boards.

reads.best: A polished, screenshot-documented Desktop product turns Hermes's own Kanban data into useful live and historical views while opening every board database read-only.
reads.worst: It serves Hermes Kanban users only, has no agent tools or model interaction, and requires separately enabling both the plugin and Desktop page.

plugins.name: enterprise-pathfinder
plugins.author: DavidDiazMerino
plugins.does: Provides SAP source guidance, live document reading, OData contract inspection and claim tests, with evidence-gated SAP skill writes.

reads.best: It makes Hermes's own research and learned SAP skills more verifiable through parsers, a local evidence ledger, and a strict write gate, with substantial tests.
reads.worst: The first and only domain pack targets a specialized SAP audience, and the network reader can cache large remote documents locally.

plugins.name: command-reviewer
plugins.author: spideysri2802
plugins.does: Reviews shell and code execution calls using deterministic blocks, script-content inspection, model review, approvals, and hash-bound precedents.

reads.best: It adds a substantive defense layer to Hermes execution, including hard rules, review of actual script bytes, operator escalation, and extensive regression cases.
reads.worst: It depends on private terminal internals and external model judgment, increasing maintenance and privacy risks while script contents are sent to the configured model.

plugins.name: comemo
plugins.author: andausman
plugins.does: Replaces Hermes's single memory provider with parallel Honcho, Mem0, and Supermemory backends, merging reads and retrying failed writes.

reads.best: It changes Hermes's memory layer itself and adds multi-provider fan-out, deduplication, secret-scoped setup, and an offline retry queue.
reads.worst: It forwards conversations to multiple configured cloud services and the repository has only a small provider test suite for a complex asynchronous integration.

plugins.name: glasses-platform
plugins.author: 100yenadmin
plugins.does: Adds smart glasses as a Hermes gateway channel for voice turns, photos, streamed replies, and scheduled pushes.

reads.best: A real platform integration brings Hermes sessions, memory, approvals, photos, and later pushes to wearable devices, with extensive simulator and gateway tests.
reads.worst: A device token grants full agent access, the default listener binds all interfaces without TLS termination, and real glasses hardware remains untested.

plugins.name: pokeit
plugins.author: kbtbc
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to the hosted PokeIt MCP server for live Pokemon GO data and adds a Desktop Radar map, chip, catch/scan cards and a watch backed by a read-only local proxy.

reads.best: Product-grade Desktop UI with a screenshot, a hardened read-only proxy (fixed hosts, timeouts, size caps, CSP), about 60 tests and CI, and it needs no key.
reads.worst: Every agent tool lives on a remote server that is not in the repo and can change after install, so what the agent can do cannot be audited from the code, and the audience is a niche.

plugins.name: skillens
plugins.author: PhucNguyen-Dev
plugins.does: Watches tool calls against the numbered steps of loaded skills, shows a fidelity checklist pane in Desktop and nudges the agent about skipped steps.

reads.best: Novel, cheap (no LLM judge) check that the agent actually follows its skills, with Desktop pane and screenshots.
reads.worst: No tests found; heuristic step matching may miss or misjudge steps.

plugins.name: hermes-reliability
plugins.author: MadBonzz
plugins.does: Builds evidence-backed agent reliability campaigns from source snapshots and datasets, then reviews, executes, and freezes them for regression comparisons.

reads.best: A rich end-to-end testing workbench joins scenario generation, independent review, evidence audits, frozen benchmarks, Hermes memory references, and dashboard views.
reads.worst: The breadth creates a large compatibility and execution surface: generated evaluators can run on the host, parts of the target harness use private APIs, and full autonomous live campaigns remain unverified.

reads.best: Immutable benchmark provenance and validity-aware comparisons provide a serious regression workflow with native tools, background workers and a dashboard.
reads.worst: At the field pin evaluator preflight inherits the full environment and execution approval uses a global rule key; the documented complete autonomous live campaign also remains unverified.

plugins.name: canary-trap
plugins.author: Tarekkharsa
plugins.does: Injects a decoy credential into every turn's context and blocks/locks any tool call whose arguments leak that decoy (in plain, encoded, reversed or fragment form), acting as a prompt-injection tripwire.

reads.best: Compact, well-tested (11 parametrized disguise-detection cases plus concurrency and manifest-consistency tests), makes no network calls, and candidly lists what it does NOT catch in a 'Limits' section.
reads.worst: Only catches exfiltration that touches the planted decoy string; a leak that never references it passes through undetected, as the README itself admits.

plugins.name: homelab-watch
plugins.author: lpsmurf
plugins.does: Monitors homelab services and job heartbeats, tracks model costs and optionally routes delegated work to cheaper models.

reads.best: Read-only root-cause rollups and a shadow-first delegation provider improve both home operations and the agent itself.
reads.worst: DNS probes use blocking gethostbyname without the configured timeout, and judge failures can fall through to heuristic routing despite the README promising the normal route.

plugins.name: a11y-lens
plugins.author: Johnlocke0347
plugins.does: Runs axe-core in real Chromium, stores accessibility evidence and compares scans to verify repairs and identify regressions.

reads.best: A complete scan-repair-rescan loop pairs isolated browser execution and DNS pinning with evidence-aware comparison, self-tests and readable reports.
reads.worst: It audits one unauthenticated page at a time, and blocking other hosts can leave remote pages partially rendered; a clean automated scan does not establish accessibility conformance.

plugins.name: peripheral
plugins.author: okyssta
plugins.does: Gives Hermes searchable screen history through local capture, OCR, image recall and a timeline of agent actions.

reads.best: Capture, deduplication, time-aware recall and agent-event correlation provide useful memory of screens that have disappeared.
reads.worst: Redaction protects indexed text but not stored screenshots or image attachments, so secrets visible on screen can still reach the model despite the privacy wording.

plugins.name: myfolks
plugins.author: fresfrida
plugins.does: An encrypted store of facts about the people in your life, answered word for word by deterministic code in a gateway hook without calling the model, with Google contacts sync and a Desktop page.

reads.best: Deterministic, private recall that bypasses the model and transcript, with Hermes-managed OAuth, atomic encrypted writes and about 34 test files.
reads.worst: The AES key sits in a 0600 file next to the store unless keyring is installed, so a copy of the Hermes folder opens it (disclosed in the README).

reads.best: Reads secrets via agent.secret_scope.get_secret rather than files, encrypts storage at rest, and ships 34 test files plus a dedicated evidence pack of safety checks.
reads.worst: The underlying idea (a structured people/contacts memory store) is a fairly direct application of a known pattern rather than something new for agents.

plugins.name: hermes-gatekeeper
plugins.author: percyhendrux123-prog
plugins.does: A deterministic pre_tool_call gate that checks outbound message sends against suppression/STOP, consent, recipient quiet hours, double-texting and approved wording, escalating unparsed sends to owner approval.

reads.best: Rigorous fail-closed design (log, commit or classifier failure blocks the send) with hashed recipient storage, 0600 SQLite and 19 test files.
reads.worst: In practice it fully checks only literal 'hermes send' / 'imsg send' terminal calls, the README is dense with no screenshots, and the catalog entry sha is TBD.

plugins.name: hermes-hands
plugins.author: Ridwannurudeen
plugins.does: A terminal backend that runs Hermes's terminal and file tools on a paired Windows or Linux computer over a signed outbound relay, with a witness mode where the person at that computer consents and watches.

reads.best: Changes where Hermes runs, with the relay seed in Hermes's secret store, stripped from subprocesses, signed receipts and a real device+relay e2e test.
reads.worst: Heavy setup (pipx from git, HTTPS relay), relies on private Hermes internals, and witness mode blocks all device tools if any other plugin registers a pre_tool_call hook.

plugins.name: vitrail
plugins.author: elomkdn
plugins.does: Lets the model write GLSL fragment shaders that get validated, rendered live via a GPU-backed Hermes Desktop companion, and saved with auto-generated slider/color controls.

reads.best: Generated standalone HTML players are tested for being inert against injected titles/code (XSS-safe), and shader IDs are validated against path traversal.
reads.worst: Value is capped for users without a GPU-capable Hermes Desktop session, since the richest feature (live on-GPU compilation) depends on that companion.

plugins.name: ideacut
plugins.author: ranggaoscar
plugins.does: An AI video studio: tools that capture or record public web pages in headless Chromium, build typed-scene storyboards, preview them in a Desktop gallery/editor page and export MP4 with music and voice-over.

reads.best: A real Desktop gallery and editor sharing one renderer with the FFmpeg exporter, with an SSRF-guarding proxy for browser capture and timeouts on every subprocess.
reads.worst: Heavy dependencies (Playwright, Chromium, FFmpeg) and the README itself says the v1.2 Desktop click-through is unverified and voice-over uses an internal Hermes TTS import.

plugins.name: honeytrap
plugins.author: imabhays
plugins.does: Plants decoy credentials in the agent workspace and uses pre/post_tool_call hooks to block, quarantine and alert when any decoy (even encoded or split) appears in a tool call.

reads.best: Honeytoken-based hijack detection with normalisation against base64, hex, zero-width and homoglyph evasion, checked by parametrized tests and a runnable demo.
reads.worst: Protects only against exfiltration of its own decoys, so its value depends on an attacker going for the planted file, and the quarantine can block legitimate outbound tools until released.

plugins.name: fieldkit
plugins.author: Snehal707
plugins.does: Lets Hermes draft and publish offline observation forms, collect entries with photos, voice, GPS and signatures in an offline phone PWA, sync them through a dashboard API and read them back with 12 tools.

reads.best: A finished product: demo video, screenshots, PWA and dashboard tab, publish gated in code on user_approved, and about 67 Python tests plus app and end-to-end tests.
reads.worst: A very large surface (PWA, service worker, multi-MB bundles) for a niche audience, and the README says model files are checked against pinned SHA-256 hashes although the OCR entries carry none.

plugins.name: hostbook
plugins.author: Timidan
plugins.does: Hosts dashboard and SSH tools so Hermes can check and fix machines on your network under per-machine rules.

reads.best: Polished product with dashboard, screenshots, security docs and approval hooks that fail closed.
reads.worst: Read-only guard is a keyword regex and SSH accepts new host keys on first connect.

plugins.name: hermes-wrapped
plugins.author: devpras22
plugins.does: Turns Hermes session records into a deterministic personalized weekly or periodic recap video with synthesized music and optional delivery.

reads.best: It is an unusually polished, privacy-aware product experience with deterministic analytics, themed visuals, music, screenshots, and tests.
reads.worst: It is mostly a delightful retrospective rather than a capability that improves everyday agent work, and rendering requires large external tooling.

plugins.name: track-record
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Logs every reply in which the agent claims a fix worked, checks it against the next test/build exit code and the user's next message, reports hit rate, calibration gap and Brier score per model, and tells the agent its record when its certain claims fall below 80%.

reads.best: A new idea that only hooks can do: it measures the user's own agent's honesty and feeds the record back to make it check before claiming, using local pattern matching with no model calls.
reads.worst: Claim and outcome detection is regex pattern matching, so a vague next user message or an untested claim can be scored wrongly or left unchecked, and the README has no screenshot or demo.

plugins.name: backstop
plugins.author: themahis
plugins.does: Captures failed terminal commands, opens a restricted diagnosis session in Desktop, tracks stale or resolved incidents, and drafts an optional fix chat ([pinned source](https://github.com/themahis/hermes-backstop/tree/99fd96995d363de92050fdf61a902979b5926f1e)).

reads.best: The integrated failure-to-diagnosis-to-fix workflow includes source excerpts, stale-result detection, passing-command resolution, Desktop controls and meaningful Python and JavaScript tests.
reads.worst: The pinned file tools omit Hermes's sensitive-file denylist, allowing credential files within the chosen cwd, and search opens file symlinks without checking their resolved containment ([backstop_core.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/themahis/hermes-backstop/99fd96995d363de92050fdf61a902979b5926f1e/backstop_core.py)).

plugins.name: plugin-scout
plugins.author: bscharenberg
plugins.does: Recommends catalog plugins from local usage signals and checks installed plugins for collisions, updates and configuration warnings.

reads.best: Combines local history, memory and explicit interests with explainable picks and actionable setup checks without installing or changing other plugins.
reads.worst: conflicts.check treats every memory-category plugin as an exclusive memory provider and recommends removing extras, which can misclassify compatible memory utilities.

plugins.name: screentime
plugins.author: aldot311
plugins.does: Measures product visibility and spoken mentions in videos, evaluates typed sponsorship terms, and renders evidence reels using Hermes models or Meta services.

reads.best: Combines object verification, deterministic term checks and visual evidence, reserving Meta-call costs before spending and escalating ambiguous object matches to a person.
reads.worst: Unreadable vision-tracking batches are counted as not seen, so a partial model failure can produce a definite contract-term FAIL instead of an unknown result.

plugins.name: hermes-jobs
plugins.author: CrowBe
plugins.does: Synchronizes Hermes cron jobs with one Google Calendar board, including schedule edits, recurring events, and run outcomes ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CrowBe/hermes-jobs/34c0490fcc08d5e0b60cd56d32f3fa1f7317c317/__init__.py)).

reads.best: Automatic sync holds calendar-originated changes for confirmation, while provenance journaling and a per-profile lock protect job ownership ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CrowBe/hermes-jobs/34c0490fcc08d5e0b60cd56d32f3fa1f7317c317/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: Moving one recurring occurrence needs an explicit additional-run opt-in or an experimental skip workaround because the original slot otherwise still executes ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CrowBe/hermes-jobs/34c0490fcc08d5e0b60cd56d32f3fa1f7317c317/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: openloft-memory
plugins.author: blok-hamster
plugins.does: Adds an external long-term memory provider with automatic recall and turn ingestion plus five memory-curation tools.

reads.best: It integrates automatic recall and ingestion through the memory-provider interface, preserves secret scope and includes backend contract and isolation tests.
reads.worst: provider._ingest waits only five seconds for its predecessor before starting another write, while remember permits 120-second requests, contradicting the promised single-in-flight ingestion.

plugins.name: borrowed-hands
plugins.author: alext8900
plugins.does: Lets cloud Hermes request locally granted, approval-gated Xcode builds and system information from a paired Mac through an outbound authenticated connection.

reads.best: Signed job contracts, Mac-enforced grants, single-use approval tickets and a separately sandboxed build runner give cloud Hermes a substantive new hardware capability.
reads.worst: The generated signing key is stored in plugin-data outside Hermes secret storage, and the README discloses that default media attachment behavior can expose it without a tool call or approval.

plugins.name: wp-manager
plugins.author: danieljwonder
plugins.does: Manages WordPress fleet updates, health checks and content through native tools, a Desktop page and a bundled WordPress connector.

reads.best: A complete maintenance workflow combines approval-gated changes, unattended-run guards, credential-safe redirects and extensive privacy and connector tests.
reads.worst: Updates have no backup or rollback, and the optional direct 1Password CLI credential route is less aligned with catalog secret-scope rules than the default Hermes-secret path.

plugins.name: hermes-market
plugins.author: snuff12
plugins.does: Lets the agent search paid services, draft listings from skills and quote/purchase via x402 only after separate human wallet approval.

reads.best: Payment path keeps approval outside the agent (digest match, loopback gateway, no signer, redacted results).
reads.worst: Needs separately run seller/directory/gateway servers; default public demo depends on one host.

plugins.name: selenite
plugins.author: simongonzalezdc
plugins.does: Skills, hooks, tools and a desktop/dashboard UI that find and shrink human-handoff friction, fake kanban gates and pedantry.

reads.best: Polished product with branding, many tests, CI and hooks/tools/UI that act on kanban boards.
reads.worst: Scope sprawls and its abstract premise is hard for a new user to get value from quickly.

plugins.name: pagecast-director
plugins.author: flabanabba8
plugins.does: Editable cast audiobook pipeline: import TXT/EPUB, assign quotes to voices, resumable multi-engine TTS rendering and M4B/Android export with a Desktop editor.

reads.best: Deep working pipeline with credentials through the secret store, resumable locked renders and many tests.
reads.worst: Linux-only verified, hosted-voice routes tested only against mocks, and the 85KB books.py is dense.

plugins.name: daily-edition
plugins.author: ousiaresearch
plugins.does: Desktop personal newspaper compiled from user interests with clustering, back issues, optional editorial voices and a daily_edition tool.

reads.best: Finished product with a Desktop UI, print pipeline, CI and a deep Python and JS test suite.
reads.worst: Reliant on Google News RSS personal-use terms, and its optional model key is read from an env var.

plugins.name: hermes-continuum
plugins.author: mohamad-shafeez
plugins.does: A nine-subsystem plugin (event spine, encrypted checkpoints, reviewed memory, security tripwire, impact previews, retry circuits, skill forging) with a Desktop console.

reads.best: Ambitious, heavily tested (~20 test files) and deeply hooked into Hermes sessions, tools and memory.
reads.worst: ~28k lines across nine mythologically named systems make it hard to read and review, the kind of sprawl the catalog reviewer pushes back on.

plugins.name: engagements
plugins.author: latentoperator
plugins.does: A file-based client and project memory in Markdown: tools to find, bind, create and update clients, a pre_llm_call banner, and binding of sessions by working directory.

reads.best: A thoughtful, heavily tested memory layer that binds sessions to clients automatically and keeps records in human-editable Markdown.
reads.worst: An rc1 release with complex binding rules, and the repo ships a spike/ probe plugin alongside the real one.

plugins.name: memtomem-memory
plugins.author: memtomem
plugins.does: Automatically recalls memtomem notes each turn and optionally mirrors Hermes built-in memory writes through the existing MCP connection.

reads.best: A real memory-provider lifecycle adds bounded recall, stale-result fencing, explicit MCP grants and extensively tested admission control.
reads.worst: The provider constructs PluginContext through compatibility-sensitive core imports, and its documented in-memory mirror queue can lose writes on crashes.

plugins.name: hephaestus
plugins.author: madebylegion
plugins.does: Lets an agent draft a Hermes plugin, validates and installs it disabled, presents a consent card, and supports rollback.

reads.best: The checked-draft hash gate, disabled installation, rollback flow, Desktop consent card, and comprehensive lifecycle tests are an ambitious native product.
reads.worst: When approvals are disabled or YOLO is used, forge_check can import and execute an agent-authored draft unsandboxed, while the documented guard has acknowledged bypasses.

plugins.name: hermes-snitchboard
plugins.author: NeumannTechTips
plugins.does: Shows OpenSnitch outbound connection records, findings and an integrity check in a Hermes dashboard tab.

reads.best: Its read-only dashboard, separate collector, hash-chained records, redaction and extensive tests make firewall evidence understandable.
reads.worst: Live use is limited to Linux users who run and configure OpenSnitch; the author calls out untested machine and database variants.

plugins.name: coursewright
plugins.author: NehuenD
plugins.does: Researches a topic and builds a self-contained interactive HTML course with three depths, figures and exercises.

reads.best: It validates model output into a bounded spec, renders polished offline pages, marks provenance and covers core paths with extensive tests.
reads.worst: A full build needs many model and research calls plus optional video tooling, making completion slow and dependent on host capabilities.

plugins.name: proofgate
plugins.author: Whydiriki700
plugins.does: Records same-session tool evidence and rewrites or blocks final completion claims that its deterministic checker cannot support.

reads.best: It directly improves agent trustworthiness by enforcing evidence checks at the final-output hook.
reads.worst: The checker covers only a few shallow claim families and has a small scenario suite, so its evidence matching can be over- or under-inclusive.

plugins.name: seatbelt
plugins.author: deeworksonline-debug
plugins.does: Interposes policy checks before trading-looking tool calls to allow, block, ask the human or clamp leverage, with paper mode, limits, logs and halt controls.

reads.best: It adds a reusable safety boundary to Hermes across exchanges and trade-like tools, defaults to paper mode, fails closed on uncertainty and has strong pure-engine and integration tests.
reads.worst: It depends on adapters and Hermes approval-hook behavior, cannot see exchange-app actions, and its own README acknowledges MCP-hook coverage is untested.

reads.best: The implementation makes a serious attempt to fail closed across hooks and middleware, including durable limits and human-only live controls.
reads.worst: The pinned submission has no README and no tests, leaving a safety-critical integration hard to validate or operate.

plugins.name: sovereign-finance
plugins.author: gabonaut
plugins.does: Gives the agent a self-custodial smart wallet on BNB Chain and Ethereum where a passkey is admin and an onchain-scoped session key lets the agent run V3 liquidity and swap actions within daily caps.

reads.best: Layered limits (onchain scope and caps, plugin-side plan encoding, Hermes approval) with withdrawals only via Desktop plus WebAuthn, honestly disclosed, 48 tests and a full Desktop pane.
reads.worst: One 'Always' approval covers every later batch for that pool or swap pair regardless of amount (rule key ignores size), with slippage up to 5000 bps or a zero minAmountOut, so trades can move value without per-transaction approval.

plugins.name: hermes-a2ui
plugins.author: Revenue-Architect
plugins.does: Adds one validated tool, a2ui_present, that draws interactive A2UI views in Desktop and Webapp chat, sends clicks back as chat messages, and falls back to text elsewhere.

reads.best: Generative UI inside the chat with real round-trip interaction, a Python and browser validator kept in parity, and roughly 125 Python and 70 vitest tests.
reads.worst: The manifest says views load https images while the renderer also accepts http (including LAN hosts) and data: images, the README is short with no screenshots, the bundle is 2.1 MB, and no CI runs the tests.

plugins.name: detonator
plugins.author: shreyasudupi
plugins.does: Runs another Hermes plugin at a pinned commit inside a locked-down, no-network Docker sandbox with decoy secrets and a clock jump, then reports undeclared behaviour against deterministic rules mapped to MITRE ATT&CK/ATLAS.

reads.best: A new kind of agent tool: dynamic detonation with audit hooks, stub imports, time-bomb clock shift and rug-pull diffing, gated by ctx.ask_choice approval and about 83 tests.
reads.worst: Needs Docker on the user's machine, and its headline catalog-wide run and malicious-fixture results rest on private data that cannot be checked from the repo.

plugins.name: twitch-assist
plugins.author: Techkeyy
plugins.does: A Twitch chat platform adapter that lets allowlisted viewers !ask the streamer's Hermes agent and lets mods run a Backseat chat vote whose winner becomes the agent's next task.

reads.best: Real stdlib IRC-over-TLS platform with a careful trust model (server tags decide who votes, pinned toolsets, cooldowns, notice filtering) and 87 tests against a fake IRC server.
reads.worst: Public-channel safety still depends on the user setting up a dedicated profile correctly, and the pre_tool_call guard allows calls if session context cannot be imported.

plugins.name: strategic-arena
plugins.author: trillionverselabs-boop
plugins.does: Runs a background multi-agent stakeholder simulation over a repo, paper or post through the session's own model and returns a friction score, veto players, priced objections and dated claims scored later in a Desktop pane.

reads.best: About 4,300 lines of engine code with 260 tests, model access only through Hermes's plugin LLM facade, friendly provider-error messages and a 2,800-line Desktop pane.
reads.worst: A niche decision-review tool whose 27,000-character README and committed internal notes (HANDOFF, SESSION-PROMPT, PROGRESS) promise more rigor (Shapley-priced objections, calibration) than a hundred-call LLM debate can deliver, and the PR is still unmerged.

plugins.name: physis
plugins.author: ilPez00
plugins.does: Adds repository graph retrieval, verification hooks and operator-approved replay of learned command recipes [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ilPez00/hermes-physis/330e795b92544ff8d7ca9ab3d099d943dbc2185c/tools.py).

reads.best: It connects real edit and verification events to reusable recipes, with approval and replay exposed through operator slash commands rather than model tools [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ilPez00/hermes-physis/330e795b92544ff8d7ca9ab3d099d943dbc2185c/tools.py).
reads.worst: The verification hook returns no objection after exceptions such as command timeouts and skips attempts after the first, so it does not consistently enforce a passing check [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ilPez00/hermes-physis/330e795b92544ff8d7ca9ab3d099d943dbc2185c/tools.py).

plugins.name: apple-doc-plugin
plugins.author: AndrewMason7
plugins.does: Brings Apple documentation lookup, compiler-error grounding, @apple context references and a Desktop documentation workspace into Hermes [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AndrewMason7/apple-doc-plugin/0385ad680ffb2d8ad4eb45ea66249885a349197f/bridges/hermes/__init__.py) [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AndrewMason7/apple-doc-plugin/0385ad680ffb2d8ad4eb45ea66249885a349197f/desktop/plugin.js).

reads.best: The compiler-output hook and context-reference provider put API documentation into the agent's existing coding workflow, beyond a standalone search tool [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AndrewMason7/apple-doc-plugin/0385ad680ffb2d8ad4eb45ea66249885a349197f/bridges/hermes/__init__.py).
reads.worst: Desktop search failures silently substitute a small canned symbol set, including unrelated default hits and hard-coded latency, so a failed backend can still look functional [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AndrewMason7/apple-doc-plugin/0385ad680ffb2d8ad4eb45ea66249885a349197f/desktop/plugin.js).

plugins.name: sochen
plugins.author: N-45div
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Sochen for cloud jobs and US business phone calls, including mid-call answers, job updates, and a Desktop desk.

reads.best: Native credit-spending approval, scoped secrets, bounded job tracking, and tested Desktop and phone-call flows make this more substantial than a simple API wrapper.
reads.worst: The response shaper reports a reply with no status as ok:true, so a malformed service response can appear to be an accepted job.

plugins.name: pinocchio
plugins.author: tobadaniel
plugins.does: Records tool-call receipts and annotates closing claims as verified, contradicted or unverified, with a verification hook that requests correction.

reads.best: Deterministic receipt capture and output hooks tackle misleading completion claims without another model or network service.
reads.worst: Claim matching uses broad regexes and the latest category receipt, so a successful narrow or merely test-labelled command can incorrectly verify an all-tests claim.

plugins.name: accessible-session-list
plugins.author: denis-skripnik
plugins.does: Adds a keyboard and screen-reader-oriented Desktop session picker with title search, native list focus and explicit tab-opening actions.

reads.best: Native accessible controls, focus restoration, SDK-only navigation and Node/browser tests solve a concrete Desktop accessibility problem.
reads.worst: It searches only the creation-ordered first 500 fetched sessions, Ctrl+H can lose to core handling, and real screen-reader acceptance remains unverified.

plugins.name: caprover-operator
plugins.author: fmercurio
plugins.does: Plans immutable-image deployments for one configured CapRover app, requires correlated native approval, and reconciles uncertain outcomes without replaying a consumed plan.

reads.best: A carefully implemented durable ledger and approval middleware preserve uncertainty after crashes and distinguish deployment metadata, HTTP health, and exact-image runtime evidence.
reads.worst: Its scope is one existing CapRover app with in-process interactive approvals, and the separate preflight read cannot prevent races with external operators.

plugins.name: airpods-approvals
plugins.author: cineglobe
plugins.does: Uses a locally built macOS motion-and-audio helper to read Hermes approvals and questions through AirPods and return deliberate nod or shake answers.

reads.best: An unusually inventive hardware interface includes recorded-motion regression tests, authenticated helper pairing, stale-request checks, and once-only approval responses.
reads.worst: The helper stores and reads the Gemini key directly through macOS Keychain instead of Hermes secret routing, contrary to catalog credential rules; recognition also cannot rule out an unintended rhythmic nod.

plugins.name: circuit
plugins.author: odtboun
plugins.does: Builds two-layer PCB designs with a part library, placement, routing, design checks, fabrication exports and a Desktop board viewer.

reads.best: A substantial local engine produces Gerbers, drills, KiCad and STEP files from a shared board model rather than merely generating design prose.
reads.worst: In drc.py, trace bounding boxes omit trace width but the clearance prefilter uses those boxes, so it can skip real copper-clearance violations.

plugins.name: hermes-guardian
plugins.author: Oluseyix
plugins.does: Enforces deterministic tool and local-path policies through native approval hooks, with redacted audits and an operator policy simulation and activation workflow.

reads.best: Fail-closed policy parsing and audit failures, fresh approval keys and reviewed activation provide unusually careful enforcement boundaries.
reads.worst: The terminal grammar permits only seven simple commands, and allowing an external tool checks its name without inspecting its arguments, sharply limiting practical protected workflows.

plugins.name: sendsafe
plugins.author: NSEVEjk0
plugins.does: Inspects Word and Excel documents for hidden content, guards selected reads and creates separately verified visible-content sharing copies.

reads.best: Bounded archive parsing, hidden-content canary tests and fingerprint-bound exports protect originals while keeping hidden values out of tool reports.
reads.worst: Protection covers only read_file in configured folders, and sharing snapshots discard formatting, images and other content rather than preserving a full document.

plugins.name: renor
plugins.author: patrickpassosb
plugins.does: Registers a shared-memory provider with hosted HTTP or local stdio MCP transport, bounded recall, background durable-statement saves and explicit recall/remember tools.

reads.best: Native memory lifecycle integration, scoped credentials, redirect refusal, bounded prefetch and untrusted-memory handling provide substantially more than a recall skill ([provider](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renorai/hermes-renor/91320b6f936205b8566e6d6444a420d9bed553d0/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: The deduplication cache marks statements seen before successful persistence and keeps failures seen, so a dropped or exhausted write may not be retried later in the process; built-in memory deletions are also not mirrored ([write paths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/renorai/hermes-renor/91320b6f936205b8566e6d6444a420d9bed553d0/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: tablekeeper
plugins.author: kaverimeshram
plugins.does: Runs persistent tabletop campaigns with code-owned dice, combat rules, player identity and a Desktop battle grid. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaverimeshram/tablekeeper/a5cde35ec584c2b71b5b032a186478fdd4f291d0/tablekeeper/README.md)

reads.best: The rules engine and real-loader integration tests enforce ownership, turn order and persistent state independently of model narration. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaverimeshram/tablekeeper/a5cde35ec584c2b71b5b032a186478fdd4f291d0/tablekeeper/README.md)
reads.worst: The narration guard compares numbers against a shared set, so a valid number attributed to the wrong creature or action can escape correction. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaverimeshram/tablekeeper/a5cde35ec584c2b71b5b032a186478fdd4f291d0/tablekeeper/__init__.py)

plugins.name: infra-atlas
plugins.author: hnasheralneam
plugins.does: Builds a live infrastructure graph from Markdown runbooks and discovery, gates infrastructure operations on prior reading, and tracks drift and downtime.

reads.best: The integrated topology UI, drift reconciliation and read-before-touch hooks directly improve how Hermes operates the user’s own infrastructure.
reads.worst: Its credentials.py implements a separate file-backed credential vault with plaintext fallback, violating catalog rule 11, and auto-heal defaults to executing local restart commands.

plugins.name: homegrown
plugins.author: Cam-Smith-One
plugins.does: Lets Hermes build persistent HTML mini-apps with per-app SQLite records, version rollback, and live Desktop/chat rendering.

reads.best: Turns one-off generated apps into persistent, agent-accessible tools with independent data, reversible code changes, and live updates from any chat platform.
reads.worst: Its CSP injection matches <header> and commented or late <head> tags, so generated app code can run before the promised network restriction is active.

plugins.name: openrouter-everything
plugins.author: dadhalfdev
plugins.does: Adds OpenRouter-backed web, image, video, speech and transcription providers plus decision, extraction, reranking, embedding and configuration tools.

reads.best: Makes five native Hermes capabilities available through one profile-scoped key, with task/model checks, bounded video polling and detailed protected-media-path regression tests.
reads.worst: Much of the value consolidates existing services; web extraction returns model-generated text rather than guaranteed original content, and capability validation allows requests when catalog retrieval fails.

plugins.name: goneby
plugins.author: rahlquist
plugins.does: Captures turns into encrypted project logs and uses the shipped artifact to filter entries for embedding, vector storage and scoped recall.

reads.best: Per-turn capture, encrypted WALs, host-model judging and project-scoped semantic recall form a distinctive agent-memory workflow with extensive plumbing tests.
reads.worst: The Hermes adapter judges entries in chronological order but passes the flags unchanged to BackwardWalker, which reverses the entries, so asymmetric relevance verdicts retain the wrong memories.

plugins.name: faultline
plugins.author: bigmantech001
plugins.does: Records HTTP traffic through a loopback proxy, learns response contracts, injects failures and replays requests through agent tools and dashboard/Desktop studios.

reads.best: A real proxy, SQLite recorder, drift checks and replay receipts give Hermes an evidence-based debugging loop, with usable UIs and concurrency and policy tests.
reads.worst: Replay can repeat side-effecting POSTs without a code-enforced human confirmation, and redaction or truncation means the stored request is not always an exact reproducible original.

plugins.name: blast-radius
plugins.author: namanomar
plugins.does: Intercepts destructive tool calls to measure affected files and Git state, request approval or block them, and preserve recovery copies.

reads.best: Concrete impact reports and selective backups make an approval decision much more useful than a generic command warning.
reads.worst: Restore accepts unvalidated capsule IDs and trusts manifest source and destination paths, weakening the undo tool’s safety boundary.

plugins.name: chat-tree
plugins.author: Ronitron007
