plugins.does: Adds a Desktop conversation graph with branching, ancestor merges, model-written digests and lineage-scoped history retrieval.

reads.best: Combines a rich branch-and-merge interface with capped, redacted model digests and read-only history privacy tests.
reads.worst: Node navigation deliberately queries internal app markup and dispatches an internal timeline event, violating catalog rule 8 and creating a fragile Desktop dependency.

plugins.name: belive-aihub
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Adds BeLive AI Hub as a named Hermes model provider with tool-capable model discovery and live context-length metadata.

reads.best: Uses the public provider API, profile-aware secrets, bounded discovery requests and redirect refusal, with host-level credential-resolution tests.
reads.worst: A conventional single-vendor inference gateway adds little novelty, and the documented live qualification covers staging rather than production or vision.

plugins.name: youbench
plugins.author: liferacer780
plugins.does: Captures personal coding tasks and starting files, replays them on selected models, and reports test results, quality, cost and timing.

reads.best: Hooks, git snapshots, host-managed replay agents and a Desktop leaderboard address model selection using the user’s actual work.
reads.worst: The claimed confinement is unsafe: map_path accepts relative traversal as inside, and terminal handling only rewrites paths and workdir without containing commands.

plugins.name: polyglot
plugins.author: Subramanyarao11
plugins.does: Turns enabled gateway group chats into multilingual text and voice conversations with per-member language preferences.

reads.best: A gateway dispatch hook translates without starting agent turns, retains normal assistant addressing, and supports optional Sarvam with profile-scoped secrets and fallback tests.
reads.worst: Translation errors silently consume the message, inputs are cut to 2,000 characters, and fallback speech transcription depends on an internal Hermes tool import.

plugins.name: sidecar
plugins.author: rkfshakti
plugins.does: Runs a remote Hermes agent’s terminal and file-tool commands on a paired local machine through a terminal backend and approval daemon.

reads.best: The terminal-environment provider directly addresses cloud-agent access to the user’s own local workspace, with useful pairing, diagnostics and audit tooling.
reads.worst: The daemon trusts a client-supplied base64 policy comment while executing a separate unchecked body, so a paired client can label arbitrary execution as a safe command and skip local approval.

plugins.name: zaprite
plugins.author: welliv
plugins.does: Creates merchant checkout requests through Zaprite, watches payment state and exposes related account operations.

reads.best: Its secret-store access, per-call human approval and payment-state re-fetch have focused tests and a polished demo.
reads.worst: It serves merchants with Zaprite accounts and depends on Zaprite for actual checkout and payment truth.

plugins.name: escalation-governor
plugins.author: jusst01
plugins.does: Detects repeated tool failures and stalled model progress, then adds an escalation packet directing Hermes to delegate or report the blocker.

reads.best: Deterministic, configurable signals can nudge Hermes out of retry loops without adding a network service or blocking tool calls.
reads.worst: The packet only directs the model to delegate; the plugin does not enforce that escalation, and its sole unit-test file offers limited assurance for the many lifecycle hooks.

plugins.name: hermes-gauge
plugins.author: SidelightAi
plugins.does: Tracks estimated context-window use by session, reports the effective window and token breakdown, and can alert when a session approaches configured thresholds.

reads.best: It turns session lifecycle and model-window data into actionable per-session readings and opt-in alerts, with histories, dashboard surfaces, and screenshots.
reads.worst: Token counts are approximate and can be UNKNOWN until enough information exists; much of the live validation is described but the PR contains no test or check results.

plugins.name: sampler
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: A middleware plugin that sets the temperature/top_p sampling parameters on outgoing LLM requests across chat_completions, Anthropic Messages and Bedrock Converse, based on default/platform/model rules or a per-session override.

reads.best: Extremely disciplined safety design (deepcopy, no conflicting params on Anthropic, respects Hermes's own fixed-temperature omit list) with 48 tests covering precedence and each request type.
reads.worst: Narrow value since most casual users never touch sampling parameters, and session overrides are lost on restart.

plugins.name: plan-usage
plugins.author: ziadelboshy
plugins.does: A Hermes Desktop status-bar/dashboard plugin that aggregates plan-usage percentages across the user's Claude/ChatGPT credential pool, Nous Portal credits, and optional Anthropic/OpenAI org API spend.

reads.best: Unusually rigorous reliability: secrets read exclusively through Hermes's secret-scope API (never os.environ/.env), enforced by both a runtime test and a static AST test that bans raw env/token access, plus a redirect-refusal test proving admin-key headers can't leak via HTTP redirects.
reads.worst: The underlying idea (a usage dashboard) is not novel — the README itself lists six competing catalog plugins it differentiates against — and it ships no screenshots despite a full desktop UI.

plugins.name: hermes-cobrowse
plugins.author: sandman-sh
plugins.does: Runs multi-window Playwright browsing in a live local canvas where a person can take over and resume the agent.

reads.best: It implements a polished, real multi-session browser canvas with CDP frames, telemetry, and a tested human 2FA handoff.
reads.worst: Its agent tools still expose unrestricted browser clicking and page JavaScript, with no code-enforced approval or handoff gate for sensitive actions.

plugins.name: follow-through
plugins.author: Agenziamaia
plugins.does: llm_execution middleware that catches a final reply promising future work and turns it into a follow_through tool call telling the agent to do the work now.

reads.best: Rewriting the model's final response at the middleware layer fixes a common agent failure no prompt can enforce, and it fails open and caps nudges per turn.
reads.worst: Never checks whether work is actually running, and a bare "I'll" / "started" regex branch makes the trigger much broader than a promise; only 9 tests.

plugins.name: stitchslop
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Lets Hermes inspect and operate the Stitch Slop embroidery digitizer through a local bridge, a live Chrome pane, digitizing tools, and DST/PES export.

reads.best: It makes a real graphical specialist app controllable and observable by the agent while keeping the person in the loop, with carefully gated pairing and substantive security tests.
reads.worst: The use case is highly specialized and Linux-only, and it requires a separately running browser, X display, and manual first-time token pairing.

reads.best: The bridge provides real app commands and user takeover through a visible viewer, with tests for export persistence, relay authentication, origin and navigation restrictions.
reads.worst: Chrome launches with --no-sandbox and the fixed ~/.stitchslop state and browser profile are shared across Hermes profiles; first pairing and Linux Chrome/Xvfb setup also require manual work.

plugins.name: garmin-connect
plugins.author: adrianlaborda
plugins.does: Reads Garmin health and activity data, computes personal baselines and training-intensity flags, and displays them in Hermes Desktop.

reads.best: Deterministic calculations, a finished Desktop panel and extensive credential, timeout and data-edge tests make a strong personal-data integration.
reads.worst: Its audience needs a Garmin account and compatible device, and health interpretation remains dependent on wrist-sensor estimates and Garmin’s service.

plugins.name: budget-leash
plugins.author: jusst01
plugins.does: Meters estimated model spend and tool calls against session and daily limits, warning near the limit and blocking subsequent calls when it is reached.

reads.best: The [budget engine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusst01/budget-leash/7b4126703e84826e8ff8a8926432057f7790686c/leash.py) combines model-call cutoff decisions with a persistent day ledger whose updates re-read and add deltas under an exclusive file lock.
reads.worst: The [cap check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jusst01/budget-leash/7b4126703e84826e8ff8a8926432057f7790686c/leash.py) uses completed usage without reserving in-flight calls, so concurrent calls can overshoot the ceiling and a priced tool is forecast against the session cap but not the daily cap.

plugins.name: artemis-owner-proof
plugins.author: LukeJJones
plugins.does: Adds a mobile web companion that opens canonical Hermes Bot Chats through existing owner Web Access and gateway APIs.

reads.best: Readable bundled UI, scoped drafts, explicit reconnect logic and security-focused Markdown and identity tests make the mobile access concept concrete.
reads.worst: Remote sign-in and canonical conversation continuity remain unverified in the disclosed evidence, and access retains full owner authority rather than a revocable phone-only grant.

plugins.name: hermes-chan
plugins.author: AlleyBo55
plugins.does: Adds an animated desktop companion and a native computer-use backend that performs the agent's clicks and typing. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlleyBo55/hermes-chan/54041f8180c69f0d5100aee8bd87c623b89fb920/README.md)

reads.best: Synchronizes real native input with character animations through a public computer-use provider while Hermes retains approval gating. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlleyBo55/hermes-chan/54041f8180c69f0d5100aee8bd87c623b89fb920/hermeschan/backend.py)
reads.worst: Requires a Rust/Tauri build and platform permissions, with native Wayland windows unsupported and Windows runtime behavior still unverified. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlleyBo55/hermes-chan/54041f8180c69f0d5100aee8bd87c623b89fb920/README.md)

plugins.name: hermes-blueprint
plugins.author: winchxyz
plugins.does: Turns ideas into evidence-backed plans through stored phase gates, independent research checks, estimates and kanban handoff.

reads.best: Quote-checked evidence, persisted verdicts, computed effort/calendar estimates and focused offline tests enforce useful planning discipline.
reads.worst: A failed or malformed independent verifier is stored as skipped and still satisfies the briefing freshness gate, so a plan can advance without a successful independent check.

plugins.name: hackertube
plugins.author: rcmiller01
plugins.does: Adds a Hermes dashboard for source-backed video, podcast, book and audiobook discovery with model-assisted ranking and a profile-local library.

reads.best: Product-level dashboard and library are backed by scoped secrets, explicit searches, supervised cancellation, privacy/deletion flows and broad boundary tests.
reads.worst: It adapts an existing discovery concept, depends on external catalog coverage and ranking quality, and the prepared seed is only development content rather than a curated endorsement library.

plugins.name: read-once
plugins.author: batmnnn
plugins.does: Uses tool and model middleware to replace eligible repeated local file reads with a reference to an unchanged result still present in the current model request.

reads.best: Exact-result visibility checks, content fingerprints, scoped invalidation and loader-level regression tests make repeated-read suppression deliberately conservative.
reads.worst: It re-reads files to hash them, optimizes only a narrow local read_file path, and cannot reliably detect a backend retained solely in Hermes’s private task cache.

plugins.name: sarvam
plugins.author: Subramanyarao11
plugins.does: Adds Indian-language speech recognition, live transcription and speech synthesis plus translation, OCR and long-recording tools.

reads.best: Real Hermes speech providers, streaming sessions, scoped-key lookup and resumable batch jobs extend voice access beyond a standalone translation skill.
reads.worst: All processing depends on a paid hosted API, tests mock that service, and returned storage URLs are checked only for an initial HTTPS prefix rather than host or redirect confinement.

plugins.name: hermes-quote-to-chat
plugins.author: ivanvanes18
plugins.does: Adds removable, per-chat quote cards to Hermes Desktop and merges them into the next message at send time.

reads.best: Native composer middleware and slots preserve the draft while attaching quotes to idle and busy sends, with focused behavioral tests.
reads.worst: Rejected-send recovery depends on a timed draft-text comparison, and the test runner needs manually supplied jsdom and nanostores dependencies.

plugins.name: hyprland
plugins.author: mddragon18
plugins.does: Adds a Wayland-native Hyprland computer-use provider for screenshot capture, window targeting, pointer input and typing ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mddragon18/hyprland-computer-use/eef766e18200338b772b14c20dbf03d603c84982/plugin/hyprland/README.md)).

reads.best: Enables Hermes on a desktop environment through an actual provider seam, with readable C source and checks against clicks outside the captured window.
reads.worst: Requires a local native build and several system utilities; tests are manual smoke drivers, while negative-origin monitor layouts and modifier-pointer gestures remain unsupported or unverified.

plugins.name: caduceus
plugins.author: 100yenadmin
plugins.does: Builds a local searchable health and DNA vault with importers, source-linked genetics and trends, reports, and research-watch blueprints.

reads.best: A substantial local data pipeline distinguishes absent evidence from negative results and tests privacy across search, reports, trends, and research terms.
reads.worst: The vault is unencrypted at rest and defaults to open disclosure, while tool results expose selected health data to the configured model provider.

plugins.name: chroma
plugins.author: TobiasDraven
plugins.does: Provides a Desktop skin gallery, palette editor and theme importers with optional gateway-wide skin synchronization.

reads.best: A finished visual customization product with import formats, previews, provenance-aware deletion and substantial frontend/backend tests.
reads.worst: Synchronization needs the optional backend and installed transport skins, and native theme painting also reaches outside the plugin SDK through window.hermesDesktop.

plugins.name: agent-app
plugins.author: zfoong
plugins.does: Adds tools and dashboard interfaces for building, installing, operating and connecting to Agent Apps through framework CLIs.

reads.best: A substantial app-management interface connects app sessions, marketplace installation and task operations to Hermes.
reads.worst: Remote-app authentication is delegated to a CLI that stores credentials in ~/.a2app/credentials.json instead of Hermes credential routes, and the framework must be installed separately.

plugins.name: snooze
plugins.author: AIverflow
plugins.does: Repeats chat reminders without LLM calls until an exact answer, then optionally hands a follow-up to Hermes.

reads.best: Deterministic confirmation, capped reminders, sender locking and broad tests make persistent reminders a practical gateway capability.
reads.worst: It depends on private gateway/send surfaces and can consume the first unrelated chat message after a reminder as an invalid answer.

plugins.name: iolite
plugins.author: simongonzalezdc
plugins.does: Shortlists models by capability and cost, measures local usage and displays an agent-controlled model landscape.

reads.best: Works offline with bundled attributed data and integrates personal plan pricing, local measurements and acknowledged Desktop controls.
reads.worst: Benchmark-derived intelligence is a proxy for a user task, and fast ranking favors intelligence rather than speed until all candidates have speed measurements.

plugins.name: counterparty
plugins.author: Mattbusel
plugins.does: Screens counterparties against vendor-list data and public-record APIs before outward tool actions and adds research warnings.

reads.best: A pre-action approval hook with cited findings and bundled offline matches adds due diligence even when the model forgets to ask.
reads.worst: In default ask mode an offline clean-looking name passes silently, contrary to the promised offline note, and internal hook errors also fail open.

plugins.name: trurl
plugins.author: oblomovunleashed
plugins.does: Keeps a private taste profile and sourced recommendation graph, then produces curated picks and visual editions.

reads.best: The code separates explicit feedback from tentative hypotheses and builds inspectable, sourced recommendation paths.
reads.worst: The workflow asks the agent to coordinate ten tools and research steps, which adds setup and execution complexity.

plugins.name: concord-for-hermes
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Coordinates existing-file GitHub replacements with SQLite reservations, conditional writes, verified receipts, and idempotent replay.

reads.best: Its state machine treats uncertain writes as held operations rather than retrying, with extensive concurrency, crash, identity, and recovery tests.
reads.worst: Protection covers only this one tool and a shared coordinator database; ordinary git, other tools, and separate machines bypass it.

plugins.name: corpus-open
plugins.author: teakesdev
plugins.does: Adds local court-case tools, citation annotations, source-document and quotation guards, deadline briefs and a Desktop case pane.

reads.best: Case-aware hooks check quotations against registered documents before supported writes and keep citation findings and deadline confidence visible, with extensive regression fixtures.
reads.worst: The native plugin falls back from Hermes secrets to a CourtListener token stored in a separate file, violating catalog rule 11; quotation guards also deliberately pass uncheckable content.

plugins.name: ticklist
plugins.author: mchevatheachiever
plugins.does: Adds persistent Desktop checklists that users can tick while six agent tools read and edit the same lists, with actions optionally posted into chat.

reads.best: A complete local UI provides tabs, pinning, reorder, undo, export and a mute toggle, backed by persistence and API tests.
reads.worst: File locking is POSIX-only and disappears on Windows, weakening the cross-process consistency claim; every row is rendered and notices can consume model turns.

plugins.name: z-midi-console
plugins.author: zorroukk
plugins.does: Builds a Desktop MIDI control surface with hardware learning, modulation, recording, MIDI export and agent-operated controls.

reads.best: A substantial hardware engine and editable multi-device UI integrate live controls, modulation and recording.
reads.worst: The chat endpoint obtains raw provider credentials through resolve_runtime_provider and constructs subscription Authorization headers instead of using the catalog-required credentialed_provider_request route.

plugins.name: lemma
plugins.author: udirobert
plugins.does: Extracts scientific claims, runs bounded numerical audits with positive controls in a sandbox, and preserves evidence-backed verdict artifacts and traces.

reads.best: The evidence trail, mandatory control, sandbox boundary, provider credential route, and Desktop audit room turn paper checking into a real agent capability.
reads.worst: It ships a large dependency stack and relies on LLM-generated audit scripts and external paper/providers, leaving significant operational complexity despite the safety defaults.

reads.best: The vendored pipeline enforces passing positive controls for decisive verdicts and refuses generated execution when no sandbox is available unless the operator explicitly opts in.
reads.worst: Storage is resolved once at tools.py import rather than per call, and detached full audits expose status but no cancellation or hard whole-run deadline; scientific validity still depends on model-generated experiments.

plugins.name: bench-rewind
plugins.author: rusty4444
plugins.does: Undo history for a physical device teardown: records removal steps on your own photos with part regions, bags and dependencies, answers 'where does this go?', and plans reassembly in valid reverse order via four tools and a Desktop page.

reads.best: Exceptionally finished: ~150 tests (model, store, images, browser UI), metadata stripping on photos, no-follow private store, a screenshot, a demo kit and a script-free printable reassembly packet.
reads.worst: The agent only drives a record-keeping engine the user fills in by hand; the core value is the standalone workbench rather than a change to what Hermes itself can do, and it ships a 700 KB built web bundle.

plugins.name: hermes-receipts
plugins.author: iket72183-collab
plugins.does: Records immutable, deterministic evidence that explicit file, native-test, and website checks passed, failed, or remain unverified.

reads.best: It observes real native tool activity and fails closed while preserving clear evidence boundaries rather than trusting model-reported results.
reads.worst: It verifies only criteria a user specifies and is limited to Linux/macOS, so it cannot certify general task completion.

reads.best: Honest scope, read-safety for .env files, descriptor-relative reads and a real test suite.
reads.worst: The bundled catalog yaml is a template with empty repo and sha, and there are no screenshots or demo.

plugins.name: sentinel
plugins.author: folarihn
plugins.does: A pre_tool_call policy guard that checks every tool call against built-in rules, user rules and mission scopes, then allows, blocks or routes it to Hermes approval, with a redacted SQLite audit log, file checkpoints and a local Control Room web UI.

reads.best: Fails closed when it errors, is honest that it is not an OS sandbox, and ships about 117 Python plus 53 frontend tests, screenshots and thorough docs.
reads.worst: The Control Room is a separate local web server rather than a Desktop pane, shell-command checks are allowlist word-splitting that can be bypassed, and restore only covers write_file/patch under a single-directory mission.

plugins.name: stage
plugins.author: adindamochamad
plugins.does: Hooks write_file and patch so edits land in a scratch copy until stage_apply, with diffs and SHA-256 receipts.

reads.best: A real safety layer over Hermes's own file edits, using only the standard library, with tests for protections and review.
reads.worst: Install is by symlink only, and the README has no screenshots.

plugins.name: hermes-walrus-memory
plugins.author: takaolovely
plugins.does: An append-only, hash-chained memory provider that keeps corrections beside the originals, cites lines on recall and can optionally mirror to Walrus Mainnet.

reads.best: Tamper-evident memory that works with no configuration, with a minimal child environment and secrets fetched through get_secret.
reads.worst: The plugin folder has no README, and the Walrus side is a niche crypto storage service.

plugins.name: hermes-guard
plugins.author: elianjuan-g
plugins.does: Local deterministic prompt-injection guard that scans inbound messages and tool args via pre_llm_call/pre_tool_call hooks and quarantines suspicious ones.

reads.best: Fail-closed hooks with ~170 tests, a quarantine log and owner-only release commands.
reads.worst: Pattern-based detection that, as its own README admits, novel obfuscation will pass.

plugins.name: embargo
plugins.author: inkandwire
plugins.does: Detects 'EMBARGOED UNTIL' headers in what the agent reads and blocks any tool call from sending that text out until the release time, with a Desktop countdown card.

reads.best: A genuinely new outbound-guard idea enforced in pre_tool_call with ~50 tests and a Desktop card.
reads.worst: Serves a narrow newsroom/PR audience.

plugins.name: hermes-sanctuary
plugins.author: Med34000
plugins.does: Shows a living, animated scene in Hermes Desktop and the web dashboard where characters wake as their tools are used and a guard reacts to errors, loops, fallbacks, budget and pending approvals.

reads.best: Exceptionally finished Desktop pane, sidebar page and dashboard strip, built only from 11 observer hooks, with bilingual docs and a demo GIF.
reads.worst: It has no tests, it is mostly a visual layer, and the web dashboard iframe is not sandboxed although the README says it is.

plugins.name: gif-tool
plugins.author: tuancookiez-hub
plugins.does: Opens, edits, captions and compresses GIFs locally with Pillow, in an editable Desktop card and studio, and can create a meme GIF via the Codex sign-in.

reads.best: Finished product feel: Desktop card and studio, size presets for Discord/Telegram/X, screenshots and 27 tests.
reads.worst: Value depends on the Desktop UI and Codex sign-in for creation; the GIF niche is modest.

plugins.name: falsify
plugins.author: CodexOperator
plugins.does: Has the coding agent pre-register a claim and a check, then runs the check on its change and on reverted copies hunk by hunk, marks checks that pass either way VOID, and records results in a hash-chained ledger.

reads.best: A real Hermes approval gate (pre_tool_call plus post_approval_response grants), drafter secrets read via secret_scope, and about 79 tests that use real git repos.
reads.worst: No sandbox (disclosed), agent-chosen timeouts with no cap, git calls without timeouts, and its headline study results rest on recordings not in the repo.

plugins.name: wazoo
plugins.author: EthanThatOneKid
plugins.does: Memory provider that stores typed memories in a hosted Wazoo RDF world with hybrid search and SPARQL tools.

reads.best: Proper memory-provider integration with prefetch recall, token-like statement refusal and scoped secrets; 42 tests and CI.
reads.worst: Depends on a third-party hosted service; README sparse on failure behavior.

plugins.name: proactive-agent
plugins.author: JerryLiu369
plugins.does: Governs chat turns on chosen platforms: turn time reminders, terminal auto-detach, subagent briefs, loop stopping and a background-result ledger.

reads.best: Deep hooks and middleware reshape Hermes delegation and responsiveness.
reads.worst: Defaults to weixin only, many interacting timers that may surprise users; plugin folder itself thin on docs.

plugins.name: hermes-salespilot
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Sales desk: import or find leads, qualify, draft outreach, send by SMTP only after approval, and track replies in Desktop views.

reads.best: Human approval before every send with SMTP/IMAP TLS hardening and 185 tests.
reads.worst: A CRM in a plugin; niche for most Hermes users and large surface area.

plugins.name: hermes-anchor
plugins.author: Aayu095
plugins.does: A context engine that deterministically detects decisions, amounts and dates, pins them, and on compression re-inserts them verbatim while folding the middle into a capped extractive digest with zero model calls.

reads.best: Replaces Hermes's context engine via register_context_engine, with tests that compress 100 times and check pins never drift.
reads.worst: Pins live in one global pins.json shared by every session and never expire, so facts from one conversation are injected into all others and the carrier grows without bound.

plugins.name: hermes-web-crawl4ai
plugins.author: axAilotl
plugins.does: Adds a Crawl4AI extraction backend and a bounded same-site crawler that routes page fetches through a user-configured service.

reads.best: It adds a practical extraction and crawl path with page/depth/deadline bounds, per-target URL policy checks, and tested failure handling.
reads.worst: It requires a separate reachable Crawl4AI server, and does not itself search the web or provide extraction without that service.

plugins.name: salesforce-guard
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Reviews Salesforce source and snapshots for release impact, dependency paths, selected-user configuration and bounded security signals, producing local reports without deploying.

reads.best: It offers a deep, evidence-backed release-review workflow with explicit input approvals and clear limits on what static signals and access snapshots establish.
reads.worst: Its scope is specialized to Salesforce and its security and impact results remain human-reviewed heuristics rather than deployment or runtime guarantees.

plugins.name: internship-scout
plugins.author: aditkole
plugins.does: Searches public Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby postings, inspects application questions and blockers, and tracks applications locally with deduplication.

reads.best: Pre-screening real application forms for blockers before a user starts is a sharply useful workflow beyond generic job search.
reads.worst: The pinned tree has no test suite and depends on changing third-party ATS schemas, with conditional form questions necessarily invisible.

plugins.name: doorman
plugins.author: TwoRobotsinaTrenchcoat
plugins.does: Wake-on-LAN hooks that wake a sleeping local inference box before a model request and keep it awake for the request's life.

reads.best: Novel use of api_request hooks to make Hermes run on user's own sleeping hardware, bounded and fail-safe.
reads.worst: Single ~1000-line file, README thin relative to complex config forms.

plugins.name: jg-provider-usage
plugins.author: jerrygooch
plugins.does: Desktop status chip, popover and page showing provider account usage limits, reset times and balances.

reads.best: Product-grade Desktop UI with demo video, screenshots and broad Python/JS tests.
reads.worst: Screenshots are harness renders, not the packaged app, and it mostly displays rather than acts.

plugins.name: visor
plugins.author: samundra0
plugins.does: Gives Hermes a persistent live canvas for charts, tables, media and other blocks through a bundled HTTP/SSE server.

reads.best: A self-contained visual surface with boards, connectors and exports makes agent results much easier to inspect.
reads.worst: The plugin falls back to reading an API token from a state file, and its media-path check does not reject hidden components of the resolved symlink target.

plugins.name: emporium
plugins.author: 0xdopewilly
plugins.does: Runs paid agent services through an x402 gateway and lets Hermes hire other shops with budgets and payment receipts.

reads.best: Sealed job sessions, tool locks, replay protection and payment-on-delivery accounting give agent commerce a substantive platform implementation.
reads.worst: The default buyer policy spends up to $0.10 without human approval, and the approval gate does not pin the price or recipient later used for signing.

plugins.name: hermes-arena
plugins.author: JustinPerea
plugins.does: A pixel-art platform fighter that runs as a Hermes Desktop page, against a CPU, a local second player, or an online opponent over WebRTC.

reads.best: A remarkably complete game drawn entirely in code, with netplay, gamepad support, Shadow DOM isolation and a clean destroy() lifecycle.
reads.worst: It has nothing to do with the agent: Hermes Desktop is only the host page, and the 4,300-line plugin.js is a generated build of game/pixel-hermes.html.

plugins.name: grounded-recall
plugins.author: joaquinbyagentx
plugins.does: A pre_llm_call hook that searches the user's notes or vault, secret-manager item titles and recent sessions, then injects a bounded evidence block labelled by freshness.

reads.best: Retrieval is deterministic and bounded (1.5 s cap) and audited every turn, with 77 security-focused tests and a minimal environment for the secret-title CLI.
reads.worst: Mostly lexical keyword injection; the demo eval baseline is stacked (plugin-off with no tools), and docs have TODOs, a wrong config key and a missing demo.gif.

plugins.name: chalk
plugins.author: Nnadijoshuac
plugins.does: Renders narrated, animated chalkboard lessons inline in Hermes Desktop, with replay and video export.

reads.best: A structured lesson format, automatic layout and the existing Hermes TTS route turn explanations into a distinctive multimodal teaching surface.
reads.worst: Only four Python tests cover validation and basic creation; the large canvas renderer, TTS integration and chunked video export lack automated coverage.

plugins.name: hermes-x-bookmarks
plugins.author: winchxyz
plugins.does: Syncs X bookmarks through the official API, classifies them with Hermes, and exports them to Desktop, Obsidian, Notion, or Google Docs.

reads.best: It connects a real personal knowledge workflow across several useful destinations with OAuth scopes, a Desktop board, digest actions, and a substantial test suite.
reads.worst: The number of auth and export integrations creates many configuration and API failure modes, while the core classification remains model-dependent.

plugins.name: screenpipe
plugins.author: vdimarco
plugins.does: Searches a local Screenpipe OCR/audio corpus and injects relevant timestamped context before Hermes sees a turn, with explicit recall tools.

reads.best: The pre-LLM hook, relevance gating, cooldown cache, untrusted-context prefix, bounded timeout, and graceful degradation make ambient recall practical.
reads.worst: It requires a separate always-on Screenpipe capture service and sends highly sensitive local context into the model, even though the plugin itself is careful about limits.

plugins.name: hermes-sysadmin
plugins.author: kdegeek
plugins.does: Manages on-prem Windows and Active Directory through 71 typed tools, a 231-entry vetted PowerShell catalog, tiered approvals, an audit log and a Desktop dashboard.

reads.best: Serious engineering: tiers, protected objects, parameter binding, audit log, offline and live test suites, Desktop dashboard.
reads.worst: Audience is niche (AD admins), and the password for WinRM needs an env passthrough for cron.

plugins.name: claude-pacer
plugins.author: Rubenkivilang
plugins.does: Reads a user's Claude Pro/Max 5-hour and weekly usage windows via Hermes's own usage-fetch API and computes a pacing mode to throttle agents and gate cron jobs so the weekly allowance lasts and some is reserved for the human.

reads.best: About 105 stdlib unit tests covering edge cases like NaN/Infinity rejection and fail-open behavior, and it explicitly never reads, holds or writes a credential itself.
reads.worst: No Desktop UI or visual component; it is a CLI/tool/slash-command utility whose value depends entirely on users who run heavy scheduled automation against subscription limits.

plugins.name: hermes-egm
plugins.author: willbohn
plugins.does: A single egm_review tool that runs fresh, tool-free LLM review passes over a caller-supplied text snapshot and validates that every cited piece of evidence is a literal quote from the stated source line.

reads.best: 47 tests cover concurrency, SQLite persistence and restart, and dozens of malformed/forged-evidence inputs; the docs are unusually self-critical ('Reviewers can miss defects, hallucinate reasoning or agree wrongly') rather than hyping the tool.
reads.worst: It is a fairly narrow advisory review tool for text snapshots; usefulness is real but aimed at a specific coding/review niche rather than a broad Hermes user base.

plugins.name: fusen
plugins.author: Tokagehausu
plugins.does: A single editable 'sticky note' that can be pinned to many chats at once and is injected into the model's context only when stale, with revision history and an optional approve-before-write mode.

reads.best: 49 real unit tests cover revision/revert, optimistic-concurrency conflicts, and stale-detection logic; the README states plainly 'Network: none. No telemetry, no remote calls, no API keys,' matching the code (all state is one local JSON file).
reads.worst: It is a genuinely useful but narrow productivity feature; the submission's own checklist admits a recorded demo and some catalog-entry items are still unchecked.

plugins.name: webnovel-studio
plugins.author: wyi006636-cyber
plugins.does: A long-form fiction runtime that plans, writes, reviews and saves serialized novel chapters through role-routed ctx.llm calls, with cross-chapter story memory (SQLite FTS5), resumable runs, a project lock and a guard hook protecting the book's state.

reads.best: Real machinery a prompt cannot hold: a pre_tool_call guard that stops other tools rewriting canonical story state, resumable runs, a cross-process lock and about 6,500 lines of tests.
reads.worst: It vendors 3.5 MB of an upstream project, including a minified prebuilt dashboard bundle, and pulls in fastapi, uvicorn and watchdog for a niche (mostly Chinese web-novel) audience.

plugins.name: hermes-call-me
plugins.author: fozagtx
plugins.does: Gives Hermes three tools that phone the owner through CALL-E for approval, help or a report, checks a spoken PIN and a one-time code itself, and can block risky tools until a single-use phone approval exists.

reads.best: Fails closed throughout: the plugin rather than the voice agent compares the PIN, approvals are single-use and expire, one allowlisted number, daily cap, secrets come from Hermes's secret config, and there are tests.
reads.worst: Needs a paid CALL-E account and a phone call per approval, and the risky-tool guard is off by default and matches tool names only by regex.

plugins.name: hyperrizz
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Agent-led HyperFrames video production with project/review/produce tools, a live review pane and render verification.

reads.best: Polished product with pane, CI, browser and verifier tests.
reads.worst: Heavy local Node/Chromium/FFmpeg and npm downloads on first build for a niche creative workflow.

plugins.name: last-price
plugins.author: iamdflame
plugins.does: Lets Hermes negotiate sales with a hidden owner-set price floor, restricted deal tools and a held-output price audit.

reads.best: Separates confidential pricing policy from model context and uses real output hooks, tool restrictions and adversarial regression fixtures to constrain negotiations.
reads.worst: Payment links remain placeholders and live messaging deals are unverified; the free-text safety audit depends on a heuristic price parser.

plugins.name: dossier
plugins.author: Frazzlesprite
plugins.does: Builds persistent sourced organisation and professional-person briefs with claim evidence, snapshot diffs and PDF/Desktop views.

reads.best: Quote-gated claims, explicit contested evidence and persisted snapshots turn repeat research into an auditable workflow.
reads.worst: adapters/base.py checks only the original hostname against a regex before urllib follows redirects, leaving its claimed private-network protection incomplete.

plugins.name: dioramic
plugins.author: faze39
plugins.does: Turns a validated structured scene specification into a Blender-rendered vertical video and supports iterative scene tweaks.

reads.best: It converts model output to bounded data rather than Blender code, scrubs the render environment, limits resources, and includes demos and render tests.
reads.worst: It requires a local Blender installation and rendering hardware, which makes the otherwise polished workflow a niche, heavyweight setup.

plugins.name: decision-ledger
plugins.author: GeoffP17
plugins.does: Stores proposed decisions and human-confirmed receipts with exact scope, conditions, replacements, and revocations across Hermes sessions.

reads.best: The code separates model draft/read operations from a foreground human confirmation flow, records durable receipts, and clearly explains its limits as recordkeeping rather than an execution gate.
reads.worst: It is a specialist governance ledger with a manual Linux foreground-console workflow; its own documentation says same-user database access can bypass application checks.

plugins.name: meeting-copilot-live
plugins.author: adam4788
plugins.does: Hermes Desktop pane plus a dashboard API that captures a consented meeting, transcribes it (local Whisper, Meta cloud or Meetily), searches a chosen project folder and returns a cited answer to a question you trigger.

reads.best: Careful secret handling (allowlisted names through scoped Hermes secrets, keys passed to workers over stdin), consent gating, and a full Desktop pane with native macOS capture and an overlay.
reads.worst: No tests ship ('runtime-only source release'), and the README itself calls it an early preview with unverified live answers and Windows path; the Meta ASR endpoint could not be verified.

plugins.name: load-lock
plugins.author: aron98
plugins.does: Machine-wide counting semaphore with 17+ tools, heartbeats and Desktop/dashboard UI so parallel coding agents take turns on heavy builds.

reads.best: Polished cross-agent coordination with dashboard, Desktop pane, screenshots and session hooks.
reads.worst: Relies on an external daemon outside the plugin folder; no tests in the plugin folder and a heavy tool surface.

plugins.name: mindhall
plugins.author: jai-srinivas
plugins.does: A shared, signed 'mind' (work, dates, notes, change log) that Hermes and other AI apps (ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor) can all read and write via an included MCP server, injected into every Hermes turn as context.

reads.best: Correctly reads its settings through Hermes's profile-aware secret_scope rather than opening .env files directly, and is explicitly designed to never break a turn if the store can't be read.
reads.worst: The optional external MCP server (for connecting ChatGPT/Claude) protects access with a secret-bearing URL rather than real authentication, and has only modest test coverage (engine + settings, 237 lines) relative to its cross-app scope.

plugins.name: nightshift
plugins.author: Pavilion-devs
plugins.does: Supervises local training runs, detects unhealthy metrics, and manages checkpoint recovery, bounded interventions, alerts and Desktop charts ([pinned source](https://github.com/Pavilion-devs/nightshift/tree/8bbbd6e4163db347af5d4795134bfae22d036d4c/nightshift)).

reads.best: Deterministic detectors, checkpoint selection, intervention budgets and substantial process/recovery tests make the training supervisor much more than an occasional model-generated diagnosis.
reads.worst: The pinned ProcessHandle.launch passes the full Hermes environment to arbitrary trainers, exposing inherited secrets, and is_ours accepts a missing saved fingerprint when reattaching to a process ([nightshift/core/process.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pavilion-devs/nightshift/8bbbd6e4163db347af5d4795134bfae22d036d4c/nightshift/core/process.py)).

plugins.name: onair
plugins.author: perfect7613
plugins.does: Makes Hermes an OBS operator with scene design, screen questions, overlays, automatic failure/fix marks, highlight reels and a Desktop studio ([pinned source](https://github.com/perfect7613/hermes-onair/tree/2245b9158300f2a60a5dda859f037b3cc3244b03)).

reads.best: The complete recording-to-reel workflow combines OBS control, persistent marks, native Desktop controls and substantive protocol, media and recovery tests.
reads.worst: Browser sources accept unchecked URLs and local or model-written HTML, while approval for source/design changes only fires during streaming, allowing unapproved local-page execution and private-network reads ([core/studio.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/perfect7613/hermes-onair/2245b9158300f2a60a5dda859f037b3cc3244b03/core/studio.py), [core/guard.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/perfect7613/hermes-onair/2245b9158300f2a60a5dda859f037b3cc3244b03/core/guard.py)).

plugins.name: llmapi
plugins.author: romanbesedinskiy-jpg
plugins.does: Adds an LLM API model provider with model-specific protocol routing, catalog capabilities, gateway error classification and account-cost reporting.

reads.best: Integrates native Messages, Responses and Chat Completions routing with Hermes caching, reasoning settings and billing-aware fallback behavior.
reads.worst: The process-global model catalog is not keyed by base URL, so profiles using different gateways can reuse the wrong endpoint's model metadata.

plugins.name: agentpurse
plugins.author: maaz-bin-hassan
plugins.does: Adds merchant search, quoting and PayPal sandbox purchases guarded by human approval, allowances, receipts and a kill switch.

reads.best: The handler independently requires a matching one-time human-approved grant and refuses unattended or model-approved spending, with targeted tests.
reads.worst: It remains a hosted-service-dependent sandbox checkbook: captured receipts do not place retailer orders, and approved price watches can later purchase without a second Hermes prompt.

plugins.name: token-master
plugins.author: karmsheel
plugins.does: Adds a Hermes Desktop dashboard aggregating token usage across profiles, models and machines, with account labels and provider quota views.

reads.best: Makes Hermes's existing usage records understandable through a native chart, breakdowns and read-only database aggregation.
reads.worst: Account rows reuse provider-wide usage and quota for every credential of that provider, so they do not establish per-account attribution.

plugins.name: kujo-hermes
plugins.author: robertdevore
plugins.does: Exposes Kujo engineering tools through native discovery, execution, approval, cancellation and hash-verified local receipts.

reads.best: Exact workspace trust, single-use request-bound approvals, bounded subprocesses and receipt verification form a substantial engineering integration.
reads.worst: Setup needs a separate Kujo runtime and numerous pinned source checkouts, with browser, container and producer-binding gaps explicitly remaining.

plugins.name: grok-bot-twin
plugins.author: hudsonwa
plugins.does: Keeps a Grok desktop app bot and its Hermes twin profile in step through the botport CLI, with a Twins desktop page, conflict handling, restore points and a demo mode.

reads.best: Very thorough: attested external binary, secret detection, honest scope, large test suite with fake botport, demo needing no account.
reads.worst: Audience limited to Grok-app bot owners, and real use needs a separate unofficial CLI.

plugins.name: agentygg
plugins.author: RP0-undefined
plugins.does: A gateway platform that long-polls the hosted Agent'Ygg broker so agents on other harnesses can message and wake this Hermes, with a ygg tool to send messages, hand decisions to the human and fetch files.

reads.best: Strong security design: OAuth held by Hermes via credentialed_provider_request, default-deny senders, exec approvals from peers refused and decisions routed to the human.
reads.worst: By its own README sign-in fails on current Hermes 0.23.0 until an unmerged core fix lands, and it depends on a third-party hosted broker.

plugins.name: inbox-sentinel
plugins.author: eddwithers
plugins.does: Watches Gmail (read-only OAuth) or IMAP, has the model triage important mail and pushes alerts with draft replies.

reads.best: Uses Hermes-managed OAuth and secret store, read-only scope, and 12 real test files.
reads.worst: IMAP untested against real providers and the test tool advertises a deliver option it always refuses.

plugins.name: accountability-partner
plugins.author: ZK-Snarky
plugins.does: A promise-tracking plugin that stores user commitments in a local SQLite ledger, verifies completion via user replies or rule-based checks against other tools' real results, and gates user-chosen consequences (payments, app blocks) through Hermes's own tool-approval system.

reads.best: Code-enforced guardrails prevent the model from self-certifying a promise as done or exceeding user-set money/payee caps for consequences, backed by real unit tests.
reads.worst: A user can opt a promise into a 24-hour-cooloff 'locked' state that then fires a real consequence (payment or app block) without a fresh approval prompt on that specific miss.

plugins.name: aegis-gate
plugins.author: Rainyy99
plugins.does: Registers a fail-closed pre_tool_call hook that scans every tool call's arguments for EIP-712 payloads, contract execution (checked on Sourcify) and injected instructions, then blocks it, escalates it to human approval or allows it.

reads.best: A real guard that only a plugin can add: it classifies calls by content, caps its time budget inside Hermes's callback timeout, escalates rather than allows on error, and ships per-gate tests and an SSRF fetch guard.
reads.worst: Its value is mostly for agents that touch EVM wallets, its injection scoring is heuristic, and as its README admits, a WARN is auto-approved on unattended surfaces (cron, --yolo).

plugins.name: lazy-plugin
plugins.author: RegeneratusLabs
plugins.does: Desktop page and lazyplugin_create tool where your agent drafts a spec, four fixed templates generate a new plugin, and the page validates, contract-checks and test-dispatches each tool.

reads.best: A plugin that builds, validates and grades Hermes plugins, with about 106 tests, secret-store keys in generated code and a designed Desktop page.
reads.worst: The README says templates can't carry injected code, but the raw title/description goes into a generated docstring that create() imports in-process, so a description with triple quotes can run code.

plugins.name: nerdit
plugins.author: lwi00
plugins.does: Deploys folders the agent builds as supervised local Docker services with URLs through the Nerdit engine and warns the agent when one goes down.

reads.best: Gives Hermes persistent self-hosting with outage alerts, a pre_tool_call guard and a CI-run test against a fake engine.
reads.worst: The guard is a fixed name list that misses stop_service and pass-through nerdit_call, the child engine inherits every host env var including API keys, and an injected hint steers the agent away from other hosts.

plugins.name: hermes-microduck
plugins.author: arcabotai
plugins.does: Lets Hermes inspect and operate a simulated Microduck robot through ten tools backed by a mock or a separately run MuJoCo policy server.

reads.best: A polished and novel agent/robotics demo with real-policy simulation, a human-clearable e-stop, a fail-closed motion interlock, screenshots, and focused tests.
reads.worst: It is simulation-only, while its full backend requires a separately installed simulator and downloaded assets.

plugins.name: k6pane
plugins.author: fozagtx
plugins.does: Generates, fences, runs, stores, summarizes, and compares local Grafana k6 load tests from Hermes tools.

reads.best: This is a production-minded local testing integration with target/IP fencing, explicit resource caps, secret-scope handling, result comparison, and unit plus real-k6 end-to-end tests.
reads.worst: It requires a separately installed k6 binary and is intentionally constrained to locally reachable or owner-allowlisted targets.

plugins.name: time-machine
plugins.author: Prasad-PingFederate
plugins.does: Captures workspace snapshots around tool calls and offers diff, diagnosis, and restoration through tools and UIs.

reads.best: The private Git store, timeline surfaces, and targeted rollback offer a substantial agent workflow upgrade.
reads.worst: The dashboard restore API defaults user_approved to true, so its claimed human approval boundary is not enforced by that route.

plugins.name: zambo-receipts
plugins.author: zambodotdev
plugins.does: Journals Hermes tool calls and creates public, verifiable Zambo session receipts.

reads.best: It uses lifecycle hooks, hash-only journaling by default, bounded durable retry buffering, and tests its receipt lifecycle.
reads.worst: Automatic journaling and wrapping send session metadata to an external service and publish a receipt by default, making its value dependent on a third party and careful user configuration.

plugins.name: hindsight-curator
plugins.author: trenthalden
plugins.does: Bulk scan, dry-run plan, invalidate and roll back stale Hindsight memories from chat tools or a Desktop page.

reads.best: Safe dry-run plan plus journal-based restore, fake-server e2e tests and a Desktop page.
reads.worst: Depends on a Hindsight server, and one screenshot file is a stub placeholder.

plugins.name: external-agents
plugins.author: NomieC
plugins.does: Routes ordinary Hermes delegation to an external AGY agent through a paired process-provider plugin.

reads.best: Native delegation routing, bounded process supervision and a durable job fence address lifecycle and accidental replay rather than merely wrapping a prompt.
reads.worst: It requires a separately installed companion and vendor login, cannot relay vendor approval prompts, and does not enforce Hermes tool restrictions inside AGY.

plugins.name: lampstand
plugins.author: vincitamore
plugins.does: Maintains shared project memory and rules in a git repository, with native task tools, subagent context, a Desktop cockpit, and optional rooms and scheduled jobs.

reads.best: Shared task records, git history, constitution projections, and room wakeups connect persistent user context across sessions, subagents, and Desktop.
reads.worst: The pinned release reads Hermes .env directly, forwards the gateway environment to external Agora code, and lets newly edited scheduled jobs run without renewed operator approval.

plugins.name: hermes-witness
plugins.author: BenCoy09
plugins.does: Grades newly written Hermes skills against tool outcomes and user constraints, quarantines weak skills, and records later usage outcomes in a hash-chained ledger.

reads.best: Native hooks connect skill creation and later use to a local evidence trail, with reversible quarantine and regression tests for the main grading and recovery paths.
reads.worst: The error matcher treats "0 failed" as failure and the constraint matcher can flag "never git push main", so the default gate can quarantine valid skills.

plugins.name: dead-drop
plugins.author: KMX415
plugins.does: Exchanges bounded questions, answers and acknowledgments between approved agents through a private GitHub mailbox [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KMX415/dead-drop-hermes/40c1551a9ed8b9d8fc15b481fdf2f4fc746487c6/plugin/runtime.py) [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KMX415/dead-drop-hermes/40c1551a9ed8b9d8fc15b481fdf2f4fc746487c6/plugin/engine/github.mjs).

reads.best: A durable SQLite ledger preserves exact retry payloads, enforces message and attempt budgets, and links answers before acknowledging questions [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KMX415/dead-drop-hermes/40c1551a9ed8b9d8fc15b481fdf2f4fc746487c6/plugin/runtime.py).
reads.worst: The GitHub transport rewrites a single mailbox JSON document capped at 750,000 bytes, after which further writes require archiving [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KMX415/dead-drop-hermes/40c1551a9ed8b9d8fc15b481fdf2f4fc746487c6/plugin/engine/github.mjs).

plugins.name: clean-exit
plugins.author: ladyFaye1998
plugins.does: Tracks newly created files in a selected Windows session folder and offers reviewed archiving and restoration [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ladyFaye1998/hermes-clean-exit/1df8501113e5a195fef3794e660ac3839900987f/clean_exit/plugin.py) [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ladyFaye1998/hermes-clean-exit/1df8501113e5a195fef3794e660ac3839900987f/clean_exit/review.py).

reads.best: Archiving checks recorded bytes and file identity, refuses occupied destinations, and records the destination before moving files so interrupted work remains recoverable [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ladyFaye1998/hermes-clean-exit/1df8501113e5a195fef3794e660ac3839900987f/clean_exit/review.py).
reads.worst: Tracking only observes Windows write_file calls, leaving files produced by shell commands or other editing tools outside its cleanup workflow [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ladyFaye1998/hermes-clean-exit/1df8501113e5a195fef3794e660ac3839900987f/clean_exit/plugin.py).

plugins.name: loshify
plugins.author: iHeavyShoes
plugins.does: Curates Spotify playlists from listening history and proposed tracks while filtering dislikes, duplicates and recent repeats [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iHeavyShoes/loshify/4e247cb54f81264107f2cca2d30ad9510b6abf94/core/curate.py).

reads.best: Track proposals must resolve against Spotify search results and pass taste filters, and refreshes refuse playlists absent from its own managed-playlist ledger [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iHeavyShoes/loshify/4e247cb54f81264107f2cca2d30ad9510b6abf94/core/curate.py).
reads.worst: Creating and filling a playlist are separate operations, so a fill failure can leave an empty playlist and retrying in new mode creates another [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iHeavyShoes/loshify/4e247cb54f81264107f2cca2d30ad9510b6abf94/core/curate.py).

plugins.name: hermes-axioma
plugins.author: percyhendrux123-prog
plugins.does: Renders accessible inline risk signals and stages advisory cards inside Hermes approval prompts.

reads.best: Binds cards to exact tool arguments and uses fresh approval keys, with extensive malformed-markup and accessibility tests.
reads.worst: Risk classification and signal placement remain partly model-driven, and the shell parser cannot see destructive actions hidden inside scripts or nested commands.

plugins.name: vibeline
plugins.author: wsbatlp
plugins.does: Visualizes agent sessions and tool timelines across TUI, CLI, and web, with feedback and rewind/retry controls.

reads.best: Makes real session and subagent work inspectable and adds guarded rewind through Hermes APIs with token and origin checks.
reads.worst: Multi-machine access carries session-control authority over plain HTTP, and rewinding conversation state cannot undo files already changed.

plugins.name: hermes-model-board
plugins.author: driptothebone
plugins.does: Adds a phone-friendly dashboard for previewing and confirming model-route and reasoning-effort changes across local Hermes profiles.

reads.best: Single-use expiring previews, revision checks, explicit confirmation and per-profile readback protect bulk model-setting edits.
reads.worst: It depends on private, version-sensitive host authentication and config APIs, supports only in-process local-file dashboards, and ships no automated tests.

plugins.name: abeyance
plugins.author: 0xkinno
plugins.does: Parks risky scheduled tool calls, keeps a persistent ledger, and resumes the exact call through Hermes approval after owner and drift checks. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xkinno/abeyance/4e8ddabfa8e2a000418df97886ed58d1f9257a0b/README.md)

reads.best: It materially improves unattended Hermes work with deterministic approval cards, owner checks, expiry, replay protection and focused adversarial tests.
reads.worst: Its --local filter-driver check misses included Git config before host-side git status, allowing repo-controlled filters to execute outside the agent sandbox; see [pinned drift code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xkinno/abeyance/4e8ddabfa8e2a000418df97886ed58d1f9257a0b/abeyance/drift.py).

plugins.name: hermes-chrome
plugins.author: whoisdhana
plugins.does: Lets Hermes control a paired logged-in Chrome across chat channels, with visible actions, human handoff, workflow recording and extraction/export tools. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whoisdhana/hermes-chrome/b47cc7300bd4391cf125f5c9e4be50bb9e3475bb/README.md)

reads.best: It brings the user’s real browser to their Hermes agent, with isolated tab groups, extension-owned approval windows, revocable pairing and real-extension browser tests.
reads.worst: It imports aiohttp without declaring it, so a minimal install can fail to load, and its tailscale child inherits provider secrets; see [hub code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whoisdhana/hermes-chrome/b47cc7300bd4391cf125f5c9e4be50bb9e3475bb/hub.py) and [manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whoisdhana/hermes-chrome/b47cc7300bd4391cf125f5c9e4be50bb9e3475bb/plugin.yaml).

plugins.name: liv
plugins.author: demos-ra
plugins.does: Replaces the memory provider with folder-specific local transcript tables and an agent-written RDF knowledge graph, with automatic overviews and retrieval tools.

reads.best: The actual memory-provider lifecycle preserves exact words across sessions and connects graph concepts back to their originating turns without a network service.
reads.worst: Graph validation and append are not one locked transaction, transcript books are written separately, and retrieval repeatedly loads whole growing files despite paginated output.

plugins.name: assetrizz
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Searches a bundled game-art catalog and composes, previews and exports layered 2D scenes using verified assets fetched on demand.

reads.best: Combines searchable art, deterministic scene composition, layout diagnostics and a Desktop pane with hash-verified, bounded downloads.
reads.worst: The README and PR explicitly disclose that the Desktop pane has not been proven on a live Hermes Desktop host.

plugins.name: privacy-shield
plugins.author: MOTHR
plugins.does: Pseudonymizes detected personal data in outgoing user messages and model reasoning, restores approved-channel replies and provides audit and Desktop controls.

reads.best: Request middleware, reasoning-intake hooks and session-scoped reversible tokens address privacy at several real Hermes lifecycle seams with broad regression coverage.
reads.worst: The pinned code still reads PRIVACY_SHIELD_KEY_FILE outside Hermes secret scope, disables shielding when a key is absent, and documents unmasked core summary calls despite broad compliance claims.

plugins.name: birdie
plugins.author: koshikraj
plugins.does: Connects each Hermes conversation to a local agent message bus, supporting addressed messages, replies, inboxes and opt-in wake delivery.

reads.best: Conversation-specific routing, compaction/deletion handling, acknowledgement after delivery and cancellation-aware waits go well beyond an MCP messaging wrapper ([code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koshikraj/birdie/fa9c7a13bd7733ec990942a835b915d0ab21cd28/integrations/hermes/__init__.py), [tests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koshikraj/birdie/fa9c7a13bd7733ec990942a835b915d0ab21cd28/integrations/hermes/test_plugin.py)).
reads.worst: It requires a separate running bus and setup step; conversations become reachable only after a turn and again need a turn after restart, limiting always-on availability ([lifecycle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koshikraj/birdie/fa9c7a13bd7733ec990942a835b915d0ab21cd28/integrations/hermes/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: phoenix
plugins.author: Ratz00007
plugins.does: Journals tool-call intents and outcomes in SQLite and offers explicit crash recovery, optional deduplication and a fault-injection report interface.

reads.best: A durable per-tool ledger and native execution middleware target the important ambiguity between a side effect and its recorded result.
reads.worst: core.py marks an operation recovered whenever any fingerprinted target changed, so a partial or unrelated write can be mistaken for full completion despite the exactly-once claims.

plugins.name: prevent-this-next-time
plugins.author: AceVikings
plugins.does: Enforces chat-managed block or owner-approval rules on configured connector writes, staging exact requests for one-shot release from a Telegram DM.

reads.best: Owner identity checks, canonical destinations and crash-resistant approval claims give real enforcement rather than a model’s promise to ask first.
reads.worst: Preventing alternate write paths requires a dedicated restrictive profile and a separate launcher tied to Hermes 0.23.1 internals, with manual connector declarations.

plugins.name: glassbox
plugins.author: rkfshakti
plugins.does: Adds a macOS Seatbelt terminal backend with filesystem and network policies, file-tool preflight checks, and local audit reports.

reads.best: Extends Hermes at the terminal-provider layer so shell and file tools share containment, with inspection commands, a self-test, and an HTML audit timeline.
reads.worst: provider.py writes profile.sb inside run_dir and passes that same directory as writable scratch to the policy, allowing a sandboxed command to alter the profile reused for subsequent commands.

plugins.name: hermes-android
plugins.author: TechFlipsi
plugins.does: Controls a paired Android device through 58 tools and a self-hosted relay with a Kotlin companion app.

reads.best: Provides extensive physical-device capabilities, phone-side capability gates, human approval for selected risky tools, and regression tests that reject gated macro steps.
reads.worst: The shipped android_relay.py loads ANDROID_AGENT_TOKEN_* credentials from relay-config.json rather than Hermes secrets; setup docs also mix stale tool counts and German instructions.

plugins.name: calm-mode
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Scores user frustration from message text and, past a threshold, injects careful-mode guidance and holds risky commands and extra file edits until the user agrees.

reads.best: Enforces caution in a pre_tool_call hook instead of only prompting, with no model calls and tests.
reads.worst: Keyword heuristics for frustration are crude and can misfire.

plugins.name: svault
plugins.author: Nifemi0
plugins.does: Encrypts sensitive JSON database fields at rest, redacts them on agent reads, blocks tools from reading the keys and reveals one value only with local human approval.

reads.best: Real X25519+AES-GCM encryption, a pre_tool_call guard on key files, local-only reveal and CI tests.
reads.worst: Keys live in a ~/.svault folder rather than Hermes's secret store, and the guard can be turned off by an env var.

plugins.name: write-gate
plugins.author: 2vic1
plugins.does: A pre_tool_call hook that blocks file writes with invalid JSON/TOML/Python, NUL bytes, oversized content or broken user regex contracts and returns a precise error to the model.

reads.best: Deterministic enforcement inside the tool loop that handles patch fragments carefully so they are not falsely rejected, with about 50 tests.
reads.worst: Only a few syntaxes are checked, and it matches tool names and argument keys by guesswork, so it can miss write tools it does not recognise.

plugins.name: hermes-t3sidebar
plugins.author: V1rgul
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop session sidebar with working-state shelves, drafts, project controls, usage charts and account-limit forecasts.

reads.best: Extensive session-management UI and cross-client state address everyday Hermes workflow friction, backed by broad frontend and backend tests.
reads.worst: The pinned sampler directly reads Claude Code .credentials.json outside Hermes secret routes and relies on many private core interfaces, despite disclosing those deviations.

plugins.name: pugin
plugins.author: ShawnCRMer
plugins.does: Shows a Desktop companion tracking the focused chat, subagents, processes and linked Kanban work, with attention nudges and confirmed stop controls.

reads.best: Turns the pet into an actionable job monitor using session-qualified runtime reads, read-only Kanban queries and explicit confirmation before stopping work.
reads.worst: No tests are shipped at the pinned commit despite nontrivial polling, session ownership, stale-state and interruption logic.

plugins.name: launch-desk
plugins.author: baseddesigner
plugins.does: Builds an approved launch pack with ranked post references, mechanically checked copy, branded images, optional video, and consented Hermes check-ins. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/README.md)

reads.best: The implemented workflow preserves the founder's own words, exposes failed checks, exports usable media, and schedules reminders only after an explicit Yes. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/launch_desk/wizard.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/README.md)
reads.worst: Its niche value depends on posts.design for fresh references and a separate renderer for finished video; deterministic copy checks cannot establish that every prose claim is true. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/launch_desk/wizard.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posts-design/hermes-launch-desk/745208481188ebad236eb5dc8f9291fecc7aad22/README.md)

plugins.name: gambit
plugins.author: itsflownium
plugins.does: Adds chess play and coaching through a terminal board, chat tools, and Desktop, with local engine analysis and public-game replay. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsflownium/gambit-hackathon/9c725ad0b04c2bc32f16efd00dfc1b4d421360cb/README.md)

reads.best: The code validates legal moves, guards against stale asynchronous replies, and tests a deadline fallback so a stalled model cannot make a second late move. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsflownium/gambit-hackathon/9c725ad0b04c2bc32f16efd00dfc1b4d421360cb/README.md)
reads.worst: It needs a separately installed Stockfish and a working model for conversational coaching, and the documented verified catalog scope is macOS only. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsflownium/gambit-hackathon/9c725ad0b04c2bc32f16efd00dfc1b4d421360cb/README.md)

plugins.name: ask-ledger
plugins.author: bhaskarduvvuri
plugins.does: Captures user asks and todos in a durable local log and reminds the agent of unresolved work across sessions.

reads.best: Automatic capture, user-only closure, persistent reminders and shared-chat privacy handling solve a real agent memory gap.
reads.worst: The append-only plaintext ledger grows indefinitely and shared-chat ownership has a documented timing ambiguity.

plugins.name: focus
plugins.author: Kattegat-crew
plugins.does: Routes each turn to relevant memory and skills through a pre-inference hook and injects selected context.

reads.best: It integrates intent triage, skill indexing, memory retrieval and per-turn receipts into the Hermes context path.
reads.worst: The advertised 250 ms deadline is not enforced around synchronous model calls, so the default router can delay a turn.

plugins.name: spendwarden
plugins.author: matrixneoaiagent
plugins.does: Checks payment-shaped tool calls against local spending policy and stores manually reported payment receipts.

reads.best: Deterministic budget checks, x402 decoding and an idempotent SQLite receipt ledger are implemented with focused tests.
reads.worst: Default mode only observes, policy errors pass through by default, and recorded spend depends on a separate tool call.

plugins.name: fractal-memory-engine
plugins.author: pCwOrM
plugins.does: Persists three rings of local text memory, recalls them with lexical heuristics, and injects matching memories into Hermes turns.

reads.best: It changes ongoing Hermes context with persistent local memory and includes tool and hook tests for the core memory flow.
reads.worst: The implementation's custom resonance scheme is not meaningfully validated for retrieval quality, and the README is diluted by extensive unrelated material.

plugins.name: call-recorder
plugins.author: jacebenson
plugins.does: Records a call (browser mic, or mic plus system audio on a local or SSH-reachable Linux/Windows machine), transcribes it with faster-whisper and lists recordings and transcripts in a Desktop pane with a composer record button.

reads.best: A full Desktop product (composer button, status chip, pane, screenshots) with about 175 tests, path confinement, upload limits and subprocess timeouts.
reads.worst: It registers no agent tools at all and leans on passwordless SSH, ffmpeg and a remote faster-whisper install; macOS system-audio capture is not implemented, and it records both sides of a call with no consent prompt.

plugins.name: caduceus-governance
plugins.author: Epistetechnician
plugins.does: Hooks skill_manage and the skills tree to judge what the agent writes into its own skills, keeping a tamper-evident ledger and reverting or holding unadmitted writes, especially after untrusted web/MCP content entered the session.

reads.best: A serious, deterministic guard on self-modifying skills: fail-closed enforce mode, provenance quarantine after untrusted input, sandboxed operator checks, and 340 tests in the repo.
reads.worst: The catalog folder ships only hooks and UI: the caduceus CLI its README tells operators to use (status, release-effect, device-add) lives outside the plugin folder, the folder itself has no tests, and the jargon-heavy docs make it hard to adopt.

plugins.name: hermes-chronos
plugins.author: DevTarlow
plugins.does: Snapshots the workspace into a private shadow git repo before risky tools (write_file, patch, terminal, execute_code) run, with tools, a /chronos command and a Desktop pane to diff and roll back.

reads.best: Practical undo for agent edits: argv-only git with timeouts, model-initiated rollback routed through Hermes approval, and a readable Desktop pane.
reads.worst: The manifest and README promise 'speculative branching' that no code implements, there are only 29 tests in 2 files, and it overlaps Hermes's own rewind.

plugins.name: onbrief
plugins.author: faze39
plugins.does: A pre_tool_call hook that checks outbound post text against a campaign rules file (hashtags, banned words and patterns, X-weighted length, links, near-duplicates) and blocks the call with a fix for each failing rule.

reads.best: It enforces what a prompt can only ask for: rules are validated on load and fail closed when broken, with 22 unit tests plus a real Hermes-loop e2e test and a block/approve/warn mode.
reads.worst: A niche (social campaign managers), and it only guards tools whose names and argument fields match its globs.

plugins.name: hermes-visual-memory
plugins.author: majorminorlabs
plugins.does: Watches a desk through an Echo Show camera (Hermes Eye) and remembers objects over time to answer what changed or where something was last seen.

reads.best: Novel persistent visual memory with local change detection, ~150 tests and before/after screenshots.
reads.worst: Needs a specific Echo Show running a companion app, and reads the Eye token from a file as a fallback instead of only the secret store.

plugins.name: recall
plugins.author: memeshee
plugins.does: Keeps a private on-device SQLite FTS5 index of the user's documents and uses a pre_llm_call hook to put likely matching files in front of the model, with five tools and an @recall: reference.

reads.best: It fills a real gap (finding the file in ~/Downloads) entirely offline, with a secret denylist, symlink and decompression-bomb guards, 30 stdlib tests and an honest-limits section.
reads.worst: recall_forget only deletes index rows, so the session-start refresh brings a forgotten folder back, and recall_open reads any non-denylisted absolute path up to 64 MB, even outside the indexed roots.

plugins.name: htmi
plugins.author: Thamirawaran
plugins.does: Lets people pin review comments to exact parts of HTML/Markdown documents the agent writes, notifies Hermes of new comments each turn, and lets it make checked edits and replies via 11 tools, a /htmi command and a dashboard Review tab.

reads.best: A fresh workflow: reviewing agent-written HTML on the page itself, with a localhost-only, token-protected review server, stale-edit refusal and human-only resolution.
reads.worst: The work runs in a 70k-line bundled Node engine (htmi.mjs) whose source is elsewhere in the repo. Only 5 tests cover the plugin, and the GitHub publish/pull tools have none.

plugins.name: autorag
plugins.author: vkehfdl1
plugins.does: Bundles an AutoRAG Lite MCP server and skills so Hermes can search local files and Slack/Discord/Telegram/email archives with cited evidence, plus a Desktop search pane.

reads.best: Local-first hybrid retrieval over many chat/mail archives and Korean HWP files, with setup/schedule/automate skills and a Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Launches an unpinned-transitive npx download of a large package and about 1.5 GB of models, with remote npm allowed; setup is heavy and the plugin itself contains little verifiable code.

plugins.name: signet-drive
plugins.author: craczkow
plugins.does: Gives the agent its own encrypted Signet Drive (save, fetch, list, restore through the signet CLI) and backs up MEMORY.md and USER.md automatically after memory writes.

reads.best: Memory backup through post_tool_call and session hooks, a restore that saves the current state first, no credential held by the plugin, and 73 tests against a fake client.
reads.worst: signet_drive_save will upload any local file the agent names, with no path allow-list; the 'read-only' /files route can create a share and blocks the event loop; macOS only.

plugins.name: live2d-rigger
plugins.author: flabanabba8
plugins.does: Tools to generate, layer, rig, compile and motion-preview Live2D characters with the user's own Umamo/Cubism toolchain.

reads.best: Genuinely novel creative pipeline with honest 'experimental' caveats and about 49 tests.
reads.worst: Needs a heavy self-installed toolchain (Umamo, JDK 21, Cubism SDK, Playwright, ffmpeg); tiny audience.

plugins.name: babelaz-pareto-aaa
plugins.author: fonminer
plugins.does: /aaa builds a small web game in rounds, checks it in a real Playwright browser and has a model judge it until it scores 8/10.

reads.best: Real browser checks (FPS, page errors, axe) gate each round, with honest documented run results.
reads.worst: Narrow use case, heavy Playwright dependency and long expensive runs; self-judging by same model.

plugins.name: bonsai-garden
plugins.author: thehangingforest
plugins.does: A Desktop-only page that draws a pixel-art garden with one bonsai per agent profile, showing busy state, cost and cron routines, and lets the user open or interrupt an agent.

reads.best: Original artwork wired to real per-profile Desktop SDK state, honest 'Unavailable' fallbacks and 25 node tests including a build-matches-source check.
reads.worst: Mostly decorative value, Linux-only with a manual copy deploy, and a README that reads like internal notes with a local /home path.

plugins.name: eta
plugins.author: FrederickSonsAI
plugins.does: A deterministic statistical ETA calculator for agent/kanban/cron work that tracks run history in a local SQLite file and computes likely/worst-case time ranges with percentile and queueing math.

reads.best: No network calls, shell commands, or credentials at all; opens Hermes's own kanban/cron/session databases strictly read-only (mode=ro, query_only pragma), and the README is candid about its own limitations and past bugs found via backtesting.
reads.worst: The underlying feature category (time estimation for work queues) is fairly common, and there is no visual/UI polish (no screenshots, no desktop UI) despite thorough text documentation.

plugins.name: taskreel
plugins.author: SuryaXyz-art
plugins.does: Records tool calls into named SQLite routines and replays their exact arguments through Hermes tool dispatch with checkpoints.

reads.best: Model-free replay with stop-on-failure checkpoints turns completed agent work into reusable automation.
reads.worst: Replay bypasses other plugins’ pre-tool hooks, and saved exact arguments can retain secrets.

plugins.name: yuanbao
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Moves Hermes’ Yuanbao messaging adapter and its group, DM, and sticker tools into a standalone platform plugin.
