reads.best: The migration preserves existing tool names while testing secret scope, backpressure, and platform registration.
reads.worst: It serves one messaging platform and is a migration of existing Hermes functionality rather than a new agent capability.

plugins.name: minicpm-ocr
plugins.author: PovedaAqui
plugins.does: Adds OCR, asynchronous document jobs, verification scoring, and a persistent human review queue across hosted and local MiniCPM-OCR deployments.

reads.best: The read-score-reread-human-gate workflow directly addresses silent OCR errors instead of merely exposing an OCR endpoint.
reads.worst: The useful local document pipeline has substantial external model, GPU, and service setup complexity, while the hosted path remains a remote dependency.

plugins.name: hermes-decay-context
plugins.author: nimbus7772017
plugins.does: Replaces context compression with eviction and rolling digests, and reinjects stored operator directives through a pre-model hook.

reads.best: A real context-engine extension preserves recent tool-call structure and includes tested pruning and deterministic digest fallbacks.
reads.worst: Fresh installs have no wired pin-capture path, and optional router sizing reads an API key directly from config.yaml instead of Hermes’s secret scope.

plugins.name: hermes-committee
plugins.author: abualnassr
plugins.does: Runs several models through independent answers, anonymous peer review, and a chairman synthesis, with a Desktop interface and exportable reports.

reads.best: Its [deliberation engine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abualnassr/hermes-committee/c7ed1b63feee39185aed90eac0d0f9185109e959/committee/engine.py) implements concurrent independent answers, randomized anonymous reviews, quorum checks, and a separate synthesis stage.
reads.worst: The chat tool's [evidence loader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abualnassr/hermes-committee/c7ed1b63feee39185aed90eac0d0f9185109e959/__init__.py) reads model-supplied local paths directly with no allowed-root or Hermes file-approval check, allowing sensitive files to enter model evidence.

plugins.name: bulk
plugins.author: sniperchief
plugins.does: Runs one instruction independently over files, CSV rows, or JSON records as resumable background jobs with SQLite state and exports.

reads.best: Its [job engine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sniperchief/Bulk/99a3f1780de549ac1c0a0e878b29f6d8d248be4a/jobs.py) rechecks source hashes before processing, retries transient failures with shared rate-limit backoff, and recovers claims left by dead workers.
reads.worst: Its [recovery contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sniperchief/Bulk/99a3f1780de549ac1c0a0e878b29f6d8d248be4a/jobs.py) is at least once: a crash after a billed model response but before saving it can cause the same item to run and be billed again.

plugins.name: live-translate
plugins.author: WestWaters
plugins.does: Adds local speech recognition, translation, cloned-voice output, captions, and call-audio routing controlled through Hermes tools and a companion app. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WestWaters/hermes-live-translator/315085f89fc675b119e1a412ef38873c1365c6da/README.md)

reads.best: The implemented multi-process audio pipeline, hardware-aware setup, model routing, and finished companion UI substantially extend local hardware use. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WestWaters/hermes-live-translator/315085f89fc675b119e1a412ef38873c1365c6da/README.md)
reads.worst: The loopback server serves its control token without validating Host and compares Origin to the supplied Host, leaving DNS-rebinding protection incomplete; real-time performance was not exercised in this read-only review. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WestWaters/hermes-live-translator/315085f89fc675b119e1a412ef38873c1365c6da/live_translate/server.py)

plugins.name: uniichat-recall
plugins.author: DevvGwardo
plugins.does: Replaces Hermes memory with an append-only conversation log, summary tree and evidence-bearing recall tools.

reads.best: Integrates with the memory-provider lifecycle and returns original records with session IDs and excerpt offsets rather than only lossy summaries.
reads.worst: Setup guidance is thin, Windows cannot load its fcntl store, and absolute zero-hallucination claims exceed a lexical matcher plus optional generated answers.

plugins.name: holdings
plugins.author: ShepShepDev
plugins.does: Adds a read-only Desktop portfolio and activity workspace with exchange and wallet connectors, evidence-linked chat and encrypted review storage.

reads.best: A substantial Desktop workflow combines original-record evidence, explicit private-model opt-in, human-confirmed transfer suggestions and security regression tests without moving funds.
reads.worst: Protected reviews need an external vault secret and in-process loading, while live exchange matching and complete history coverage are explicitly limited.

plugins.name: gmi-nexus
plugins.author: Joystonm
plugins.does: Adds GMI Cloud model discovery, task routing, benchmarking, multimodal generation and development tools with a dashboard and spend controls.

reads.best: Broad readable implementation combines real tool dispatch, scoped secrets, approval hooks, recovery tests and a documented demo and dashboard.
reads.worst: BudgetGuard.daily_spend returns zero on storage errors, weakening the advertised hard daily cap, while goal planning largely uses fixed templates and clause splitting rather than general adaptive planning.

plugins.name: branchpoint
plugins.author: Sahil-SS9
plugins.does: Explores alternative coding plans, builds selected routes in Git worktrees, compares evidence, and supports adoption or convergence. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/hermes-branchpoint/7051eda3b968b90602c3c183c45f97f72153d8f7/README.md)

reads.best: Real worktree builds, reversible adoption and evidence-linked blind comparisons extend the agent's development workflow substantially. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/hermes-branchpoint/7051eda3b968b90602c3c183c45f97f72153d8f7/README.md)
reads.worst: The mypy availability probe runs unsandboxed with the route worktree as its working directory, allowing route-written mypy.py code to execute on the host. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/hermes-branchpoint/7051eda3b968b90602c3c183c45f97f72153d8f7/checks.py)

plugins.name: model-explainer
plugins.author: tuancookiez-hub
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop model-comparison page, benchmark/cost charts, local usage statistics and a guarded model-switch button. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tuancookiez-hub/hermes-model-explainer/4b876bb5021c56fe14e14a15d4e379b5e6506c9e/desktop/plugin.js)

reads.best: It integrates the real model picker with sourced comparison data, an offline fallback and explicit confirmation for guarded model switches. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tuancookiez-hub/hermes-model-explainer/4b876bb5021c56fe14e14a15d4e379b5e6506c9e/desktop/plugin.js)
reads.worst: Measured speed and spend are aggregated by normalized model ID without separating providers, so one provider's measurements can affect another's comparison. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tuancookiez-hub/hermes-model-explainer/4b876bb5021c56fe14e14a15d4e379b5e6506c9e/desktop/plugin.js)

plugins.name: lookahead
plugins.author: ericklindberg
plugins.does: Captures upcoming commitments from chat and schedules preparation briefs and one follow-up, with optional read-only calendars.

reads.best: Durable reservations, operator binding, quiet hours, STOP and forget handling make proactive assistance substantially more than a reminder prompt.
reads.worst: Same-day extraction is explicitly unreliable in the documented small trial, and the private ICS URL is read from plain plugin config rather than Hermes secret scope.

plugins.name: mem-diffs
plugins.author: daji-dev
plugins.does: Shows memory, skill and background self-improvement edits as session-linked Desktop diffs captured around existing Hermes tools.

reads.best: Middleware makes Hermes persistent-context changes inspectable, strips display fields from model requests and tests profile/session isolation and deletion.
reads.worst: The README supplies no installation walkthrough, click-to-revert is still TODO, and stored full diffs remain visible to compaction despite conversational-request cleanup.

plugins.name: hermes-psfn-avatar
plugins.author: axAilotl
plugins.does: Adds a reactive 3D VRM avatar, motion studio and optional PSFN emotion synchronization to Desktop and Dashboard.

reads.best: Real skeletal motion playback, mood envelopes, avatar uploads and lifecycle integration go well beyond a decorative prompt.
reads.worst: The authenticated PSFN bridge validates only the initial loopback URL and uses default redirect-following urllib, leaving a potential bearer-token leak through a redirected endpoint.

plugins.name: idle-compact
plugins.author: npetroff24
plugins.does: Schedules background context compaction before model cache expiry and replays the captured request to seek warm-cache summaries.

reads.best: Addresses a widespread latency and token-cost problem with model-aware timers, persistent deadlines, savings accounting and targeted tests.
reads.worst: The pinned warm path reads agent.api_key and sends its own authenticated HTTP requests instead of Hermes credential routing, an explicitly unresolved admission blocker; it also depends heavily on private core APIs.

plugins.name: gmi-speech
plugins.author: zkasuran
plugins.does: Registers GMI Cloud as a Hermes TTS provider, mapping speech models and voice/format options through GMI queue APIs and downloading audio.

reads.best: Native TTS integration uses profile-scoped secrets, schema-aware validation, bounded polling, no automatic paid-job retries and offline transport/provider tests.
reads.worst: Requires paid GMI service, lacks streaming and voice-bubble support, and invokes chargeable generation without a separate approval prompt.

plugins.name: inference-exchange
plugins.author: qzyu999
plugins.does: Starts an opt-in local Inference Exchange provider while Hermes CLI is idle, then drains it before user inference, with pause and status controls.

reads.best: Lifecycle hooks, bounded draining, process-tree cleanup, scoped credentials and restricted child environments make idle hardware sharing more than a skill.
reads.worst: Setup needs a separate IE environment, model and llama-server, while tests use mock inference and production GPU behavior and alpha coordinator availability remain unverified.

plugins.name: agent-inception
plugins.author: ethanwiegert
plugins.does: Lets Hermes inhabit and modify a voxel island through MCP while the user watches in a sandboxed Desktop pane.

reads.best: The pinned repository contains a real deterministic game, an extensible content catalog and substantial simulation and relay tests.
reads.worst: The installed package does not launch the game, requires a separately running browser world, and stores bearer world links in plain settings.

plugins.name: custody
plugins.author: Parker-Fawcett
plugins.does: Resolves destructive terminal targets, estimates their blast radius and requests approval for targets classified as user-owned ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parker-Fawcett/custody/c9a6ebb882a7ddfee305c20609ad4b42fc9b801b/README.md)).

reads.best: A valuable approval-hook integration that models shell and PowerShell target expansion rather than trusting a command description.
reads.worst: Relative targets use the process cwd rather than the terminal session cwd, and missing targets pass the added guard; ownership also treats edits as creations and is not session-filtered ([resolver policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parker-Fawcett/custody/c9a6ebb882a7ddfee305c20609ad4b42fc9b801b/policy.py), [ledger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parker-Fawcett/custody/c9a6ebb882a7ddfee305c20609ad4b42fc9b801b/ledger.py), [write hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Parker-Fawcett/custody/c9a6ebb882a7ddfee305c20609ad4b42fc9b801b/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: werk
plugins.author: aaddrick
plugins.does: Runs engineering work items through builder/reviewer roles and domain-pack checks, producing a mechanical model package with an explicit gap report.

reads.best: Combines tracked work, adversarial review and validated, hash-checked CAD tool outputs while exposing unmeasured engineering gaps.
reads.worst: Its own pinned documentation admits failed reviewer calibration, checks that cannot establish some claimed requirements, and several-million-token demonstration cost.

plugins.name: antemuse
plugins.author: roosiq
plugins.does: Adds bounded walk, daydream, dream, doomscroll and unstuck states with persistent context, optional tool restrictions and a Desktop visualization.

reads.best: An unusual state engine combines concept graphs, memory-derived material, lifecycle hooks and a visual pane, with extensive state and integration tests.
reads.worst: State and optional tool restrictions are profile-wide rather than session-bound, so closing tools in one chat can affect another chat on the same profile.

plugins.name: vibeleak-atlas
plugins.author: abundantbeing
plugins.does: Provides a native Desktop workbench for approved website assessments, read-only local inspection, and unsent fix-plan drafts.

reads.best: The Desktop workflow implements explicit scope and cost consent, installation-bound receipts, redacted drafts, and bounded native folder inspection.
reads.worst: Website assessments require a paid VibeLeak owner key; local checks are limited static patterns, and native acceptance is Windows-only.

plugins.name: meridian
plugins.author: unifyWeb3
plugins.does: Discovers lifecycle state machines in Python and JavaScript-family code and checks accepted transition specs with source anchors and an audit ledger.

reads.best: Provides deterministic source-linked checks, CI exit codes, edit-time advice, and a hash-chained ledger without a model or network.
reads.worst: The Python analyzer treats equality inside OR conditions as a state guard and identifies fields by name without receiver identity, so its claim of authoritative transitions exceeds the analysis.

plugins.name: commonplace
plugins.author: ChrisAaronNewton
plugins.does: Replaces Hermes memory with curated Markdown entries, lexical recall, turn journals, handover cards, and pre-compression archives.

reads.best: Integrates directly with the memory lifecycle and includes host-manager tests for checkpoint failures and profile isolation.
reads.worst: Its checkpoint preserves only user/assistant text, omitting tool results and non-text evidence, and atomic replacement is not fsynced despite the durable-archive claim.

plugins.name: glorya
plugins.author: aadilghani1
plugins.does: Integrates Glorya creative jobs with persistent chat progress, human choices, media attachments and a Desktop studio.

reads.best: Background job followers and native chat/Desktop delivery add real integration, and the pin gates ad spending and publishing on human approval.
reads.worst: It requires a paid external Glorya service, whose creative generation and campaign execution cannot be inspected in this pinned repository.

plugins.name: hermes-village
plugins.author: tuancookiez-hub
plugins.does: Runs a persistent village simulation in Hermes Desktop, with model-planned councils and free deterministic progression.

reads.best: Ships a complete interactive game, deterministic action validation, transactional saves and a council budget gate backed by broad simulation tests.
reads.worst: Its main benefit is entertainment rather than improving everyday agent work, and council budget admission relies on estimated input-token counts.

plugins.name: prompt-firewall
plugins.author: Gaijin-01
plugins.does: Quarantines regex-detected prompt injections in tool results and blocks or escalates risky tool actions through native hooks.

reads.best: Tool-result transformation plus an action gate provide deterministic enforcement that a reminder prompt cannot supply.
reads.worst: The pinned runtime tree excludes all claimed tests, and pattern matching leaves documented language, execution-path, and approval-cache gaps.

plugins.name: incognito
plugins.author: nicolasbuelvas
plugins.does: Adds ephemeral Hermes sessions with storage deletion, tool guards, prompt filtering, and optional in-memory PII masking.

reads.best: It integrates lifecycle hooks, request middleware, Desktop controls, and explicit session cleanup across Hermes surfaces.
reads.worst: Its zero-trace verifier checks live SQLite rows and named files only, so its strong forensic assurance exceeds what that code proves.

plugins.name: gogogoogle
plugins.author: josefacero
plugins.does: Delegates work to Antigravity CLI workers with per-call approval, background jobs, and a separate verifier conversation.

reads.best: Fresh approval keys, a minimal child environment, read-only role rules, verdict downgrades, and regression tests go well beyond a delegation prompt.
reads.worst: The do role bypasses Antigravity permissions after approval, while read-only checks are not OS isolation and miss ignored or already-untracked file edits.

plugins.name: ball
plugins.author: askclaw-vesper
plugins.does: Tracks which gateway chats await a person, have finished, or appear stalled, and shows an on-demand cross-chat board.

reads.best: Lifecycle hooks, group-scoped boards, bounded stored excerpts, and stale-update guards provide useful local coordination without automatic nudges.
reads.worst: Question and promise classification is heuristic, CLI/TUI chats are untracked, and reload recovery depends on a private state.db schema.

plugins.name: emotion-chip
plugins.author: 100yenadmin
plugins.does: Renders agent-authored delivery cues into Fish Audio and ElevenLabs speech through a registered TTS provider and compatibility middleware.

reads.best: Dialect-aware rendering, scoped ElevenLabs secrets, session-aware stitching, explainable cue drops, and focused transport tests add real voice functionality.
reads.worst: Full cues work on text_to_speech calls rather than ordinary spoken replies or live voice mode, and the default backend requires a separate Fish Audio plugin.

plugins.name: on-brand
plugins.author: Mhiah
plugins.does: Adds brand profiles, deterministic copy linting, model-assisted repairs, outbound posting guards and a Desktop monitoring pane.

reads.best: Three hooks put brand checks into the agent workflow, repairs are re-linted within a shared time budget, and tests include loading through Hermes PluginManager.
reads.worst: The guarantee exceeds enforcement: default reply checks require recognized fenced blocks, outbound checks depend on tool names and known text keys, and streaming is held only when explicitly enabled.

plugins.name: data-saver
plugins.author: ahmardchain
plugins.does: Forecasts command download sizes, gates expensive downloads and meters network usage against configurable data budgets.

reads.best: Registry size forecasts and approval middleware address a concrete problem for users on metered connections.
reads.worst: The ledger stores raw command or URL prefixes without redaction, potentially retaining embedded secrets; system-wide counters also limit attribution accuracy.

plugins.name: fast-chat
plugins.author: iyoda
plugins.does: Adds a CLI command that creates a fresh Hermes session with a chosen model, provider, reasoning level, and Fast or Ultrafast service tier.

reads.best: It checks the Gateway session contract and tier availability before opening a frontend, with bounded RPC/bootstrap waits and real local WebSocket tests.
reads.worst: It depends on recent Hermes Gateway APIs and websockets packaging, is verified live only on macOS, and may leave an empty session if tier validation fails.

plugins.name: delegation-scout
plugins.author: vdimarco
plugins.does: Delegation backend that routes each delegate_task run to a model route using task heuristics and recorded outcomes in SQLite, with a scout_stats tool.

reads.best: Changes how Hermes delegates (a backend plus outcome learning), stdlib only, fails closed with no routes, has unit and e2e tests.
reads.worst: Needs hand-written routes config; benefit is hard to see for most users and the heuristics are keyword-based.

plugins.name: btw-studio
plugins.author: SBMatthew
plugins.does: Desktop /btw side-channel that answers questions mid-turn without touching the transcript, plus a read-only state.db session radar, loop-guard detectors, mid-turn steering and a self-curated steer playbook.

reads.best: Genuinely deep Desktop integration (composer middleware, steer/subagent RPCs, read-only state.db radar) with a large test suite and CI.
reads.worst: Most of the work lives in an 18,000-line runtime.py and a 10,000-line plugin.js that are very hard to review, and the README leans on jargon and a cited 'arXiv:2610.14224' paper the code cannot vouch for.

plugins.name: struggle-guard
plugins.author: gisc
plugins.does: Runs teacher-armed Socratic tutoring sessions, counts student attempts, limits hints by state, screens responses, and records a teacher trail.

reads.best: It uses Hermes middleware and persistent per-session state to make hint progression and teacher reporting more than prompt instructions, with adversarial and integration coverage.
reads.worst: Its answer screening is heuristic and fail-open, and CLI streaming can reveal unscreened output unless disabled; only CLI has been verified.

plugins.name: prompt-autocomplete
plugins.author: bystac
plugins.does: Adds local-history sentence completion and a small-model fallback to the Hermes Desktop composer with directional acceptance keys.

reads.best: It extends the actual composer through SDK surfaces, with immediate local suggestions and careful stale-response handling.
reads.worst: No test suite ships, editor detection reaches into core DOM, and the model fallback rejects Arabic output despite the advertised RTL support.

plugins.name: kokpit
plugins.author: sahindemirbas
plugins.does: Maintains a local Markdown vault with chat capture, session receipts, contextual recall and source-quoted next-step proposals.

reads.best: Meaningful-result hooks and verified source quotations give users portable continuity across Hermes and other agents.
reads.worst: Calendar, weather, usage and job features depend on the separate Kokpit database, and quote presence alone does not prove a proposed next step is justified.

plugins.name: hermes-workflow
plugins.author: SaM-0777
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop graph editor and tools for reusable Python nodes and saved executable workflows.

reads.best: A substantial native visual editor, reusable node library and importable illustrated demos make workflows inspectable inside Hermes Desktop.
reads.worst: The add_node_to_workflow handler incorrectly applies the config validator to execution data, and the backend executes arbitrary node Python without isolation or a timeout; no tests are shipped.

plugins.name: piquesignal
plugins.author: 24skpz
plugins.does: Embeds a Solana memecoin research board in Hermes with charts, selected-coin context, delegated checks, spoken briefs and optional member feeds.

reads.best: The rich Desktop integration is backed by bounded, rate-limited feed clients, Hermes secret storage and extensive tests for member-data isolation.
reads.worst: Its core signal engine is a hosted dependency outside the pinned code, and many guarded private Hermes imports create maintenance risk.

plugins.name: toolrecall-light
plugins.author: whiskybeer
plugins.does: Replaces repeated tool outputs across turns with compact references and exposes a recall tool backed by local SQLite storage.

reads.best: Public result-transform and compaction hooks implement deterministic deduplication with fail-open behavior, a streak guard and focused tests.
reads.worst: The recall handler falls back from a failed session-scoped lookup to an unrestricted lookup, allowing a known result ID from another session to retrieve its stored output.

plugins.name: lean-mode
plugins.author: aoyamari
plugins.does: Delegates briefed tasks to a cheaper Hermes subagent with usage tracking, watchdog cancellation, fallback escalation and cost receipts.

reads.best: Public subagent lifecycle calls and usage hooks make model delegation, cancellation and per-run cost accounting more capable than a workflow prompt.
reads.worst: Escalation is passed the full original budget rather than the remainder, and rejected tool narrowing automatically retries with all parent tools.

plugins.name: call-your-shot
plugins.author: chadius-maximus
plugins.does: Measures the agent's predicted tool-call count and duration against hook-observed work and feeds back a persistent calibration record.

reads.best: Uses measured tool-loop activity and SQLite history to turn effort estimates into a feedback loop with no external service.
reads.worst: Participation still depends on a prompt the model can ignore, and wall-clock measurements include approval delays while excluding delegated subagent calls.

plugins.name: brownout
plugins.author: Osiyomeoh
plugins.does: Watches the host's power (pmset, sysfs or NUT UPS), alerts you on mains loss with a measured battery runway, and parks Hermes by pausing cron jobs and blocking tool calls.

reads.best: A fresh, grounded take on keeping Hermes safe on its own hardware, with 36 tests on parsers, runway maths and policy and recorded live traces.
reads.worst: A single missed power reading moves PARKED to UNKNOWN and park state is never reloaded after restart, so paused cron jobs can stay paused despite the 'every park is undone' claim.

plugins.name: codemode
plugins.author: junbo-hh
plugins.does: Adds one codemode tool where the model writes JavaScript run in a QuickJS child process that calls MCP and allowlisted tools via tools.x(), found by BM25 search.

reads.best: A compact, well-isolated sandbox (minimal env, memory cap, hard kill, call budget) that gives the model a real orchestration runtime, with 12 tests.
reads.worst: Tool dispatch runs synchronously in the parent with no deadline, so a slow or approval-waiting tool can run far past the 120 s timeout, and all MCP tools are exposed by default.

plugins.name: agent-wallet
plugins.author: BlackHelio
plugins.does: Runs a separate wallet daemon holding an encrypted keystore so the agent can request XMR/BTC/XRP/EVM payments through 23 tools that a human approves by PIN in a Desktop pane, with signed receipts.

reads.best: A serious separation of agent and keys: a daemon enforces spend policy, the PIN is never a tool argument, receipts are signed and hash-chained, and about 600 offline tests run in CI.
reads.worst: Claims run ahead of the code: the manifest says nothing is signed until a human types a PIN, yet a handed-over sandbox pays any address without asking; keys and the signer password live in the plugin's own files rather than Hermes's secret store; and a download host is assembled from string pieces to get past Hermes's install scanner.

plugins.name: basekit
plugins.author: D0xedDevi0
plugins.does: Gives Hermes six read-only tools for live Base chain facts (gas, portfolios, decoded transactions, token and allowance reads), a gated context hook, a CLI and a Desktop pane with status chip.

reads.best: Read-only by construction with no dependencies, every answer carrying its block, 114 tests with CI, and documentation that publishes a measurement showing its own hook does not save model calls.
reads.worst: It is a crypto-only niche that leans on public RPC and price endpoints, its context hook's keyword gate fires on common words such as 'base', 'swap' or 'portfolio', and its catalog pull request is closed.

plugins.name: truthgate
plugins.author: cyberNoman
plugins.does: Snapshots files before write_file/patch calls and, in a pre_verify hook, makes Hermes continue the turn if it newly introduced hollow Python functions or embedded-secret patterns.

reads.best: Deterministic, standard-library-only and fail-open, with baselines so old findings are not re-reported, secrets reduced to type/line/hash, and 24 tests across six files.
reads.worst: Narrow scope (Python stubs and a handful of regex secret shapes), no screenshots or demo, and failing open means it silently does nothing whenever a baseline is missing.

plugins.name: botsesh
plugins.author: meowsigma
plugins.does: Registers BotSesh shared rooms as a native Hermes gateway platform with OAuth through Hermes auth, SSE room streaming, peer handoffs, nine room tools and DM controls.

reads.best: A real platform adapter with 17,000 lines, 154 tests, a security policy and documented recovery paths, and sign-in handled by Hermes rather than a key file.
reads.worst: The README says this catalog build needs an unmerged Hermes PR (#151209) and that stock Hermes users should install a different version from main, it is Linux-only, and the dense 27,000-character README makes setup hard to follow.

plugins.name: proofchain
plugins.author: iamzulx
plugins.does: Records Hermes tool calls in a redacted hash chain with HMAC sealing, verification, search, and signed export for audits.

reads.best: The durable tamper-evident ledger is a concrete audit primitive with secret redaction and verification surfaces integrated at tool boundaries.
reads.worst: It largely records activity rather than improving the agent’s work, and its HMAC key lifecycle and evidence semantics deserve more external operational documentation.

plugins.name: living-field
plugins.author: abuz8studios-ship-it
plugins.does: Adds a deterministic canvas-based Hermes Desktop pane and status chip whose animation reflects the host's busy, gateway, and model state.

reads.best: The visual is unusually honest for a dashboard: it uses host state, avoids fabricated metrics and network access, and has a stable seeded field.
reads.worst: It is a narrow visualization with no agent tools, tests, or README setup beyond enabling the pane, so relatively few users need it on day one.

plugins.name: eyes
plugins.author: Agenziamaia
plugins.does: A transform_tool_result hook that finds media files a tool just wrote, measures them with ffprobe/ffmpeg, and appends a note with warnings when the output is black, frozen, empty or silent.

reads.best: A fresh idea: the agent gets measured feedback on the images, video and audio it just made, through one small, readable, fail-open hook with no network.
reads.worst: Only 5 tests (4 need ffmpeg), the README example relies on a probe.py that isn't included, and the path regex misses relative paths and paths with spaces.

plugins.name: relic-gumi
plugins.author: yuzushi-dev
plugins.does: A longitudinal AI-companion plugin that injects relational context into conversations, runs consented check-ins and proactive outreach over Telegram/Desktop, and builds a psychometric baseline of the user, stored entirely on-disk.

reads.best: Exceptionally thorough documentation (850+ line spec-like README, arXiv paper link, onboarding/porting docs) and ~60 test files covering delivery lifecycle and consent guards.
reads.worst: Reads its Telegram bot token and allowed-user-ID from a plaintext .env file in the plugin's own profile directory instead of through Hermes's secret store, which is exactly the kind of practice the catalog reviewer sends plugins back for, even though the README discloses it candidly.

plugins.name: incognito-private-mode
plugins.author: Tranquil-Flow
plugins.does: Adds request privacy flags, memory stripping, tool vetoes, coverage reporting and consent-gated cleanup of closed private sessions.

reads.best: Uses request/execution middleware and provenance-fenced deletion with extensive adversarial tests and unusually explicit coverage limits.
reads.worst: The pinned tree commits executable Python bytecode caches, including enforcement modules, violating catalog rule 17; background and MoA requests also remain outside protection.

plugins.name: stash
plugins.author: RegeneratusLabs
plugins.does: A 'read-it-later' capture-bin plugin that saves links, images and notes into a local JSON file with server-side thumbnail/title enrichment, exposed through chat tools and a Desktop sidebar UI.

reads.best: The most finished product of the batch: a full React Desktop sidebar UI, dashboard backend, screenshot, and SSRF/path-traversal hardening on its own enrichment fetches, despite its secrets-sounding name holding no credentials at all.
reads.worst: No automated test suite exists anywhere in the repository, unlike comparable entries.

plugins.name: formwork
plugins.author: ladyFaye1998
plugins.does: Adds a native Desktop workspace to fill PDF packets from source documents, review cited answers and export checked editable originals.

reads.best: Source-quote validation, explicit review, stale-result protection and saved-appearance verification make a useful document workflow unusually concrete.
reads.worst: The supported input range is narrow: printable ASCII AcroForms only, with no OCR, radio groups or signing, and retained packet data has no cleanup interface.

reads.best: The PDF engine is unusually conservative about unsupported forms, source quotes, and explicit user review before export.
reads.worst: The pinned tree lacks a manifest, README, tests, and the promised Desktop workspace implementation, making the submission incomplete as a catalog plugin.

plugins.name: artifactguard
plugins.author: Mahgal
plugins.does: Statically disassembles pickle/torch/joblib/numpy artifacts to report the globals they would invoke, with a pre_tool_call hook that blocks loads of dangerous files.

reads.best: Never unpickles: an opcode-level abstract interpreter reports exactly which callables an artifact would invoke, backed by 24 tests and a demo video.
reads.worst: The guard hook only spots load calls by regex in a fixed set of code tools, so loads phrased differently pass unchecked, and the idea overlaps existing picklescan-style scanners.

plugins.name: wavebots
plugins.author: xBuildy
plugins.does: Verifies Wave bot listings on the Theta blockchain and installs each as a locked-down Hermes profile, with a Desktop/dashboard store tab and an optional paid ask_wave call to Wave OS.

reads.best: Wave OS key read only via Hermes secret_scope, every add/update/remove/ask goes through the approval prompt and is refused in scheduled jobs, with 27 tests.
reads.worst: Serves a niche chain and store, starts a network re-check thread on load, and the README and dashboard docstring say nothing is paid or sent to Wave although ask_wave can spend TFUEL.

plugins.name: hermes-eye-memory
plugins.author: isthatananya
plugins.does: Local photo/webcam index giving the agent search, albums, duplicates, receipt extraction and recall with 16 eye_* tools.

reads.best: Fully local visual memory with no cloud upload, real tests and good docs.
reads.worst: eye_forget with delete_files can delete up to 500 original photos without a confirm, and deletion errors are counted as removed.

plugins.name: nostr
plugins.author: dadofsambonzuki
plugins.does: Platform adapter connecting Hermes to Nostr DMs and groups through a separate local daemon over a Unix socket.

reads.best: Adds a whole new messaging platform with careful fail-closed handling and scoped secrets.
reads.worst: Needs an external daemon and hand-copying the adapter into Hermes, and uses private host functions.

plugins.name: multi-chat
plugins.author: BColsey
plugins.does: Web Dashboard tab with 1 to 16 xterm panes, each attached to Hermes's own /api/pty real TUI.

reads.best: Candid README, about 72 tests across Python, vitest and Playwright, reproducible bundle with readable source in the repo, and screenshots.
reads.worst: Locked to Hermes 0.22.6 because it reads private PTY_REGISTRY internals; the PR is still open with the maintainer's change request not addressed; no Desktop plugin.

plugins.name: antigravity-acp-provider
plugins.author: rhgo1749
plugins.does: A model provider that runs Google's official antigravity-acp server as a child process and talks ACP JSON-RPC over stdio, with a pinned binary hash and a warm process pool.

reads.best: A real new model backend for Hermes with about 729 tests against a fake ACP server and CI on Linux and Windows.
reads.worst: It auto-approves the Google agent's native file edits and shell commands, bypassing Hermes terminal approval with no switch, and its own status table says real auth and inference are unverified for this release.

plugins.name: agssh
plugins.author: mosesman831
plugins.does: Registers SSH hosts as first-class Hermes tools (run command, read lines, grep, list hosts) over one persistent multiplexed connection per host, returning structured JSON instead of raw shell strings.

reads.best: 44 test functions across unit/integration/acceptance suites, a pre_tool_call guard that blocks raw ssh calls to registered hosts, and a documented private-API disclosure (docs/PUBLIC-SURFACE.md).
reads.worst: Dangerous commands route through Hermes's own approval classifier rather than the plugin forcing approval on every remote command, so safety depends on that classifier being well tuned.

plugins.name: wellness-nourish
plugins.author: davidmosiah
plugins.does: An MCP-server nutrition tracker exposed to Hermes: searches USDA/Open Food Facts/TACO food databases, estimates meals from photos or text, and logs meals, water and goals to local JSON/JSONL files.

reads.best: 36 real regression scripts covering concurrency locking, path-traversal defenses and localization, plus an optional API key that is explicitly resolved and forwarded by Hermes rather than read from disk.
reads.worst: Destructive tools (delete/clear/undo of logged intake) rely on the skill's advisory text for user confirmation rather than a code-enforced approval gate.

plugins.name: card-grader
plugins.author: Agenziamaia
plugins.does: Computer-vision plugin that measures a trading card's centering from a photo to derive a PSA centering ceiling, checks whitening/clarity, optionally asks the user's vision LLM for a surface opinion, and pulls sold prices and live listings for a grade-or-not verdict.

reads.best: Unusually honest engineering: BENCH.md and bench_odds.json show the author abandoned an initial 'predicted grade' claim after benchmarking against 64 real slabs, downgrading the claim rather than overselling it.
reads.worst: Its audience is a specific hobby (trading-card grading), so most Hermes users would have no use for it day one.

plugins.name: inventory-reminder
plugins.author: ether-btc
plugins.does: Indexes a cached host inventory and gives Hermes tools to search installed capabilities or summarize the machine's state.

reads.best: It supplies a genuinely useful host-awareness surface with read-only cached lookups, clean unavailable results, and broad fixture coverage.
reads.worst: Its answers are only as current and complete as an externally scheduled inventory refresh, rather than live host state.

plugins.name: hermes-teamops
plugins.author: agentworker33-droid
plugins.does: Deploys and monitors multi-agent team blueprints with CLI tools, a local dashboard, and optional integrations.

reads.best: It turns team blueprints, deployment checks, fleet monitoring and rollback into native Hermes operations.
reads.worst: The dashboard has unauthenticated cross-origin actions that start local scripts or deploy teams, and the Twilio integration reads a credential file instead of Hermes secrets.

plugins.name: mailbridge
plugins.author: MadanChaollaPark
plugins.does: Captures legacy POP or EML mail and migrates a frozen inventory into Gmail with resumable workers and destination readback.

reads.best: Its approval binds an exact destination and inventory fingerprint, while uncertain uploads are reconciled before another write.
reads.worst: The provider profiles and real Gmail migration were not live-tested at the pinned commit, and setup demands Google OAuth plus operator configuration.

plugins.name: ultimate-dashboard
plugins.author: Yazeed-A-H
plugins.does: Dashboard page for Desktop and Webapp with cards for approvals, sessions, jobs, spend, health, files, memory and skills, backed by plugin routes.

reads.best: Broad, useful single-pane view with documented install, platforms and bilingual RTL support.
reads.worst: Tests are not in the plugin folder and UI coverage on Linux/Windows is admitted untested; a 234KB bundled JS file is hard to read.

plugins.name: costguard
plugins.author: Whydiriki700
plugins.does: Meters token usage per session and day from provider usage blocks, warns and blocks tool calls once a budget is exceeded.

reads.best: Hooks enforce a spend budget and the README is honest about estimates and limits; has tests.
reads.worst: Cannot stop the reply already generating, no Desktop UI or screenshots.

plugins.name: house-rules
plugins.author: AIverflow
plugins.does: Refuses tool calls matching user-written command/regex rules or leaving allowed folders, with a stop action that freezes the rest of the turn.

reads.best: Precise pre_tool_call guard with an e2e suite, a demo video and a candid 'not a security boundary' note.
reads.worst: A rule list resembles existing approval and denylist features.

plugins.name: prsn-id
plugins.author: craczkow
plugins.does: Gives a Hermes agent a PRSN ID identity read from the PRSN Connect desktop app and lets it seal emails and files with a hardware-held key after human approval.

reads.best: Approval before every seal, a key kept in secure hardware, 80 tests, Desktop pane and screenshots.
reads.worst: Only useful to people with a PRSN ID account and the vendor's desktop app.

plugins.name: lastgood
plugins.author: Dr-Enuf
plugins.does: Records which user-chosen checks (file opens, text present, files exist, URL loads) passed against a fingerprint of the checked files, runs them after agent edits, and answers /blame for what changed since the last good state.

reads.best: Thorough: 134 tests, standard library only, paths kept inside the project, and SSRF-safe url_loads with pinned addresses checked on every redirect hop.
reads.worst: The README says only the user can add url_loads checks, but the model can write lastgood-config.json directly; the repo is cluttered with build logs and AI-review notes, and there is no UI.

plugins.name: hermes-vault-broker
plugins.author: Karasumikura
plugins.does: Fills saved website logins from a separate root-installed broker daemon (scrypt plus AES-GCM, mlock'd key) that types the password over Chrome DevTools, so the agent's tool call carries only a handle and origin.

reads.best: Real cryptography and process isolation (separate system user, peer-uid socket checks, hardened systemd unit) with 83 tests across Python versions in CI.
reads.worst: It claims more than the code does. In default mode the password lands in a browser whose DevTools port is shared with the agent's browser tools, and the repo's own test reads it back from the field. Setup also needs root and a running daemon.

plugins.name: afterimage
plugins.author: LucianaiB2004
plugins.does: Records a computer_use click-flow once with per-step screenshots, rehearses it under a see-through HUD that compares live pixels, then replays matching steps with zero model calls.

reads.best: Turning an expensive vision-model desktop flow into a zero-token pixel-checked replay is a new and practical idea for agents.
reads.worst: Rehearse defaults to 'repair' (the README calls it opt-in) and clicks a model-chosen coordinate without confirmation. Screenshots are left in /tmp, the overlay is never torn down, and xdotool is required but undocumented.

plugins.name: lifeboat
plugins.author: superskie
plugins.does: Rescues assets from a sweeper-drained EVM wallet with one EIP-7702 transaction paid by a fresh operator, after scan, plan, simulate and approval.

reads.best: Simulation, in-memory approvals with a TTL, and an env opt-in gate before execute, plus 16 test files.
reads.worst: Narrow audience and it handles a private key and moves funds, which the catalog reviewer scrutinises heavily.

plugins.name: penguin
plugins.author: Crystal32378
plugins.does: Four deterministic tools for IANA time-zone conversion, whole-meeting overlap and saved team settings, with a themed four-clock Desktop planner page.

reads.best: Deterministic time-zone and DST handling that models get wrong, with a bundled tzdb, core and integration tests, and a heavily polished Desktop page with real screenshots.
reads.worst: Meeting-time conversion is a well-trodden idea, and much of the release effort goes to animation, artwork and music rather than to the tools.

plugins.name: belive-aihub-media
plugins.author: hassanabidpk
plugins.does: Makes BeLive AI Hub the backend for Hermes image_generate, video_generate, text_to_speech and speech-to-text.

reads.best: Careful transport: key via the secret scope, redirects refused, no retries on billable calls, resumable video jobs, and a broad test suite.
reads.worst: Tied to one vendor's paid gateway, so few Hermes users would install it on day one.

plugins.name: backup-sentinel
plugins.author: Brianmacu-BMS
plugins.does: Offline auditor for local tar.gz backups checking freshness, gzip/tar integrity, required files and SQLite snapshots.

reads.best: Fail-closed, read-only design with ~140 tests including adversarial ones and stdlib-only code.
reads.worst: A narrow Linux-only tar.gz scope; a script outside Hermes could do much the same.

plugins.name: spawn-backrooms
plugins.author: verycuriousdev
plugins.does: Connects Hermes over OAuth to the SPAWN job marketplace to browse, accept, work, deliver files for and submit assigned jobs, with approval prompts, a lease keeper and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Careful engineering: native OAuth, terms re-checked against human approval before accept/submit, idempotent envelopes and a large test suite.
reads.worst: Only useful to SPAWN marketplace workers, and its own README says it is a development preview with live acceptance incomplete and a private repository.

plugins.name: life-manager
plugins.author: Daisuke134
plugins.does: Stores stated commitments and habit streaks, injects a current board into turns, and offers tools and a scheduled check-in.

reads.best: Its focused state model, lifecycle wiring, and tests make persistent commitments actionable across sessions.
reads.worst: Commitment detection is deliberately simple phrase matching, so it will miss or misclassify natural-language commitments.

plugins.name: pdf-shrink
plugins.author: Hazem-Samak
plugins.does: Inspects and locally recompresses PDFs to a requested size while preserving the original and verifying the output.

reads.best: It has a careful quality ladder, write confinement and source-integrity checks, previews, and a broad synthetic test suite.
reads.worst: It is a strong implementation of a familiar document utility rather than a change to Hermes itself.

plugins.name: secret-remediation
plugins.author: AdrianTanz
plugins.does: Detects credential-shaped text in Hermes flows, redacts later exposure, records fingerprints, and can purge selected local traces.

reads.best: It is unusually thorough about detecting leaks across hooks, transcripts, SQLite stores, histories, and explicit limitations.
reads.worst: A detected or blocked string automatically triggers destructive rewrites of chat and shell history by default, so a false positive can alter data without a separate approval.

plugins.name: scopeledger
plugins.author: 221h0lmes
plugins.does: Reconciles staged service-project scope, deliveries, approvals, and invoices into evidence-linked review reports.

reads.best: Deterministic minor-unit accounting, source hashes, document verification gates, and extensive tests support cautious review.
reads.worst: The workflow serves a narrow agency use case and requires substantial manual staging and attestation of source records.

plugins.name: rails
plugins.author: grimmjoww
plugins.does: Uses local decision and vision models in Hermes hooks to flag off-scope actions, enforce coding workflow checks, and annotate decisions.

reads.best: Multiple hooks and vision tools make agent decisions and screen verification observable and actionable.
reads.worst: Its main guard depends on a separate local d1 server the plugin does not provide, while much of the default scope gate only warns and the UI text is personalized to one user.

plugins.name: blazephoenix
plugins.author: blazephoenixxyz-crypto
plugins.does: Gets DEX swap quotes through the user's RPC and locally checks unsigned router calldata before signing.

reads.best: It never signs or handles keys and cross-checks its hosted decode and calldata against a user-configured RPC response.
reads.worst: Quotes still rely on BlazePhoenix's hosted prepare/decode service and an independently configured RPC endpoint.

plugins.name: xscapes
plugins.author: donlucasx
plugins.does: Forwards fifteen Hermes lifecycle events to the separately installed xscapes CLI for an animated terminal scene and activity notifications ([pinned source](https://github.com/donlucasx/hermes-xscapes/tree/3a12d11bdc4e7fd917b256014e7efcf4e79c9e3d)).

reads.best: The event bridge covers subagents, context usage and human-input waits while limiting conversation excerpts and stripping provider keys from the child environment.
reads.worst: The renderer is outside this repository's pin, and send() writes unbounded tool arguments to a blocking stdin pipe before starting its timeout cleanup thread ([__init__.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/donlucasx/hermes-xscapes/3a12d11bdc4e7fd917b256014e7efcf4e79c9e3d/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: ros2-console
plugins.author: vgenev
plugins.does: Inspects ROS 2 robots locally or over SSH, visualizes topic health, captures camera frames and allows bounded opt-in topic publishing.

reads.best: Graph health includes measurement evidence and publisher QoS, while a default-empty publish allowlist and delivery checks make the write path unusually deliberate.
reads.worst: The README still installs OWNER/ros2-console and its Safety section incorrectly says every tool is read-only despite the implemented ros2_publish tool.

plugins.name: sessioncrew
plugins.author: harukaxxxx
plugins.does: Adds a multi-profile Desktop session panel with observed activity, completion acknowledgements, projects, folder creation and optional IDEA.md saving.

reads.best: A substantial bilingual session-management UI is backed by extensive routing, filesystem-safety and completion-state regression tests.
reads.worst: Live owner-routing acceptance remains incomplete, and the IDEA.md endpoint echoes supplied project ownership rather than independently authenticating it.

plugins.name: hebe-longevity
plugins.author: chrisbaumannai-stack
plugins.does: Imports confirmed blood panels, computes PhenoAge trends and formula drivers, and supports research plans screened by vendored PLSI and a separate model call.

reads.best: A complete Desktop experience joins strict panel validation, traceable local calculations and user-confirmed data changes with tests of the planning boundaries.
reads.worst: Planning lacks medication and condition context, and a separate challenger call is not guaranteed to use a different model, limiting the safety and independence claims.

plugins.name: world-window
plugins.author: alamonato
plugins.does: Pull-only world news tool grouping headlines across rated outlets with source links and feed health, plus Desktop UI.

reads.best: Honest design (no summaries), with tests, Desktop and dashboard parts.
reads.worst: News readers are common and need no model or key.

plugins.name: starlearner-nexus
plugins.author: BigBossRabbit
plugins.does: Fetches a user's starred GitHub repositories, keeps an incremental ledger, categorizes them (optionally via the host LLM), and auto-generates/registers new Hermes skills from templates.

reads.best: A creative 'GitHub stars into reusable skills' pipeline with correctly-implemented secret handling (agent.secret_scope.get_secret, never raw env reads, verified by its own tests) and genuine new-skill-registration capability.
reads.worst: The README and code comments are saturated with self-referential rule-ID justifications (e.g. 'R05', 'R11', 'R16') and a forensic git-log provenance dispute about a sibling project, reading like it was engineered to satisfy an automated catalog-rule checker rather than to explain the plugin to a user — a polish/trust concern worth a human judge's attention.

plugins.name: recalllayer
plugins.author: er-s-an
plugins.does: Local-first SQLite memory provider with working, episodic and semantic layers, five tools, auto recall and capture, and a CLI.

reads.best: A real native memory provider that changes what Hermes remembers, with layers, hook mapping and a mirror of builtin memory.
reads.worst: Keyword-only FTS recall, auto-capture with little filtering, daemon threads, and the README lists only a store unit test.

plugins.name: art98
plugins.author: StanLukuvka
plugins.does: Lets Hermes drive a real Windows 98 SE VM (screenshots, clicks, keys, Win32 calls) and render scene scripts to video, with a dashboard tab and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Highly original: agent control of a real retro VM, with careful subprocess timeouts, a token from get_secret, and dashboard and Desktop UIs.
reads.worst: No tests at all; setup is heavy (Linux, a separately run VM); render runs unsandboxed scene code, and approval fails open if the approval module can't be imported.

plugins.name: aftercare
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Remembers public URLs the agent said were deployed or live, re-checks them every few hours with one GET, and tells the agent at the next turn when one stops (or starts) answering.

reads.best: A fresh idea, holding the agent to its own past claims, built carefully: private and localhost addresses refused even after DNS or redirects, background checks, and context injected once per change.
reads.worst: Claims are spotted by sentence regex, so it misses deploys described differently, and it only re-checks at session start or from a cron command the user must set up.

plugins.name: capturekit
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Web-extract backend that returns page Markdown through the CaptureKit API.

reads.best: Small and clean: key read only through Hermes's secret scope, clear errors, mocked-network tests and a plain what-it-does-on-your-machine section.
reads.worst: One paid third-party API, with no screenshots and little novelty.

plugins.name: hermes-multibot
plugins.author: ivanvanes18
plugins.does: Adds up to eight extra DM-only Telegram bot transports, each with its own alias and allowlist, that share one Hermes profile in the same gateway.

reads.best: Registers real platforms via register_platform, reads every slot token through get_secret, fails closed on bad config, and tests token locks, duplicate tokens, ACL replay and media caps.
reads.worst: A niche need, DM-only, installed by copying files by hand, and the README itself says it is not a sandbox between users who share the profile's memory.

plugins.name: hermes-stage
plugins.author: davidpgil
plugins.does: Provides a terminal room where the user's Hermes profiles share a transcript and converse through public mentions over gateway WebSockets [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidpgil/hermes-stage/964c43b976124ea98b58a30cc8efbeb966d261fd/stage/entry.mjs).

reads.best: It gives existing profiles a shared terminal interface with bounded peer rounds, persistent completed messages and an explicit approval UI [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidpgil/hermes-stage/964c43b976124ea98b58a30cc8efbeb966d261fd/stage/entry.mjs).
reads.worst: Gateway readiness and RPC promises have no deadlines, and socket closure does not reject outstanding RPCs, so a dropped connection can leave startup or room actions waiting indefinitely [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidpgil/hermes-stage/964c43b976124ea98b58a30cc8efbeb966d261fd/stage/entry.mjs).

plugins.name: email-steward
plugins.author: kaosjammo
plugins.does: Triages Gmail into durable obligations and scheduled private briefs, with rules, reminders and explicit owner controls [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaosjammo/hermes-email-steward/a14b1c6ab76d23fb01e07a97b02990f6d4442273/email_steward/worker.py) [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaosjammo/hermes-email-steward/a14b1c6ab76d23fb01e07a97b02990f6d4442273/email_steward/plugin.py).

reads.best: Durable intake checkpoints and an explicit uncertain-delivery state preserve work and prevent blind notification resends after crashes [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaosjammo/hermes-email-steward/a14b1c6ab76d23fb01e07a97b02990f6d4442273/email_steward/worker.py).
reads.worst: The pinned delivery and profile-binding paths still call private Hermes internals such as _live_adapter and _profile_runtime_scope, creating catalog-rule and compatibility problems despite substantial defensive logic [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaosjammo/hermes-email-steward/a14b1c6ab76d23fb01e07a97b02990f6d4442273/email_steward/plugin.py).

plugins.name: hermes-local-voice
plugins.author: soilgrowerx
plugins.does: Records microphone audio and transcribes local files or inbound voice attachments using local Whisper backends.

reads.best: Validates audio containers and sizes, preserves recordings on transcription failure, and integrates both inbound hooks and CLI tools.
reads.worst: Requires external audio binaries and cached models, and microphone state tracks only a PID without verifying process identity before signaling it.

plugins.name: unblockbruecke
plugins.author: studioluftbruecke
plugins.does: Draws creative recovery cards for people or stalled agents, with editable decks, a journal, and Desktop controls.

reads.best: A finished Desktop experience pairs opt-in failure-streak hooks with concurrency limits, deck validation, and tests that preserve tool-failure verdicts.
reads.worst: The recovery advice itself is lateral prompting, and another transform_tool_result hook can consume the result first while its journal still marks a card attached.

plugins.name: hermes-music-studio
plugins.author: KeyArgo
plugins.does: Adds a local music studio with draft approval, render workers, take history, playback, export, checkpoints and bounded audio section edits. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KeyArgo/hermes-music-studio/e0fa23a5f16092a040feb575bd878aab8f687c28/README.md)

reads.best: A substantial Desktop studio, version-bound drafts, take provenance, audio checks and broad regression tests make it feel like a product for local music creation.
reads.worst: The reachable cloud-setup routes save and read API keys in cloud-keys.json instead of Hermes secrets, a catalog-policy problem despite the otherwise substantial implementation; see [credential code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KeyArgo/hermes-music-studio/e0fa23a5f16092a040feb575bd878aab8f687c28/music_studio/setup.py).

plugins.name: local-first-routing
plugins.author: 1anter
plugins.does: Registers a delegation backend that returns an explicitly pinned provider/model route or a categorized refusal, with no automatic fallback.

reads.best: It extends Hermes delegation through the public provider API and tests exact pins, refusal categories, lack of fallback, and configuration immutability.
reads.worst: It cannot verify that an endpoint is local or authenticate caller-declared prior outcomes, and installation documentation still uses repository placeholders.

plugins.name: answer-summary
plugins.author: ArronPK
plugins.does: Adds automatic reply summaries, bounded session recaps, and contextual side discussions with copyable handoffs to Hermes Desktop.

reads.best: A coherent Desktop experience integrates cached summaries, session context, model selection, and structured handoffs through public SDK surfaces.
reads.worst: Discussion-only behavior is merely prompted rather than tool-disabled, and long recaps discard middle chunks while describing them as condensed; there are no automated behavior tests.

plugins.name: bot-drops
plugins.author: chrisbaumannai-stack
plugins.does: Previews shared Hermes bots, adopts reviewed snapshots as new profiles, and publishes personality-and-skill packages with GitHub Pages cards.

reads.best: The finished sharing flow combines exact reviewed payloads, new-profile-only adoption, explicit confirmations, local cards, and extensive defensive tests.
reads.worst: profile_credentials directly reads the selected profile's .env and auth.json for secret scanning, contrary to the catalog prohibition on reading credential stores, and publishing relies on a vendor CLI login.

plugins.name: weightscope
plugins.author: dukemawex
plugins.does: Inspects and compares safetensors checkpoints using streamed tensor metrics, with optional local GPU or remote worker execution.

reads.best: The bounded checkpoint parser, numeric edge-case tests and guarded remote client make the implementation unusually careful.
reads.worst: It serves a specialist checkpoint-analysis niche and reports numeric weight differences rather than model behavior or quality.

plugins.name: hermes-sentinel
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Blocks repeated identical tool calls and credential-shaped new messages, redacts and bounds tool results, and keeps a local audit ledger.

reads.best: Four runtime hooks provide deterministic intervention, with redaction before audit previews and tested storage-failure fallbacks.
reads.worst: The fixed third-call breaker can block legitimate repeated polling, and unconditional output truncation can discard information needed by the agent.

plugins.name: equitylayer
plugins.author: andreacfbloom
plugins.does: Tracks research theses and sector readings using EquityLayer MCP, local baselines, scheduled checks and a local HTML dashboard.

reads.best: Persistent research baselines and cron-aware acknowledgment prevent unattended checks from silently dismissing information needing a person.
reads.worst: Its usefulness depends on one external research service and narrow sector coverage, with some advertised themes still missing live readings.

plugins.name: shelly-direct
plugins.author: cyberpz
plugins.does: Discovers and controls Shelly devices directly on the LAN with read-back verification and a web dashboard.

reads.best: Generation-aware device control, bounded private-network discovery and stateful device-stub tests make the hardware integration concrete.
reads.worst: The chat settings loader omits allow_model_sweep, so enabling that documented setting never reaches the handler through ctx.get_config.

plugins.name: pilot
plugins.author: LangerSword
plugins.does: Gives Hermes persistent interactive tmux terminals it can read and drive with text and keystrokes while a human can attach to the same pane.

reads.best: A small readable implementation and real-tmux tests cover persistent REPLs, vim keystrokes, screen polling and fast-exit recovery.
reads.worst: All calls share the fixed hermes-pilot socket and ignore session context, so separate Hermes profiles or conversations can list and control each other's panes.

plugins.name: reset-rescue
plugins.author: bwoliveira
plugins.does: Schedules redemption of expiring Codex reset credits across Hermes pool accounts, verifies results by readback and provides reminders and Desktop controls.

reads.best: Centralized consume authorization, persistent request IDs, readback confirmation and extensive failure-path tests support a polished account-wide rescue workflow.
reads.worst: It depends on undocumented ChatGPT mutation endpoints and explicitly deviates from catalog credential routing by handling pool tokens directly; automatic irreversible redemption is enabled by default.

plugins.name: hermagotchi
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Adds cooperative virtual pets, deterministic battles, cosmetics and social play through eight tools and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: A substantial game UI, opt-in networking and autonomy, and extensive client/server tests make this more than a pet-themed prompt.
reads.worst: The online client reads, writes and refreshes access and refresh tokens in its own session.json rather than using Hermes’s secret routes, contrary to catalog rule 11.

plugins.name: vigil
plugins.author: nesaon03
plugins.does: Detects refusal-like replies in model middleware, triggers Hermes’s configured fallback chain and exposes context-bound reviews and observed retry outcomes.

reads.best: Model middleware plus a substantial Desktop review UI provide genuine routing behavior and distinguish observed fallback outcomes from mere detections.
reads.worst: Detection remains heuristic and named profiles outside a hard-coded list of thirteen bot IDs silently pass through, limiting general installation usefulness.

plugins.name: nyx-wiki-recall
plugins.author: blacksmithFF
plugins.does: Injects decision-model-selected Markdown wiki glimpses into Hermes turns and writes daily transcripts, optionally serving as a memory provider.

reads.best: Native hooks and an optional memory provider combine hierarchical wiki recall with automatic daily transcript capture and extensive edge-case tests.
reads.worst: Lookups send unredacted conversation context to OpenRouter and can add roughly twenty seconds per turn, while installation needs a documented workaround to avoid replacing the existing memory provider.

plugins.name: flower-shop
plugins.author: k-reeeee
plugins.does: Adds a local business workspace for orders, inventory, production, deliveries, financial records, and approval queues, with a Hermes Desktop interface.

reads.best: A shared transactional SQLite service layer connects agent tools to a complete Desktop workspace with onboarding, inline approval cards, and extensive business-workflow tests.
reads.worst: With chat approvals enabled by default, flowershop_decide_approval accepts any nonempty model-supplied owner_statement and executes as owner(chat), so human authorization is asserted rather than verified.

plugins.name: hermes-templates
plugins.author: Ilyassbm
plugins.does: Shares and installs curated Hermes profile bundles through a CLI and Desktop page, with optional GitHub publishing.

reads.best: Implements a complete preview-and-install product with checksum and archive-path validation, paused packed routines, screenshots, and extensive safety tests.
reads.worst: The installer copies self-indexed bundles without re-sanitizing config or pausing imported cron jobs, so a hand-built bundle can activate unsafe behavior despite its preview; it also directly reads .env files.

plugins.name: creator-studio
plugins.author: flabanabba8
plugins.does: Bundles researched video and podcast production, caption generation and repair, and narrated Linux window recordings with a caption-review Desktop page.

reads.best: Real FFmpeg assembly, reusable narration takes, source-tracked projects and caption review make this substantially more than a media-writing prompt.
reads.worst: The bundle has many external runtime requirements and its replacement Hermes-held Google OAuth speech route has only mocked verification, with no live signed request at this pin.

plugins.name: hermes-plant
plugins.author: tuancookiez-hub
plugins.does: Adds a persistent Desktop garden with procedural plants, care actions, a play-money shop and two agent tools that share its state.

reads.best: A complete companion experience includes keyboard controls, reduced motion, save migration and cross-language parity tests for the Python and JavaScript garden rules.
reads.worst: It offers little improvement to agent capability beyond a companion game, and its floating UI uses an owned DOM overlay because the SDK lacks an overlay slot.

plugins.name: hermes-r0b0t-vibecad
plugins.author: am423
plugins.does: Executes approved local CAD scripts or prepares STL meshes, checks printer envelopes, renders previews and stages geometry for slicers and Bambu profiles.

reads.best: Real geometry checks, hash-bound script execution, detail previews and extensive approval/export tests connect Hermes to a practical local fabrication workflow.
reads.worst: It needs a separately bootstrapped CAD runtime and private Hermes approval/cancellation APIs, and approved Python retains full filesystem and network access.

plugins.name: hermes-shadow-clone
plugins.author: NotSusOk
plugins.does: Runs concurrent Gemini personas, an arena judge, claim verification, failover, and optional Telegram reporting for second opinions.

reads.best: The concurrent adversarial/architect/performance perspectives make model deliberation an actual Hermes tool rather than a prompt convention.
reads.worst: The pinned snapshot has only a small validation test surface for a networked multi-model system, plus optional Telegram code and a simulated offline path that make operational behavior less convincing.

plugins.name: agent-data-tools
plugins.author: Nutshell2000
plugins.does: Provides three MCP tools that discover and call a hosted catalog of hundreds of web, data, finance, chain, compliance, AI, and utility tools.

reads.best: The compact find/details/call interface gives Hermes broad live-data reach without flooding context with hundreds of separate tool definitions.
reads.worst: Nearly all value and reliability are delegated to an external paid service outside the pinned code, with no local implementation or tests to inspect.

plugins.name: myradio
plugins.author: newjordan
plugins.does: Lets Hermes DJ a local myradio station with queue tools, song requests, slash controls and scheduled shift restrictions.

reads.best: A substantial local-radio product has integration tests, illustrated setup and code-level restrictions reserving public broadcasting for a human command.
reads.worst: Its child adapter reads the station’s control.token file instead of obtaining credentials through Hermes, and a separate running station is required.

plugins.name: runproof
plugins.author: Biznomad
plugins.does: Verifies completed cron runs against fresh JSON reports and atomically releases accepted bytes once per workflow slot to a SQLite outbox.

reads.best: Checks report consistency and execution-window freshness, hashes the accepted bytes, and tests concurrent deduplication and transactional rollback.
reads.worst: Freshness trusts report writers and filesystem timestamps, validates only top-level field presence or true flags, and depends on internal cron-history helpers.

plugins.name: aletheia
plugins.author: ousiaresearch
plugins.does: Registers a Weft-backed external memory provider that ingests turns, retrieves profile-scoped evidence and returns recall receipts.

reads.best: The reviewed Weft 1.1.1 provider uses real memory lifecycle integration, scope checks, asynchronous turn ingestion and session-keyed queued recall.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains only an import shim and metadata tests; its actual provider resolves separately within a package range and needs separately cached models with an Apple-Silicon default embedder.

plugins.name: prize-radar
plugins.author: cacx097
plugins.does: Finds Devpost and Superteam opportunities, estimates crowding, and tracks deadlines and results with persistent reminders.

reads.best: Combines source parsing with persistent event claims, independent session reminders and concurrency/restart regression tests.
reads.worst: Discovery covers a limited set of sources and page formats, while prize-per-registrant ranking is only a crowding proxy rather than a likelihood of winning.

plugins.name: helper
plugins.author: benhens
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop onboarding dashboard and animated assistant with documentation-grounded replies and confirmed setup-import actions.

reads.best: New users get integrated setup cards, model-error fallbacks, secret-pattern checks and narrowly allowlisted import commands behind explicit clicks.
reads.worst: It is explicitly unfinished, has no shipped screenshots or videos, and its README opens by claiming it never installs or changes settings before disclosing importer and plugin-install actions.

plugins.name: guardrails
plugins.author: eddiemessiah
plugins.does: Adds spend caps, human-approval directives, idempotency reservations and an audit ledger for its own and configured third-party payment tools.

reads.best: Uses transactional budget reservations and Hermes approval directives, with scoped test-mode Stripe secrets and concurrency tests.
reads.worst: The pinned tree commits prohibited Python bytecode, and third-party retries awaiting approval can each proceed because only its own payment handler atomically claims a reservation.

plugins.name: mascot-guide
plugins.author: kangmochi
plugins.does: Desktop-only floating mascot showing agent activity, tokens, context and cost, with compress/stop buttons and extensive appearance settings.

reads.best: Finished-product polish: demo video, screenshots, seven locales, clear no-network disclosure.
reads.worst: A cosmetic status widget in one 560KB inlined file with only a smoke test and no agent-side capability.

plugins.name: hermes-intercom
plugins.author: greqone
plugins.does: Lets Hermes sessions discover each other and send messages, with loop protection, via session_list/session_send and a pre_llm_call hook.

reads.best: Novel inter-session agent messaging with very heavy test coverage.
reads.worst: Relies on private host APIs, delivery is not exactly-once, and the shipped Desktop file renders nothing.

plugins.name: visual-gate
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Screenshots pages through real Chrome via CDP, diffs against baselines and audits WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, returning PASS/FAIL with an HTML report.

reads.best: Concrete agent-verifiable UI gate with alignment anti-flake, contrast math and tests.
reads.worst: Needs a local Chrome and is a frontend-dev niche.

plugins.name: africastalking
plugins.author: geraldkombo
plugins.does: Adds SMS and USSD conversations through Africa’s Talking, with webhook intake, capped SMS replies, and cron delivery.

reads.best: USSD-to-SMS handoff brings an agent to feature phones, and callback handling avoids duplicate agent turns.
reads.worst: There is no plugin README, and the webhook accepts unauthenticated callbacks when the optional secret is unset.

plugins.name: omonpakari
plugins.author: tamamo510
plugins.does: Maintains a health journal, cycle ranges, interaction checks and pressure correlations, and injects a compact personal context note before replies.

reads.best: Persistent typed records and tested, nonblocking context assembly make the agent’s everyday suggestions more personally informed.
reads.worst: Health context is enabled by default across the profile’s human chats, including shared chats, while several interaction references are only generic literature labels.

plugins.name: linear-agent
plugins.author: realpetru
plugins.does: Bridges Linear agent sessions to Hermes runs and posts replies under the app’s own identity, with profile routing and setup diagnostics.

reads.best: Signature verification, delivery deduplication, capacity handling and app-authored replies form a well-developed workflow with extensive tests and a recorded demo.
reads.worst: It directly stores, loads and refreshes Linear OAuth tokens in linear-tokens.json instead of using Hermes’s required OAuth credential route.

plugins.name: stageglass
plugins.author: Benito3262
plugins.does: Publishes a redacted local audience overlay of Hermes prompts, tool steps and approvals, controlled by ON AIR, HOLD and OFF modes.

reads.best: Redaction happens before feed storage and again before HTML/SSE publication, with uncertainty holds and explicit broadcast controls.
reads.worst: A single process-global feed ignores session identity, so simultaneous sessions in one host process can mix their content while broadcasting is enabled.

plugins.name: chronos
plugins.author: Shikhyy
plugins.does: Tests model-supplied candidate file changes in isolated git worktrees and can merge the highest-scoring passing candidate.

reads.best: Its [merge path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shikhyy/hermes-agent/5b2a4b4a2c43e8a9b1e7bf8d32484a651bffedf0/plugins/chronos/chronos/engine.py) rejects stale or failed branches, checks for changed workspace files, and routes writes through Hermes with rollback on refusal.
reads.worst: The [automatic verifier](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shikhyy/hermes-agent/5b2a4b4a2c43e8a9b1e7bf8d32484a651bffedf0/plugins/chronos/chronos/verifier.py) selects npm test --if-present and treats exit zero as a pass even with zero tests, so a project without a test script can produce a falsely verified winner.

plugins.name: ikigai
plugins.author: Pierrem57
plugins.does: Conducts a deterministic personal-profile interview and compiles consent-oriented USER.md proposals, a SOUL draft, and local profile sheets.

reads.best: The [profile compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pierrem57/hermes-ikigai/59f405f8b98c2f0ecb4a29fe90322c76ea47ce95/core.py) preserves unrelated memory entries, fits its additions to the character budget, and excludes inferred and local-only answers from compiled profiles.
reads.worst: In [interview_turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pierrem57/hermes-ikigai/59f405f8b98c2f0ecb4a29fe90322c76ea47ce95/core.py), tagged widget replies skip the session-ownership check, so a matching tagged reply from another chat can alter the active interview.

plugins.name: herms-gate
plugins.author: plutoskiz
plugins.does: Filters known injection patterns and invisible characters from tool results and gateway input using local deterministic rules. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plutoskiz/herms-gate/26b6f797cd3fb3a4f1669953060d6ea3317ac04e/gate.py)

reads.best: It intervenes before the model sees tool output, preserves JSON structure, and tests rule parity and metadata-only logging. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plutoskiz/herms-gate/26b6f797cd3fb3a4f1669953060d6ea3317ac04e/gate.py)
reads.worst: Fixed patterns can miss encoded or rephrased attacks and alter legitimate quoted text; on Hermes 0.21.5 hidden-message blocking falls back to a model-facing note. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plutoskiz/herms-gate/26b6f797cd3fb3a4f1669953060d6ea3317ac04e/README.md)

plugins.name: exam-desk
plugins.author: darshak26
plugins.does: Adds Desktop practice exams with timed assisted or mock sittings, deterministic grading, missed-question drills, and model-assisted review. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/darshak26/hermes-exam-desk/72340210bb92c1f38831dbff271423785fda2f65/README.md)

reads.best: Server-enforced timing, answer-key hiding until submission, concurrency guards, and grading regression tests support a coherent study workflow. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/darshak26/hermes-exam-desk/72340210bb92c1f38831dbff271423785fda2f65/README.md)
reads.worst: AI review requires in-process plugin isolation, and paper sourcing or drafting still depends on agent skills and available web tools. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/darshak26/hermes-exam-desk/72340210bb92c1f38831dbff271423785fda2f65/README.md)

plugins.name: hermes-voice-gateway
plugins.author: SRai22
plugins.does: Connects a Twilio phone line to Hermes for inbound conversations, restricted inventory/enquiry tools and human-approved callbacks. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SRai22/hermes-voice-gateway/d91bf6723b44b598d87d170d5d1b30fef31f36a3/README.md)
