reads.best: Caller tools require matching live call identity and expiring database grants, with callbacks approved separately by a person. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SRai22/hermes-voice-gateway/d91bf6723b44b598d87d170d5d1b30fef31f36a3/caller_tools.py) [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SRai22/hermes-voice-gateway/d91bf6723b44b598d87d170d5d1b30fef31f36a3/README.md)
reads.worst: The caller workflow is tied to a bundled sample inventory and requires carefully configured toolsets and private Hermes interfaces. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SRai22/hermes-voice-gateway/d91bf6723b44b598d87d170d5d1b30fef31f36a3/README.md)

plugins.name: trophy-room
plugins.author: abundantbeing
plugins.does: Turns Hermes activity into 120 illustrated Desktop achievements with tiers, collectible cards and unlock notifications. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abundantbeing/hermes-trophy-room/80852baa4207e8269f83e4a5681d77b5e9ae5016/README.md)

reads.best: The Desktop experience includes collectible art, reduced-motion support, deferred notifications and per-profile replay of achievements earned while away. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abundantbeing/hermes-trophy-room/80852baa4207e8269f83e4a5681d77b5e9ae5016/README.md)
reads.worst: Sixty trophy definitions come from the existing bundled achievements plugin, limiting the novelty of its gamification concept. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abundantbeing/hermes-trophy-room/80852baa4207e8269f83e4a5681d77b5e9ae5016/README.md)

plugins.name: personal-assistant
plugins.author: 100yenadmin
plugins.does: Adds persistent personal-operation records, scoped action authorization and optional daily-operation and conversation-delivery workflows.

reads.best: The durable action gateway binds exact arguments to session/task identity, claims execution once and preserves uncertain outcomes for reconciliation.
reads.worst: The first-turn hook can inject owner preferences and people into another participant’s shared-chat turn, while ordinary unscoped calls remain outside PA exact-action enforcement.

plugins.name: claim-check
plugins.author: cryptobandit-builds
plugins.does: Annotates agent success claims with deterministic receipts derived from a local tool-result ledger.

reads.best: Observes actual tool results through hooks and tests contradictions, stale tests, session separation and optional correction nudges.
reads.worst: Regex matching can verify quoted or compound commands without proving execution, shell edits do not stale test receipts, and stored command/output fragments have no secret redaction.

plugins.name: shorguard
plugins.author: Akanimoh12
plugins.does: Inspects proposed Hermes writes and commands for classical public-key cryptography, supplies post-quantum alternatives and scans repositories into readiness reports.

reads.best: The pre-tool hook catches newly introduced crypto before writing, with migration recipes and tested multi-language rules.
reads.worst: The model can bypass enforcement by inserting shorguard allow comments; pattern matching also misses indirect crypto and silently skips oversized text.

plugins.name: hermes-backup
plugins.author: shaun-xenon
plugins.does: Backs up Hermes data to local and S3-compatible restic repositories, stages restores and runs restore-and-compare disaster recovery drills.

reads.best: Dual-target backup and actual restore drills address the valuable problem of preserving a user’s agent state.
reads.worst: Secrets.load falls back to a password file even without a standalone-mode guard, contrary to catalog rule 11; restore confirmation is only an agent-supplied boolean.

plugins.name: zkagent-attest
plugins.author: MCPVOT
plugins.does: Records tool-call digests and policy-unit costs, then drives a checksum-pinned prover to attest, verify and selectively disclose recorded actions.

reads.best: A real hook-to-proof workflow includes replay and tamper guards, preserved evidence on failure, selective disclosure, examples and a Desktop surface.
reads.worst: Proofs cover an agent-authored ledger and configurable policy units rather than complete activity or real spend; single-party setup limits trust, and unconditional fcntl imports break the advertised Windows path.

plugins.name: ghost-subscriptions
plugins.author: Max35j
plugins.does: Detects recurring charges and billing anomalies in local CSV or OFX bank exports and generates cancellation letters and reminders.

reads.best: A substantial offline engine supports bank formats, confidence scoring, privacy filtering and cancellation packs, with broad fixture-based tests.
reads.worst: Detection needs three charges and may misclassify irregular billing; bank profiles are not all verified against live exports and cancellation letters remain generic.

plugins.name: hermes-zotero
plugins.author: gerdosi
plugins.does: Indexes a private snapshot of the local Zotero library for passage search, bounded reading, annotations and citations ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gerdosi/hermes-zotero/f25a01ed2e481d30cca26f0ac79958337836478f/README.md)).

reads.best: Substantial local retrieval code includes WAL-aware snapshotting, incremental sync, locks, structured errors and tests built from synthetic Zotero libraries.
reads.worst: Search and its strong/thin/none coverage verdict are lexical term-count heuristics, so relevant synonyms can be missed and coverage is not evidence quality.

plugins.name: house-style
plugins.author: Sahil-SS9
plugins.does: Watches code edits and user corrections, then proposes project style rules for an explicitly confirmed context-file update.

reads.best: Captures actual edit outcomes across local and remote backends and preserves user-written rules when merging confirmed updates.
reads.worst: At the pin, capture requires an unshipped ctx.redact_text API, and the patch-hint regex has the blocking backtracking issue documented in PR #150474.

plugins.name: ag4te
plugins.author: simongonzalezdc
plugins.does: Mines local git history into eras, activity patterns, authorship summaries and interactive Desktop strata visualizations.

reads.best: A distinctive, detailed Desktop visualization is backed by repository-root checks, cancellable bounded subprocesses and tests of real git history.
reads.worst: Work classifications and practice-health signals are keyword heuristics rather than code analysis, while first use also needs uv and a separate DevArch download.

plugins.name: innerscape
plugins.author: simongonzalezdc
plugins.does: Connects Hermes tools and a native Desktop page to a self-hosted check-in, journal, and inbox service.

reads.best: Implements bounded HTTP, redirect and proxy refusal, secret-scope tokens, gateway restrictions, and detailed consent and failure-path tests.
reads.worst: Requires a separately hosted server and expiring full-account token, and agent save consent relies on a model-set boolean rather than an independent approval.

plugins.name: hot-hermes
plugins.author: firetussin
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop dashboard for profile readiness, host resources and explicitly retained profile connections.

reads.best: Retention is explicit, sequential and metadata-verified, with tested timeout and late-handle cleanup instead of invented readiness metrics.
reads.worst: It retains connections rather than agent or tool memory, and neither switching-speed gains nor per-profile resource costs are established.

plugins.name: cronforge
plugins.author: EikeAhlers
plugins.does: Observes recurring Hermes cron executions and generates model-free shell replay scripts with activation and rollback tools.

reads.best: Reducing repeated model work through recorded execution evidence and scheduler integration directly improves the user’s agent.
reads.worst: Command flattening discards working directories and timeouts, and generated scripts assume exit zero rather than preserving recorded exit assertions, weakening the claimed equivalence.

plugins.name: keychain
plugins.author: shoaibyazdani
plugins.does: Resolves Hermes credentials from macOS Keychain at startup and offers migration, inventory and audit tools.

reads.best: Uses the native SecretSource extension and verifies stored credentials before removing dotenv values.
reads.worst: Despite native SecretSource integration, migration directly reads dotenv credentials contrary to catalog rule 11, strips only the first duplicate definition and retains plaintext backups.

plugins.name: shipwrit
plugins.author: ShalyX
plugins.does: Checks deployment HTTP journeys, records redacted receipts and nudges Hermes to verify releases before claiming success.

reads.best: Multi-step capture-and-lookup checks distinguish a healthy endpoint from a working user outcome, with focused tests and explicit scope limits.
reads.worst: Any passing receipt clears the project pending marker without binding it to the attempted deployment target or revision; the finish hook only nudges once.

plugins.name: visual-oracle
plugins.author: valenciayuna
plugins.does: Captures stable browser screenshots, pixel-diffs baselines and nudges Hermes on unexpected visual changes.

reads.best: Dependency-free image comparison includes separate change regions, masks, declared-change contracts and focused browser and decoder tests.
reads.worst: The verification hook only notices stored FAIL or REVIEW verdicts, so a capture error after a prior PASS leaves no failing gate; Chrome sandboxing may also be disabled automatically.

plugins.name: postkitty
plugins.author: mertkayacs
plugins.does: Creates checked social-platform text and media variants with face-aware framing, local renders, and an HTML review board.

reads.best: A substantial local media pipeline checks and repairs outputs and provides a useful review board across eight platforms.
reads.worst: FFmpeg rendering and probing include subprocess calls without timeouts, so malformed media or a stuck process can hold a tool call indefinitely.

plugins.name: finder
plugins.author: oways
plugins.does: Adds a Hermes Desktop sidebar for searching and managing projects and sessions with usage statistics.

reads.best: A native Desktop pane makes project-name search and session navigation available without asking the model.
reads.worst: The pinned repository has no automated tests, its README retains a screenshot placeholder, and search covers loaded session metadata rather than full histories.

plugins.name: hermes-handle-it
plugins.author: casualsav
plugins.does: Runs customer-support chats in a browser and optional phone calls, pausing for user approval before sensitive replies.

reads.best: Its browser loop persists chats and routes offers and personal details through a human approval gate.
reads.worst: The commitment guard is regex-based, real company chats are untested, and phone-call safety largely depends on the external voice agent following instructions.

plugins.name: apparent
plugins.author: simonvanlaak
plugins.does: Lets Hermes inspect screen-and-voice recording bundles as transcripts and image pixels, with a staged Desktop recording workflow.

reads.best: Inspection has explicit source selection, bounded subprocesses, guarded image reads, private Connect cleanup, and focused failure-case tests.
reads.worst: The pinned hermes directory lacks desktop/plugin.js, so the recording button requires a separate build and the PR leaves installed compatibility unverified.

plugins.name: rariflat
plugins.author: wadezigh96
plugins.does: Tracks tool outcomes locally, recommends previously observed tools by lexical fit and usage metrics, and offers Desktop status cards and an opt-in retry guard.

reads.best: Public pre/post-tool hooks support measured feedback and loop blocking, with redaction, profile-scoped storage and Python/Desktop contract tests.
reads.worst: Recommendations use fixed lexical and rarity weights without evidence that they improve task outcomes, and have no useful history at installation; success detection is heuristic.

plugins.name: printsi
plugins.author: magnusahmad
plugins.does: Ships a local MCP server with 19 tools and a Desktop pane that preflight-checks a PDF for print, quotes and orders printed flyers for US delivery, and tracks the order.

reads.best: It reaches the physical world safely: a real preflight with a to-scale Desktop pane marking each issue, and payment only through a link a person opens and pays on Stripe.
reads.worst: The package has no tests, the work depends on the entrant's own API on a workers.dev host that receives the user's PDF and address, the server is one 838 KB bundled file, and it covers only flyers in the contiguous US.

plugins.name: vivarium
plugins.author: r3adaszer0
plugins.does: An artificial-life simulation in which every agent tool call feeds a 48x48 dish and every learned skill hashes into a new species, with renders, a codex, gallery and /vivarium command.

reads.best: Highly original and very polished, with images, clips, PDFs and about 370 tests.
reads.worst: Intrusive for a toy: pre_llm_call injects text telling the agent to relay its card verbatim, a polling thread starts at import in every process, and it reads parent processes' /proc environ.

plugins.name: oddsradar
plugins.author: WV629
plugins.does: Read-only Polymarket odds search and a watchlist with move and threshold alerts checked by a no-agent cron script that costs zero tokens.

reads.best: Clever zero-token cron design with a deterministic, well-tested alert engine (25 offline tests, CI), host allowlist, timeouts and no keys or trading.
reads.worst: Modest scope, and the watchlist claimed to be shared safely across chat, CLI and cron is guarded only by a threading lock, so separate processes can lose updates.

plugins.name: goalpost
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: A pre_tool_call hook that blocks write_file, patch and terminal calls which weaken tests (skip markers, deleted tests, removed assertions, || true, --no-verify) and records every decision in a local ledger.

reads.best: Small, deterministic and honest: 600 lines, 32 tests, no network or model calls, and a limits section that says exactly what it cannot catch.
reads.worst: The detector is text counting on a guessed test-file pattern, blocks legitimate test deletion, and the README admits it was not yet tested on Linux, macOS or Docker.

plugins.name: component-workbench
plugins.author: 1anter
plugins.does: A review/governance workflow that stores immutable candidate file snapshots, runs static syntax-only checks, freezes a candidate against a committed hash, and records human review verdicts in a tamper-evident SQLite ledger, with no execution or promotion ability at all.

reads.best: Tests (outside the plugin's own folder) cover path-traversal rejection, DB tamper detection, and an explicit 'no execution or promotion' guarantee; secrets like .env/auth.json are explicitly blocked from being stored.
reads.worst: Its test suite lives at the parent repo root rather than inside the plugin's own tests/ folder, an organizational inconsistency, and the README itself flags the plugin as experimental/unaudited.

plugins.name: wally
plugins.author: sanchitmonga22
plugins.does: Adds RunAnywhere's OpenAI-compatible Wally service as a Hermes model provider with model discovery and reasoning/image handling.

reads.best: It gives Hermes a provider path to a broad catalog of open-weight models with no extra dependency.
reads.worst: It is a thin provider adapter with modest local surface area, limited documentation evidence beyond the README and no distinctive agent behavior.

plugins.name: rule-injector
plugins.author: klautimus
plugins.does: Injects user-defined trigger-matched rules at pre_llm_call, into tool results, and at the pre_verify gate instead of keeping them in the system prompt.

reads.best: Puts rules at the point of need, with compound triggers and a demo video and dashboard.
reads.worst: The repo is cluttered with one-off stage migration scripts, the manifest has no author, and many top-level test files hold no test functions.

plugins.name: babysit
plugins.author: aarav1656
plugins.does: Watches a long job's log with zero model calls and wakes the agent on NaN, OOM, tracebacks, stalls, process exit or custom alerts.

reads.best: Fills a real gap in Hermes's rate-limited watch_patterns with its own wake budget and marks log text as untrusted.
reads.worst: No tests shipped in the plugin folder.

plugins.name: bundlebees
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Lets Hermes dispatch leased coding briefs to a configured sandbox-worker launcher and inspect attempts through tools and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Scoped secrets, pinned-address network checks and a separate user-run verification CLI make remote worker orchestration unusually deliberate.
reads.worst: It supplies the coordinator client rather than the worker launcher or Cua runtime, so the advertised quick start assumes substantial external infrastructure.

plugins.name: hermes-ledger
plugins.author: elyga408-oss
plugins.does: Records tool calls and approvals in a redacted, hash-chained, signed local log with verifiable session receipts.

reads.best: Signed receipts with content-free stubs and concurrency tests make agent activity independently inspectable.
reads.worst: It reads its private signing key from a local PEM file rather than Hermes secrets, and local key access permits rewriting the audit history.

plugins.name: warden
plugins.author: Zaygalx
plugins.does: Adds scoped security scans, an agent action ledger, evidence-backed investigations, campaign correlation and containment planning.

reads.best: Operator-owned scopes, canonicalized targets, bounded scanner execution and real Hermes dispatch tests give its six-tool security workflow substance.
reads.worst: Containment cannot execute, scanners need separate installation, and correlation quality is established on a synthetic corpus rather than field data.

plugins.name: hermes-openready
plugins.author: socraticblock
plugins.does: Wraps the external Open-Ready CLI as five release-gate tools and adds a pre_tool_call hook that blocks terminal gh/curl commands making a repo public without a digest-scoped owner approval.

reads.best: A fail-closed enforcement hook with about 87 tests (188 cases with parametrization), CI, an allowlisted child environment and process-group timeouts.
reads.worst: Does nothing without the separately installed Open-Ready CLI, only guards the terminal tool, and claims to read the origin remote, which no code does.

plugins.name: imagination-studio
plugins.author: drowzeys
plugins.does: Standard-library HTTP bridge with ten tools that sends image, video, voice, song and sound jobs to a locally run Imagination Studio server and returns the files as MEDIA.

reads.best: Well-hardened bridge (no redirects, key only to private hosts, path confinement, size caps and download deadlines), key from Hermes get_secret, 28 tests, nine screenshots and a GIF.
reads.worst: All generation happens in a separate GPU-bound app, so the plugin itself is a thin client, and tool calls can block for up to 600s.

plugins.name: completion-proof
plugins.author: yuanshen101
plugins.does: Runs operator-configured checks and stores PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN receipts tied to fingerprints of declared files, marking old passes stale after changes.

reads.best: The local deterministic engine uses configured argv, bounded execution, scoped fingerprints, and carefully states what a passing check does not establish.
reads.worst: The pinned README's install route points to a standalone archive missing from the fetched tree and says this is not a submitted entry; operators must resolve that packaging and entry-status contradiction.

plugins.name: gateway-guardian
plugins.author: kawsthingz
plugins.does: Reads Hermes gateway logs and processes to classify Telegram health and produce an operator-approved recovery plan.

reads.best: The read-only, approval-gated design makes a vague gateway failure actionable without silently restarting or killing processes.
reads.worst: It is a narrow pattern scanner with no hooks or live remediation, so detection quality depends on local log/process conventions.

plugins.name: defuzz-componentize
plugins.author: defuzzr
plugins.does: Guides turning Python scripts into reusable components, compares saved baseline output, and applies bounded project kits with a desktop settings view.

reads.best: It provides unusually concrete component contracts, evidence, path-safety checks and many tests around a code-organization workflow.
reads.worst: It is a specialized developer workflow with Linux/Python 3.13 requirements, and its runner can execute user-supplied commands or imports with host permissions.

plugins.name: stripe-commerce
plugins.author: adroidian
plugins.does: Manages a Stripe merchant catalog with restricted keys only; every write needs an exact offline preview and then a one-time human approval in native Telegram/Discord.

reads.best: Its human approval gate for writes is strict (mandatory approval policy, one-use lease, preview binding) and it has 100 tests; the key comes from Hermes's secret store.
reads.worst: The README admits that writes depend on unreleased Hermes core APIs, so on stable Hermes it is read- and preview-only; the docs are dense, with a 632-line validation log.

plugins.name: hermes-wallpaper
plugins.author: jangomango76
plugins.does: Desktop-only plugin that puts a user-chosen image, GIF or video behind the whole Hermes Desktop window, with look and layout controls, a library and a slideshow.

reads.best: Finished like a product: banner, three screenshots, status-bar popover, command-palette actions and settings page, with no network, backend or secrets.
reads.worst: Cosmetic only: it does nothing for the agent, and its testing is a single end-to-end Desktop script.

plugins.name: network-xray
plugins.author: rusty4444
plugins.does: Runs a bounded DNS, TCP, verified TLS and HTTP HEAD probe in a child process, imports the same probe run from another machine, and compares the two stage by stage, with a Desktop workbench page.

reads.best: Careful engineering: a sandboxed child process with a hard deadline, about 91 tests with CI, and claims that match the code.
reads.worst: Niche diagnostics that a terminal skill with curl and dig could largely cover; it can probe private and loopback hosts and does not support Windows.

plugins.name: eselsbruecke
plugins.author: studioluftbruecke
plugins.does: A toggleable Desktop toolbox (today pad, pomodoro, time log, formatter, converters, regex/diff/UUID/cron/QR) that the agent can also call for exact answers.

reads.best: Broad, well-tested tools with a polished Desktop page and dashboard.
reads.worst: It is a grab-bag of common utilities rather than one new capability.

plugins.name: chat-shield
plugins.author: james-see
plugins.does: LLM middleware that redacts PII with an on-device NER model plus regex and restores values in replies.

reads.best: Placeholder-and-restore design at the llm_request layer keeps PII off providers.
reads.worst: No tests at all, and it downloads a model from Hugging Face at runtime; the HIPAA-style claims go beyond what the code proves.

plugins.name: teach-back
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Tracks every file the agent writes or patches through post_tool_call and runs /teachback quizzes, written and graded by the user's own model, on what that code does.

reads.best: A fresh idea, paying down 'comprehension debt' by quizzing the user on agent-written code built from the real diffs, with a lines-understood score.
reads.worst: The pull request says it is 'Not yet verified with a live model', and the questions and grading rest entirely on LLM prompts.

plugins.name: changefreeze
plugins.author: arults
plugins.does: Gates deploy/push shell commands via pre_tool_call during a user-set quiet window, asking for approval or blocking.

reads.best: Uses a real pre_tool_call veto with ledger, evidence docs, demo video and 15 tests.
reads.worst: The agent itself has changefreeze_allow_once and changefreeze_set tools, so it can lift its own gate, and the regex list is easy to bypass.

plugins.name: qbo-ops
plugins.author: blackghostosint
plugins.does: Read-only QuickBooks Online tools (health, P&L, backdated-entry audit, deposit trace, guarded SQL) with a Desktop pane and a bookkeeping skill.

reads.best: Credentials go only through Hermes's oauth/secret route, qbo_query is SELECT-only with clamped results, and setup docs are complete.
reads.worst: Setup still needs an Intuit developer app and manual refresh-token workaround, and date inputs are interpolated into queries unvalidated.

plugins.name: preflight
plugins.author: soyluisarca
plugins.does: Terminal backend that runs commands in a copy of the workspace, writes an exact diff, and applies changes only when the user runs a sandboxctl script.

reads.best: Dry-run-with-diff approval is a fresh idea that changes where Hermes executes commands.
reads.worst: Admits it is not isolation (host process, best-effort guards), the sandbox tests are underscore-named and not collected, and approval happens in an external script, not in Hermes.

plugins.name: wiro
plugins.author: EminBudak
plugins.does: A model-provider plugin that adds the Wiro AI OpenAI-compatible gateway, with a table of 14 models and a reasoning-effort mapping.

reads.best: WIRO_API_KEY is declared as a secret and handled only by Hermes, and CI runs integration tests against Hermes releases and main.
reads.worst: The capabilities are a hardcoded snapshot although the docstring says they come from the live catalog, and background tasks are billed from the wallet through a fixed paid model.

plugins.name: turn-completion-nudge
plugins.author: ether-btc
plugins.does: post_llm_call hook that scores whether a turn ended prematurely via a remote scorer and nudges the agent to continue.

reads.best: Fail-open with bounded per-turn guard, secret read via Hermes secret scope, and 62 tests.
reads.worst: The plugin folder has no README of its own (it is at the repo root), and scoring sends turn text to an external endpoint when enabled.

plugins.name: which-copy
plugins.author: Hazem-Samak
plugins.does: Diagnoses command shadowing by comparing Hermes and login-shell PATH resolution, installed copies, provenance and versions.

reads.best: Bounded stripped-environment probes, conservative provenance reports and tripwire tests address a concrete source of local-agent failures.
reads.worst: It does not measure the terminal tool's final PATH, and the POSIX login-shell implementation leaves Windows unsupported.

plugins.name: earnfi
plugins.author: earnfidotfun
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted marketplace and payment MCP service, with diagnostics, commands, and workflow skills for work and escrow flows.

reads.best: It has unusually complete operational and security documentation, secret-schema fields, diagnostics, and an untrusted MCP posture for writes and payments.
reads.worst: Core job, escrow, and payment behavior remains a large uninspectable hosted MCP surface, making reliability hard to establish from the pinned code.

plugins.name: serpkite
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Registers SerpKite as Hermes’s web search and page-extraction provider, returning search results and extracted page content.

reads.best: It plugs search and extraction into Hermes’s existing web-provider interface and reads its API key through Hermes’s provider environment/secret lookup.
reads.worst: It depends on a paid third-party service and sends user queries and requested URLs to that service; the functionality is a backend option for familiar web tools.

plugins.name: claim-market-router
plugins.author: misakamikotoghr-5205
plugins.does: Delegation backend and llm_request middleware that routes subagent tasks across models via a cost/quota-aware claim market.

reads.best: Hooks into Hermes delegation and request middleware to shape model choice and effort, something a skill cannot do.
reads.worst: No tests at all for a non-trivial pricing/routing engine.

plugins.name: gmi-image
plugins.author: zkasuran
plugins.does: An image_gen provider backend that creates and edits images through GMI Cloud's Seedream, Gemini and other models.

reads.best: A clean image-generation provider that reads GMI_API_KEY through Hermes's secret scope and is tested offline against a fake GMI server.
reads.worst: Every call spends the user's GMI credits with no Hermes approval prompt (disclosed in the README), and it is one more hosted image provider rather than a new idea.

plugins.name: half-life
plugins.author: dominator509
plugins.does: Hooks post_tool_call and transform_tool_result to stamp read-only tool results (file reads built in) as FRESH, TTL_VALID, STALE or UNKNOWN and flag re-reads whose file changed.

reads.best: A fresh idea for agents: tells the model when a file it read earlier has changed, through result-transform hooks a skill cannot reach, and fails open.
reads.worst: Only one regression script for the tests, a config file read outside Hermes's settings that can stop registration, and a README full of internal release caveats rather than setup.

plugins.name: prediction-market-scout
plugins.author: HATWHY4041
plugins.does: Read-only Polymarket research: six tools, /pm command, price-alert watchlist and scheduled-briefing blueprints.

reads.best: Complete stdlib tool set with persistent watchlist, a /pm command and automation blueprints, plus a 24KB test file.
reads.worst: A niche audience, and the data is public Polymarket API calls a script could do.

plugins.name: shinjuku
plugins.author: Shinjuku-StAItion
plugins.does: Launches a locally installed private USDC wallet over MCP so the agent can price-check and pay x402 services privately.

reads.best: Careful launcher that never downloads, a clear privacy account and skill rules that payment happens only on request, with Hermes approval.
reads.worst: Moves money through an external npm wallet whose code is not in the repo, setup is manual, no Mac, and the README says it was lightly tested.

plugins.name: dosbox-mcp
plugins.author: shakeyourbunny
plugins.does: Packages dosbox-automation's MCP bridge for Hermes (started with uvx dosbox-mcp==0.2.4) plus a skill, so the agent can type, read the screen, record media, run Lua and read/write memory in a running DOS emulator.

reads.best: The bridge behind it is a tested Python package (about 5,000 lines of code and tests), pinned to an exact version, with a token file instead of a pasted key and an emulator-side mount allowlist.
reads.worst: The Hermes plugin itself is only a manifest, an mcp.json and a skill; it needs the emulator installed and running separately, and DOS automation is a small audience.

plugins.name: esp32-debug
plugins.author: snakeyear
plugins.does: Adds ESP32 port discovery, reset-confirmed chip inspection, bounded serial capture and panic backtrace decoding with Espressif tools.

reads.best: Connects redacted serial captures to structured panic analysis, source locations and ELF fingerprint diagnostics for a practical hardware-debugging workflow.
reads.worst: The decoder runs addr2line before comparing ELF fingerprints and still returns ok=true on a mismatch, leaving misleading source locations in a successful response alongside the warning.

plugins.name: baro
plugins.author: Lotus015
plugins.does: Launches the pinned Baro coding orchestrator and turns its planning and execution events into a persistent Desktop dependency board ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jigjoy-ai/hermes-baro/79cb40f9baf20529e4587f07653d31ea2654bf41/tools.py)).

reads.best: The integration follows run state, reports failed or cancelled work, and provides plan, run, status, and cancellation tools ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jigjoy-ai/hermes-baro/79cb40f9baf20529e4587f07653d31ea2654bf41/tools.py)).
reads.worst: The launch approval names only a configured backend although tool arguments can select a remote model endpoint, leaving the actual data recipient undisclosed ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jigjoy-ai/hermes-baro/79cb40f9baf20529e4587f07653d31ea2654bf41/core/consent.py)).

plugins.name: agentpay-guard
plugins.author: tmdry4530
plugins.does: Applies spending and risky-tool policies through Hermes hooks, queues approvals, and records observed spending ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmdry4530/hermes-guard-plugin/84c44e53ec43d3bac2c1a43d6a21aea0d58d4051/hooks.py)).

reads.best: Its pre-call interception, hard-limit rechecks, and post-call accounting give Hermes a reusable policy layer across tools ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmdry4530/hermes-guard-plugin/84c44e53ec43d3bac2c1a43d6a21aea0d58d4051/hooks.py)).
reads.worst: If policy evaluation fails and recording the fallback blocked-payment decision also fails, pre_tool_call returns None and permits execution instead of failing closed ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmdry4530/hermes-guard-plugin/84c44e53ec43d3bac2c1a43d6a21aea0d58d4051/hooks.py)).

plugins.name: vt-check
plugins.author: Aravinth-Earth
plugins.does: Hashes files locally for VirusTotal reputation checks and inspects archives in memory for traversal, bombs, hidden executables, and related hazards.

reads.best: It provides useful local archive forensics without uploading files and obtains its API key through Hermes's secret scope.
reads.worst: VirusTotal coverage and quotas limit certainty, while several archive formats remain deliberately uninspectable without external tools.

plugins.name: openbao
plugins.author: Schultzenator
plugins.does: Registers a Hermes secret-source provider that resolves bao:// references against an OpenBao/Vault KV HTTP API so other plugins' secrets can come from Vault.

reads.best: Bootstrap token is read only via Hermes's own secret-source environment API, marked protected, and the plugin explicitly never touches .env or auth.json.
reads.worst: Only 3 test functions; KV v1 fallback, namespace headers, HTTP error codes and the response-size cap are all implemented but untested.

plugins.name: contractguard
plugins.author: Mohamedhazeem
plugins.does: Checks an HTTP API against its OpenAPI spec inside Hermes: offline request preflight, live GET/HEAD to loopback only, drift diff against an approved baseline, and approval-gated baseline promotion with redacted SQLite run records.

reads.best: Carefully scoped safety design: loopback-only GET/HEAD with no redirects, auth headers rejected and redacted, promotion behind Hermes's approval hook with a SHA-256 re-check, plus ADRs, SECURITY.md and CI.
reads.worst: The loopback check compares hostnames, not resolved IPs, and there are no tests for the diff rules, promotion or live-transport safety checks the README says are tested.

plugins.name: treasury-cash-forecast
plugins.author: Prabhusekaran
plugins.does: Builds a 12-month direct cash-flow forecast workbook from a template using ETS/SARIMA models, with scenarios and cent-level reconciliation.

reads.best: Deterministic, tested forecasting engine (67 tests) so the model never computes numbers; offline, no credentials.
reads.worst: Narrow corporate-treasury audience.

plugins.name: model-doctor
plugins.author: ChainShieldSn
plugins.does: Hooks API request results and errors to track per-model health, classify failures and report it via two tools.

reads.best: Observes Hermes's own API traffic with no network or credentials, saved atomically.
reads.worst: Claims more than the code: it is passive, not proactive; the rolling window is never used; and the refresh tool duplicates the status tool.

plugins.name: linear-digest
plugins.author: TakeshiTGAL
plugins.does: Schedules a model-free 08:00 cron message of open Linear issues assigned to you, plus a read-only tool.

reads.best: Very careful network and secret handling: secret scope, no redirects or proxies, bounded reads, schema tests.
reads.worst: Narrow Linear-only use and a long README.

plugins.name: afriradar
plugins.author: Risingtell
plugins.does: Gives Hermes Nigerian and Kenyan mutual-fund data (from SEC Nigeria and CMA Kenya public reports) to find, rank, compare and project returns for funds, plus a watchlist with weekly change alerts.

reads.best: Does all financial arithmetic (projections, basis-point moves) in code rather than letting the model estimate it, is covered by a 481-line test file, and needs no API key since it reads public regulator data.
reads.worst: Narrow geographic niche (only Nigerian and Kenyan collective-investment data) limits how many Hermes users would find it useful.

plugins.name: hunk-consent-guard
plugins.author: misakamikotoghr-5205
plugins.does: Stages file edits per hunk for user-only approval, revokes approvals on SHA-256 drift and keeps rollback receipts.

reads.best: User-only approval and drift revocation through Hermes file-safety and write_file dispatch.
reads.worst: No tests and a heavy, jargon-filled API for a review flow most users will not adopt.

plugins.name: soloknuckle
plugins.author: z99wE
plugins.does: Scans diffs for leaked secrets, firewalls risky shell commands, and scores an npm project's health, exposed as three Hermes tools with no hooks or middleware.

reads.best: Unusually self-limiting documentation that explicitly lists what it deliberately did not build (a secret source, self-update) and why, plus cross-engine TS/Python parity tests.
reads.worst: Secret scanning and a command firewall are well-worn security-tool concepts, so it scores low on originality despite strong execution.

plugins.name: waiting-on-you
plugins.author: irsan-dimyati
plugins.does: Adds /waiting and hermes waiting, which read every profile's session store read-only and list the unanswered questions your bots ended their replies with, merged and oldest first.

reads.best: Read-only SQLite access (mode=ro, 2-second timeout) with a privacy default that limits messaging chats to their own profile, plus privacy tests.
reads.worst: Detection is a heuristic on English and Indonesian phrasing, and with no tools or hooks it is a reporting command only.

plugins.name: dramatis
plugins.author: kaizen-builds
plugins.does: Spoiler-safe EPUB reading companion that answers only from text up to your reading point.

reads.best: Original idea with tests that prove later chapters are never read.
reads.worst: Niche use, no UI, and the model's own knowledge of famous books can still spoil.

plugins.name: fivedive
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Provides a Hermes gateway platform that exchanges app messages, voice-note flags and files with the 5dive bridge through a local spool [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/5dive-ai/5dive-plugins/d9e8ad1ad0f6e109d54a213e743d25284389f875/plugins/dashboard/hermes/adapter.py).

reads.best: A small platform adapter brings Hermes to the user's web and mobile chat, including media replies and standalone cron delivery without its own network listener [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/5dive-ai/5dive-plugins/d9e8ad1ad0f6e109d54a213e743d25284389f875/plugins/dashboard/hermes/adapter.py).
reads.worst: take_inbox deletes the entire fetched batch before dispatch, so a crash or an exception handling one message can lose pending messages with no adapter retry [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/5dive-ai/5dive-plugins/d9e8ad1ad0f6e109d54a213e743d25284389f875/plugins/dashboard/hermes/adapter.py).

plugins.name: usage-hud
plugins.author: aktogde1
plugins.does: Shows Codex account quota windows, reset countdowns and focused-session usage in the Hermes Desktop status bar [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aktogde1/hermes-usage-hud/097bbb5ef882dd6eb19d9afd9003e565130050e1/desktop/plugin.js).

reads.best: It rejects invalid or expired quota readings, keeps multiple account pools separate, and labels remaining quota distinctly from used context [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aktogde1/hermes-usage-hud/097bbb5ef882dd6eb19d9afd9003e565130050e1/desktop/plugin.js).
reads.worst: Account reporting is hard-coded to openai-codex and its Session/Weekly windows, so users of other providers get no account-limit view [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aktogde1/hermes-usage-hud/097bbb5ef882dd6eb19d9afd9003e565130050e1/desktop/plugin.js).

plugins.name: watch-with-me
plugins.author: jcrabapple
plugins.does: Builds subtitle-anchored film commentary and releases sourced notes alongside Plex playback [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jcrabapple/watch-with-me/adb0c77fafd65d6302e51ea5b3b063cf894ec921/watch_with_me/cues.py).

reads.best: Commentary anchors must resolve against actual subtitle lines, and release filtering checks spoiler dependencies before showing a note [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jcrabapple/watch-with-me/adb0c77fafd65d6302e51ea5b3b063cf894ec921/watch_with_me/cues.py).
reads.worst: Optional Jev API keys are written to and read from jev-api-key.json instead of remaining exclusively in Hermes secret storage [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jcrabapple/watch-with-me/adb0c77fafd65d6302e51ea5b3b063cf894ec921/watch_with_me/jev.py).

plugins.name: factkit
plugins.author: MohamedElsiddig
plugins.does: Adds semantic memory recall before model calls, reorders fact-store search results, and indexes new facts after sessions [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohamedElsiddig/hermes-plugin-factkit/ffe3e255755e5b2b92bd5a06dfb89a0d549544d9/__init__.py).

reads.best: Optional recall has bounded embedding requests, failure fallback and a circuit breaker, while session-end indexing has a separate wait budget [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohamedElsiddig/hermes-plugin-factkit/ffe3e255755e5b2b92bd5a06dfb89a0d549544d9/__init__.py).
reads.worst: The loader accepts file and environment credentials and globally caches the resolved key and database configuration without a profile boundary, creating a credential and memory isolation risk [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MohamedElsiddig/hermes-plugin-factkit/ffe3e255755e5b2b92bd5a06dfb89a0d549544d9/__init__.py).

plugins.name: hermesmade
plugins.author: Noshkoto
plugins.does: Shares sanitized bot profiles to a community shelf, installs reviewed bot packages, and migrates Grok Bot exports.

reads.best: Provides Desktop previews, secret scanning, safe archive extraction, paused schedules, disabled MCP servers, and approval hooks.
reads.worst: Despite these safeguards, upload and unshare read management credentials from shared.json rather than Hermes secret storage, conflicting with catalog rule 11.

plugins.name: pioneer
plugins.author: acadine-core
plugins.does: Uses local work context and public search signals to propose product gaps, check existing alternatives and keep a scored evidence board. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acadine-intelligence/hermes-pioneer/5aa55141db765138a5ce1cf96db1295d7f3442d7/README.md)

reads.best: Ledger citation checks, coded absence-score limits, source failures and a persistent Desktop/HTML trail make brainstorming more inspectable than a free-form prompt.
reads.worst: Citation checks establish ledger membership rather than truth, and demand ratings and absence rulings still depend on the proposing model and incomplete default search coverage.

plugins.name: vitam
plugins.author: taylorwtf
plugins.does: Connects a modified PS Vita microphone and camera to Hermes through a local speech and audio-reply bridge.

reads.best: A readable Lua handheld client and Python bridge bring push-to-talk voice and camera input to unusual user-owned hardware.
reads.worst: The bridge sends Authorization as three asterisks plus the key instead of Bearer, exposes unauthenticated LAN endpoints, and has no committed tests.

plugins.name: openrouter-provider-picker
plugins.author: PotatoWareGit
plugins.does: Provides a Desktop settings page and agent tool for discovering OpenRouter upstream providers and saving global or per-model routing preferences.

reads.best: A real provider search and editing UI, status chip, shared backend validation and literal dotted-model YAML keys make a useful Hermes model-control feature ([UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PotatoWareGit/hermes-openrouter-provider/afba3e648ecbfd18688f845e9f3ec7cf86315ff5/desktop/plugin.js), [backend](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PotatoWareGit/hermes-openrouter-provider/afba3e648ecbfd18688f845e9f3ec7cf86315ff5/dashboard/plugin_api.py)).
reads.worst: Saving a model pin through the UI reconstructs it without existing data_collection or require_parameters overrides, silently discarding them; backend validation also drops an explicit require_parameters=false ([UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PotatoWareGit/hermes-openrouter-provider/afba3e648ecbfd18688f845e9f3ec7cf86315ff5/desktop/plugin.js), [validation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PotatoWareGit/hermes-openrouter-provider/afba3e648ecbfd18688f845e9f3ec7cf86315ff5/dashboard/plugin_api.py)).

plugins.name: creative-review
plugins.author: peterpeeterspeter
plugins.does: Provides image review boards with point annotations, version comparison, revision briefs and approval-history exports. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peterpeeterspeter/hermes-creative-review/3f09cdce305c9c9db19ce9d752134ca1a35344e0/README.md)

reads.best: The Desktop-to-composer workflow turns spatial feedback into a persistent, structured revision brief with board ownership checks. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peterpeeterspeter/hermes-creative-review/3f09cdce305c9c9db19ce9d752134ca1a35344e0/README.md)
reads.worst: The central live Electron review-to-generation handoff remains unverified, with screenshots and a demo recording still pending. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peterpeeterspeter/hermes-creative-review/3f09cdce305c9c9db19ce9d752134ca1a35344e0/README.md)

plugins.name: gmi-sandbox
plugins.author: avinxshKD
plugins.does: Runs Hermes terminal and file operations in disposable GMI Cloud sandboxes through a native terminal-environment provider.

reads.best: The provider extends where Hermes executes code while retaining command guards, profile-scoped secrets and explicit cancellation and cleanup handling.
reads.worst: The author explicitly reports offline-only verification, so real provisioning, file operations and billable-resource cleanup remain unproven.

plugins.name: creature-workshop
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Exposes a shellops project's declared toolchain, installation, testing and linting through Hermes tools, session hooks and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Coordinates the agent and Desktop on a user-selected repository, checks project consent centrally, and strips most inherited environment variables from child processes.
reads.worst: Requires the shellops project layout, executes approved project scripts outside the terminal sandbox, and the pinned tree contains no dedicated plugin regression suite.

plugins.name: moment
plugins.author: noprijbi99-dotcom
plugins.does: Detects mid-session changes to the active profile’s soul and memory files and adds timestamped drift receipts before model calls. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noprijbi99-dotcom/moment/1af58dda54a9ad9310acb4cad928a6db63f8403b/tools.py)

reads.best: It solves a concrete stale-memory problem through a native pre_llm_call hook with per-call profile resolution and silence when nothing changed. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noprijbi99-dotcom/moment/1af58dda54a9ad9310acb4cad928a6db63f8403b/tools.py)
reads.worst: Shared state uses an unlocked read-modify-write with a fixed temporary filename, risking lost receipts during concurrent turns, and no regression tests are shipped at this pin. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noprijbi99-dotcom/moment/1af58dda54a9ad9310acb4cad928a6db63f8403b/tools.py)

plugins.name: dreamer
plugins.author: Cosmonautic1
plugins.does: Uses idle time to summarize local session residue into LLM-generated dreams and injects their insights into a later fresh session.

reads.best: The idle scheduler, persistent journal and first-turn hook create actual cross-session consolidation through the host-owned LLM.
reads.worst: In dream_engine.py, pending_wake parses the timestamp column as insight targets and misindexes timestamp/count metadata, silently losing stored destinations from wake context.

plugins.name: fleet-memory
plugins.author: tylerjharden
plugins.does: Registers a profile-local memory provider that prefills turns with fleet notes, exposes search/ingest tools and optionally imports Notion search results.

reads.best: It uses the native prefetch and sync_turn lifecycle with profile-specific storage and scoped secrets, so recall happens automatically before a turn.
reads.worst: Notion sync stores only each page title as both title and body, while retrieval is substring matching rather than meaningful page-content memory.

plugins.name: netscope
plugins.author: Mxhi-04
plugins.does: Analyzes local pcap and pcapng captures into structured network findings, cached queries and interactive standalone HTML reports.

reads.best: A dependency-free parser, explainable heuristics and polished offline report are backed by corrupt-input and report-injection regression tests.
reads.worst: Its reader budget is not an end-to-end timeout, memory grows with capture complexity, and lightweight heuristics cannot replace full protocol analysis.

plugins.name: hermes-phone-control
plugins.author: jinsu133
plugins.does: Connects a same-device Hermes/Termux agent to an Android companion for bounded phone observation, accessibility actions and voice interaction.

reads.best: Authenticated loopback transport, bounded responses, device identity checks and Android-owned action confirmation are supported by extensive defensive test code.
reads.worst: The pinned preview reads and stores pairing credentials in files contrary to the catalog rule, omits Android build prerequisites, and has no verified end-to-end spoken conversation.

plugins.name: leash
plugins.author: nicoarias81
plugins.does: Provides scope-gated web security probes, multi-identity access-control checks and an evidence ledger with reports.

reads.best: Concrete replay, fuzzing and crawl primitives produce measured evidence rather than asking the model to invent security findings.
reads.worst: Session credentials are stored in plaintext identities.json outside Hermes secret storage, and DNS authorization is separated from the later connection lookup.

plugins.name: decision-forge
plugins.author: mintymac
plugins.does: Routes, lints and renders structured decision briefs as interactive HTML and Markdown with a Desktop field guide.

reads.best: A coherent set of six formats, escaped HTML compilation, Markdown fallbacks and a finished Desktop guide make the presentation useful.
reads.worst: Most of the decision discipline is a bundled prompt contract; the code checks structure and wording rather than whether evidence or recommendations are sound.

plugins.name: spotify-desktop
plugins.author: amitamit10
plugins.does: Adds a Hermes Desktop status-bar Spotify Connect remote with playback, search, playlists, queue, volume, and device transfer controls.

reads.best: It delivers a polished Desktop surface while reusing Hermes's existing Spotify authentication and token-refresh machinery.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains no tests and depends on private/internal Spotify integration seams, so compatibility failures are easy to imagine.

plugins.name: us-air-rules
plugins.author: entersidbellad
plugins.does: Seven tools that screen a plant or household against EPA Title 40 rules using live eCFR and Federal Register data and bundled rule packs, returning applies/check/skip verdicts with citations, plus scenario compare and state SIP lookup.

reads.best: Deep, citation-backed domain engine that uses only the standard library, needs no API key, caps its cache and Federal Register calls, has about 1,400 lines of offline tests and CI, and states clearly that it is not a compliance determination.
reads.worst: The audience is a small niche (cement and lime plants, EPA air rules), and the plant layer covers only a few industries.

plugins.name: netease-cloud
plugins.author: BoosterCore
plugins.does: Desktop status-bar NetEase Cloud Music player with search, lyrics, likes and playlists via a local FastAPI backend.

reads.best: Polished Desktop player with screenshots and bilingual README, stdlib-only crypto.
reads.worst: Stores the MUSIC_U login cookie in a plain file instead of Hermes's secret store; no tests.

plugins.name: sarvam-provider
plugins.author: Subramanyarao11
plugins.does: Model-provider profile adding Sarvam AI (Sarvam-105B and hosted open models) to Hermes.

reads.best: Handles Sarvam specifics (reasoning_effort mapping, 16384 max tokens, filtering non-chat models) in a tiny clear profile with tests.
reads.worst: A ~60-line provider profile; niche audience and a common kind of plugin.

plugins.name: anki
plugins.author: suhas-svg
plugins.does: Tools to add cards, search, list due cards and grade answers in a local Anki collection via AnkiConnect.

reads.best: Local-only AnkiConnect client with tests, CI and a study skill; preview-then-add flow.
reads.worst: Single test file and depends on the user running Anki with AnkiConnect.

plugins.name: autom
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Adds Autom's Google SERP API as a Hermes web_search backend provider.

reads.best: A clean native web-search provider: the key comes from Hermes's secret store, it uses only the standard library, and its tests mock the network.
reads.worst: One more paid search backend, with search only (no extract).

plugins.name: agentci
plugins.author: EikeAhlers
plugins.does: Runs prompt-based Hermes regression suites and model comparisons using session records, file hashes and generated reports.

reads.best: Checks real workspace changes, tool usage and token consumption rather than relying on the agent’s assertion of success.
reads.worst: The runner unconditionally starts Hermes with --yolo without a sandbox or approval gate, violating the catalog’s child-process approval rule.

plugins.name: session-receipts
plugins.author: ryanomara
plugins.does: Builds offline HTML session receipts and weekly digests from Hermes session and kanban records, with optional redacted copies. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ryanomara/hermes-plugin-receipts/c7df9d35f6234eca9adeaa030e450b5ac8ea10e6/receipts/plugin.py)

reads.best: Read-only store access, preserved failure history, cost reconciliation, rendered examples, and extensive privacy tests make the reporting useful and reviewable. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ryanomara/hermes-plugin-receipts/c7df9d35f6234eca9adeaa030e450b5ac8ea10e6/receipts/plugin.py)
reads.worst: Redaction remains pattern-based and requires manual review before sharing, while the README still uses placeholder repository install commands. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ryanomara/hermes-plugin-receipts/c7df9d35f6234eca9adeaa030e450b5ac8ea10e6/README.md)

plugins.name: citation-guard
plugins.author: ChienNguyen23
plugins.does: Checks citations against scholarly registries and appends warnings to Hermes replies for mismatched, missing, or retracted references. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChienNguyen23/hermes-citation-guard/6916b2ae7f561765883c57b32441db049e246113/__init__.py)

reads.best: Deterministic registry verification distinguishes network failures from nonexistent references and includes extraction tests and benchmark fixtures. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChienNguyen23/hermes-citation-guard/6916b2ae7f561765883c57b32441db049e246113/__init__.py)
reads.worst: The optional NCBI API key is read from ordinary config rather than the secret route, and NCBI request URLs containing that key become disk-cache keys. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChienNguyen23/hermes-citation-guard/6916b2ae7f561765883c57b32441db049e246113/sources.py)

plugins.name: airflow-mlops
plugins.author: dayzell
plugins.does: Adds Airflow monitoring, failure diagnosis, targeted task retries, audit reports, and optional Docker testing of DAG changes. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dayzell/MLOps_Assistant_Hermes_x_AirFlow/1417f40f29c28fd7aac571758c34475c6dc11ad9/README.md)

reads.best: Read-only defaults, hidden-failure detection, retry previews, approval hooks, and a journal-before-write guard make it more than a reporting prompt. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dayzell/MLOps_Assistant_Hermes_x_AirFlow/1417f40f29c28fd7aac571758c34475c6dc11ad9/README.md)
reads.worst: The pinned plugin branch omits the advertised unit and end-to-end tests, so its complex remediation and DAG-write guards cannot be assessed against shipped regression coverage. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dayzell/MLOps_Assistant_Hermes_x_AirFlow/1417f40f29c28fd7aac571758c34475c6dc11ad9/README.md)

plugins.name: dome-relay
plugins.author: nerdcakes
plugins.does: Queues structured cross-agent jobs through an HTTPS relay and retrieves or cancels their results in the originating conversation.

reads.best: Persistent job state, idempotency, compaction lineage and conservative uncertain-delivery handling are backed by focused relay and plugin tests.
reads.worst: Users must operate a separate relay and worker plus an executive routine, and automatic push delivery is explicitly unsupported.

plugins.name: pocket-platform
plugins.author: AgentMadeThis
plugins.does: Registers an authenticated radio-companion platform with bounded Hermes chat, notes and optional local music controls.

reads.best: Native session integration includes HMAC and peer checks, explicit owner enrollment, durable replay prevention and a dedicated-process veto on all model tools.
reads.worst: The submitted install subdirectory is only the host plugin; usable hardware firmware, bridge service wiring, enrollment and a clean consumer installation remain external gaps.

plugins.name: hermes-cartographer
plugins.author: nnazinwaogu
plugins.does: Adds an incremental code index, repo-map context injection, symbol lookup/reference tools and Python rename previews. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nnazinwaogu/hermes-cartographer/f8b6739af2aaa2f0da2c7c392e9d69e404deedee/README.md)

reads.best: Local indexing and bounded first-turn repo maps provide useful code context without embeddings, network access or extra model calls. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nnazinwaogu/hermes-cartographer/f8b6739af2aaa2f0da2c7c392e9d69e404deedee/README.md)
reads.worst: Rename traverses every indexed Python file and matches identifiers by spelling without binding or scope resolution, so unrelated same-named symbols can be renamed together. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nnazinwaogu/hermes-cartographer/f8b6739af2aaa2f0da2c7c392e9d69e404deedee/carto/rename.py)

plugins.name: aegis-spend-guard
plugins.author: georgeonweb3
plugins.does: Applies owner-defined spending caps, recipient policies and a freeze switch before spend-shaped tool calls.

reads.best: Uses real pre-tool block/approval directives and a tested integer-cent policy engine rather than asking the model to obey a budget.
reads.worst: Detection is heuristic and the ledger has no atomic reservation for concurrent spends, so parallel calls can exceed the daily cap and dynamically constructed payments can evade detection.

plugins.name: explainer
plugins.author: suhas-svg
plugins.does: Renders model-authored storyboards into narrated MP4 explainers with synchronized captions, slides and a local video library.

reads.best: Implements timed narration, caption alignment, video encoding and tested SSRF-resistant image retrieval with actionable setup diagnostics.
reads.worst: Narration depends on an online Edge TTS service and local ffmpeg, and the presentation workflow largely remains conventional tooling that a skill could orchestrate.

plugins.name: sentinel-governance
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Audits proposed Hermes tool actions against deterministic policies and optionally requests native approval or blocks them.

reads.best: Privacy-conscious audit records and fresh per-event approval keys are backed by adversarial tests and clear audit-versus-enforcement semantics.
reads.worst: Its classifier recognizes only a tiny terminal grammar; enforcement blocks routine unknown tools, audit mode does not enforce, and neither mode proves actual execution or provides a sandbox.

plugins.name: iv-studio
plugins.author: hollisorg
plugins.does: Registers local IV Studio image and video generation providers, readiness checks and resumable video-render retrieval for Hermes’s native media tools.

reads.best: Provider registration brings local GPU rendering and character-aware video jobs into Hermes’s existing image_generate and video_generate workflow.
reads.worst: Model-supplied picture URLs go directly to urlopen without internal-address checks, the child inherits all environment variables, and the pinned plugin has no automated tests.

plugins.name: spacewise
plugins.author: ardianreffa
plugins.does: Scans selected folders for duplicate media, weak photos and installers and offers approval-gated trash moves with undo.

reads.best: Category-only trash selection, protected-path checks, keeper revalidation and reversible moves make cleanup unusually careful.
reads.worst: Windows supports reports only, video similarity is unavailable, and photo quality judgments are simple local heuristics rather than semantic selection.

plugins.name: picky
plugins.author: decentralpapi
plugins.does: Finds and ranks OSM lodging and routes, estimates ride options and builds user-confirmed booking links ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/decentralpapi/picky/58501e01835fa78355be1f76543ff2795f542573/README.md)).

reads.best: A polished keyless workflow with fixture tests, allowlisted bounded HTTP, useful fallbacks and explicit human booking/payment.
reads.worst: Its best-stay and best-ride choices lack live vacancy, room prices and ride quotes, relying on OSM tags and static regional fare assumptions.

plugins.name: pickwise-photos
plugins.author: ardianreffa
plugins.does: Locally scores photo sharpness/exposure and bursts, learns corrections, and offers dry-run sorting, sidecars and reversible moves ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ardianreffa/pickwise-photos/14a07d0d6b1d6d707926f1ad02cf79ca573349ee/README.md)).

reads.best: Useful computation beyond chat: resumable cached analysis, RAW/JPEG pairing, disk checks and partial-failure tests support a practical photo workflow.
reads.worst: Image metrics cannot tell whether the subject is sharp or eyes are closed; that requires a separately requested Hermes vision check, and RAW quality depends on embedded previews.

plugins.name: language-lock
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Detects reply-language drift locally and injects a correction on the next turn, with per-session language settings and status commands.

reads.best: Adds automatic session-aware monitoring through pre/post-LLM hooks without network calls, dependencies or extra model usage.
reads.worst: It cannot repair the current streamed reply, and script/common-word detection plus broad translation-request matching can miss or misclassify multilingual turns.

plugins.name: lane-keeper
plugins.author: MindSproutStudios
plugins.does: Keeps persistent active and dormant project lanes in Markdown, injects focus context, and reserves promotions for user slash commands.

reads.best: Separates model capture and checkpoint tools from user status controls and tests cap handling, stale notices, and tampered Markdown.
reads.worst: The advertised hard gate uses best-effort tool-name and command-text matching that can miss indirect registry writes; the JSON registry also lacks cross-process locking.

plugins.name: raise
plugins.author: GenesisEngine-Triolith
plugins.does: Maintains a fundraising pipeline with evidence-based investor ranking, deterministic contact gates and checked outreach drafts.

reads.best: Code enforces contact cooldowns, cited scoring and draft checks, with focused safety tests and an offline demonstration.
reads.worst: Its draft-only guard relies on recognizing tool names and recipient text and returns no block on exceptions, so it is not a comprehensive sending boundary.

plugins.name: vail-assurance-panel
plugins.author: mnshah
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop fleet assurance panel that uploads reviewed profile source to VAIL and displays risks, probes, changes, and local fix records.

reads.best: The native panel offers per-profile scan progress and an explicit upload review, with allowlisted packaging and redaction tests.
reads.worst: Redaction is regex-based and skips multiline YAML secret values, while tests cover packaging but not the complete remote scan lifecycle.

plugins.name: taster
plugins.author: Yonkoo11
plugins.does: Runs a native plugin once in a macOS sandbox with canary files and environment variables, then reports observed behavior against its declarations.

reads.best: Tests exercise real-home denial, canary access, forged reports and several environment-read evasions, and the report explicitly avoids declaring a plugin safe.
reads.worst: Only macOS is supported, tools are probed with empty arguments, and the target shares the Python monitor process, allowing unobserved paths or monitor tampering.

plugins.name: podcast
plugins.author: suhas-svg
plugins.does: Turns structured scripts into multi-host MP3 episodes with speech synthesis, mastering, chapters, transcripts and a daily-briefing blueprint.

reads.best: Production code implements paced synthesis retries and speaker-aware mixing, and an ffprobe-based test checks the actual mastered audio metadata and chapters.
reads.worst: Speech depends on Microsoft Edge online TTS, and without ffmpeg the fallback loses mastering, pauses and embedded chapters; there is no Desktop production interface.

plugins.name: compound-security
plugins.author: imranye
plugins.does: Provides 13 security workflow skills with local scripts for dependency evidence, audit records, patch tracking, verification, and reusable prevention.

reads.best: It combines scoped audit and remediation workflows with tested local validators and explicit evidence records, and its docs state the limits of each stage.
reads.worst: It supplies no sandbox or scanners, has no end-to-end host/model audit validation, and most of its behavior is skill guidance that relies on the host's shell and agent capabilities.

plugins.name: agent-music-jam
plugins.author: vdimarco
plugins.does: Starts a token-protected loopback web app where you conduct a four-piece synthesized band in natural language while Web Audio keeps the groove playing.

reads.best: Solid engineering: 127.0.0.1 bind with token, Host and Origin checks, bounded buffers, and failed plans never replace the playing pattern; 14 tests plus evidence logs.
reads.worst: A niche toy fixed to one key outside Hermes Desktop; the jam_start result puts the access token into the transcript and the subagent path runs on a thread after the tool returns.

plugins.name: zotero
plugins.author: suhas-svg
plugins.does: Lets Hermes search the user's local Zotero library, read PDF highlights and full text, format citations with Zotero's engine, add papers by DOI/arXiv and check a draft's citations.

reads.best: Seven tools over Zotero's loopback API using only the standard library, with user-actionable errors, 32 tests and CI on Linux and Windows.
reads.worst: It serves only Zotero desktop users, has no screenshots or Desktop UI, and its catalog pull request is closed.

plugins.name: crown
plugins.author: SAMBAS123
plugins.does: Gives several Hermes instances on one Linux host a single renewable 'speaker' lease and a durable shared SQLite record of reports, questions and human answers, with stale speakers fenced out.

reads.best: A carefully fenced lease (generation checked in the same SQLite transaction as each publish) with 22 standard-library tests and recorded kill/pause failure proofs, and loading starts nothing until /crown here.
reads.worst: It publishes only to its own local SQLite outlet on a single Linux host and its README calls it a prototype, so few users have a use for it today.

plugins.name: intents-pay
plugins.author: ayinmodeolarewaju-bot
plugins.does: Prices and invoices a cross-chain payment to a NEAR account through the NEAR Intents 1-Click API, dry-run by default, and verifies quote signatures locally without moving funds.

reads.best: It handles money conservatively: no keys, an explicit recipient, a pre_tool_call hook that escalates payable calls to Hermes's approval prompt, the optional API key read from the secret store, and 16 tests with CI.
reads.worst: It only produces quotes and invoices for NEAR recipients, a narrow need for Hermes users, and its catalog pull request is closed.

plugins.name: rom-studio
plugins.author: erosika
plugins.does: A toolkit for building your own handheld game from a user-supplied GBA decomp by chat: a bun CLI builds the ROM and drives a headless emulator for screenshots, and a Desktop pane shows the feed, maps, music and dialogue.

reads.best: A genuinely original use of an agent with a large readable toolkit (emulator driver, map/music/dialogue tools, BPS patch sharing), no ROM shipped, and loopback/Host/Origin gates on its local servers with tests.
reads.worst: The Hermes plugin itself registers zero tools and zero hooks, the README's own "Not tested yet" section lists the pane inside Desktop and the skill loaded through the plugin, and setup needs a heavy Linux-only toolchain.

plugins.name: dike
plugins.author: Grizaceo
plugins.does: One tool that runs a vendored, offline Chilean-law engine in a sandboxed subprocess to check every statute article citation in a legal brief against a hash-verified local corpus of 25 statutes, marking each verified or unverified with a reason.

reads.best: Verification is deterministic and auditable: the corpus ships with SHA-256 sums, the engine runs with a minimal environment and no credentials, and the adapter validates the engine's answer against a fixed contract with 50 tests.
reads.worst: A Linux-only, Spanish-language tool for Chilean lawyers with five Python dependencies, a slow first-call unpack, and a README section left as a placeholder to be completed by the maintainer.

plugins.name: tallyseal
plugins.author: Venkat-RJ
plugins.does: Checks a grouped CSV report against a SHA-256-pinned source CSV, group by group, and seals exactly the report bytes that passed.

reads.best: Rigorous: it catches errors that cancel out in the grand total, rejects symlinks/FIFOs, seals atomically, and has 8 thorough tests plus a demo through the real Hermes loader.
reads.worst: Narrow niche (integer minor units, exact columns, one tool), with no UI.

plugins.name: tightbeam
plugins.author: skeptical-agency
plugins.does: Audits and optimizes YouTube catalogs and uploads, schedules and monitors multi-platform shorts through OpusClip.

reads.best: Host-owned OAuth and MCP credentials, resumable catalog sweeps and automation blueprints combine into a useful creator workflow.
reads.worst: Scheduling treats a failed collision lookup as an empty calendar and counts writes as scheduled without matching read-back entries; no regression tests are shipped in the pinned tree.

plugins.name: whatsapp-plus
plugins.author: amitamit10
plugins.does: Extends Hermes WhatsApp with persistent group context, trust tiers, messaging tools, campaigns and optional voice calls.

reads.best: Persistent group context and trust-tier hooks address practical limits of using a personal agent in busy chats.
reads.worst: The pinned code re-registers the bundled WhatsApp platform, rebuilds its bridge at runtime and directly reads .env; these conflict with catalog requirements, and the maintainer explicitly declined the listing.

plugins.name: hermes-mark-words
plugins.author: hey-yx
plugins.does: Renders model-authored hidden word directives as persistent Desktop underlines, hover explanations and follow-up composer actions.

reads.best: The in-band directive format supports immediate interactive annotations without an extra model request, with detailed UI regression tests.
reads.worst: It queries internal transcript selectors such as [data-role="assistant"] and .aui-md and observes the document tree, conflicting with the catalog SDK-only policy; annotations also depend on the replying model spotting its own doubtful terms.

plugins.name: video-xray
plugins.author: LuuMoss
plugins.does: Analyzes sampled video frames and speech into timestamped reports and video-generation prompts, with a Desktop workbench and resumable jobs.

reads.best: The implemented pipeline combines configurable frame sampling, local or cloud transcription, persisted segment progress and extensive workbench controls.
reads.worst: Cloud ASR keys are saved in asr-engines.json rather than Hermes secrets, and the pinned repository contains no automated test suite.

plugins.name: universal-plugin-port
plugins.author: friendly-neighborhood-coding-man
plugins.does: Inspects foreign agent packages and stages or repairs bounded Hermes-compatible skills with provenance, review and rollback.

reads.best: Hash-bound candidates, explicit unsupported-capability reports and regression tests make migration losses visible and repairs reviewable.
reads.worst: The guided workflow remains limited to a pinned pilot and disposable homes, while model-facing staging accepts a model-supplied approval flag for unsandboxed foreign-code inspection.

plugins.name: hermes-bim-studio
plugins.author: stupidburgers
plugins.does: Inspects local IFC building models, exports traceable quantity and optional priced reports, and generates an interactive offline 3D viewer.

reads.best: Quantity coverage and IFC-unit conversion are explicit, with security tests, confined output paths and vendored viewer assets.
reads.worst: The pinned README still describes arbitrary output paths and silent overwrites despite the security fix, and rendering is limited to 150 elements.

plugins.name: hostyourai
plugins.author: cogitor
plugins.does: Registers HostYourAI as a model provider with task/policy routing hints, optional automatic task classification and private balance reporting.

reads.best: Scoped-key handling, redirect refusal, bounded automatic classification and detailed tests support a well-documented provider integration.
reads.worst: Most model selection happens in a proprietary external service, and routing preferences are shared across every chat on the profile.

plugins.name: repager
plugins.author: clawpawtech
plugins.does: Captures a public page's hero section in Chromium, has you approve its exact copy and CTA, lets ctx.llm pick among four fixed layouts, verifies in a browser and exports HTML/CSS.

reads.best: Evidence-bound design: the model can't write copy or HTML, records are signed, 232 tests, and a sandboxed browser subprocess with SSRF blocking and timeouts.
reads.worst: Narrow audience with heavy setup (Node, Playwright, Chromium) and strict model-route rules; the README is dense jargon with no screenshots, and approval is an agent-callable tool.

plugins.name: roster-compiler
plugins.author: COSMICnoob80
plugins.does: Parses hospital rosters, reports uncovered shifts, double bookings, excessive runs and unsafe night-to-day transitions, then exports corrected CSV and HTML reports.

reads.best: Deterministic parsers, explicit warnings instead of guesses, input protection, and focused tests make the safety-critical path trustworthy.
reads.worst: It is a specialized file tool without Hermes hooks, Desktop, or broader agent-platform changes, and PDF/image support has format limits.

plugins.name: hive-intelligence
plugins.author: rishabhng
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted Hive MCP service offering broad crypto prices, research, wallet, security, DeFi and prediction-market tools.

reads.best: Its discovery loop and broad normalized crypto-tool catalog can save an agent from stitching together many providers.
reads.worst: The submitted package is primarily remote configuration and skills, so correctness, availability and much of the security boundary depend on a proprietary hosted service outside the pinned code.

plugins.name: subscription-sheriff
plugins.author: HATWHY4041
plugins.does: Tracks subscriptions and free trials from plain-English messages in plugin state, warns before charges via two scheduled-task blueprints and a /sheriff command, and summarizes spend per currency.

reads.best: Fully offline, standard-library code with 31 tests, month-end date rolling, per-currency totals without invented exchange rates, and quiet de-duplicated reminders.
reads.worst: A familiar subscription-tracker idea; much of it (a list plus a cron reminder) could be approximated with Hermes memory and a scheduled prompt.

plugins.name: constraint-vault
plugins.author: jusst01
plugins.does: Pins exact user constraints (numbers, addresses, hard rules) in a local JSON store and re-injects them verbatim every turn via pre_llm_call and again right after compaction via transform_tool_result, logging a SHA-256 of each injection.

reads.best: A targeted fix for a real failure (compaction paraphrasing exact values) using hooks only a plugin has, with a hash-logged delivery record and size caps.
reads.worst: Only three tests, failures are swallowed silently (a failed save is dropped with no error), the injection log grows without bound, and an agent can pin text from untrusted tool output that then rides every turn.

plugins.name: hermes-studio
plugins.author: Morkeeth
plugins.does: Composes local transcription, media selection, portrait video edits and technical review, with an optional SSH workstation queue and explicit Telegram preview delivery.

reads.best: Uses real editable video projects, source hashes, idempotent queue requests, and uncertain-delivery handling instead of claiming a render succeeded.
reads.worst: Setup depends on a separate editor, speech model and private reviewed recipe; the complete new-footage attachment-to-reply-edit loop is not verified.

plugins.name: exoself
plugins.author: cYoren
plugins.does: Creates a persistent per-profile temperament and evolves a managed SOUL.md block after sessions.

reads.best: Deterministic identity certificates, managed-block preservation and lifecycle tests make an evolving persona concrete.
reads.worst: Registration writes profile identity files and can run two CLI calls with separate eight-second timeouts, exceeding the ten-second host load budget it cites.

plugins.name: grounder
plugins.author: hdiggity
plugins.does: Registers Grounder as Hermes's web-search backend with search-key or Hermes-managed OAuth access.

reads.best: The provider integrates native web search and host-managed OAuth, with clear setup, failure messages and local API-stub tests.
reads.worst: provider.py assumes results is a sliceable list of mappings and reads entire response bodies, so malformed or oversized upstream responses bypass its promised graceful-failure boundary.

plugins.name: agentic-operations
plugins.author: ryanteoyx
plugins.does: Provides a synthetic manufacturing control room with constrained plans, durable simulated purchases, reconciliation and evidence-backed forecast correction.

reads.best: Transaction-backed reservations, stable action identity and crash-recovery tests demonstrate a credible execution-and-learning loop across tools and dashboard.
