reads.worst: All business data and ERP actions are synthetic; no production connector or company RBAC makes this usable for a real manufacturer yet.

plugins.name: hermes-issue-orchestrator
plugins.author: krantikaridev
plugins.does: Uses GitHub issues as a Hermes task queue with claim, progress and handoff tools plus automatic session-scoped token-usage comments ([pinned source](https://github.com/krantikaridev/hermes-issue-orchestrator/tree/9996a56a4dbdcf2bcd56f31f6940425b205af8da)).

reads.best: Scoped secrets, strict GitHub destinations, durable comment deduplication and tests for lost responses and rate limits give the queue a carefully engineered core.
reads.worst: Auto-claim examines only the first thirty open issues without pagination and claims are check-then-act, so busy queues can falsely appear empty and competing instances can claim the same issue ([service.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krantikaridev/hermes-issue-orchestrator/9996a56a4dbdcf2bcd56f31f6940425b205af8da/service.py)).

plugins.name: hermes-agent-radio
plugins.author: Sahil-SS9
plugins.does: Embeds a remote radio player in Hermes Desktop and exposes station feeds, show sources, listener requests, and voting to chat ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/hermes-agent-radio-plugin/088a67e1e0bc2f233a1939ab73a80658298be5cd/__init__.py)).

reads.best: Its player dock, full page, pop-out, and source-linked show notes make the station convenient while working in Hermes ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/hermes-agent-radio-plugin/088a67e1e0bc2f233a1939ab73a80658298be5cd/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: Programming, playback, and moderation depend on a separate station service, leaving the submitted plugin primarily a player and API bridge ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/hermes-agent-radio-plugin/088a67e1e0bc2f233a1939ab73a80658298be5cd/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: hermes-session-signal
plugins.author: raitoxlol
plugins.does: Adds Working badges and a clickable count for navigating busy mounted sessions in Hermes Desktop.

reads.best: The small readable implementation uses public SDK atoms and navigation, cleans up contributions and ships an installed-app verification script.
reads.worst: Counts exclude unmounted rows, and differing runtime and durable IDs can hide background Working state until the session is focused.

plugins.name: send-lock
plugins.author: percyhendrux123-prog
plugins.does: Installs a default-deny pre-tool-call policy that permits only a narrow configurable set of read, draft, and explicitly enabled iMessage actions.

reads.best: The registered hook fails closed and its compact active policy is tested separately from the legacy matrix.
reads.worst: Its fixed, highly restrictive policy and Axiom-specific configuration make it useful chiefly for a particular tightly managed agent setup.

plugins.name: hermes-camera-watch
plugins.author: arcabotai
plugins.does: Polls named RTSP or HTTP cameras for frame changes and saves stills, local motion captions and dashboard events.

reads.best: An allowlist interlock, hardware-free mock porch and local HTTP tests make the camera workflow inspectable without uploading frames.
reads.worst: Authenticated cameras take passwords embedded in settings URLs and pass RTSP URLs to ffmpeg argv instead of using Hermes secret scope, conflicting with catalog credential rules.

plugins.name: eventforge
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Proxies a local EventForge control plane into Hermes with approval-gated webhook/event/subagent tools and verified-event context injection.

reads.best: Approval gates, get_secret token handling, https enforcement for remote planes and hook tests.
reads.worst: Only useful with the author's separate EventForge service running.

plugins.name: skill-governance
plugins.author: moonlight-lupin
plugins.does: Tracks skill provenance via fingerprinted manifests, acknowledgements and advisory contrastive probes through skill/session/tool/LLM hooks.

reads.best: Uses skill lifecycle hooks for drift detection that a skill alone cannot do.
reads.worst: Very large, abstract codebase whose value to ordinary users is hard to see.

plugins.name: openrouter-balance
plugins.author: maeinomatic
plugins.does: Shows the live OpenRouter credit balance as a Desktop status-bar chip, through a dashboard route that proxies /api/v1/credits with the key Hermes already holds.

reads.best: Small and focused: it reads the key through agent.secret_scope.get_secret, never sends it to the renderer, uses a 15s timeout, and refetches after each turn.
reads.worst: There is no README, no tests and a register() that does nothing; the repo is just five files.

plugins.name: aws-manager
plugins.author: ParichayMago
plugins.does: A Desktop dashboard to launch, start, stop and terminate EC2, invoke Lambda and manage S3, with a demo mode and activity verification.

reads.best: Destructive actions require typing the target, and a credential-free demo plus screenshot make it easy to try.
reads.worst: It is a cloud console with no tests and no agent tools, so it adds little that Hermes itself does.

plugins.name: callit
plugins.author: k58v2hbzkk-del
plugins.does: Turns group chats into a prediction league: calls, sides, auto-settled results from oracles, a leaderboard, and optional stakes via a Solana escrow.

reads.best: Persistent per-chat league with a cron referee that settles from real results, plus a written escrow program.
reads.worst: Commits a devnet deployer keypair in escrow/devnet/deployer.json and has a referee key sign escrow settlements of staked money without a per-payment human approval.

plugins.name: va-claims
plugins.author: lEWFkRAD
plugins.does: Seven tools and a Desktop page for US veterans: a 38 CFR filing guide, intent-to-file and benefit deadline tracking, and live claim status and contention lookup through the VA Lighthouse APIs.

reads.best: A real, underserved use with live VA Lighthouse API calls, local deadline tracking that works with no setup, and a Desktop benefits page with screenshots.
reads.worst: It signs the VA client assertion with an RSA private key read from a file path rather than Hermes's secret store, there are no tests, and the pull request was closed unmerged by its author.

plugins.name: ember-radar
plugins.author: sicutdeusvult
plugins.does: Read-only Ember Solana launchpad tools, a watchlist with a pre_llm_call pulse, an /ember command and a daily-brief blueprint.

reads.best: Ten tools with timeouts, caching, fixtures-based tests and screenshots, no keys needed.
reads.worst: Serves a narrow crypto-launchpad audience and is mostly a read-only API wrapper.

plugins.name: evident-evidence
plugins.author: Akshay-Scalelabs
plugins.does: Opens a site in a locked-down headless Chromium, has the configured model review how it comes across to buyers, and writes an offline HTML report with annotated screenshots and re-runnable checks.

reads.best: Serious safety design: origins denied by default, DNS-pinned transport, delete gated on confirm_delete, model access only through ctx.llm, and 72 unit tests plus integration scripts.
reads.worst: Very dense one-line code (report.py about 100KB), licensing 'not yet specified', a system-prompt section that claims routing 'even when the previous topic was another plugin', and report CTA links to the author's commercial service.

plugins.name: icon-index
plugins.author: minutechreview
plugins.does: Bundles a catalog of 40 CC0 3D icons that the agent can search, embed or save into a project, plus a Desktop gallery pane.

reads.best: The built desktop/plugin.js matches its readable source, and icon_save never overwrites, with a size cap and timeout; 12 tests.
reads.worst: Narrow use (40 icons from the author's own library), and the 3D viewer and recolouring run on a remote page that is not in the repo.

plugins.name: spoonmaster
plugins.author: gueysito
plugins.does: Restaurant-choosing workflow that runs bounded parallel research and presents a sourced pick with alternatives and optional private tastes.

reads.best: Over 100 tests and careful evidence handling with budgets and expiry.
reads.worst: Its own README calls it a local pilot, not a released catalog plugin, and the task is one a search-plus-prompt skill largely covers.

plugins.name: hermes-verify
plugins.author: BrandonDucar
plugins.does: Flags risky tool calls, logs audit receipts and labels finished agent prose as unverified, with a verify_claim URL tool.

reads.best: Candid about limits and uses held-output hook with boundary tests.
reads.worst: README admits it is a development candidate; labelling every reply unverified adds little value.

plugins.name: hermes-windows-network
plugins.author: Yicheng-Mark
plugins.does: Two read-only tools that list Windows network adapters and diagnose one adapter's IP, gateway and DNS via PowerShell NetAdapter cmdlets in a language-independent way.

reads.best: Thoughtful engineering: language-independent cmdlet fields, timeouts and typed errors, no console flash, plus unit tests and a validation note.
reads.worst: Narrow scope (Windows only, two read-only queries) that an agent with a terminal could largely reproduce with ipconfig.

plugins.name: sourcebind
plugins.author: blucca
plugins.does: Binds a job to a local JSON source file and, via a pre_tool_call hook, blocks a selected tool if its job/customer_id arguments do not match the current file.

reads.best: A real execution-boundary guard using pre_tool_call, subagent_start and post_compaction hooks, with a standard-library test suite and a demo video.
reads.worst: The use case is narrow and contrived (one customer_id field against a JSON file), and the only protected tool shipped is a fictional demo updater.

plugins.name: leonardo
plugins.author: RichardChua1234
plugins.does: Adds Leonardo.AI as a text-to-video and image-to-video generation backend for Hermes's video_gen provider system, polling Leonardo's REST API to completion.

reads.best: Reads its API key correctly through agent.secret_scope rather than the filesystem or raw environment, and is transparent that it does not meter the user's Leonardo spend.
reads.worst: No test suite at all for a plugin whose only files are __init__.py, plugin.yaml and README.md.

plugins.name: glide
plugins.author: kvnloo
plugins.does: Bundles a large pre-existing forked terminal-UI project (hermes-tern) together with a small original 'Glide' add-on that locally recalls past user corrections and tracks deep-work hours to hold back non-critical notices.

reads.best: Browser-automation actions are gated behind an explicit tools.override capability grant the plugin never grants itself, and the genuinely new Glide memory sync opens the session DB read-only with a test that blocks any socket/subprocess use during sync.
reads.worst: The repo's extensive docs and test counts come overwhelmingly from the inherited hermes-tern frontend (PRs #2-#28 attributed upstream); the hackathon-original Glide slice is comparatively modest, mostly a local corrections-recall hook and an attention heuristic.

plugins.name: ship-reel
plugins.author: AshThunder
plugins.does: Plans and records browser walkthroughs, renders demo videos, verifies and repairs the outputs, and drafts accompanying posts [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AshThunder/ship-reel/1b72949d32ea8a8c33afe67dab15c6473d822ab2/tools.py).

reads.best: Its connected plan-record-edit-verify-fix workflow provides persistent jobs, actionable shot feedback and bounded repair attempts instead of stopping at raw browser footage [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AshThunder/ship-reel/1b72949d32ea8a8c33afe67dab15c6473d822ab2/tools.py).
reads.worst: At the pin, model-controlled allow_risky bypasses payment and destructive-click restrictions, while URL validation accepts private-network hosts, leaving material approval and data-exposure risks [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AshThunder/ship-reel/1b72949d32ea8a8c33afe67dab15c6473d822ab2/engine/plan.py).

plugins.name: plan-tracker
plugins.author: Hjuanma
plugins.does: Turns markdown checklists into a Desktop progress pane with milestones, history, effort estimates, and editable task checkboxes.

reads.best: It makes existing markdown plans usable as a session-aware progress interface, with content-hash checks on checkbox edits and extensive parser and Desktop tests.
reads.worst: At the pinned commit, POST and DELETE /block pass unchecked IDs into JSON filenames, allowing path traversal and modification of files outside the plugin data directory.

plugins.name: voicestudio-tts
plugins.author: EternalShade3D
plugins.does: Registers a live-configured local VoiceStudio TTS provider for Hermes Read aloud and automatic spoken replies. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EternalShade3D/voicestudio-hermes-plugin/40ee4663df7c81190bc02c79f09369466ddab1f6/README.md)

reads.best: It integrates directly into Hermes speech playback, with voice-name selection, per-profile settings, illustrated setup and actionable server errors.
reads.worst: No automated tests are committed at the pin, and enabling the voice dropdown rewrites the installed manifest, complicating updates.

plugins.name: sessionguard
plugins.author: Whydiriki700
plugins.does: Records local task checkpoints and tool summaries, then briefs later sessions about unfinished work from the same sender and platform.

reads.best: Automatic checkpoint evidence and recovery reminders address real continuity problems without network services.
reads.worst: Although recovery briefings filter by sender, sessionguard_status and /guard read all profile checkpoints without sender filtering, exposing other users' work on a shared gateway.

plugins.name: injection-guard
plugins.author: moneya
plugins.does: Screens selected tool outputs for prompt-injection patterns, redacts matches and wraps flagged text in an untrusted-data envelope.

reads.best: The middleware intervenes before results reach the model, with envelope escaping, report mode and tests for benign-content preservation.
reads.worst: Enforce mode rebuilds flagged output from only the first 200,000 characters by default, silently dropping the remaining content; later-only attacks are not scanned.

plugins.name: survey-desk
plugins.author: ferzerz5-lab
plugins.does: Computes and adjusts closed survey traverses, diagnoses misclosure, converts coordinate systems and exports annotated plans in image and geospatial formats.

reads.best: Independent area checks, ranked blunder candidates and explicit datum-shift accuracy make the survey output more useful than unchecked model arithmetic.
reads.worst: Bearing parsing extracts unsigned numbers, so a string such as -5 is accepted as positive 5, and the polygon check misses collinear overlaps and endpoint touches.

plugins.name: intentrivet
plugins.author: MrRosc
plugins.does: Lets Hermes prepare Telegram channel posts while a separate executor requires the owner’s approval of the exact version before one send attempt.

reads.best: Immutable snapshots and transactional permission consumption keep model-controlled text separate from owner approval and prevent automatic duplicate sends.
reads.worst: Installation requires a separately isolated Linux executor and potentially SSH tunneling, while granted permissions neither expire nor support revocation.

plugins.name: adapt
plugins.author: OpeyemiMoses
plugins.does: Implements a memory-provider adapter for tiered persistent recall, preference capture, and pre-compaction preservation, but lacks its required storage package.

reads.best: The provider integrates recall and compaction handling into the agent lifecycle and includes tests describing continuity, retrieval and owner isolation.
reads.worst: The pinned tree omits adapt/storage even though engine.py and tests import adapt.storage modules, so the provider cannot import as shipped despite the passing-test claims.

plugins.name: agent-almanac-first-aid
plugins.author: pjt222
plugins.does: Detects repeated tool failures and context compaction, suggests bundled recovery practices, and records a session logbook.

reads.best: Uses bounded per-session state, cooldowns and extensive regression tests, while keeping failure annotations out of known unattended runs and untrusted results.
reads.worst: Its intervention is mainly skill advice, and annotating attended failures resets result hashes and delays core stall/cycle notices, as the README explicitly discloses.

plugins.name: patchreview
plugins.author: Bilalsnz
plugins.does: Requests native Hermes human approval with a diff before recognized file-writing tool calls.

reads.best: Adds a real pre-execution review gate without model-callable approval tools or a separate file writer, and tests exact replacements and fail-closed unsupported patches.
reads.worst: _extract_change resolves relative paths against process cwd while the hook discards session context, so its preview may describe a different target; shell writes and opaque patches are not covered.

plugins.name: source-first
plugins.author: raidbeforebed
plugins.does: Classifies factual questions, injects a live-research directive and appends a visible warning when no recognized web tool was called. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raidbeforebed/source-first/d1b3d7fc6f747c40737f7a2cfb4fca652fbf4a2f/README.md)

reads.best: A native output-transform hook makes missing research visible to the user, and shipped table tests cover classification, settings and session isolation. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raidbeforebed/source-first/d1b3d7fc6f747c40737f7a2cfb4fca652fbf4a2f/README.md)
reads.worst: Skip words such as hermes, docker and plugin override even explicit lookup requests, while a failed or merely matching web-tool name can suppress the warning without usable evidence. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raidbeforebed/source-first/d1b3d7fc6f747c40737f7a2cfb4fca652fbf4a2f/classifier.py)

plugins.name: jobby
plugins.author: desaianm
plugins.does: Builds a persistent job-search shortlist from an imported resume and prepares source-backed PDF and DOCX application drafts in a Desktop desk.

reads.best: Local document generation, source provenance, generation hashes and application holds support a concrete workflow with substantial regression coverage.
reads.worst: The resume importer accepts only supported text-PDF layouts, Linux/POSIX is the supported host, and international provider success remains partly unverified.

plugins.name: greenlight
plugins.author: Datwebguy
plugins.does: Prepares xStocks trade proposals for human review, then releases an unsigned wallet handoff after approval, with limits and local receipts.

reads.best: A clear Desktop approval pane, practice flow, expiring proposals and tested concurrent rejection preserve a useful human-review step without holding wallet keys.
reads.worst: get_trade_status rebuilds aged approved transactions without rechecking quote drift, so a later wallet handoff can escape the price-change tolerance checked at approval.

plugins.name: disko
plugins.author: emirkaan5
plugins.does: Controls a separately installed disko AI DJ app through tools, slash commands, a CLI, and live now-playing context. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emirkaan5/hermes-disko/92941008c78981e935af6744e09ce2d441056e48/README.md)

reads.best: Real Unix-socket integration tests cover playback controls, safe argument construction, launch failures, and refusing to quit a process the plugin did not start. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emirkaan5/hermes-disko/92941008c78981e935af6744e09ce2d441056e48/README.md)
reads.worst: The substantial DJ engine and Mac setup are external prerequisites, and optional remote control sends its bearer token over plain HTTP. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emirkaan5/hermes-disko/92941008c78981e935af6744e09ce2d441056e48/README.md)

plugins.name: memory-bridge
plugins.author: summero
plugins.does: Lets Hermes search and read operator-approved Markdown notes under profile-specific access rules.

reads.best: Descriptor-based file access, fail-closed policy checks and extensive security tests protect shared notes.
reads.worst: An undocumented delegated-child import triggers a catalog warning, and real delegated runs remain unverified.

plugins.name: live-video
plugins.author: dacheah
plugins.does: Provides a Hermes tool for starting and inspecting a separately deployed phone-camera live-video relay and its vision watch logs.

reads.best: The relay control and verifier-log presentation are unusually well documented and expose a genuine live-camera capability.
reads.worst: The plugin depends on a separately provisioned Node/Python relay and Gemini service, while its tests mostly cover control and parsing paths.

plugins.name: hermes-plugin-dev
plugins.author: mojomast
plugins.does: Bundles a Hermes plugin development skill with template scaffolding and offline static lint tools.

reads.best: The lint tool checks manifests, registrations, schema cost, and common security pitfalls without importing the target plugin.
reads.worst: Its audience is plugin authors, and much of its guidance is a skill that can age as Hermes changes.

plugins.name: omnihermes
plugins.author: DataGuy-Eterniti
plugins.does: Attempts to gate risky Hermes tool calls with local face verification, liveness checks, and a timed unlock window.

reads.best: It has a real hook and biometric pipeline with a fail-closed branch and targeted unit tests.
reads.worst: The supposedly read-only shell allowlist accepts command substitution, its encryption key defaults to a local file, and the claimed continuous away monitor has no camera loop.

plugins.name: hermes-studiotwin
plugins.author: dbitzas
plugins.does: Connects Hermes and Desktop to the StudioTwin remote MCP for 3D, material, rig, motion and SFX generation, with a Desktop workspace and helper scripts.

reads.best: Finished product feel: Desktop workspace, per-tool cost estimates for the approval UI, key kept in the secret store, tests and docs.
reads.worst: Paid generation with no session spend cap, a private repo, Chromium run with --no-sandbox, and the tool list is from a fixture snapshot; mostly a vendor MCP wrapper.

plugins.name: delivery-shelf
plugins.author: mechkw
plugins.does: Saves files Hermes delivers, groups them into versioned deliveries, and offers /shelf commands, a Desktop Saved page and a Telegram panel.

reads.best: Broad surface (Desktop, Telegram, chat commands) with changelog, security policy and honest scope limits.
reads.worst: Selection of what to save is manual (/shelf add), file-type and size limits apply, and I could not confirm test coverage or hooks from the docs.

plugins.name: tmux-live
plugins.author: maksymhs
plugins.does: Adds a Tmux tab to the Hermes web dashboard that lists the host's tmux panes, streams them in colour over a WebSocket and lets you type into them or kill processes.

reads.best: Careful backend: argv-only tmux calls, a strict pane-target whitelist, a fixed key set and no command-execution endpoint, with screenshots and a bilingual UI.
reads.worst: No tests at all, and it relies entirely on the dashboard's auth gate for routes that can send keystrokes and kill processes on the host.

plugins.name: hermes-focus-widget
plugins.author: elianjuan-g
plugins.does: A Pomodoro timer for Hermes Desktop whose focus time only runs while the agent is active, with a floating widget, status chip, /pomodoro command, session log and streak.

reads.best: Tidy, local-only code with five test files, screenshots, a settings page and a classic wall-clock mode.
reads.worst: Tying the user's focus timer to the agent's activity is a questionable premise, and the hooks (including a pass-through transform_llm_output) only note activity.

plugins.name: tmewai
plugins.author: hadialjurdi7-dot
plugins.does: Indexes a user’s Facebook export in local SQLite for Arabic-aware search and bounded evidence bundles.

reads.best: The archive importer validates ZIP contents, reports per-file coverage, and has a substantial offline test suite.
reads.worst: Only four JSON shapes are parsed, and the evidence tool records consent metadata without sending evidence to a provider.

plugins.name: agentic-soc
plugins.author: CyStrat-Services-GmbH
plugins.does: Provides deterministic local THOR evidence parsing and triage, SOC profile templates, and approval-gated local scanner execution.

reads.best: Conservative evidence grouping, bounded imports, metadata audit records and argument-fingerprinted host approvals are implemented rather than delegated to personas.
reads.worst: The broad technology catalog is inactive planning scaffolding, with no verified live connectors and no validated real vendor scan at this pin.

plugins.name: andreed
plugins.author: Agozie180
plugins.does: Audits an owner-authorized Android phone and offers fixed ADB operations for force-stop, metered background-data policy and cache trimming.

reads.best: Validated argv, third-party-package checks, shared-UID refusal, fresh approval keys and after-state policy verification make a focused hardware tool.
reads.worst: Live evidence is read-only and OEM network counters vary; the subprocess output cap is checked after capture_output has already buffered the response.

plugins.name: playbox
plugins.author: Epistetechnician
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a local MCP server for cross-owner agent rooms with shared git work, scoped grants, sandboxed tasks and verifiable histories.

reads.best: Substantial readable Rust implementation enforces expiring member grants, scoped collaboration and bounded Docker tasks, with protocol and abuse tests.
reads.worst: The Hermes adapter requires a separately installed binary, and its documented installer fetches the latest unsigned release with a checksum fetched alongside it, so the catalog pin does not fix the executable users run.

plugins.name: hermes-continuity-capture
plugins.author: Goitonthefloor
plugins.does: Captures session, subagent and Kanban lifecycle metadata into a redacted SQLite spool with optional NATS or JetStream delivery.

reads.best: Local-first spooling, pre-persistence data minimization, deterministic identities and transport tests provide useful operational event capture.
reads.worst: A single module-global controller fixes the first context’s profile, spool and transport for subsequent callbacks, which risks misrouting events in a shared multi-profile process.

plugins.name: money-rules
plugins.author: francis-codex
plugins.does: Schedules and proposes capped Solana USDC payments, splits, sweeps and alerts under user-approved rules.

reads.best: User-only approval commands, on-chain delegated spending caps and tested rule logic make the automation concrete.
reads.worst: The spending helper key is generated and read from helper.json rather than Hermes secret storage, contrary to the stated catalog credential rule.

plugins.name: booking-bridge
plugins.author: kyle-bartlett
plugins.does: Finds availability and books, lists, moves or cancels Google Calendar consultations through Hermes-managed OAuth.

reads.best: Calendar writes use Hermes approval cards plus attended-session checks, while mocked tests cover conflicts, retries and unattended refusal.
reads.worst: The submitter explicitly reports no live Google test, setup needs a user-owned OAuth client, and duplicate protection is a non-atomic search before insertion.

plugins.name: pollinations
plugins.author: greythx
plugins.does: Adds a Pollinations image-generation provider with live model discovery, keyless generation, and authenticated editing.

reads.best: Native provider integration adapts picker capabilities and pricing to the live catalog, with scoped secrets and bounded image handling.
reads.worst: No tests are shipped, and the paid-model setting filters the picker rather than preventing a directly selected paid model from being requested.

plugins.name: plugin_foundry
plugins.author: julian-saint-work
plugins.does: Generates and tests native SQLite-backed folder-scanning or JSON-API-polling plugins for human review and installation.

reads.best: Careful host-bound approval handling and confinement tests protect generation and execution outside its data root.
reads.worst: Only two fixed templates are supported, and the generated API fetch reads an unbounded response with no public-address or redirect guard despite calling the URL public.

plugins.name: mission
plugins.author: EikeAhlers
plugins.does: Visualizes session activity, cost and searchable history in a local web dashboard that can also launch and stop Hermes jobs.

reads.best: A dependency-free visual map and text tools make the agent’s existing session records easier to inspect.
reads.worst: Despite read-only/no-subprocess claims, jobs.py launches Hermes with --yolo and writes logs; the unauthenticated server accepts origins by localhost substring matching.

plugins.name: looprunner
plugins.author: itxLikhith
plugins.does: Schedules repository verification and repair loops with branches, commits, PRs, checkpoints and issue-driven tasks.

reads.best: Persistent loop state, stall budgets, branch guards and failure analysis go well beyond a single coding prompt.
reads.worst: The model-callable loop_approve tool directly adds commands to Hermes permanent approval allowlist, and card approvals accept comment text without verifying a human author.

plugins.name: hermes-hyperframes
plugins.author: wesleymatosdev
plugins.does: Adds Hyperframes video tools and a dashboard with managed Studio preview and composition-aware agent chat.

reads.best: The dashboard connects visual selection, preview, and a persistent Hermes session for an integrated video-editing workflow.
reads.worst: The backend directly reads API_SERVER_KEY from Hermes .env and accepts a plaintext config override, violating the catalog credential route.

plugins.name: stepup
plugins.author: defisensei-maxxing
plugins.does: Adds expiring TOTP unlocks for selected tools on messaging platforms while consuming unlock messages before the model sees them.

reads.best: A small standard-library implementation adds replay protection, sender lockouts and scoped-secret lookup without replacing Hermes approvals.
reads.worst: The guard explicitly allows protected tools when session identity is absent or evicted, so its security boundary fails open on missing lifecycle context.

plugins.name: cron-consolidator
plugins.author: Moodtuner997
plugins.does: Reads a profile's cron jobs, usage audit and execution DB read-only and prints a plan of merge candidates, same-minute collisions, failure streaks and unconfirmed deliveries, without model calls.

reads.best: Strictly read-only (DB opened read-only, no --apply), clean code, and 29 test cases that check it writes nothing.
reads.worst: overlap() requires every cron field to overlap, ignoring cron's day-of-month OR day-of-week rule, so some collisions can be wrong; it has no UI, and a stray CLAUDE.md holds the developer's personal notes.

plugins.name: hermes-make-it-smart
plugins.author: tesla963
plugins.does: Indexes every Hermes profile's sessions read-only, classifies them with DeepSeek plus rules, and renames or tags sessions through cellar_* tools and a Desktop catalogue page.

reads.best: A real 3,600-line Desktop page plus an on_session_end index that tackles a genuine pain: hundreds of untitled Hermes sessions.
reads.worst: It reads the DeepSeek token straight from ~/.hermes/auth.json instead of the secret store, and cellar_rename/cellar_tag overwrite titles on the model's confirm=true with no human approval, unlike the README's 'only when you press Rename'.

plugins.name: demand-radar
plugins.author: LeonardIrimia
plugins.does: Turns an idea into queries against Stack Exchange, HN Algolia and GitHub issues, keeps posts asking for or complaining about it, and returns a rule-based GO/NARROW/KILL/NO SIGNAL/UNKNOWN verdict with an HTML report.

reads.best: Deterministic, honest verdicts from official APIs, an optional GitHub token from the secret store, escaped HTML reports and 19 offline tests.
reads.worst: Keyword matching on three public sources is a shallow demand signal, and there is no UI beyond the /radar command and the report.

plugins.name: tensorfold
plugins.author: atakann
plugins.does: Registers TensorFold's local inference server as a Hermes model provider and adds a dashboard stats tab.

reads.best: Brings a local inference engine into Hermes's model picker on the user's own hardware.
reads.worst: Very small (~46-line provider), no tests, tied to one niche engine; README has users echo the key into ~/.hermes/.env.

plugins.name: skill-stats
plugins.author: minhng92
plugins.does: Counts every skill load and reports period statistics in chat, TUI, CLI and the web dashboard.

reads.best: Four surfaces with store, charts and tests, no setup needed.
reads.worst: README banner is copied from another project and the idea is a simple counter.

plugins.name: adextract
plugins.author: heyytars
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a read-only hosted MCP service for competitor ad-library search and image/video creative analysis across four platforms.

reads.best: It packages a focused, practical marketing-research workflow with platform-specific skills and an explicit read-only/cost disclosure.
reads.worst: The entry is configuration and instructional text only; the core search and analysis service is remote, paid, and not testable from the pinned snapshot.

plugins.name: model-forge-image
plugins.author: mr-pewpy
plugins.does: Registers an image-generation backend that routes Hermes's native image_generate to any OpenAI-compatible local images endpoint.

reads.best: It plugs a provider into the native image_generate tool so images come from the user's own hardware with no account, with clear errors when no endpoint or model is configured.
reads.worst: The package folder is two files with no README, no requires_hermes and no tests of its own, it reads settings through a private hermes_cli.config loader, and it is a thin wrapper over the OpenAI client with a 30-minute timeout.

plugins.name: hackathon-judge
plugins.author: Brianmacu-BMS
plugins.does: Statically inspects a local plugin's source against a packaged snapshot of the catalog and hackathon rules and records hash-bound human review decisions.

reads.best: It never imports candidate code in its audit, fails closed, and is backed by about 213 tests and two CI workflows; it contains no text aimed at steering a judge.
reads.worst: It is tied to this one hackathon (the Nov 11 deadline and rule snapshots are hard-coded), most of its 33 requirement rows are manual checklist items, and its catalog pull request is closed.

plugins.name: cartridge
plugins.author: Frazzlesprite
plugins.does: A Hermes Desktop pane with a Game Boy / Game Boy Color emulator that a person plays while a turn runs and that pauses and mirrors the approval card when Hermes needs an answer.

reads.best: Polished, candidly documented Desktop work: a hardware-styled pane tied to busy/approval state, save states, only a WTFPL homebrew test ROM shipped, a readable bundle CI diffs against source, and golden-frame tests.
reads.worst: plugin.yaml has `homepage:` indented under `license: MIT`, which is not valid YAML, so the manifest may not load; register() is a deliberate no-op and the agent gains no capability, and the pane shows approval buttons for clarify prompts it says it cannot answer.

plugins.name: design-discovery
plugins.author: adip1303
plugins.does: Runs a guided conversational design session that resolves colors/fonts/tokens from a curated vocabulary, checks WCAG contrast, tracks user consent, and exports a DESIGN.md handoff file.

reads.best: A large real test suite (161 test functions) exercises the actual token-resolution, contrast-math and consent-tracking logic, not stubs.
reads.worst: Core code is written in a very dense, unidiomatic style (long chained statements, giant nested ternaries) that hurts readability and maintainability.

plugins.name: jw3
plugins.author: agnostic4321-ops
plugins.does: Wraps an external jw3 trading CLI with 17 Hermes tools for market data and order execution/cancellation on crypto positions, gated behind a human-approval token.

reads.best: Trades require a fail-closed, one-shot sha256 approval token bound to the exact order arguments, with tests for argv-injection and env-allowlisting of the child process.
reads.worst: It is a thin wrapper around a separate external CLI the user must install themselves, and the trading-wrapper concept is a fairly common idea.

plugins.name: factledger
plugins.author: explorelifehus-eng
plugins.does: Maintains a durable TSV ledger of typed (scope, subject, predicate) facts where a new value supersedes rather than deletes the old one, exposed via 9 tools.

reads.best: Atomic file writes with bounded retry plus a dedicated packaging test that keeps the bundled plugin copy byte-identical to the root module.
reads.worst: A disciplined structured-notes skill could approximate much of the supersede/history behaviour, so the case for needing a plugin over a skill is only moderate.

plugins.name: hermes-share
plugins.author: Sahil-SS9
plugins.does: Adds /share and /unshare to publish redacted sessions as secret GitHub gists via gh after confirmation, and import them back.

reads.best: Careful confirm-before-upload flow, mandatory redaction, no token held, good tests and RELEASE notes.
reads.worst: Depends on ctx.redact_text and a hermes import flag that are not merged upstream, so by its own README it is not installable yet.

plugins.name: nomads-planner
plugins.author: lawmight
plugins.does: Read-only Nomads.com plugin with seven tools and /nomads that joins your trips, favorites, city facts and meetups into a next-stay brief.

reads.best: Profile-safe get_secret, GET-only client, coded errors, caching for rate limits, tests and a skill.
reads.worst: Serves a small digital-nomad audience, and the composing brief is the only part a skill could not do.

plugins.name: cybopal-one-devkit
plugins.author: drowzeys
plugins.does: Controls a CyboPal robotic-screen simulator through pose, display, camera, routine and emergency-stop tools ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drowzeys/hermes-cybopal-one-devkit/ede0088906682517e5228b1f618c8d518ec239cd/README.md)).

reads.best: Readable dependency-free code validates routines before motion, refuses E-stopped moves and bounds camera downloads, with fake-device tests and screenshots.
reads.worst: Physical-device compatibility is prospective, and clearing an emergency stop relies on a model-supplied boolean and skill guidance rather than an enforced human approval gate.

plugins.name: ruse
plugins.author: HillaryIkhais
plugins.does: Provides lease-limited browser tools with frozen write proposals, commit budgets, expiry and audit receipts ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HillaryIkhais/Ruse/e81a230e9ded745bdd52d603fc6b64f3bac040b2/README.md)).

reads.best: The lease engine checks exact origins, paths and write bodies and consumes a matching prepared write once.
reads.worst: The broker reads credentials.json directly and uses page.request.get outside route enforcement for preparation and verification, undermining its claimed browser-wide boundary ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HillaryIkhais/Ruse/e81a230e9ded745bdd52d603fc6b64f3bac040b2/broker.py)).

plugins.name: token-dashboard
plugins.author: Whydiriki700
plugins.does: Displays focused-session token usage and reported or estimated costs in a Hermes Desktop pane and status chip ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Whydiriki700/token-dashboard/39949565742a74d00ec03c9921c7ef3eee208d88/README.md)).

reads.best: It uses live SDK usage state and honestly limits recent-session history to metadata instead of inventing historical token totals.
reads.worst: No tests are shipped, fallback prices are a small hardcoded table, and the status-chip cost tooltip does not distinguish estimates from reported cost ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Whydiriki700/token-dashboard/39949565742a74d00ec03c9921c7ef3eee208d88/desktop/plugin.js)).

plugins.name: valun
plugins.author: fitzss
plugins.does: Lets agents negotiate and sign service-for-credit deals on the experimental Valun network using locally held keys.

reads.best: Commitment approvals bind to terms or delivery hashes, and the code independently verifies signatures and credit-note arithmetic.
reads.worst: Practical usefulness depends on an experimental external credit network with synthetic units and no settlement; local issued-note state lacks cross-call locking.

plugins.name: wow-addon-forge
plugins.author: SnoobieJunes
plugins.does: Builds and checks WoW addons using a client API index, embedded Lua simulation, install tools and in-game error readback.

reads.best: Its multi-client simulator, bytecode checks, tested building blocks and backup-aware installer form a substantial addon development toolkit.
reads.worst: Addon Lua executes in-process without an instruction or wall-clock budget, so a looping addon can hang verification.

plugins.name: word-miner
plugins.author: trenthalden
plugins.does: Local SQLite spaced-repetition vocabulary deck: the agent mines words from pasted text, and you study them in chat (/deck) or a Desktop flashcard pane.

reads.best: A real SRS engine with an event log, about 34 tests, no network or secrets, and a banner, screenshots and demo video.
reads.worst: Mastery depends on sub-2s response times the chat flow can't hit, the Desktop pane can't answer graduation cards, CSV import has no tool, and the license is TBD.

plugins.name: hermes-business-brain
plugins.author: unsulabs
plugins.does: Offline toolkit of 19 tools and 21 skills to create, validate and query Obsidian business-knowledge vaults.

reads.best: Network-free, path-scoped engine with 35 test files and JSON schemas.
reads.worst: Much of the bundled data/schemas is in Spanish and the README miscounts its own tools (18 vs 19); niche audience.

plugins.name: hermes-x402-pay
plugins.author: ciperx
plugins.does: Pays x402 HTTP-402 APIs in USDC on Base with EIP-3009 signatures, per-call and daily caps, dry-run default and a SQLite receipt ledger.

reads.best: Caps are checked before signing, dry-run is the default and the key goes through Hermes's secret_scope.
reads.worst: Once dry-run is off it pays with no per-payment human approval, which the catalog reviewer rejects, and it falls back to reading the key from the environment.

plugins.name: hermes-australian-legal
plugins.author: drfinlaymccall
plugins.does: Five tools for dated Australian regulatory provision lookup, review gates, exact-decimal earn-out arithmetic and quote checks, plus a counsel-preparation skill.

reads.best: Evidence-linked, dated provision reads that refuse dates past the corpus, with tests and careful scope docs.
reads.worst: A self-described experimental prototype for a narrow legal niche that depends on an external Git corpus and says it is not for real use.

plugins.name: proxmox
plugins.author: cgray2222
plugins.does: Adds Proxmox inventory, health, snapshot, backup and VM-execution tools plus live @pve context references.

reads.best: Scoped API-token access and on-demand cluster context make the user's own virtualization hardware accessible without extra dependencies.
reads.worst: Snapshot deletion and arbitrary guest execution rely on a model-supplied confirm flag rather than a host-enforced human approval; tests mostly mock the client.

plugins.name: hostd-client
plugins.author: violetSoftware
plugins.does: Sends host command requests from Hermes through VSOCK or HTTP to a separately managed hostd daemon.

reads.best: It uses Hermes scoped credentials and validates command responses, request IDs, redirects and response sizes.
reads.worst: The daemon and approval mechanism are external and untested live, while timeout zero permits an indefinite wait and optional ntfy approvals are unauthenticated by its own disclosure.

plugins.name: case-trail
plugins.author: flabanabba8
plugins.does: Provides citation-anchored tools for examining supplied court-opinion text, researching treatment, and saving review receipts.

reads.best: It consistently ties proposed legal research to exact passages and clearly labels incomplete evidence as unverified.
reads.worst: It remains a niche, provider-dependent legal-research aid with limited automated coverage for its many live-source paths.

plugins.name: uk-companies
plugins.author: TakeshiTGAL
plugins.does: Builds source-separated UK company research sheets from official registries and can schedule a local change watch.

reads.best: It has careful secret-store access, bounded official-source requests, explicit uncertainty, and substantial test coverage.
reads.worst: Its value is specialized to UK company research and depends on external registries and user-provided API keys.

plugins.name: simular-box
plugins.author: dora-dotcom
plugins.does: Packages Simular's hosted MCP server so Hermes drives a cloud Linux desktop with Chrome and a shell.

reads.best: Gives the agent its own always-on computer, with the key declared as a secret.
reads.worst: No code in the folder: just mcp.json, a manifest and a skill wrapping a commercial service; manual copy install.

plugins.name: hey-pcb
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Packages HeyPCB's MCP server (pinned npm @heypcb/mcp) with per-tool cost declarations, a spend limit and a workflow skill to design, quote and order KiCad PCBs from a text brief.

reads.best: Spend-aware manifest: server marked untrusted with declared per-tool costs and a per-chat spend limit so paid calls need approval.
reads.worst: No code of its own: all the work is in a third-party npx package fetched at launch, and the pinned commit has no tests.

plugins.name: hermes-tv
plugins.author: helenn-szn
plugins.does: Gives Hermes webOS TV display, speech, YouTube, notification and remote-control tools with a Desktop status chip and dashboard remote ([pinned source](https://github.com/helenn-szn/hermes-tv/tree/0423785699fb856bceb2beed1b49e451f3cc97a9)).

reads.best: The implementation turns existing household hardware into an agent display and speaker, with local discovery, media serving and simulated-TV tests covering the main workflows.
reads.worst: Pairing keys are read from a plugin-owned JSON file rather than Hermes secrets, and tv_show reads user-specified text/configuration files without a sensitive-file guard before serving them on the LAN ([hermes_tv/state.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helenn-szn/hermes-tv/0423785699fb856bceb2beed1b49e451f3cc97a9/hermes_tv/state.py), [hermes_tv/core.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helenn-szn/hermes-tv/0423785699fb856bceb2beed1b49e451f3cc97a9/hermes_tv/core.py)).

plugins.name: hermes-phone-use
plugins.author: brucexu-eth
plugins.does: Bridges fourteen Pinky phone-control tools into Hermes with persistent MCP sessions, approval notices, and screenshots returned to chat ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brucexu-eth/hermes-phone-use/a2fc998c4a23351d8659654d8db3338a05a8b349/__init__.py)).

reads.best: It adds session renewal and approval handling while registering only the pinned tool snapshot and constraining screenshot paths ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brucexu-eth/hermes-phone-use/a2fc998c4a23351d8659654d8db3338a05a8b349/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: The actual phone operation and safety boundary remain in an external Pinky server on a Mac, limiting the plugin's independent capability ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brucexu-eth/hermes-phone-use/a2fc998c4a23351d8659654d8db3338a05a8b349/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: bot-dashboard
plugins.author: trookish
plugins.does: Two Hermes Desktop sidebar panes showing the focused bot's profile, jobs, notes, widgets and vault tasks, and a group chat's members, activity and shared tasks.

reads.best: Read-only Desktop panes with tool-backed panel notes and widgets, two test files and graceful empty states when no notes vault is set.
reads.worst: Most useful to people running several bot profiles with an Obsidian-style vault, and the dev deploy.sh copies itself into every profile by poking install venvs.

plugins.name: dosbox-full-auto
plugins.author: EternalNooblet
plugins.does: Downloads a pinned, checksum-verified native DOSBox-automation bundle, registers it as an MCP server exposing about 55 emulator tools, and ships a skill to drive DOS apps.

reads.best: Supply chain handled with care: the release tarball is refused unless its sha256 matches a pinned table, and the VLLM key is read only via get_secret and never minted without an explicit terms step.
reads.worst: The plugin itself is a thin installer with no tests of its own that fetches and runs 16.5 MB of native binaries, and its visual checks depend on a third-party Decision API key; DOS automation is a narrow audience.

plugins.name: piloterr
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: A web-extract backend that sends web_extract fetches through the Piloterr scraping API (plain, JS-rendering or anti-bot engines).

reads.best: Clean and small: the key comes only from Hermes's secret scope, requests have timeouts, errors are per-URL and clear, and mocked tests cover the main and failure paths.
reads.worst: A vendor adapter for a paid scraping service; it does one ordinary thing and spends the user's credits.

plugins.name: ziztu
plugins.author: 0xnirlin
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted video production and bundles four writing skills with local script and prompt checkers.

reads.best: Detailed production templates, worked examples and text-checking helpers support a coherent writing-to-video workflow.
reads.worst: The actual generation tools are hosted outside the pinned code, and no automated test suite verifies the connector or its paid production workflow.

plugins.name: tripscout
plugins.author: marcofailli
plugins.does: Searches flights and lodging together, ranks total trip costs, and keeps local price history with a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Hotel-first budget pruning and cached total-cost comparisons automate work that ordinary flight searches leave to the user.
reads.worst: Google scraping is fragile and the documented flight parser can miss cheaper fares; price_one also totals a missing hotel or flight as zero.

plugins.name: hermes-arcade-tui
plugins.author: Takumixbt
plugins.does: Adds terminal chess, kart racing, and Dino games, including model opponents and generated kart controllers.

reads.best: Ships substantial playable game engines, terminal graphics fallbacks, demos, and tests rather than a chat-only game prompt.
reads.worst: The /race path immediately executes model-written Python with the inherited process environment and no sandbox; a timeout does not constrain its file or network access.

plugins.name: sentinel-security
plugins.author: Cogkreates
plugins.does: Statically scans referenced scripts or execute_code input before execution, requesting approval or blocking risky patterns, with optional VirusTotal hash lookup.

reads.best: The pre-tool hook makes findings actionable through Hermes approval/block responses and reads the optional VirusTotal key through secret scope.
reads.worst: The submitted repository URL contains literal angle brackets; the exact SHA is readable at cogkreates/Sentinel-Security, but the guard misses terminal inline code and scans only the first 2 MB of at most five scripts.

plugins.name: hermes-fal-video
plugins.author: axAilotl
plugins.does: Adds FAL video editing, extension and reference-to-video tools with per-model argument validation and local media uploads.

reads.best: Model-specific payload validation, multiplex-safe secret access and tests for uploads, discovery and timeout cancellation make the API integration careful.
reads.worst: No live FAL generation is demonstrated, and the local-upload guard checks filename extensions and size rather than actual media content.

plugins.name: vail-agent-assurance
plugins.author: mnshah
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted VAIL source scans and probe generation, with skills guiding local agent testing and approved fixes. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/projectvail/vail-agent-assurance/b987cb9c459568eca591a4cdcd130fb24ea7aa15/README.md)

reads.best: It targets improving the user’s own agents, with scoped secret configuration and careful guidance distinguishing suspected risks from tested behavior.
reads.worst: The pinned package is an MCP manifest plus skills, so the scanning/grading engine is hosted or downloaded and cannot be audited here; the companion Desktop panel is a separate plugin.

plugins.name: rubal-oracle
plugins.author: X0EF
plugins.does: Stores deadline commitments, evaluates available Git or Calendar evidence, and injects history-based forecasts into model context.

reads.best: Persistent commitments and forecasts based on prior outcomes offer an interesting accountability loop tied to actual agent context.
reads.worst: calendar_connected reads Hermes auth.json directly, violating catalog secret-store rules, while the live source builder never supplies the advertised GitHub, Notion, Linear, Gmail, kanban, or fitness integrations.

plugins.name: odoo-prod-guard
plugins.author: tylerjharden
plugins.does: Provides Odoo JSON-2 tools and a production-write approval hook with a routine allowlist and gate-history pane.

reads.best: A native pre-tool approval hook makes production policy enforceable beyond a prompt, and credentials use Hermes secret scope.
reads.worst: It defaults to ungated dev mode even with live credentials, and interpolates unchecked model/method strings into request URLs rather than validating that the executed endpoint matches the gate decision.

plugins.name: gnothi
plugins.author: vrindachaa
plugins.does: Recomputes quantitative claims and statistical comparisons, qualifies conclusions and optionally appends narrow automatic audit warnings.

reads.best: Deterministic local checks distinguish missing evidence from false claims and ship substantial statistical and invalid-input regression coverage.
reads.worst: Conclusion checking is pattern matching over unauthenticated supplied evidence; automatic auditing only recognizes tightly labeled paired-binary comparisons, leaving most ordinary agent claims outside its scope.

plugins.name: bounded-results
plugins.author: 1anter
plugins.does: Compacts allowlisted large tool results into byte-bounded previews with hash-addressed retrieval of the full text.

reads.best: Unicode round-trip, corruption and error-preservation tests support a small implementation that bounds the serialized preview itself.
reads.worst: The fixed allowlist leaves most tools untouched, outputs above 8 MB pass through, and setup documentation still uses repository placeholders.

plugins.name: hermes-room
plugins.author: adenijiridwan43
plugins.does: Transforms tool-result text to remove hidden/control content and mask secret patterns, optionally using the host model for review and recording audit receipts.

reads.best: The result-transform hook changes what reaches the agent, with deterministic masking, content hashes and a bounded host-model reviewer ([hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adenijiridwan43/hermes-room/b2f7b250a6fbac84d67942f63a181c9d267e6303/__init__.py), [reviewer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adenijiridwan43/hermes-room/b2f7b250a6fbac84d67942f63a181c9d267e6303/reviewer.py)).
reads.worst: After local secret masking it sends the original raw output to the reviewer, then persists the reviewer dictionary including cleaned_text, instruction snippets and _raw_text, undermining the before-model masking and metadata-only privacy claims ([hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adenijiridwan43/hermes-room/b2f7b250a6fbac84d67942f63a181c9d267e6303/__init__.py), [reviewer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adenijiridwan43/hermes-room/b2f7b250a6fbac84d67942f63a181c9d267e6303/reviewer.py)).

plugins.name: rekindra
plugins.author: jakeefr
plugins.does: Recovers images and text from local folders and lets Hermes turn the evidence into animated browser scenes with preview and WebM export.

reads.best: A substantial local recovery and rendering pipeline separates source evidence from generated interpretation and checks previews before export.
reads.worst: The pinned preview.py passes os.environ.copy() to Chrome/Edge/Chromium, exposing any inherited provider secrets to the browser child instead of using a minimal environment.

plugins.name: delivery-gate
plugins.author: ToniAdreal
plugins.does: Runs declared task checks through Hermes terminal dispatch and returns a RELEASE or BLOCK verdict with hash-linked evidence records.

reads.best: The pinned revision routes checks through Hermes approvals and the configured terminal backend, disables local execution by default, and tests failures, timeouts, and evidence linking.
reads.worst: No hook enforces delivery blocking: the agent must choose to call the tool, and evidence reads do not verify the stored record hash or chain.

plugins.name: common-ground
plugins.author: knownquantity
plugins.does: Stores collaboration goals, contributions, evidence and versioned commitments, with reviewed proposals, discrepancy handling, queries and Markdown briefs.

reads.best: Implements transactional proposal application, stable history, exact source-quote checks, stale-write protection and contained exports, with substantive persistence and concurrency tests.
reads.worst: Extraction and approval still depend on the model following the workflow: apply is directly callable, and the reported guided demo required corrections to inferred commitments and deadline handling.

plugins.name: theta-edge-node
plugins.author: bonesnasty
plugins.does: Provides a Windows Desktop pane to install and monitor a Theta Edge Node, inspect rewards and balances, and export its wallet.

reads.best: The pane connects installer checks, local node RPC, diagnostics and read-only agent tools, with tests for offline states and wallet operations.
reads.worst: The advanced export reads wallet keys from disk and returns a decrypted private key to the pane rather than using Hermes secret storage; the installer hash is displayed, not checked against an expected hash.

plugins.name: code-assurance-engine
plugins.author: Sahil-SS9
plugins.does: Inventories repository candidates, freezes check contracts, stores verifiable evidence and reports, and offers a separately owner-signed isolated execution lane. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/code-assurance-engine/0a502a3836b0459c8a3803831239bef624b68f8e/README.md)

reads.best: Explicit check contracts and scope-limited verdicts keep missing evidence distinct from success instead of presenting an empty findings list as safety. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/code-assurance-engine/0a502a3836b0459c8a3803831239bef624b68f8e/README.md)
reads.worst: At the pinned commit malformed /assure arguments let SystemExit escape the handler, and a FIFO in a plain directory can block candidate read_bytes indefinitely. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/code-assurance-engine/0a502a3836b0459c8a3803831239bef624b68f8e/src/hermes_code_assurance/adapters/hermes.py) [Directory reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/code-assurance-engine/0a502a3836b0459c8a3803831239bef624b68f8e/src/hermes_code_assurance/candidate.py)

plugins.name: openwall-mcp
plugins.author: MrHydeDev
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted shared public drawing wall through MCP and a painting workflow skill. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MrHydeDev/openwall-mcp-plugin/26e25c7a0acf880cdc5bbec86a1b592318a5f885/README.md)

reads.best: The pinned package declares its key as a Hermes secret, marks the server untrusted for approvals, and documents public output and constrained photo uploads. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MrHydeDev/openwall-mcp-plugin/26e25c7a0acf880cdc5bbec86a1b592318a5f885/plugin.json)
reads.worst: The creative drawing behavior is entirely in an unpublished remote server outside the pin, leaving only configuration and workflow guidance reviewable. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MrHydeDev/openwall-mcp-plugin/26e25c7a0acf880cdc5bbec86a1b592318a5f885/README.md)

plugins.name: asset-curator
plugins.author: dev-willbird1936
plugins.does: Finds, downloads, prepares and procedurally generates game assets through MCP tools, preserving license and provenance metadata.

reads.best: Its acquisition pipeline combines explicit policy choices, bounded extraction and staged writes that preserve existing outputs on failure.
reads.worst: Setup requires a manual dependency-install step, and the README explicitly leaves macOS/Linux and several external rendering runtimes unverified.

plugins.name: arcmira
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Arcmira’s hosted YouTube transcript-search and monitoring MCP service and bundles eleven research skills.

reads.best: Package tests exercise actual Hermes loading, profile-scoped keys, OAuth precedence and cross-origin credential stripping.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains configuration and skills rather than the hosted search implementation, so server behavior and credit-consuming writes cannot be verified from its code.

plugins.name: underwriting
plugins.author: johnnyminer
plugins.does: Provides deterministic commercial-property screening, price sweeps, return modeling, document extraction and a saved deal book.

reads.best: Hand-computed arithmetic fixtures, explicit assumptions, incomplete-data verdicts and guarded exports make deal calculations inspectable.
reads.worst: Extraction marks a number verified when a numeric variant appears anywhere in the document, without verifying its field meaning, and retains unmatched values with warnings.

plugins.name: hermes-lang-tr
plugins.author: neekimyong
plugins.does: Provides Turkish locale catalogs for Hermes core, TUI and Desktop through the native language-pack interface.

reads.best: A static locale plugin translates host UI surfaces a prompt cannot reach, with no runtime side effects or credential handling.
reads.worst: It is a conventional AI-assisted translation pack with no shipped regression tests or UI demo, and core/TUI Turkish already exists in Hermes.

plugins.name: dsh-pet
plugins.author: yucode-kk
plugins.does: Runs an upstream Electron desktop pet as a managed sidecar and maps Hermes session and tool events to its activity state.

reads.best: The adapter includes extensive lifecycle tests, a fully locked npm tree, scrubbed child environments and owned-process cleanup.
reads.worst: A thin integration around an existing pet requires Node plus large runtime and Electron downloads, and only Windows has been verified.

plugins.name: bluff
plugins.author: salch-cred
plugins.does: Benchmarks a Hermes model on 24 real and fabricated functions, exceptions, and elements, saving graded reports and model comparisons. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/salch-cred/bluff/4c43c96be7a4411d91ebc0b7de59086639ce0507/README.md)

reads.best: Balanced real-item controls, deterministic sampling, ground-truth tests, and fail-fast provider handling make the narrow benchmark auditable. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/salch-cred/bluff/4c43c96be7a4411d91ebc0b7de59086639ce0507/judge.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/salch-cred/bluff/4c43c96be7a4411d91ebc0b7de59086639ce0507/README.md)
reads.worst: Scoring trusts the explicit exists field rather than checking whether the answer text fabricates details, so this is a narrow lower-bound probe rather than a general hallucination measure. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/salch-cred/bluff/4c43c96be7a4411d91ebc0b7de59086639ce0507/judge.py)

plugins.name: hermes-proof
plugins.author: CodedAccorn
plugins.does: Evaluates bounded deterministic local-file contracts and stores retrievable JSON evidence reports.

reads.best: Its small contract language is deliberately root-confined, rejects traversal and links, and has regression tests for verification and persistence.
reads.worst: It verifies only file predicates the user supplies; it neither establishes broad task completion nor ties proof to an agent lifecycle.

plugins.name: keepvoice-hermes
plugins.author: yablokolabs
plugins.does: Three tools to submit, track and export KeepVoice voice-cleanup jobs, releasing export only after the creator approves the revision.

reads.best: Strict literal rights confirmation, idempotency keys and approval-gated export.
reads.worst: Only useful to KeepVoice customers and the repo carries build-prompt clutter.

plugins.name: puppetmaster-learn
plugins.author: professorpalmer
plugins.does: On session finalize, turns a completed Puppetmaster swarm's findings into a reviewable skill candidate under ~/.hermes/skills-candidates.

reads.best: Closes a learning loop safely: it only writes candidates for review and never live skills.
reads.worst: Only useful to Puppetmaster users; one hook, no tests in the plugin folder.

plugins.name: chiron
plugins.author: percyhendrux123-prog
plugins.does: A pre_llm_call hook that estimates your expertise per topic from keyword patterns and tells the agent how to pitch its answers, including asking before risky steps.

reads.best: Deterministic, no model call, atomic locked store with 18 tests, and an honest small A/B eval for its ask-before-deleting claim.
reads.worst: Crude regex keyword matching (one 'just do it' pins the level); a good system prompt or skill would get most of the effect.

plugins.name: field-from-above
plugins.author: kneblewskitomasz-sys
plugins.does: Two tools that take a Polish parcel or a lat/lon point and return a Sentinel-2 NDRE/NDVI crop-vigour measurement, terrain context and a PNG map.

reads.best: Scientifically honest output: pixel counts, confidence intervals, distinct no-data vs service-down statuses, and band downloads locked to one https host.
reads.worst: It downloads whole band files (four per query, up to 600 s each) and fetches terrain point by point, so one call can run many minutes and pull close to 1 GB; the README is short and has no screenshots.

plugins.name: nousviz
plugins.author: statsdroneadmin
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to self-hosted NousViz analytics servers with 15 tools for browsing the catalog, running SQL and building dashboards, alerts and annotations.

reads.best: Practical multi-server REST client with 20s timeouts that keeps the NousViz password in Hermes's secret store.
reads.worst: No tests, and feedback.py hard-codes a third-party collector URL and token that receive user notes and context by default, contrary to the README's claim that it calls only the configured base_url.

plugins.name: pfwa
plugins.author: MirakoolDev
plugins.does: Eight stdlib-only tools that draw provably fair random numbers from the drand beacon and read, quote and build unsigned trades for PFWA prediction markets on Robinhood Chain.

reads.best: Holds no keys: trades come back as unsigned transactions for the user's own wallet, and the drand draw commits to a future round so the proof can be rechecked.
reads.worst: No tests at all, and six of eight tools serve one vendor's prediction-market product that few Hermes users will touch.

plugins.name: grokbot-staff
plugins.author: leoresendedop-sys
plugins.does: Adds a chief-of-staff and specialist personas that answer through ctx.llm, a delegation backend for delegate_task, and an optional fail-closed webhook or inbox-folder bridge that hands jobs to the user's own Grok Bot.

reads.best: Careful bridge code: https-only webhook stored as a Hermes secret, redirects refused, path-traversal checks on job ids, and 20 tests including a manifest-matches-registration check.
reads.worst: The specialists are just system prompts a skill could carry, and the Grok Bot half is a generic webhook POST plus a shared folder because Grok Bot has no API, so little of it is specific to Hermes or Grok Bot.

plugins.name: watch
plugins.author: flabanabba8
plugins.does: Fourteen tools that search anime, films and TV, stream them from third-party streaming sites into local mpv and resume where you stopped.

reads.best: Pinned upstream provenance (ani-cli commit and hash, user-built Luffy bridge checked by SHA-256) and a TMDB key kept in Hermes's secret store.
reads.worst: Depends on scraping unlicensed streaming sites (hianime, VixSrc, LookMovie), is Linux-only and needs a user-built Go bridge for films, so it is fragile and legally risky.

plugins.name: proofread-draft
plugins.author: Icarus-B4
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop composer button that sends the current draft to an LLM for proofreading and shows a diff the user must explicitly click Apply to accept.

reads.best: The rewritten draft is never auto-applied; the user must click Apply, and the 6000-char limit is enforced in both the backend and the UI.
reads.worst: Functionally it is close to a prompt-based grammar check; the main plugin-only value is the Desktop toolbar button and REST route, not the proofreading logic itself.

plugins.name: followthrough
plugins.author: AbdullahBalfaqih
plugins.does: Four tools that let the model capture, list, complete and snooze user commitments in a local SQLite store tied to the Hermes profile.

reads.best: Prefers Hermes's own profile-scoped plugin_db storage API and a DEMO.md that explicitly lists 'claims to avoid' so contributors don't overstate it.
reads.worst: It is a fairly thin CRUD tool; nothing here (hooks, hardware, model/platform access) goes much beyond what a well-designed skill with persistent storage could approximate.

plugins.name: pmp-handoff-bridge
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Packages selected project-memory files, verifies byte integrity separately from workspace drift, and saves reception receipts.

reads.best: Strict schema, size and path checks plus negative tests support honest, append-only handoffs without treating inherited claims as verified truth.
reads.worst: It serves a narrow PMP 0.2.2 workflow with manual package transfer and provides no authentication beyond an optionally supplied trusted digest.

plugins.name: proofops
plugins.author: rasrobo
plugins.does: Runs declared checks against services and deliverables and returns sealed receipts with observed results and explicit limits.

reads.best: The [Hermes tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasrobo/proofops/5916cc80d036a4ef81a961513ee973630393fcd4/__init__.py) expose PASS, FAIL, and NOT RUN with claimability and unverified items, making incomplete verification visible to the agent.
reads.worst: At the pin, [unset operator allowed_paths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasrobo/proofops/5916cc80d036a4ef81a961513ee973630393fcd4/__init__.py) leaves filesystem roots to the model-written plan, allowing checks to read sensitive files outside Hermes's read guard.

plugins.name: calendar-agenda
plugins.author: sanpeita
plugins.does: Lists today’s primary Google Calendar events and records private outcome and slot-retention state with guarded end-time changes. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sanpeita/hermes-calendar-agenda/cb7faabcdcef8ada4b721730a995e5d60327018d/calendar_agenda_service.py)

reads.best: Hermes-managed OAuth, conditional writes, saved original end times, and read-after-write verification make the narrow workflow carefully implemented. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sanpeita/hermes-calendar-agenda/cb7faabcdcef8ada4b721730a995e5d60327018d/calendar_agenda_service.py)
reads.worst: The agenda is fixed to Asia/Tokyo and the primary calendar, and the dashboard surface supplies API routes without a frontend. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sanpeita/hermes-calendar-agenda/cb7faabcdcef8ada4b721730a995e5d60327018d/calendar_agenda_service.py)

plugins.name: talos
plugins.author: oma035
plugins.does: Scans smart-contract writes, feeds findings into agent context and gates recognized mainnet deployment commands. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oma035/Talos/f1485e33c951b0b4e5fb63a8fe7d55d8b7e183da/README.md)

reads.best: Deployment hooks distinguish blocking high-severity findings from medium findings that require Hermes's human approval. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oma035/Talos/f1485e33c951b0b4e5fb63a8fe7d55d8b7e183da/README.md)
reads.worst: Solidity scan-cache keys hash only the target file, so changes to imported code can leave cached deployment findings stale. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oma035/Talos/f1485e33c951b0b4e5fb63a8fe7d55d8b7e183da/talos/scanner.py)

plugins.name: yandex_mail
plugins.author: akinfold
plugins.does: Provides scoped IMAP mailbox operations and opt-in SMTP sending and attachment saving for Yandex Mail.

reads.best: Detailed protocol handling, current-profile credentials, bounded reads and extensive safety tests support a substantial mailbox integration.
reads.worst: Sending has no per-message approval after opt-in, permanent deletion is exposed, and attachment path translation depends on a private Hermes helper.

plugins.name: longevity-coach
plugins.author: pridiuksson
plugins.does: Adds local coaching outcome ledgers, keyword-based stress triage, biometric recovery verification and a weekly coaching automation blueprint.

reads.best: Recovery verification checks next-night biometrics and confounders, with closed-loop fixture tests rather than relying solely on coaching prose.
reads.worst: The full wearable-ingestion coaching loop requires separately installed on-disk skills and setup, while the bundled crunch itself mostly combines triage and reports.

plugins.name: pareto
plugins.author: spiceoogway
plugins.does: Registers Pareto Inference as a Hermes model provider with model-ID aliases and reasoning-effort mapping.

reads.best: Uses the native provider profile instead of ad hoc HTTP tools, leaving key handling and request transport to Hermes.
reads.worst: There are no tests in the pinned repository, and auxiliary calls fail unless users manually configure the streaming-only endpoint workaround.

plugins.name: playbox-witness
plugins.author: Epistetechnician
plugins.does: Hooks Playbox sessions to record tool-call digests and block write-capable tools after another room member’s text is read.

reads.best: A focused hook-based guard and digest-only audit trail address the real risk of other agents’ messages triggering local writes.
reads.worst: At the pinned commit, every playbox record child inherits Hermes’s environment, read-only classification trusts name prefixes, and recording silently skips a missing binary; later PR fixes are outside this pin.

plugins.name: telos
plugins.author: telosplatforms1
plugins.does: Adds Telos model and workspace-router selection with Hermes-managed browser authentication.

reads.best: Uses Hermes provider and PKCE seams instead of implementing credential storage or inference transport itself.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains no tests despite the PR describing an external contract suite, and custom auth URL validation does not require HTTPS.

plugins.name: browsersolver
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Adds BrowserSolver as a paid extract-only backend for retrieving protected webpages and returning readable text.

reads.best: Fits Hermes’s web-provider interface with secret-scope credentials, engine validation, per-URL errors, and mocked contract tests.
reads.worst: The PR reports no live API or local Hermes-validator check, and requests are sequential with a 120-second timeout each and unbounded response reads.

plugins.name: pepper
plugins.author: Akshay-Scalelabs
plugins.does: Uses ParlayTix MCP to find conditional tickets, split owned tickets into outcome rights, and manage saved drafts and watches.

reads.best: Account-scoped state, exact-term rechecks, and durable idempotency keys handle lost issuance responses carefully.
reads.worst: The workflow depends on a separately admitted ParlayTix account and eligible tickets, and most capability is supplied by the external MCP service.

plugins.name: pi-team
plugins.author: iliFalk
plugins.does: Displays parallel pi coding lanes in Hermes Desktop and lets the user answer questions and hand finished work back for review.

reads.best: The live lane board exposes diffs, questions, and review handoff across separate git worktrees.
reads.worst: The runner always parses provider keys from the Hermes .env file, violating the catalog secret-store rule; its README also has an unfilled screenshot placeholder.

plugins.name: hermes-9router
plugins.author: aligundogar
plugins.does: Adds a Hermes dashboard tab showing 9Router model groups, saved probe results, latency and optional provider connection health.

reads.best: User-triggered tests cap each batch at 25 models and use scoped secrets, with status classification, redaction and request-limit tests.
reads.worst: Concurrent test requests share an unlocked JSON state file and fixed temporary filename, and malformed success responses can escape handling; live gateway integration is not established.

plugins.name: tubesaku-creator-insights
plugins.author: webbigdata-jp
plugins.does: Provides read-only hosted-MCP research tools for emerging Japanese VTubers, schedules, live streams, game trends, and cover-song ideas.

reads.best: The package is unusually candid about hosted logging, stale observations, quotas, terms, and read-only behavior.
reads.worst: Most of the capability is a remote service; the Hermes contribution is a thin MCP connection and skill around a narrow audience.

plugins.name: findbroadband-deals
plugins.author: AdeJol
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted UK broadband-deal and outage MCP servers that use an address or provider to return prices, contract costs, and outage history.

reads.best: Exact-address whole-contract pricing and overpayment comparison solve a concrete consumer task with no credentials or purchase side effect.
reads.worst: The pinned entry is essentially manifests and documentation for two remote servers, with no local implementation or tests to inspect.

plugins.name: global-business-culture
plugins.author: pswong661-eng
plugins.does: Provides country business-culture briefs and task-weighted home-versus-host gap analysis from bundled framework data.

reads.best: The tools compute and rank cross-cultural differences locally, with country lookup, task weighting, input handling, and tests covering data and calculations.
reads.worst: Country scores and advice are author-encoded approximations with limited country-level source traceability, so confident-looking comparisons may overstate their evidence.

plugins.name: ga4-deploy
plugins.author: skeptical-agency
plugins.does: Tools to deploy GA4 channel groupings, audiences, annotations and enhanced measurement through the Admin API with quirks enforced in code.

reads.best: Encodes real undocumented API traps as validation, dry-run and read-back verification.
reads.worst: No tests shipped and write access (analytics.edit) with niche audience.

plugins.name: memory-ferry
plugins.author: gnanam1990
plugins.does: A local SQLite memory provider that migrates MEMORY.md and USER.md through a dry-run, digest-approved import, verify and rollback flow.

reads.best: Careful migration: the approval fails if the source changed after planning, and rollback deletes only records it can prove it imported.
reads.worst: Search is plain word overlap, the 'retrieval parity' check runs the same ranker on both sides, and the plugin.yaml is four lines with no screenshots or demo.

plugins.name: hermes-windows-firewall
