plugins.author: Yicheng-Mark
plugins.does: Adds read-only tools that explain Windows Firewall rules and profile settings directly from the Windows registry.

reads.best: Its locale-independent registry parser preserves unknown fields, distinguishes defaults from observed values, and has unit and live Windows tests.
reads.worst: It solves a narrow Windows-only diagnostic task and does not change Hermes's platform or core capabilities.

plugins.name: seomatic
plugins.author: Minh42
plugins.does: Config-only package that wires SEOmatic's hosted MCP server via npx mcp-remote plus twenty SEO workflow skills.

reads.best: Marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before non-read-only tools, with pinned mcp-remote and OAuth sign-in.
reads.worst: No code or tests of its own; essentially a wrapper for a paid SaaS, and OAuth tokens live in ~/.mcp-auth outside Hermes's secret store.

plugins.name: thought-we-wouldnt-notice
plugins.author: noblebrown-69
plugins.does: When a chat message is only a quarter ('25c'), Hermes skips the model and opens a small original arcade shooter in Desktop and the dashboard.

reads.best: Charming, well-tested Desktop/dashboard novelty with original art.
reads.worst: A joke with no practical use for most users.

plugins.name: 0xarchive
plugins.author: nuttykenzo
plugins.does: Declares an OAuth-connected hosted MCP service for Hyperliquid and Lighter market data and optional account/webhook operations.

reads.best: A minimal portable package delegates OAuth storage to Hermes and marks the remote server untrusted.
reads.worst: The required sign-in overrides the package trust setting unless manually restored, and the pinned repository contains neither the server implementation nor its tests.

plugins.name: hermes-droid
plugins.author: dalroot
plugins.does: Exposes Android diagnostics and control tools through an MQTT companion app with ADB fallbacks.

reads.best: The repository includes a real Kotlin device companion plus Python approval hooks, scoped-secret access and security tests.
reads.worst: Wireless screenshot and camera handlers expect image_base64, but Android returns screenshot_b64 and photo_b64, breaking the advertised cable-free visual path.

plugins.name: hermes-manas-aegis
plugins.author: elianjuan-g
plugins.does: Applies pattern-based tool-call blocking and argument rewrites, with decoy credential paths, local audit history and an authenticated loopback security dashboard.

reads.best: Real pre-tool enforcement, redacted audit state, simulation tests and a sandboxed Desktop dashboard go beyond advisory prompting.
reads.worst: The pre-tool path performs synchronous DNS resolution under the core lock without an explicit timeout, and bounded pattern scans and duplicate-call heuristics cannot provide the broad protection implied by its security framing.

plugins.name: model-forge
plugins.author: mr-pewpy
plugins.does: Inventories local and configured compute targets, recommends models, downloads weights, plans or applies chat-model selection, and submits media jobs to existing engines.

reads.best: Hardware-aware model selection and real download and media-job paths address useful local-inference setup work, with mocked planner and tool tests.
reads.worst: The pinned tools package does not deliver the promised automatic engine lifecycle or its separately packaged Desktop/providers, and authenticated downloads use default redirect handling without rechecking the token’s destination host.

plugins.name: motion-index
plugins.author: minutechreview
plugins.does: Provides a Desktop browser and agent search tools for 49 motion-design styles, generating briefs and submitting suggestions.

reads.best: A bundled offline catalog, practical input validation and handler tests make style discovery accessible through both tools and Desktop.
reads.worst: Its core output is a substituted prompt template; building or rendering the actual animation is left to other tools or skills.

plugins.name: anaella
plugins.author: isaacgounton
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted MCP service covering many business accounts and workflows through one API key and on-demand skills.

reads.best: The breadth of connected services and explicit approval guidance could cover many real workflows.
reads.worst: The catalog code is mostly manifests, skills and an npx-fetched external server, with no local tests and a README/server version mismatch.

plugins.name: solana-token-facts
plugins.author: Maxedwolf
plugins.does: Provides eight read-only Solana token and developer-history tools, a /token fact sheet, Markdown reports and an optional scheduled watch blueprint.

reads.best: Goes beyond a token lookup with developer funding and launch history, source links, Hermes-scoped RPC secrets and offline tests.
reads.worst: dev_launches counts every launch without a verified true graduation state as not graduated, so unknown or failed curve lookups become negative facts in its summary.

reads.best: Combines authority and metadata decoding, holder aggregation and launch-history analysis with scoped RPC secrets, bounded retries and offline fixtures.
reads.worst: get_dev_launches counts unknown graduation states as not graduated in its summary, undermining the facts-only promise despite otherwise explicit scan limits.

plugins.name: tap-proof
plugins.author: ladyFaye1998
plugins.does: Measures which element receives the center tap at each viewport width for a local web control, and replays the check after a fix.

reads.best: A precise and unusual check for UI regressions, with screenshots at the boundary widths.
reads.worst: Windows/Edge only, needs a manual npm ci in the installed copy, and has no tests.

plugins.name: huntapi
plugins.author: josselinlbe
plugins.does: Four tools that fetch public video metadata and start video/audio download jobs through the paid HuntAPI service.

reads.best: Clean, small, stdlib-only client with the key via Hermes's secret scope and tools hidden until it is set.
reads.worst: A thin wrapper of a commercial API, essentially a vendor connector.

plugins.name: recall-flashcards
plugins.author: nftboy07
plugins.does: SM-2 spaced-repetition flashcards in local SQLite, with a quiz offered at session start when cards are due.

reads.best: Real per-card scheduling state and hooks that a prompt cannot keep.
reads.worst: A familiar Anki-style idea, and its tests sit in one file.

plugins.name: loci
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Manifest, MCP pointer and two skills connecting Hermes to the closed-source Loci Mac app's local MCP server for summaries, extraction, search and transcription with local models.

reads.best: Careful token handling: Hermes's server_json discovery attaches the token, the server is marked untrusted, and model pulls need authorization.
reads.worst: No executable code at all; every tool lives in a closed app needing macOS 26.2+ on Apple silicon, and the only test is a manifest validation.

plugins.name: 1toolring
plugins.author: khmuhtadin
plugins.does: Config-only package that adds 1ToolRing's hosted pay-per-call MCP server (search, SEO, maps, prices, FX) to Hermes with an API key from the secret store.

reads.best: Key comes from Hermes's secret config and the server is marked untrusted so Hermes asks before paid run_tool calls.
reads.worst: No local code at all: it is an MCP URL plus a skill for a commercial reseller, and the tool list lives on the remote server outside the pinned commit.

plugins.name: reduck
plugins.author: dhuynh95
plugins.does: Config-only package that adds Reduck's hosted MCP server so the agent can run or create browser scripts on any website in the user's own signed-in Chrome or a hosted browser.

reads.best: Honest README that discloses the side effects (posting, buying as you) and a known reconnect bug, with the key held in Hermes's secret config.
reads.worst: No local code and no approval gating: the server is not marked untrusted, yet its scripts can post or buy as the user, and the tool list is not in the pinned commit.

plugins.name: hermes-entity54
plugins.author: wiredchaos
plugins.does: A Node MCP server that adds deny-by-default roles, a signed policy and hash-chained tamper-evident receipts around its own eight Linear-issue and policy tools.

reads.best: 64 tests cover spoofing, replay, downgrade and receipt-chain tampering; keys come from env, and Linear calls have abortable timeouts.
reads.worst: Roles govern only its own tools, the principal is one fixed id the model passes back, and the example USER team constraint conflicts with Linear's team-UUID field.

plugins.name: polydesk
plugins.author: clatsonhacks
plugins.does: Simulates Polymarket trades against live order books with quote tickets, risk limits, SQLite positions and optional testnet-balance backing.

reads.best: The fill engine walks actual liquidity and rechecks both price drift and portfolio limits when a ticket executes.
reads.worst: Confirmation is a model-held ticket rather than host approval, and there is no Desktop trading view; the optional wallet balance does not reserve testnet funds.

plugins.name: canonry
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Exposes a separately installed Canonry AEO/SEO runtime through a local MCP server and operator/analyst skills.

reads.best: The readable runtime has schema-validated tools, permission-aware catalogs and tests, while the portable manifest declares the server untrusted.
reads.worst: Installation requires a separate daemon/runtime and its own configuration credentials; the pinned Hermes package is chiefly MCP metadata and skills.

plugins.name: agentmail-frontdoor
plugins.author: tylerjharden
plugins.does: Claims and classifies AgentMail threads, routes them through a local ledger, and creates reply drafts.

reads.best: Its live tools stop at drafts and track the thread's workflow in a profile-local SQLite ledger.
reads.worst: The claimed send gate trusts an `approved` field supplied in tool arguments, allowing a send-shaped call to bypass the allowlist and approval directive.

plugins.name: sogni
plugins.author: RichardChua1234
plugins.does: Adds Sogni's decentralised GPU network as an image_gen provider by driving the vendor CLI, with four models and image editing.

reads.best: Reads SOGNI_API_KEY via agent.secret_scope.get_secret, so it follows the catalog's secret-store rule.
reads.worst: No tests seen, needs a global npm CLI install, and there is no spend cap on billed jobs.

plugins.name: rea-video-hermes
plugins.author: wusanjay
plugins.does: MCP server wrapping the rea-video pipeline to classify video shots (live/AI/3D/screen) with an agent vision review loop.

reads.best: Inventive agent-as-VLM review loop with a recorded end-to-end demo.
reads.worst: 84-line wrapper with no tests that relies on an uninstalled upstream package and ffmpeg; README mostly Chinese.

plugins.name: oura-mcp
plugins.author: davidmosiah
plugins.does: Agent Plugins package registering a local npx Oura Ring MCP server and a workflow skill.

reads.best: Clear setup and disclosure, gives Hermes real access to the user's own health data.
reads.worst: No code in the plugin itself; credentials are stored by the npm package locally rather than in Hermes's secret store.

plugins.name: acrylic
plugins.author: Saderius
plugins.does: Desktop-only theme plugin that gives Hermes Desktop a Windows 11 Acrylic glass look with four presets, by syncing the host's translucency store and restyling surfaces.

reads.best: Detailed engineering notes and mockups for a genuinely native-looking Win11 acrylic theme, including a terminal transparency fix.
reads.worst: No tests, and it works by overwriting the host's translucency store and force-losing xterm WebGL contexts, fragile hacks against Desktop internals for a cosmetic gain.

plugins.name: provider-endpoint-healer
plugins.author: Alvinagustus
plugins.does: Probes the model endpoints listed in config with an anonymous GET /models at session start and on /peh, and recommends the healthiest one.

reads.best: Honest, small stdlib code with tests, timeouts, a non-blocking background probe and a README that says plainly it never switches providers or reads keys.
reads.worst: Despite the name it heals nothing: it only prints a reachability ranking, and 401/403 counts as reachable, so it overlaps Hermes's own fallback_model with less use.

plugins.name: devsentry
plugins.author: Archangel20
plugins.does: Three read-only tools that inventory a project, give leads from a traceback and show tracked git diffs.

reads.best: Careful safety.py with path/symlink/sensitive-file bounds, output caps and an argument-list git subprocess.
reads.worst: The plugin folder has no tests or screenshots and only a short README; the tools duplicate what an agent already does with a shell.

plugins.name: ghostmark-mcp
plugins.author: MrHydeDev
plugins.does: Config-only MCP connector to a hosted service that watermarks images with a key and reads the mark back.

reads.best: Polished README with banner, example and an honest account of what the watermark cannot do; useful for image provenance.
reads.worst: No code of its own: every call goes to a closed third-party remote server, and nothing is tested beyond manifest validation.

plugins.name: api-architect
plugins.author: monyinet
plugins.does: Compiles OpenAPI, Swagger 2 or Postman specs into a stored manifest and then makes schema-checked HTTP calls against it with secret-slot credentials.

reads.best: Keys come only from Hermes's secret scope with redaction and a private-network guard, backed by about 249 parser/guard tests.
reads.worst: The README promises non-GET calls 'always require interactive approval' and fail under cron, but the only gate is a confirm flag the model sets itself and there is no unattended check; the README is marked work-in-progress with no setup.

plugins.name: slopcore
plugins.author: ChrisAaronNewton
plugins.does: Provides song intake, hosted vocal separation, onset-based word timing, paid video inserts and final-film measurements.

reads.best: It encodes useful media checks in executable gates and distinguishes envelope correlation from human lip-sync judgment.
reads.worst: The paid stage reads os.environ instead of scoped secrets and trusts a model-supplied ceiling; its test even accepts pass when no output clip was downloaded.

plugins.name: model-forge-desktop
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop pane that reads Model Forge compute targets and probes compatible model servers for engines and loaded models.

reads.best: A small Desktop-native cockpit makes local and LAN engine availability visible with bounded HTTP probes.
reads.worst: This subdirectory has only a manifest and pane, no dedicated README or tests; its refresh command merely displays a notice, and provider, download and hardware-detection features belong to sibling plugins.

plugins.name: shopmate
plugins.author: DaveTech2
plugins.does: Provides product search, carts, estimated delivery quotes and customer-completed Paystack or crypto payment flows for a concierge store.

reads.best: Scoped secrets, explicit demo labeling, refusal of live charges for demo items and provider payment verification support a coherent shopping flow.
reads.worst: It does not order from listed merchants or integrate delivery tracking; the operator must fulfill orders, and order_status with an explicit ID does not check the requesting conversation.

plugins.name: better-tg-cli
plugins.author: TheVilfer
plugins.does: Provides a local MCP server for reading and searching a personal Telegram account and approving message and account changes.

reads.best: The underlying CLI has broad Telegram coverage, read/write separation, explicit MCP elicitation and substantial command and security tests.
reads.worst: The MCP runtime reads the CLI's session from its own keychain or config file rather than Hermes credential routes, contrary to the catalog secret-store requirement.

plugins.name: affiliateo
plugins.author: NicoGrajales
plugins.does: Configures Hermes to use Affiliateo's hosted MCP service for an Affiliateo business account and supplies a usage skill.

reads.best: The connector uses Hermes secret configuration and marks the remote server untrusted, giving ordinary Hermes approvals a role in a broad business toolset.
reads.worst: The pinned package is only configuration and documentation; its mutable hosted tool implementation and its reliability are not reviewable from this commit.

plugins.name: data-wrangler
plugins.author: yogeshchoudhary555
plugins.does: Adds deterministic profiling, read-only SQL queries, and cleaned-copy output for local tabular files.

reads.best: Its tools compute full-file statistics and use a SQLite authorizer to reject query writes.
reads.worst: Only one local integration test covers the main path; loading large files and building the in-memory SQL table have no resource budget.

plugins.name: doom
plugins.author: SilentKnight87
plugins.does: Adds a playable Doom tab to the Hermes dashboard with verified Freedoom download or a user-provided WAD.

reads.best: The game UI and checksum-verified WAD backend are real, with safeguards against symlinked or blocking files.
reads.worst: It does little for the agent's work, and the tests cover the backend but not the browser game engine.

plugins.name: chatgpt-style
plugins.author: amitamit10
plugins.does: Adds a ChatGPT/Codex-inspired light and dark visual theme to Hermes Desktop.

reads.best: It is a substantial, well-documented theme that uses the Desktop theme API without network, storage, or agent-side privileges.
reads.worst: It has no tests and relies on many Desktop data-slot and class selectors that can silently break as the host UI changes.

plugins.name: file-intelligence
plugins.author: buttercode101
plugins.does: Scans a directory for duplicates, large and sensitive files and proposes cleanups; apply archives by rename, dry-run by default.

reads.best: Cautious design: dry-run default, symlink and containment checks, sensitive files never moved.
reads.worst: Desktop pane is a static stub and tests are thin.

plugins.name: model-forge-video
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Video generation backend routing Hermes's native video_generate tool to any OpenAI-compatible /v1/videos endpoint, including local ones.

reads.best: Plugs a local/self-hosted video engine into Hermes's native tool via the provider API.
reads.worst: Two files, no README or tests, and silent failure on catalog fetch.

plugins.name: content-engine
plugins.author: PXMichael
plugins.does: Fetches a YouTube transcript, heuristically scores 45-60s clip candidates, drafts per-platform copy, and cuts clips with ffmpeg.

reads.best: End-to-end pipeline in one ce_run call, with safe-name checks and tests.
reads.worst: Scoring and copy are deterministic keyword heuristics, weaker than what the README's pitch suggests.

plugins.name: invezgo
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: 91 tools generated from the Invezgo OpenAPI spec for Indonesia Stock Exchange data, with writes off unless INVEZGO_ALLOW_WRITE=1.

reads.best: Key comes from the secret store, and writes are disabled by default.
reads.worst: Mechanical one-tool-per-endpoint wrapper with a huge tool surface; there are no pytest-style test functions, only a smoke script.

plugins.name: northstar
plugins.author: mrcoxis-2002
plugins.does: Audits instruction files for predefined contradictions, duplicated directives and stale filesystem references.

reads.best: Read-only evidence-bearing reports and extensive synthetic tests make the narrow deterministic checks inspectable.
reads.worst: Scope selection passes None for excluded roots, but discovery replaces None with default roots, so a project-only or home-only audit can still scan the other root.

plugins.name: reapx
plugins.author: BigBossRabbit
plugins.does: Imports X bookmark data, categorizes and assesses it, and generates optionally registered Hermes skills with an incremental ledger [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BigBossRabbit/reapx/1d465e712013b59e396ddcf39a5162d34dfb1976/harvest.py).

reads.best: The pipeline keeps spending and registration settings in user configuration, caps per-call generation, and leaves skill registration off by default [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BigBossRabbit/reapx/1d465e712013b59e396ddcf39a5162d34dfb1976/harvest.py).
reads.worst: The review-then-enable path misses existing output: startup skips registered=0 skills, while reimporting seen bookmarks exits before registration [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BigBossRabbit/reapx/1d465e712013b59e396ddcf39a5162d34dfb1976/skills_out.py) [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BigBossRabbit/reapx/1d465e712013b59e396ddcf39a5162d34dfb1976/harvest.py).

plugins.name: swarm-for-hire
plugins.author: yunganas
plugins.does: Exposes tools for inspecting, posting and settling NEAR escrow jobs, including locally signed transactions [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yunganas/hermes-swarm-for-hire/a6d31079e5154a06d2cf03aa4ecafa5281be3cae/__init__.py) [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yunganas/hermes-swarm-for-hire/a6d31079e5154a06d2cf03aa4ecafa5281be3cae/near.py).

reads.best: Every money-moving tool is routed through a human-approval hook, and the signing key comes from Hermes's profile-scoped secret reader [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yunganas/hermes-swarm-for-hire/a6d31079e5154a06d2cf03aa4ecafa5281be3cae/__init__.py).
reads.worst: Transaction broadcasting has a request timeout but no status reconciliation after an ambiguous network failure, leaving the user uncertain whether a payment committed [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yunganas/hermes-swarm-for-hire/a6d31079e5154a06d2cf03aa4ecafa5281be3cae/near.py).

plugins.name: tradeguard
plugins.author: vansh-attention
plugins.does: Provides read-only stock/ETF snapshot research, optional public ticker history, comparable ranking, microstructure calculations and walk-forward experiments. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vansh-attention/hermes-tradeguard/46434c99ce192f0fa9e3c718d91d57be20d056e4/README.md)

reads.best: Explicit missing-data abstention, bounded opt-in networking and extensive evidence/chronology tests make its research boundaries unusually clear.
reads.worst: Ticker-only research lacks automatic fundamentals and holdings, relies on an unofficial endpoint, and its heuristic recommendations remain unvalidated.

plugins.name: recall-vault
plugins.author: tydavid5
plugins.does: Checks payment-like tool calls against local NEAR spending policies and requests approval for threshold crossings or policy changes.

reads.best: Policy-changing model calls require approval and the ledger associates pending payments with individual tool-call IDs.
reads.worst: Payment recognition is heuristic, unexpected pre-hook errors fail open, and pending payments do not reserve daily budget before concurrent calls execute.

plugins.name: wheelspin
plugins.author: mchevatheachiever
plugins.does: Turns lists into weighted random draws with an animated Desktop wheel, chat handoff and text-mode results.

reads.best: Cryptographic integer-weight draws share a tested persistent store with an animated Desktop pane and terminal rendering.
reads.worst: The practical benefit is narrow, and the store explicitly drops advisory locking on Windows.

plugins.name: makeirl
plugins.author: MelMayssonOwen
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted MCP service for KiCad manufacturing-readiness checks and browser checkout links.

reads.best: Uses an untrusted server declaration, Hermes-managed OAuth setup, and a clear distinction between manufacturing-rule checks and actual circuit correctness.
reads.worst: The bundled server declaration cannot authenticate on its own; users must add OAuth manually, and no checker implementation or tests are included at the pin.

plugins.name: hathor-catchup
plugins.author: DrAhmed7887
plugins.does: Checks childhood vaccination records against eight bundled schedules, generates dated catch-up visits and adds source or warning footers to vaccine replies.

reads.best: The deterministic component-level dose accounting and dated planning are backed by meaningful synthetic cases and explicit rule-review status.
reads.worst: The output guard can call any answer checked after a schedule lookup without validating its claims, and its orphan-task fallback can attribute a check across concurrent sessions.

plugins.name: keln-provider
plugins.author: kris-holy
plugins.does: Registers Keln as a first-class OpenAI-compatible model provider with live model discovery and fallback models.

reads.best: A small readable provider profile integrates model selection and an auxiliary-model default without handling credential files.
reads.worst: The pinned repository has no automated tests and mostly wraps an API Hermes could already use as a custom provider.

plugins.name: waifu
plugins.author: thewaifuai
plugins.does: Displays a Live2D dashboard companion whose visual activity follows Hermes lifecycle hooks and a user-selected live session. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/waifuai/hermes-waifu/173bd90f15f0de9ddf5cb172f6df5939b34b5ad5/README.md)

reads.best: Bounded hashed session state and an isolated renderer keep conversation payloads out of the external asset runtime. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/waifuai/hermes-waifu/173bd90f15f0de9ddf5cb172f6df5939b34b5ad5/README.md)
reads.worst: The README explicitly says rights for 52 character models and thumbnails are unestablished and remain a catalog-review blocker; rendering also depends on CDN availability. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/waifuai/hermes-waifu/173bd90f15f0de9ddf5cb172f6df5939b34b5ad5/README.md)

plugins.name: nurse
plugins.author: Megumiiiiii
plugins.does: Lists pm2 and systemd services, diagnoses log fingerprints, and performs approval-gated service actions with persisted cooldowns. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Megumiiiiii/hermes-nurse/a830f7c8a71490c69368cf2071b85b4476e561b0/README.md)

reads.best: State-changing repairs request Hermes human approval in addition to a plan/confirm step, allowlisted verbs, and a persistent repair budget. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Megumiiiiii/hermes-nurse/a830f7c8a71490c69368cf2071b85b4476e561b0/hermes_nurse/repair.py; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Megumiiiiii/hermes-nurse/a830f7c8a71490c69368cf2071b85b4476e561b0/README.md)
reads.worst: The crash-loop rate divides the cumulative pm2 restart count by the current process uptime, so historical restarts can still falsely block a healthy service; ledger updates also lack locking. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Megumiiiiii/hermes-nurse/a830f7c8a71490c69368cf2071b85b4476e561b0/hermes_nurse/repair.py)

plugins.name: bumblebee-guard
plugins.author: kahnanX
plugins.does: Wraps an external local supply-chain scanner bridge to check installed packages/MCP configs for malicious code, surfaces results as Hermes tools, and injects a rate-limited one-line alert only when findings exist.

reads.best: The scan subprocess is run with an explicitly minimized environment (only PATH/HOME/LANG/INSTALL_DIR) specifically to avoid leaking provider API keys, and this is directly unit-tested.
reads.worst: The actual scanning logic is delegated entirely to an external bridge project not bundled in this repo, so this plugin is mostly a thin wrapper and alert-injection layer around someone else's tool.

plugins.name: fullenrich
plugins.author: nyrthoughts
plugins.does: Uses a hosted MCP service and guided workflows to search B2B contacts, enrich verified details, and export results.

reads.best: It offers a concrete enrichment service with OAuth managed by Hermes and repeatedly calls out that paid operations consume account credits.
reads.worst: The pinned package is primarily instructional skills and remote connection metadata; the actual MCP implementation is hosted, and end-to-end OAuth and paid workflows were not tested.

plugins.name: tether
plugins.author: Yashop965
plugins.does: Runs a token-gated phone bridge for remote trackpad control and local speech-to-text injection into a Hermes session.

reads.best: The companion-phone concept reaches physical cursor control and local voice input that a prompt cannot provide.
reads.worst: The submitted plugin has no tests, starts a network listener and host-control service on enable, and its documented operational behavior does not match all of its implemented CLI paths.

plugins.name: firecrawl-plugin
plugins.author: rakshith48
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Firecrawl's hosted MCP for search, scraping, crawling, browser interaction, monitoring, and structured research workflows.

reads.best: It exposes a broad, immediately useful web toolset with detailed task-specific skills and marks the remote server untrusted for approval gating.
reads.worst: It ships no local implementation or tests, depends on a changing hosted service, and overlaps Hermes's existing Firecrawl-backed web tools.

plugins.name: bankconv
plugins.author: wassim
plugins.does: Packages the BankConv MCP server (npx, pinned) and a skill to convert PDF bank statements to transactions/OFX/QBO.

reads.best: Clear README on data leaving the machine, pinned MCP version and untrusted trust flag.
reads.worst: Plugin is only a manifest, mcp.json and skill; real logic and a paid key live in an external service.

plugins.name: apinex
plugins.author: Apinex-AI
plugins.does: Model-provider plugin exposing APInex's Anthropic-native and OpenAI-compatible endpoints under one API key.

reads.best: Declares APINEX_API_KEY as a secret in requires_env and adds no custom headers.
reads.worst: A reseller provider profile with UTM-tagged links; little novelty.

plugins.name: ledger-guard
plugins.author: tonightsthenight
plugins.does: One tool that deterministically checks a sales/event goal ledger CSV for double counting and arithmetic mismatches.

reads.best: Pure-stdlib deterministic checker with clear disclosure; arithmetic done in code, not by the model.
reads.worst: Very niche CSV format, no tests and no Hermes-specific integration.

plugins.name: omni-fabric-runtime
plugins.author: aidonerightcorp
plugins.does: Registers a local SQLite task-and-artifact fabric, request-budget middleware, swarm tools, and numerical cartridge compilers. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aidonerightcorp/omni-fabric-runtime/be28e1a7b8c2a518e2947393d9b6a5a97066eba8/__init__.py)

reads.best: The lease-fencing store and request middleware provide real runtime capabilities rather than prompt-only orchestration. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aidonerightcorp/omni-fabric-runtime/be28e1a7b8c2a518e2947393d9b6a5a97066eba8/__init__.py)
reads.worst: The pinned tree ships no tests for its very broad runtime, and the advertised holdout trial engine records caller-supplied rewards rather than independently evaluating a model. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aidonerightcorp/omni-fabric-runtime/be28e1a7b8c2a518e2947393d9b6a5a97066eba8/__init__.py)

plugins.name: hermes-janus
plugins.author: Yonathan-T
plugins.does: Snapshots workspace files into a content-addressed history and offers rewind, branching, merging and test-based branch selection.

reads.best: Automatic tool hooks and named restore points address a real coding-agent recovery problem without model calls.
reads.worst: Branches reuse the same workspace, post-tool snapshots ignore failure results, and model-supplied tournament commands run directly with shell=True despite claims of isolated atomic recovery.

plugins.name: apple-health-mcp
plugins.author: davidmosiah
plugins.does: Exposes local Apple Health export records, workouts and wellness summaries through a portable MCP package and workflow skill.

reads.best: The server source includes streaming export parsing, freshness and truncation reporting, privacy modes and meaningful parser and profile-boundary tests.
reads.worst: The actual plugin launches an npm release rather than the pinned repository code, needs a first-run download and manual health exports, and adds no deeper Hermes lifecycle integration.

plugins.name: fleet-sentinel
plugins.author: imperator-clawdius
plugins.does: Probes remote Hermes gateway hosts using tailnet, TCP and SSH evidence, tracks outages and offers bounded recovery actions.

reads.best: Corroborated verdicts distinguish a live gateway socket from stale state files, with time-bounded probes and tests for misleading or malformed evidence.
reads.worst: Recovery executes SSH mutations based on model-set dry_run and confirm flags rather than a Hermes approval prompt, and the PR description disagrees with the pinned implementation about storage and restart behavior.

plugins.name: hermes-windows-disks
plugins.author: Yicheng-Mark
plugins.does: Queries Windows storage classes to report physical-disk health, partition layouts, volume capacity and low-space warnings.

reads.best: Fixed read-only CIM queries and numeric-enum decoding give Hermes useful hardware facts without localized-output parsing.
reads.worst: It exposes a conventional OS query rather than new agent behavior, and subprocess timeouts or missing PowerShell escape the handler’s PowerShellError catch.

plugins.name: hermes-unlimited
plugins.author: nsolland
plugins.does: Maintains tenant-scoped companies, priced services and requests and dispatches verified requests to isolated Hermes Kanban boards.

reads.best: Trusted-identity checks, separate tenant boards and idempotent dispatch address real multi-tenant task-routing concerns.
reads.worst: Normal setup depends on an external JustYou package and signed bindings, and the code supports reading bearer tokens and HMAC authority material from files outside Hermes’s secret store.

plugins.name: habitude
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Bundles a read-only local journal-search MCP runtime and registers a Hermes skill for evidence-based reflection on an explicitly selected vault.

reads.best: Readable local retrieval code bounds excerpts and validates issued references, with synthetic-vault tests for scope and original-file preservation.
reads.worst: The native plugin registers only a skill; users must separately configure MCP, and its default scope file and cache live outside Hermes profiles.

plugins.name: lingua
plugins.author: tobadaniel
plugins.does: Maintains local vocabulary decks and SM-2 review schedules, with chat tools, due-card nudges and starter decks ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tobadaniel/lingua/c9760302432469642766ea4dc3bab956a738bb4b/README.md)).

reads.best: Persistent scheduling, locking, duplicate handling and deterministic interval tests make vocabulary practice more durable than a tutoring prompt.
reads.worst: The quiz and answer grading remain model instructions, and language normalization strips non-ASCII labels to a shared general deck ([store](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tobadaniel/lingua/c9760302432469642766ea4dc3bab956a738bb4b/vocab_store.py)).

plugins.name: hermes-windows-apps
plugins.author: Yicheng-Mark
plugins.does: Reads Windows Uninstall registry entries to list installed software and report versions, installation details and uninstaller classifications.

reads.best: A compact read-only registry implementation avoids executing uninstallers and includes fake-registry, non-Windows import and live-test coverage.
reads.worst: It only inventories registry-registered Windows software, and same-name entries collapse into a first-view summary that can hide version differences.

plugins.name: umami-digest
plugins.author: TakeshiTGAL
plugins.does: Fetches yesterday's self-hosted Umami analytics and delivers a deterministic morning letter through a no-model Hermes cron job.

reads.best: Handles pagination, unknown-versus-zero traffic, scoped secrets, bounded HTTP reads and schedule recovery with focused tests and no model cost.
reads.worst: It serves a narrow analytics niche, requires manual environment setup, and uninstalling before unscheduling can leave a cron job and script behind.

plugins.name: agent-ready
plugins.author: workpodsai-agents
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted website-audit MCP service for SEO, AI-crawler checks, site crawls and drafted fixes.

reads.best: Clear Hermes-specific setup and disclosures include an untrusted-server declaration to gate the email-based full-audit request.
reads.worst: The installed hermes folder is a remote connector rather than the audit engine, so the pinned package cannot establish hosted-check reliability or privacy behavior.

plugins.name: hermes-windows-certificates
plugins.author: Yicheng-Mark
plugins.does: Adds two read-only Windows tools that enumerate certificate stores and explain individual certificates, validity and key purposes.

reads.best: Direct crypt32 integration, explicit pointer signatures and unit/live test cases give useful diagnostics without shell parsing or elevation.
reads.worst: The self_signed field only compares subject and issuer names, so it does not verify that a certificate actually signed itself.

plugins.name: bulkpublish
plugins.author: azeemkafridi
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to BulkPublish’s hosted social publishing MCP service and supplies workflow skills.

reads.best: The portable manifest explicitly marks the remote server untrusted, supporting human approval for write tools.
reads.worst: The pinned deliverable contains configuration and skills only, with no server implementation or automated tests to substantiate the advertised remote capabilities.

plugins.name: kyte
plugins.author: 0x-saurabh
plugins.does: Packages a remote Kyte MCP options market and two skills for market reads, trade preparation, and scheduled alerts for actions awaiting the user's signature.

reads.best: It separates read-only market queries from prepare-action links, labels the MCP server untrusted, and keeps signing in the user's own wallet.
reads.worst: Live tool behavior is supplied by kyte.sh rather than the pinned repository, and the feature depends on an external finance service with no local tests or implementation to inspect.

plugins.name: cpa-status
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: /cpa slash command showing health and live quota of CLIProxyAPI account pools.

reads.best: Read-only, no timers, extensively tested.
reads.worst: Useful only to CLIProxyAPI users; companion to another plugin.

plugins.name: cellium-wallet
plugins.author: xjubiliance
plugins.does: MCP connector to a Cellium agent wallet for transfers, swaps, bridges and orders.

reads.best: Token comes from the secret store and the skill requires explicit approval.
reads.worst: Only config and a skill; all behavior is in a hosted service, and it moves money.

plugins.name: waifu-sprites
plugins.author: thewaifuai
plugins.does: A dashboard tab and draggable overlay that plays anime video clips matching the agent's state (idle, thinking, tool use) and a keyword-matched emotion.

reads.best: A visible dashboard companion driven by real agent hooks, with screenshots and a clip browser site.
reads.worst: No tests; a frontend bug (inflight.abort() on an object) throws when the state changes mid-download; 'success' and 'sleeping' states are never set; clips stream from a CDN.

plugins.name: werracle-evm-guard
plugins.author: pCwOrM
plugins.does: Intercepts selected cast send terminal commands with EVM approval/value risk heuristics and exposes hosted Radar telemetry tools.

reads.best: A real pre-tool blocking hook handles raw calldata, readable signatures and nested shell commands, while the API key uses Hermes secret scoping.
reads.worst: This is heuristic parsing rather than EVM execution simulation: the hook hardcodes Base, misses other broadcast routes and unresolved shell variables, and uses a chain-independent trusted-address list.

plugins.name: opportunity-check
plugins.author: ronigrv
plugins.does: Searches public agent-work listings, checks GitHub issue and repository signals, and saves up to five issue snapshots for manual rechecks.

reads.best: Bounded requests, redirect refusal and mocked tests accompany clear separation of advertised rewards from verified facts.
reads.worst: It checks only the first 30 open pull requests and cannot verify funding or AI eligibility, while malformed upstream JSON shapes can escape its narrow exception handling.

plugins.name: air-agent-kya
plugins.author: armanmamyan
plugins.does: Delegates an AIR identity to Hermes and presents nonce-bound selective credential proofs to KYA stores ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MocaNetwork/air-agent-hermes/4dbe09b4e77c37ab033d58007eb00f4dd68fb797/README.md)).

reads.best: The implementation keeps presentations out of model responses, restricts site origins and requests approval before live disclosures.
reads.worst: It reads and writes the agent private key and delegation bundle directly in plugin-data rather than using Hermes credential routes, conflicting with catalog rule 11.

plugins.name: print-tools
plugins.author: alxspiker
plugins.does: Adds CUPS queue status and tools to print local files, text and styled letters on Linux ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alxspiker/hermes-print-tools/babc0815a2bb6a86d09dbcdae503a7ce7f24da9d/README.md)).

reads.best: The implementation checks printer selection and file paths, limits copies, sanitizes subprocess environments and reports partial submissions honestly.
reads.worst: Setup depends on several Linux printing utilities and fonts, and PDF page limits are checked only after Ghostscript has rasterized the document.

plugins.name: attune
plugins.author: five0nit
plugins.does: Asks the user daily questions about goals and project friction, stores them in SQLite, injects calibration data into every LLM call, and runs owner-approved code proposals' unittests in a Bubblewrap sandbox.

reads.best: A careful permission model: only owner slash commands can approve, and test runs use bwrap --unshare-all with cap-drop, rlimits and a deadline, with 102 tests.
reads.worst: Its tagline overstates the code (no merge; the daily wake only returns a cron request), it adds up to about 3 KB to every LLM call, and its jargon-heavy README has no screenshots or UI.

plugins.name: brickfact
plugins.author: mo-tech55
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Brickfact's public MCP server to find LEGO sets, compare regional retailer offers and read recorded price history, with a stdlib Python helper as a fallback.

reads.best: Well-engineered helper (fixed endpoint, no redirects or proxy, size limits, clear errors) with offline tests in CI and an unusually candid privacy and affiliate disclosure.
reads.worst: It is a niche shopping connector to a vendor's hosted service, so the plugin adds no Hermes-specific capability.

plugins.name: audionotes
plugins.author: aphasingnirvana
plugins.does: An Agent Plugins package that connects Hermes through mcp-remote to Audionotes' hosted read-only MCP server (search, list and read voice notes and transcripts) with OAuth and one retrieval skill.

reads.best: Read-only, OAuth through a pinned mcp-remote version, marked 'untrusted', with a clear README on what data leaves and where.
reads.worst: No code of its own: a config pointing at a vendor's hosted MCP server that needs a paid Audionotes account, so its value rests entirely on that service.

plugins.name: hermes-ego
plugins.author: loop2zero
plugins.does: An MCP pointer, plus a skill, to a token-protected local relay and Mac daemon that let Hermes read and save pages in the user's ego(lite) browser.

reads.best: The relay code in the repo root compares tokens in constant time, rejects Origin headers, and blocks private-address image fetches, with about 90 tests.
reads.worst: The plugin installs none of that code; the README says it 'was not run against a live Hermes process', the token is also kept on disk, and the browser download is unverified.

plugins.name: neuralwatt
plugins.author: 0xGingi
plugins.does: Seven tools to check NeuralWatt API health, models, balance, costs, energy use and sessions.

reads.best: Simple, clean read-only API wrapper using the Hermes .env key.
reads.worst: Niche single-vendor account lookup with only 5 tests.

plugins.name: sauce-vids
plugins.author: Davemafy
plugins.does: Records a headless Chromium session of an allow-listed HTTPS site with Playwright and encodes it to MP4 with ffmpeg, with ffprobe metadata.

reads.best: Real browser capture and ffmpeg rendering, with a host allow-list that checks DNS answers are public addresses.
reads.worst: Thin code with 3 shallow tests; hover/click actions call Playwright's Locator.first as a method (tools.py:114,120), which looks broken; Chromium runs with --no-sandbox, and there are no demo assets.

plugins.name: chartrunner
plugins.author: ssjjul3
plugins.does: Read-only tools for the ChartRunner Solana trading app: radar, cup standings and buy verdicts, Merkle memo checks, and review links the user signs in their own wallet.

reads.best: Careful read-only design (GET only, no redirects, 1 MB cap, trades only as review links) with Merkle checks tested against upstream vectors.
reads.worst: A thin wrapper around one niche app's API with a 35-line README, no demo, and a CHARTRUNNER_ORIGIN override that can point it at any host.

plugins.name: ship
plugins.author: shipstatic-com
plugins.does: Configuration that points Hermes at ShipStatic's hosted MCP server so the agent can publish static sites and get a shareable link, with no account needed.

reads.best: Zero-setup publishing with no API key: OAuth is handled by Hermes and the server is marked untrusted.
reads.worst: A single MCP config entry whose real behaviour lives on a hosted server not in the repo; no tests cover the Hermes package, and anonymous uploads go public for days.

plugins.name: crash-lab
plugins.author: 8JBern
plugins.does: Four tools that run a simulated booking service with injected failures (timeout after success, malformed response, 503s) and an oracle that grades from service state whether the agent double-booked.

reads.best: A deterministic fault-injection harness whose PASS/FAIL comes from the simulated service's actual state, not the agent's account, with tests and recorded agent trials.
reads.worst: It is a 148-line toy with one fictional booking workflow, so it tests agents in a lab rather than making the user's own agent better.

plugins.name: gsc-magic
plugins.author: lumizone
plugins.does: Configuration-only package that connects Hermes through a pinned mcp-remote to GSC Magic's hosted MCP for Search Console, Bing, GA4, IndexNow and Core Web Vitals SEO reports, plus a usage skill.

reads.best: Clear README and skill, a pinned mcp-remote version, OAuth sign-in and the server marked untrusted so Hermes asks before write tools.
reads.worst: No code beyond a manifest and an MCP entry for a commercial hosted service; Hermes's native MCP support would do the same.

plugins.name: source-trail-supervisor
plugins.author: misakamikotoghr-5205
plugins.does: Three tools and hooks that verify citation quotes against exact Unicode spans, withhold claims when sources contradict, and flag stuck loops from repeating tool-call fingerprints.

reads.best: Deterministic exact-span quote checking with size limits is a concrete guard against fabricated citations that a prompt alone cannot enforce.
reads.worst: Three loosely related features glued from the author's other repos, covered by a single test in a shared multi-plugin test file, with a jargon-heavy README and no demo.

plugins.name: ao-bridge
plugins.author: wesleymatosdev
plugins.does: A Hermes dashboard tab that shows the local Agent Orchestrator daemon's sessions as a Kanban board, with spawn, send, kill and a live event stream.

reads.best: A tidy loopback REST client with mapped errors, an authenticated websocket, and tests against a fake AO server.
reads.worst: The README is a copy of the Hermes Agent README and never describes the plugin, and it serves only people who already run the Agent Orchestrator daemon.

plugins.name: hermes-token-ledger
plugins.author: ilPez00
plugins.does: Records token counts from API-response hooks in SQLite and reports estimated model cost with optional budget warnings.

reads.best: It uses a core lifecycle hook to make session-level usage and cost visible instead of relying on provider dashboards.
reads.worst: The pinned repository has no tests and a small implementation, while its pricing table and token shapes can become stale or incomplete.

plugins.name: postkey
plugins.author: 0xRabbithole
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Postkey’s hosted MCP service for Instagram messaging, automations, contacts, and scheduled posts.

reads.best: The package clearly discloses approvals, untrusted-server handling, OAuth, remote effects, and the fact that the real tool set is not pinned locally.
reads.worst: The pinned entry contains no executable plugin code and its 57-tool behavior is supplied by a mutable remote service, so reliability and claims are outside the commit.

plugins.name: ghl-command
plugins.author: PXMichael
plugins.does: Adds twelve native GoHighLevel CRM tools for contacts, pipelines, opportunities, email, SMS and workflow enrollment.

reads.best: It exposes practical CRM actions through Hermes secret storage and has explicit argument validation and error responses.
reads.worst: The implementation has only a small registration test despite exposing consequential delete, messaging and workflow actions, with no visible confirmation layer.

plugins.name: payops
plugins.author: BigWave45
plugins.does: Reads Paystack transactions and settlements and produces deterministic, read-only reconciliation and data-quality reports.

reads.best: It is a focused financial-operations tool with bounded pagination, secret-store use, HTTPS GETs, deterministic semantics and unit/provider tests.
reads.worst: The catalog release supports only Paystack and has no ledger matching, continuous monitoring, alerts or other higher-level operations, so its day-one audience is limited.

plugins.name: munin
plugins.author: Hugo6991
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Munin meetings over OAuth and supplies transcript-cited recall and follow-up skills.

reads.best: The connector declares remote tools untrusted and documents OAuth, write approvals, transcript citations and data exposure clearly.
reads.worst: The pinned contribution is configuration and skills rather than the meeting service itself, and OAuth plus trust settings require extra manual setup.

plugins.name: gmi-video
plugins.author: zkasuran
plugins.does: Registers a GMI Cloud video-generation provider that maps Hermes inputs to live model schemas and polls paid text-to-video or image-to-video jobs.

reads.best: A real provider backend handles schema mapping, scoped secrets, bounded polling and non-retried paid submissions with offline regression coverage.
reads.worst: Generation spends credits without an approval prompt or computed total, and a failed download is silently returned as a successful remote URL.

plugins.name: cloro
plugins.author: rbatista191
plugins.does: Adds cloro live Google results as a Hermes web search backend.

reads.best: It uses Hermes scoped secrets, validates settings and responses, and has mocked tests for the search adapter.
reads.worst: It is a conventional paid API wrapper for search only, with no extraction backend or distinctive agent behavior.

plugins.name: market-search
plugins.author: efoltyn
plugins.does: Starts an MCP server for broad live financial and prediction-market data, downloading a checksum-pinned binary on first use when absent.

reads.best: It exposes a broad set of live market sources locally without accounts or API keys.
reads.worst: The catalog payload is chiefly an MCP launcher plus skill and downloads executable code at runtime, with no Hermes-native implementation or tests in the plugin folder.

plugins.name: hermes-windows-updates
plugins.author: Yicheng-Mark
plugins.does: Queries Windows Update history and installed OS hotfixes, with title filters, failure outcomes and decoded error codes.

reads.best: Fixed read-only PowerShell queries normalize localized dates, singleton collections and signed HRESULTs into useful diagnostic results.
reads.worst: Combining only_failures with a title query that excludes actual failures incorrectly reports that every update in the window ended clean.

plugins.name: elevenlabs-convai
plugins.author: c6zks4gssn-droid
plugins.does: Provides six tools to inspect, configure and test ElevenLabs voice agents, including latency measurement and prompt backups.

reads.best: The inspect-change-measure workflow includes dry-run diffs, prompt backups and measured time to first audio.
reads.worst: convai_client.api_key falls back to raw os.environ even when the profile secret is empty, and voice-test overrides mutate live agent settings without the apply gate advertised for every write.

plugins.name: shorts-factory
plugins.author: skeptical-agency
plugins.does: Provides seven local media tools for short-video captions, audio normalization, concatenation and visual quality checks.

reads.best: The media engines encode concrete loudness, caption-render verification and stream-duration checks rather than merely returning editing advice.
reads.worst: safe_concat groups all video labels before all audio labels instead of interleaving each segment, and assumes every video has audio when any does; no committed tests cover these mixed-media cases.

plugins.name: pow-tracker
plugins.author: BigBossRabbit
plugins.does: Adds local multi-client time tracking, optional file-activity capture and invoice exports to the Hermes web dashboard.

reads.best: Per-client SQLite billing, opt-in activity capture and authenticated live updates make a usable local freelancer dashboard.
reads.worst: _newest_mtime does not exclude the current .pow-time directory, so its own database writes can be mistaken for client work and distort automatic billing.

plugins.name: soldgraph
plugins.author: soldgraph
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Soldgraph's hosted resale-listing MCP service and supplies a skill for interpreting comparable sales.

reads.best: A simple credential-substituted MCP configuration offers resale data across multiple marketplaces with clear cost and remote-service disclosures.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains only manifests and a skill, with no server implementation or tests, so its advertised search behavior cannot be audited at this commit.

plugins.name: weir
plugins.author: tarun-khatri
plugins.does: Config-only package pointing Hermes at Weir's paid hosted MCP server for public X and Reddit data.

reads.best: OAuth with PKCE and an untrusted MCP marking, so no stored secret and writes need approval.
reads.worst: No code or tests, and its 550-line skill tells the agent to reach for Weir proactively and to re-download the skill from a remote URL.

plugins.name: decision-brief
plugins.author: LaRoyBot
plugins.does: Hooks clarify calls to enrich consequential-decision questions into a compact Decision/Found/Why/Recommendation brief.

reads.best: Careful privacy (hashed ids, no raw content stored) with tests and a demo.
reads.worst: Mostly a formatting layer that a skill or prompt could largely reproduce.

plugins.name: widespread
plugins.author: TerexitariusStomp
plugins.does: Tools to discover, claim, ship and get paid for bounties on the widespread protocol, plus the payer side, with Ed25519 signing.

reads.best: Money-moving tools are gated behind Hermes approval through a pre_tool_call hook.
reads.worst: Signing seed is kept in a plain JSON file rather than the secret store, there are no tests and no README in the plugin folder.

plugins.name: amavid-hooker
plugins.author: quynhchiv
plugins.does: A Node stdio MCP server with 16 tools and two skills for generating and editing images and videos with xAI Grok Imagine, plus a local browser flow-canvas UI.

reads.best: Full TypeScript source alongside the bundle, redacted errors, and a three-OS CI matrix that builds and smoke-tests the server.
reads.worst: It is not a Hermes-native plugin and takes its credentials from the Grok CLI's ~/.grok/auth.json file instead of Hermes's secret store, spends paid xAI quota with no approval gate, and its local UI server has no auth.

plugins.name: hermes-axiom-agent
plugins.author: percyhendrux123-prog
plugins.does: Injects a nine-article written doctrine into every model turn through pre_llm_call and offers a /doctrine command that reports which separate enforcer plugins are installed and enabled.

reads.best: Unusually honest about its limits ("This plugin enforces nothing itself"), with bounded safe reads of other plugins' manifests and 55 tests.
reads.worst: What it adds is text in the prompt, which a skill or system prompt would do equally well, and its value depends on five other plugins by the same author.

plugins.name: verifyum
plugins.author: aisenseapi
plugins.does: Declares Verifyum MCP servers (hosted HTTP and npx local) and a skill for anchoring file-hash proofs on Solana, packaged in several agent-plugin formats.

reads.best: Clear docs, hash-only privacy, and a skill that forbids creating permanent anchors during tests.
reads.worst: No code of its own and no Hermes plugin.yaml or tests: it is MCP config plus a skill, and the local server runs an npx download.

plugins.name: flipletters
plugins.author: tera-sarah
plugins.does: Configures a hosted MCP connection for drafting, validating, rendering, and sharing split-flap or flip-dot board videos.

reads.best: It presents a clear, attractive niche creative workflow and correctly declares its authenticated remote server as untrusted in Hermes.
reads.worst: The reviewed commit is a thin hosted-service connector with no implementation or tests for its remote rendering and sharing behaviour.

plugins.name: local-mcp
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Packages an mcp.json and launcher that start the separately installed LMCP macOS app so Hermes gets its Mail, Calendar, Teams and Office tools.

reads.best: Clear disclosure and a skill on scoping powerful tools for unattended jobs.
reads.worst: Mostly a vendor pointer: no code of its own besides a shell launcher, macOS only, needs a third-party app, no tests.

plugins.name: shotlane
plugins.author: nothingnix
plugins.does: An MCP server/Agent Skill wrapper that forwards URLs and HTML to the external shotlane.dev SaaS to return screenshots, Markdown page content and PDFs.

reads.best: Addresses a broadly useful need (visual QA / PDF generation / scraping JS-heavy pages) with clear documentation.
reads.worst: No tests anywhere in the repo, and almost all real logic lives off-repo in the paid third-party SaaS, leaving little the plugin itself does beyond a thin API-key pass-through.

plugins.name: bankbridge
plugins.author: jakemarsh
plugins.does: Packages the BankBridge hosted MCP server URL (OAuth sign-in) and one skill so Hermes can answer questions about the user's own US bank, card and brokerage accounts at $5/month per bank.

reads.best: Read-only by design: no executable code or stored credentials, OAuth through Hermes's own mcp login, and a skill that refuses money-moving requests.
reads.worst: It is a multi-agent marketing package for a paid SaaS (Claude, Cursor and Gemini manifests): the Hermes side is only a URL plus a skill, and the read-only promise is enforced by the vendor's server, not by any code at this commit.

plugins.name: plagio
plugins.author: youssbim
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted design-capture service for website components, pages, brand tokens and motion specifications.

reads.best: The connector and skill expose a focused design-to-code workflow with clear credit and data disclosures.
reads.worst: Only manifests and a skill are pinned; the closed hosted capture implementation and runtime tool behavior cannot be inspected or tested from this repository.

plugins.name: kleos
plugins.author: demzzydev
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted small-business marketing workspace for planning, drafting, review, publishing and reporting.

reads.best: The package declares an untrusted server and a Hermes secret field, with explicit review and publishing guidance.
reads.worst: The marketing implementation is not in the pinned package, and its test report explicitly leaves the signed-in Hermes tool-call workflow incomplete.

plugins.name: orphic-eyes
plugins.author: Ilham-Musyafa
plugins.does: Captures and compares screenshots, verifies bounded pixel-edit requests, and produces visual reports and follow-up prompts for coding agents. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ilham-Musyafa/Orphic-Eyes/a0411b982b43141cd5b11ba2bb19c204cc9d76b5/README.md)

reads.best: Deterministic per-request verdicts, fixed loop goals, browser/network guards and real-browser test cases add useful evidence beyond asking a vision model to review a page.
reads.worst: Legacy file:// capture accepts arbitrary absolute paths, enabling screenshots of secret files, and launches the browser with the full inherited environment; see [capture code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ilham-Musyafa/Orphic-Eyes/a0411b982b43141cd5b11ba2bb19c204cc9d76b5/engine/capture.py).

plugins.name: delx-recovery
plugins.author: davidmosiah
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted recovery and cross-session continuity tools, with a skill for saving and resuming structured capsules. [Pinned README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidmosiah/delx-plugins/c1d4be02df59f05fe65a27000d0b06b28c9733c2/delx-recovery/README.md)

reads.best: The capsule preserves goals, completed work, next steps and refuted approaches, with clear private-identity and untrusted-handoff guidance.
reads.worst: The Hermes package is chiefly a hosted MCP connector and ritual skill: its guardian hooks do not run in Hermes, and remote storage/recovery behavior is outside the pinned code.

plugins.name: hermes-security-plugin
plugins.author: alygg77
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to remote security-header checks and penetration-testing provider lookups through two MCP servers and a workflow skill.

reads.best: The tiny package clearly discloses its remote data flows and marks both servers untrusted for Hermes approval handling.
reads.worst: No checking implementation or tests are pinned locally, so reliability depends on mutable remote tools and a skill rather than a reviewed security engine.

plugins.name: asin-hhc-proof-of-pay
plugins.author: dbottrader
plugins.does: Validates ASIN-HHC receipt structure, checks a published provenance hash chain and reads a work-market board snapshot.

reads.best: Read-only local schema and chain checks offer concrete verification while explicitly distinguishing internal consistency from independent proof.
reads.worst: The shipped test harness looks for a nonexistent nested asin-hhc-proof-of-pay package, and chain consistency cannot independently establish that the work or payment occurred.

plugins.name: agent-latency-budget
plugins.author: qawine
plugins.does: Records recent tool durations per session and exposes budget checks and percentile reports.

reads.best: Monotonic fallback timing and a Hermes-path demo make tool latency observable with little setup and no external services.
reads.worst: The manifest promises fail-fast enforcement but checks only completed calls, and per-session dictionaries have no automatic session eviction.

plugins.name: agenda
plugins.author: zzzubair
plugins.does: Maintains an agent todo list with due dates, snoozes, a searchable archive, per-turn due-item context and optional wake/cron reminders.

reads.best: Automatic, bounded due-item injection and a durable archive keep obligations visible across conversations ([code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zzzubair/hermes-agenda/d5a34a747d5d6e98cd2e398514544db6fa9d41a1/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: There are no tests, read/modify/write operations have no lock, and reminder subprocess failures return None while adding the task can still report success ([code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zzzubair/hermes-agenda/d5a34a747d5d6e98cd2e398514544db6fa9d41a1/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: api-indonesia
plugins.author: khmuhtadin
plugins.does: Adds a hosted MCP connector and reference skill for Indonesian public-data lookups, validation and calculators. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khmuhtadin/api-indonesia-examples/73d9d4bc060ad4814d0c95c9b3f5f328d07858d5/README.md)

reads.best: The package declares a Hermes secret and authenticated MCP header, documents per-call credit costs and gives detailed lookup examples and limitations. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khmuhtadin/api-indonesia-examples/73d9d4bc060ad4814d0c95c9b3f5f328d07858d5/README.md)
reads.worst: The actual tools, data freshness and error handling are served remotely outside the pinned repository, which contains examples and configuration but no server tests. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khmuhtadin/api-indonesia-examples/73d9d4bc060ad4814d0c95c9b3f5f328d07858d5/README.md)

plugins.name: commonly-hermes-plugin
plugins.author: lilyshen0722
plugins.does: Exposes Commonly pod messaging, shared context and task operations to Hermes through an npm-hosted MCP server.

reads.best: The compact package declares its secret through Hermes and documents installation, write permissions and missing mention wakeups candidly.
reads.worst: Its implementation is a config-and-skill wrapper around npm code outside the Git pin, with default trust allowing posting without confirmation.

plugins.name: veille
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Adds six tools for Veille email, domain, IP, phone, VAT and IBAN intelligence through its hosted API.

reads.best: A small read-only client uses Hermes-scoped credentials, explicit HTTP timeouts and tested API-error handling.
reads.worst: Its functionality is a thin wrapper around an external API requiring a Veille account and credits.

plugins.name: shvl-agent-plugin
plugins.author: jlucwright
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to SHVL’s hosted read-only workspace and Xero accounting tools through MCP and a workspace-review skill.

reads.best: Documents OAuth, workspace selection, read-only permissions and stale-versus-live accounting data clearly.
reads.worst: The pinned package is only manifests and a skill: the actual service implementation and tests are absent, and tool behavior can change independently of the pin.

plugins.name: realcryptocap
plugins.author: jamesparser
plugins.does: Adds crypto price and native-market-cap tools, an instant slash-command table and model-written market briefs from RealCryptoCap data.

reads.best: Readable dependency-free handlers provide live-data lookup, short caching, secret-store integration and a data-only fallback when the model is unavailable.
reads.worst: It is mainly a single-service wrapper; native-asset filtering is heuristic, and tests use fixtures and a fake model rather than Hermes integration.

plugins.name: timelinesai-whatsapp
plugins.author: museyib99
plugins.does: Configures an OAuth-authenticated hosted WhatsApp MCP connection with an inbox workflow skill.

reads.best: Uses Hermes-managed OAuth and untrusted-server approvals, with explicit recipient-and-text confirmation guidance.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains configuration and a skill only; the actual tools run remotely and cannot be audited at this commit.

plugins.name: game-lab
plugins.author: flabanabba8
plugins.does: Bundles safe-copy game modding, RPG Maker localization, sprite-sheet checks, and experimental X11 playtesting tools. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flabanabba8/game-lab/3173e1b09860be1c4aac3c952cf97b9447cdc55e/README.md)

reads.best: Revision copies, rollback, localization control-code checks, and approval-gated input are concrete safeguards for users editing their games. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flabanabba8/game-lab/3173e1b09860be1c4aac3c952cf97b9447cdc55e/README.md)
reads.worst: The pinned README reports 0/4 complete correct SuperTux batch runs and 0/2 Packet Storm runs, while the parts share no data and most end-to-end game workflows remain unverified. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flabanabba8/game-lab/3173e1b09860be1c4aac3c952cf97b9447cdc55e/README.md)

plugins.name: argorant
plugins.author: argorant
plugins.does: Skill plus remote-MCP config connecting to Argorant's hosted lead search and email campaign service via OAuth.

reads.best: Clear README, OAuth instead of keys, untrusted trust level so spending and sending asks first.
reads.worst: No code, just a wrapper for a paid hosted service a skill plus MCP config could do.

plugins.name: berrys
plugins.author: GeneralBerrys
plugins.does: Points Hermes at Berrys' hosted OAuth MCP server for generating product listing images, ads and short videos, plus a long skill.

reads.best: A polished hosted creative service with OAuth sign-in and no keys to paste.
reads.worst: There is no plugin code, only config files and a 20 KB skill for a remote paid service that does not appear at the pinned commit, and it is generic across many agents rather than made for Hermes.

plugins.name: supranalytics
plugins.author: aniketmohite
plugins.does: Packages five guided analytics skills over SuprAnalytics's OAuth remote MCP for weekly, traffic, funnel, revenue, and performance reports.

reads.best: The skills make a remote analytics connector more approachable by giving common reports clear workflows and defaults.
reads.worst: The repository adds little Hermes-side machinery beyond prompts/skills around a hosted connector, and the catalog submission is still pending.

plugins.name: model-forge-providers
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Registers Strata and Project Maya as local model provider profiles with environment-based endpoint settings and model aliases.

reads.best: It can make two local inference engines selectable as Hermes providers.
reads.worst: This package has only profile declarations: no own README, tests, engine setup, health check, or model listing.

plugins.name: session-lock
plugins.author: TightXu
plugins.does: Desktop plugin that lists Hermes active-session leases and lets you release stale 'chat open somewhere else' locks.

reads.best: Fixes a real annoyance with a status chip and confirmation before releasing live owners.
reads.worst: Edits Hermes runtime files directly, ships a Windows-only installer and its one test file has no test functions.

plugins.name: hermes-guild
plugins.author: Blackleets
plugins.does: Provides a local collaboration registry with skill matching, owner-reviewed connections and deliveries, and signed reputation exports.

reads.best: A substantial registry implements explainable matching, proposal review and portable reputation with lifecycle and tampering tests.
reads.worst: The HTTP registry generates and returns users’ private keys despite claims they never leave the client, and the Hermes command/tools are hardwired to the local registry.

plugins.name: gsc-wizard
plugins.author: jbobbink
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to the hosted GSC Wizard SEO service through MCP and bundles 34 analytics workflow skills. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gscwizard/hermes-plugin/eea7aceb947cbe503cfe1b495e5e6765d265b8be/README.md)

reads.best: The default package marks the server untrusted and supplies detailed property-selection, reporting and setup workflows. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gscwizard/hermes-plugin/eea7aceb947cbe503cfe1b495e5e6765d265b8be/README.md)
reads.worst: Its documented native-OAuth and headless overrides omit trust: untrusted, which removes the package's enforced write-approval gate under Hermes's configuration precedence. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gscwizard/hermes-plugin/eea7aceb947cbe503cfe1b495e5e6765d265b8be/README.md) [Hermes trust handling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/82c639ffa2a6f72f58fa65f6c1c9647e50d6765d/hermes_cli/agent_plugins.py)

plugins.name: distro-reader
plugins.author: DistroBrad
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Distro’s hosted Reader MCP endpoint with skills for news discovery, reading, digests, archive research and premium-content workflows.

reads.best: The package marks the server untrusted and includes a small contract smoke test plus explicit payment and tipping consent guidance.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no Reader implementation, and its smoke test checks discovery rather than article, payment or failure behavior.

plugins.name: makernice
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Makernice’s hosted image and video generation service and supplies setup, product-video, trend-remix and budget-planning skills.

reads.best: Skills consistently require fresh estimates, exact spending caps and stable request IDs for retries, backed by an untrusted-server declaration.
reads.worst: The actual generation and spending enforcement are remote and unpinned, while Hermes setup still requires manually adding OAuth server configuration.

plugins.name: quegly
plugins.author: NicoGrajales
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Quegly’s hosted MCP service for social publishing, scheduling and analytics.

reads.best: The portable manifest uses a Hermes secret setting and marks the remote server untrusted so write-capable calls require approval.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains configuration and a skill, with no server implementation or tests, so remote behavior and runtime tool changes cannot be audited here.

plugins.name: chartquery
plugins.author: josselinlbe
plugins.does: Adds four ChartQuery API tools for rendering charts, prompt-generated charts, QR codes and barcodes as public image links.

reads.best: A compact standard-library implementation uses scoped secrets, key-gated registration, network timeouts and mocked endpoint tests.
reads.worst: Every render uses a hosted credit-consuming API and share=true; the wrapper adds no approval or privacy control around publishing supplied data.

plugins.name: asin
plugins.author: josselinlbe
plugins.does: Exposes Amazon search, recorded price history and collected seller offers through three Asin API tools ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asindotdev/hermes-plugin-asin/14397b67830af4ce0a6988b828ec6d97e6fb90da/README.md)).

reads.best: A compact, readable standard-library integration uses Hermes-scoped secrets, key-gated tools and mocked endpoint/error tests.
reads.worst: It is a thin paid-service wrapper with no local analysis; its HTTP client has no response-size cap or explicit redirect restriction ([HTTP client](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asindotdev/hermes-plugin-asin/14397b67830af4ce0a6988b828ec6d97e6fb90da/_client.py)).

plugins.name: agentstatus-index
plugins.author: dulrajnr
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted MCP directory that searches, compares and forwards calls to indexed public servers.

reads.best: Server discovery followed by a single forwarded tool call can expand the agent’s reach without a separate install for each service.
reads.worst: The pinned package is configuration and a skill with no forwarding implementation or tests; its safety guarantees depend on a mutable hosted server.

plugins.name: skysay
plugins.author: skyzer
plugins.does: Packages a read-only remote MCP connection and workflow skill for inspecting Skysay workspaces, voice agents, numbers and calls.

reads.best: Uses Hermes-managed OAuth and a dedicated read-only endpoint with clear setup, revocation and sensitive-data guidance.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no server implementation or tests, so its read-only guarantees depend on an external service that cannot be audited in this tree.

plugins.name: planejamais
plugins.author: hendrykcosta75
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Planeja+ strategic plans, tasks, meetings and company administration through a hosted OAuth MCP server.

reads.best: Provides explicit company-selection guidance, detailed mutation disclosures and an untrusted MCP declaration without bundling credentials.
reads.worst: The server code and tools are outside the pin, and the documented native OAuth setup replaces the untrusted entry unless the operator separately restores that setting.

plugins.name: listeningkit-log
plugins.author: deepmroot
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to an installed logMcp process for social inbox reading, drafting and approved account actions.

reads.best: Explicit untrusted-server configuration and practical inbox workflows put approval gates around social write operations.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains no server code or tests; behavior and account-cookie handling depend on the separately installed, unpinned log runtime.

plugins.name: hermes-safeguard
plugins.author: robberdom
plugins.does: Intercepts financial tool calls and applies EVM transaction policies, simulation checks, threat lists and optional operator confirmations.

reads.best: The plugin implements substantial policy, trace-inspection and emergency-stop logic with extensive security-focused test files.
reads.worst: Execution enables auto-broadcast by default without universal Hermes approval, can start a mock RPC when localhost is unavailable, and Telegram credential handling loads a local .env instead of scoped secrets.

plugins.name: synap
plugins.author: jimmyplup
plugins.does: Registers Synap as an OpenAI-compatible model provider with live model discovery and six fallback model IDs.

reads.best: Uses Hermes provider profiles directly with no dependencies or custom credential persistence.
reads.worst: The pinned manifest omits requires_env for SYNAP_API_KEY, leaving installer key setup undeclared, and its three stub-based tests verify profile constants rather than real Hermes integration.

plugins.name: genflick
plugins.author: buildngrowsv
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to the hosted Genflick creative workspace MCP endpoint and bundles two workflow and account-connection skills.

reads.best: The connector explicitly keeps remote tools untrusted and documents the native Hermes OAuth workaround, spending boundaries and limited read-only qualification.
reads.worst: The pinned tree contains only connector manifests and skills, so creative execution and service-side approval claims cannot be inspected, and sign-in requires manual native configuration.

plugins.name: proof-lens
plugins.author: invisiblemonsters
plugins.does: Provides a local Desktop pane that checks RUP proof additions from CNF/DRAT files and displays refutation depth and a clause-depth histogram.

reads.best: Implements inspectable unit propagation and depth accounting locally, with a focused UI and no network or credential requirements.
reads.worst: Parsing silently skips malformed tokens, a capped prefix may still return valid without checking the remaining trace, and the only test file is an argument-driven CLI harness without assertions or bundled cases.

plugins.name: recloc
plugins.author: SomeoneElseSt
plugins.does: Sends address-bearing brrr notifications for an iPhone Shortcut to create location-triggered Apple Reminders.

reads.best: It keeps live geofence monitoring on the phone and distinguishes push acceptance from confirmed delivery.
reads.worst: The promised address redaction returns addresses of 28 characters or fewer unchanged, while reminder listing always returns an empty list and cancellation cannot recall delivery.

plugins.name: corallium
plugins.author: Aoyi-Feng
plugins.does: Exposes a shared claim graph with publishing, review votes, evidence verification, task leases and offline reads.
