reads.best: Claims can become contested or suspect as reviews and withdrawn ancestors change the graph, making shared knowledge revisable.
reads.worst: The client reads read_token and write_token directly from config.yaml or os.environ rather than Hermes’s secret scope, violating the catalog credential rule.

plugins.name: myeline
plugins.author: gibson-sandbox
plugins.does: Points Hermes at Myeline's hosted MCP memory server (cortex.myeline.si) and adds a skill teaching the agent when to propose, search and retract facts.

reads.best: Provenance-backed memory where AI-proposed facts wait in a human review queue, with OAuth handled by Hermes's own MCP client so the package holds no secrets.
reads.worst: The package is two manifests and a 53-line skill with no code or tests; all behaviour lives in a proprietary paid service that the plugin cannot show or verify.

plugins.name: waterloo-jane-street-qr
plugins.author: georgxzh
plugins.does: Fourteen quant tools (Black-Scholes, Heston, Monte Carlo, Almgren-Chriss, Black-Litterman and more) plus a trading-desk persona and hooks that force answers into an EV and TAKE/PASS/HEDGE format.

reads.best: Deterministic, stdlib-only pricing and execution engines with 81 known-answer, cross-model and property tests.
reads.worst: In its default strict mode a transform_llm_output hook appends a 'desk compliance' warning to every answer in every chat that lacks an EV and a verdict, and all the code sits in one 4,067-line __init__.py beside a stray git submodule.

plugins.name: screenrig
plugins.author: gersham
plugins.does: Packages a digital-signage CLI, workflow skills and a remote MCP connection for managing screens, media and playlists.

reads.best: A broad readable CLI and detailed workflows reach real physical signage, with packaging and launcher tests.
reads.worst: The bundled CLI reads and refreshes its own file-stored credentials instead of using Hermes credential routes, violating the catalog secret-store rule.

plugins.name: hermes-make-plain
plugins.author: hey-yx
plugins.does: Adds a Desktop composer button that rewrites the current draft through Hermes’s auxiliary model route and replaces it without sending.

reads.best: A focused localized UI includes busy, duplicate-click, unload and concurrent-edit guards, with stub-SDK tests.
reads.worst: The core feature is a wording-cleanup prompt, and preservation of every concrete detail is requested from the model rather than verified.

plugins.name: loredocs
plugins.author: labyrinth-analytics
plugins.does: Launches a version-pinned local MCP knowledge vault with document CRUD, version history, full-text search and paid semantic search.

reads.best: The backing service implements persistent SQLite and filesystem document storage, versioning and context retrieval beyond a prompt.
reads.worst: No test suite is present in the pinned tree, the Hermes README documents long-body tool-call failures, and the runtime licence resolver can read the sibling LoreConvo licence store outside Hermes’s secret routes.

plugins.name: fashio
plugins.author: cms-be
plugins.does: Configures a hosted MCP connector and workflow skill for generating fashion product images and catalog shoots using paid Fashio credits.

reads.best: The manifest marks the server untrusted, delegates key substitution to Hermes and documents explicit confirmation before paid operations.
reads.worst: The pinned package is configuration and a skill only: remote tool implementations and their tests are absent and can change independently of the pin.

plugins.name: subnano
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Provides a bundled local MCP server for finding, buying and publishing marketplace posts and files with Nano or Base USDC payments.

reads.best: The readable server bundle implements explicit host-form approvals, cumulative spending caps, identity binding and recovery of uncertain operations.
reads.worst: The server reads and writes account credentials and wallet keys in its own private state store rather than using Hermes credential routes, and ships no reviewable test suite.

plugins.name: fitbit-mcp
plugins.author: davidmosiah
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a version-pinned local MCP server for Fitbit activity, sleep, heart-rate and body data ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidmosiah/fitbit-mcp/c669895c6c96ded8c35978c7461c02dbed7fa0fc/agent-plugin/README.md)).

reads.best: A clearly documented portable package offers a pinned connector version, terminal setup and an explicit disclosure of local token storage.
reads.worst: The connector reads and refreshes file-backed OAuth tokens outside Hermes credential routes, leaving the catalog rule 11 admission issue unresolved ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidmosiah/fitbit-mcp/c669895c6c96ded8c35978c7461c02dbed7fa0fc/src/services/fitbit-client.ts)).

plugins.name: equipdash
plugins.author: equipdash
plugins.does: Packages a hosted EquipDash MCP connection and operating skill for rental bookings, customers and payments.

reads.best: The portable manifest marks its write-capable MCP server untrusted so Hermes can require human approval.
reads.worst: The repository contains no tool implementation or tests; the remote server and payment behavior are outside the pinned commit.

plugins.name: ctrlall
plugins.author: namangoyal3
plugins.does: Exposes a Mac ctrl+all daemon for launching and steering coding-agent chats, reading transcripts and checking git state.

reads.best: A small standard-library integration exposes fourteen practical agent-control operations and reads its token through Hermes secrets.
reads.worst: The model can request full-auto permission mode through an ungated RPC wrapper; validation is delegated to the external daemon and the included selftest only drives a mock.

plugins.name: preferly
plugins.author: preferly-ai
plugins.does: Declares a hosted Streamable HTTP MCP server offering Preferly AI-visibility tools plus a skill for crawler, robots, llms.txt, structured-data, and visibility checks.

reads.best: The service can expose specialized website visibility checks without requiring the plugin to ship a large local implementation.
reads.worst: At the pinned commit it is only a manifest, MCP URL, logo, and skill: there are no local handlers or tests, and availability and behavior are delegated to a third-party service.

plugins.name: doop
plugins.author: J182Razor
plugins.does: Config-only MCP pointer (mcp.json, plugin.json, one skill) to a doop design-canvas server on localhost.

reads.best: Marks the MCP server untrusted so writes need approval.
reads.worst: No code or tests, and the docs contradict the config (DOOP_MCP_URL is never read; it says Node is needed, but nothing uses it).

plugins.name: lastscanned
plugins.author: dragonhuntr
plugins.does: Points Hermes at the hosted lastscanned MCP server for parcel/container tracking and rate quotes, plus a skill.

reads.best: Zero-credential, simple install for tracking 549 carriers.
reads.worst: No local code: an MCP config and a skill, so it depends entirely on a third-party service.

plugins.name: openany
plugins.author: ComunionIO
plugins.does: Config-only MCP bundle connecting Hermes to OpenAny's hosted marketplace server (search_apis/get_api/run_api) with a secret-store API key.

reads.best: Uses Hermes secret config_schema and marks the server untrusted, with an honest README.
reads.worst: No code of its own; it is an MCP pointer to a commercial service that can execute arbitrary paid APIs.

plugins.name: logmine
plugins.author: rodricksz4h5
plugins.does: Exposes local log-template counting, regex search with context and timestamp-bucket timelines as three read-only tools.

reads.best: Deterministic template normalization and streaming file iteration can reduce large repetitive logs to compact counts without network services or dependencies.
reads.worst: Bounded-memory claims overreach: complete lines are read before truncation and timeline buckets are capped only after accumulation, while regex matching has no timeout and no automated tests ship.

plugins.name: relay-telegram
plugins.author: 0xCheetah1
plugins.does: Attaches to the existing Hermes Telegram bot and posts incoming RELAY agent-to-agent calls from a local Unix socket as owner-only Accept/Reject buttons, passing the decision to the separate RELAY Node bridge.

reads.best: Owner-only buttons with a one-time code, sent over a 0600 Unix socket with 2-second timeouts, keep call approval with the person.
reads.worst: The Hermes part is a thin untested shim with a bare manifest (no kind, env or settings) that regex-reads ~/.hermes/config.yaml and needs a separate Node service installed via curl | bash; its message says 30 seconds while the server defaults to 120.

plugins.name: zalodesk
plugins.author: BAODAU
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to ZaloDesk's hosted OAuth MCP service for Zalo inbox, messaging, and team-management actions.

reads.best: The manifest marks the remote server untrusted, so sensitive message, access, and credit actions use Hermes approval controls.
reads.worst: The pinned package is only an npx remote-MCP launcher and skill, with no implementation or tests for the hosted tools it claims.

plugins.name: mflow
plugins.author: vladyslavpatrick
plugins.does: Registers mFlow's hosted MCP service and a workflow skill for boards, knowledge-base work, and coding-agent delegation.

reads.best: The documentation candidly describes the OAuth alternative, destructive-operation confirmation, and current PAT limitation.
reads.worst: The package contains no working local implementation or tests, and its bundled token path depends on PAT support that the README says is not yet available.

plugins.name: predictionmarketspicks
plugins.author: predictionmarketspicks
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted prediction-market MCP service and bundles six offline quantitative calculators.

reads.best: The package offers a clean offline calculator mode and a well-documented MCP bridge for market research.
reads.worst: The advertised live tools are dynamically supplied by an opaque hosted service, and the checked-in tests cover only local tool listing.

plugins.name: buildpilot
plugins.author: Justnevo
plugins.does: Provides local SQLite-backed tools to track projects, tasks, task status, and progress checkpoints across sessions.

reads.best: The small toolset directly supports durable project context and checkpoint retrieval without external services or credentials.
reads.worst: The implementation is a conventional CRUD tracker with limited surfaced error handling and relatively basic documentation and tests.

plugins.name: snippet
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Snippet’s hosted MCP service for creator brand deals, sponsorships, and correspondence.

reads.best: A compact portable package exposes useful creator workflows through a hosted MCP service without a local runtime or dependency.
reads.worst: The package contains no service implementation, its live tools can change independently of the pin, and the README says the portable-package login path does not work and requires a separate native OAuth connection.

plugins.name: fortograph
plugins.author: fortograph
plugins.does: Three tools that upload a local image to a third-party 'Fortograph' web API to selectively encrypt (redact) regions and later decrypt them with a password.

reads.best: The password secret is resolved through Hermes's secret_scope first before falling back to a plain env var, matching the catalog's secret-handling expectations.
reads.worst: Calling fortograph_redact/unredact uploads the user's image to a remote third-party server immediately with no approval gate, and the only verification is a single manual end-to-end script requiring live network access, not an automated test suite.

plugins.name: benchline
plugins.author: ShalyX
plugins.does: One read-only tool that preflights a numeric lab-result CSV against a user-supplied analyte-to-unit map and returns a row-referenced QC summary without identifiers or values.

reads.best: Carefully bounded: 1 MiB/5,000-row cap, rejects symlinks, no network or writes, never echoes identifiers or measured values, and a 177-line validator test suite.
reads.worst: A very narrow lab-operator niche, and the work is a CSV check that a skill with a short script could largely do.

plugins.name: hermes-arcade
plugins.author: leoresendedop-sys
plugins.does: Three neon canvas games (Snake, Breakout, Pong) in a dashboard tab with a shared high-score store the agent can query through three read-only tools.

reads.best: A fun, working, hand-written arcade that uses dashboard, tools and slash command around one atomic score store.
reads.worst: No tests, the agent side is three trivial leaderboard queries, POST /scores accepts any score, and the README embeds none of its screenshots or demo gif.

plugins.name: adplug
plugins.author: danielpopamd
plugins.does: Portable package of 16 PPC skills that drive AdPlug's hosted MCP server for Google, Meta, LinkedIn, Microsoft and Reddit Ads, which the user must add to Hermes by hand.

reads.best: Deep, well-written skill content with per-platform audit and build references, and a preview-then-approve rule for every spend change.
reads.worst: The package holds no code at all, not even an mcp.json: it is Markdown skills for a paid SaaS, so a skill folder would do exactly the same.

plugins.name: superlist
plugins.author: MarcelKaeding
plugins.does: Portable package with an mcp.json pointing at Superlist's hosted MCP server plus one skill, so Hermes can manage the user's tasks and lists after OAuth sign-in.

reads.best: Marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before every write, uses OAuth through Hermes with no keys in the package, and the skill teaches find-before-change and confirm-before-delete.
reads.worst: The whole plugin is a two-line mcp.json and a skill for a vendor's existing MCP server, and the README is the generic multi-client Superlist MCP page rather than a Hermes one.

plugins.name: read-only-mode
plugins.author: chengyimingvb
plugins.does: Desktop composer toggle that prepends a read-only instruction to each message.

reads.best: Honest README with screenshots, per-session state, and clear statement that it is a soft constraint.
reads.worst: Only a prompt prefix; does not enforce read-only, no tests, and no backend code.

plugins.name: ostra
plugins.author: ostraagent
plugins.does: Config package launching the @ostraagent/mcp server so the agent runs its own USDG vault on Robinhood Chain to pay, swap and hire.

reads.best: Server is marked untrusted so Hermes asks before non-read-only tools.
reads.worst: Moves money via a seed the server writes to ~/.ostra outside Hermes's secret store, with no code or tests in the plugin itself.

plugins.name: getyoutubetranscript
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to the GetYouTubeTranscript remote MCP server for transcripts, YouTube search and channel browsing, plus four skills.

reads.best: Honest disclosure of what is sent, the credit cost, and treating transcripts as data.
reads.worst: It is only configuration and skills, with the API key read from a shell or .env variable, and the tool set is served remotely and not covered by the pinned commit.

plugins.name: groundcontrol
plugins.author: teckedd-code2save
plugins.does: Adds a /groundcontrol command and an operating skill for using GroundControl's scoped MCP deployment tools, with a conservative evidence-receipt reviewer.

reads.best: Careful safety stance: read-only by default, OAuth stays in Hermes, and receipts never echo secrets.
reads.worst: The code is a short command that returns guidance text and a JSON projection, so it adds almost nothing a skill could not do, and it needs a GroundControl server.

plugins.name: verifiable-math-kernel
plugins.author: pCwOrM
plugins.does: SymPy identity checks, integer factorization, elliptic-curve invariants and a regex Lean sorry scanner as tools, plus pre/post tool hooks.

reads.best: SymPy and factorization really run locally with no keys and no network.
reads.worst: Claims more than the code does (no Tate or 2-descent, torsion via an unchecked Lutz-Nagell test, '100% deterministic' primality), its parse timeout can't fire, and the README promotes a token.

plugins.name: aunx-decompose
plugins.author: aunysillyme
plugins.does: A planning skill where the agent writes a task as typed units with data edges, and a Python checker validates it and prints parallel waves and the critical path.

reads.best: A real stdlib checker verifies the plan's structure, with 62 tests on the checker.
reads.worst: The Hermes side is a 40-line wrapper whose /decompose only returns 'load the skill' text, none of the tests touch it, and the README says only the Claude Code plugin is packaged.

plugins.name: words-into-music
plugins.author: constantinginga
plugins.does: MCP connection metadata and a skill for generating songs from ideas or lyrics.

reads.best: Skill states the credit cost and confirms before spending.
reads.worst: Metadata only, with no code in the repo.

plugins.name: buzzmark
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: MCP connection and a skill for writing and scheduling social posts in the business voice.

reads.best: OAuth and nothing posts immediately.
reads.worst: Metadata only; the server source is not included.

plugins.name: linkjolt
plugins.author: Efesop
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to LinkJolt's hosted affiliate-management MCP and supplies six guided merchant workflows.

reads.best: The workflows clearly separate reporting, commission review, coupon setup, troubleshooting, and payouts, with confirmation language around mutations.
reads.worst: The repository contains no implementation or tests for the hosted service and depends on an npx-downloaded bridge, so the pinned plugin cannot establish end-to-end reliability offline.

plugins.name: anvilads
plugins.author: lordteez
plugins.does: Configures a remote authenticated MCP connection for reading stored AnvilAds advertising reports, accounts and lead metrics.

reads.best: The connector has a small local attack surface and clearly describes read-only, business-scoped reporting.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains configuration and a skill, with no server implementation or tests to establish remote reliability and no campaign management capability.

plugins.name: pandy-tickets
plugins.author: kenny08gt
plugins.does: Connects to Pandy Tickets public MCP for Guatemala event search, event details, checkout links and claimable event drafts.

reads.best: The public connector needs no key and keeps actual ticket purchase and event publication in a person-completed flow.
reads.worst: Only manifests, connection configuration and a skill are pinned; remote tool implementation and tests are absent, while organizer management in the README needs a separate connection.

plugins.name: scribase
plugins.author: caelum0x
plugins.does: Provisions a Scribase Postgres project and environment, polls its operation and returns database connection details and API keys.

reads.best: A small dependency-free implementation uses Hermes secret scope and reports provisioning progress rather than polling forever.
reads.worst: There are no tests or approval hook for billable provisioning, and repeating a pending call issues a fresh environment POST with a new idempotency key.

plugins.name: web-specstream
plugins.author: Specstreamai
plugins.does: A vendor adapter that registers SpecStream's paid API as Hermes's web_search and web_extract backend.

reads.best: Small and clean: the key comes from get_secret, it has timeouts and 6 mocked tests, and it plugs into Hermes's own web backend slot.
reads.worst: A thin wrapper around a paid vendor API: the limit is never sent, extract silently cuts batches to 20 URLs, and raw error bodies go to the model unbounded.

plugins.name: microbiz-desk
plugins.author: Danzilla0
plugins.does: An offline SQLite ledger of customers, sales and debts for a small trader, with exact naira money maths and a weekly report, through 5 tools and /microbiz commands.

reads.best: Stores amounts as exact whole kobo, refuses overpayments and ambiguous names, works offline, and has 13 tests.
reads.worst: Partial name matching books a sale to a new customer onto an existing one with a longer name ('Ada' onto 'Ada Obi'); the currency is hard-coded to NGN and there is no UI.

plugins.name: devtune
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Two skills plus DevTune's hosted MCP server, showing what AI answer engines and coding agents say about and pick for your product.

reads.best: It is honest and safe: the server is marked untrusted, so Hermes asks before non-read-only tools, and the key comes from the Hermes env.
reads.worst: No local code or tests; it is a marketing-analytics vendor's skills and MCP endpoint, useful mainly to DevTune customers.

plugins.name: hireko
plugins.author: mohan-metricdust
plugins.does: A stdio MCP server that lets a recruiter sign in to HireKo, create live AI screening-interview links and fetch candidate match scores from a remote AWS Lambda backend.

reads.best: Browser sign-in with a state check, and Cognito tokens cached in a 0600 file per tenant.
reads.worst: Its own VERIFICATION.md says `hermes plugins validate` fails and it must not be called install-ready; the password comes from a plain env var rather than Hermes's secret store; prod links use a hard-coded interview-test domain; and an unknown email falls back to recruiter@hireko.ai.

plugins.name: bot-shelf
plugins.author: cradrrat
plugins.does: Config-only Agent Plugins package (plugin.json, mcp.json, a skill) that connects Hermes to a remote MCP server for searching a directory of 9,000+ community Grok Bots.

reads.best: Honest disclosure of what it sends where; read-only apart from suggest_bot, with no key needed.
reads.worst: It ships no code, the server's source is not published, and it helps you find bots for a different product (Grok) rather than improving Hermes; its own skill already covers this with plain curl.

plugins.name: hermes-output-enhancement
plugins.author: annipu
plugins.does: Desktop-only CSS that restyles headings, emphasis and tables in assistant replies.

reads.best: Honest, tightly scoped and off by default, with integrity metadata.
reads.worst: Ships only one prebuilt JS file and no tests; it is cosmetic and tied to the current DOM.

plugins.name: joinsandwich-directory
plugins.author: tera-sarah
plugins.does: Points Hermes at Sandwich's hosted, no-auth MCP server so it can search caregiving resources and estimate long-term-care costs by US state.

reads.best: Gives agents a public, read-only eldercare directory and cost calculator with no account needed.
reads.worst: The package is only a remote MCP URL and a 24-line skill. All the logic is on a company server that can't be reviewed, and the README is mostly product marketing.

plugins.name: rosegold
plugins.author: mybchen
plugins.does: An Agent Plugins package pointing Hermes at rosegold's hosted OAuth MCP server, which matches Amazon offers and creator codes to the user's purchases taken from their Gmail order emails.

reads.best: No code of its own and no stored credential: Hermes keeps the OAuth token, and the README spells out what order data is sent.
reads.worst: A thin config for a commercial rewards service: it asks the agent to send the user's Amazon order items and prices to a third party, its tools run without approval under default trust, and the pull request is still open.

plugins.name: certarc
plugins.author: swaminadhankj
plugins.does: Config-only package pointing Hermes at CertArc's free hosted MCP endpoint for CISM/CISSP/CISA practice questions, exam outlines and study guides.

reads.best: No key, no local code, and a clear data-handling section with an honest list of limits.
reads.worst: Essentially a marketing funnel to a hosted quiz endpoint (links are tagged for sign-up tracking); nothing here a URL bookmark plus a skill could not do.

plugins.name: transcribo
plugins.author: santigamo
plugins.does: Connects Hermes through an MCP bridge to hosted audio/video transcription with speaker labels.

reads.best: The skill covers uploads, duplicate-job avoidance, partial transcripts and sensitive-audio disclosure.
reads.worst: The pinned package has no transcription implementation or tests, and its npx OAuth bridge stores tokens in ~/.mcp-auth rather than using Hermes-owned OAuth.

plugins.name: worldmonitor
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Configures Hermes to use WorldMonitor's hosted MCP intelligence service and a bundled research workflow skill [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koala73/worldmonitor-hermes-plugin/8db8fb2f5ea71d464c2f380a7c8564868c678986/README.md).

reads.best: The documentation clearly explains account limits, profile-owned authentication, source freshness and approval expectations for remote actions [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koala73/worldmonitor-hermes-plugin/8db8fb2f5ea71d464c2f380a7c8564868c678986/README.md).
reads.worst: The pinned contribution adds only remote MCP configuration and skill guidance, with Hermes installation and authenticated interoperability explicitly unverified [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koala73/worldmonitor-hermes-plugin/8db8fb2f5ea71d464c2f380a7c8564868c678986/README.md).

plugins.name: contract-hunter
plugins.author: NathanOyewole
plugins.does: Wraps Scout commands as Hermes tools and slash commands for finding EVM bounty targets, fetching source, running fork proofs, and producing reports.

reads.best: The wrapper uses argument lists, subprocess timeouts, a minimal child environment, and a default-off session-start pull.
reads.worst: The documented proof workflow passes --hypothesis to scout prove, but the Scout revision named by the plugin accepts only an ID there and exposes hypothesis as a separate subcommand; no plugin tests catch this mismatch.

plugins.name: meme-studio-mcp
plugins.author: MrHydeDev
plugins.does: Registers the hosted Meme Studio MCP service and a skill for selecting templates, captioning memes, and returning images or editor links.

reads.best: Clear installation, an illustrated demo, explicit remote-service disclosures, and an untrusted MCP declaration make the narrow connector easy to understand.
reads.worst: The pinned submission contains configuration and a skill only, so rendering and runtime tool behavior depend entirely on a closed-source hosted service outside the reviewed commit.

plugins.name: blindoracle
plugins.author: craigmbrown
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a remote agent-trust and paid-services MCP endpoint, with delegation guidance and a local receipt-hash verifier.

reads.best: The local standard-library verifier can compare deliverable hashes without credentials, and the package itself never signs payments.
reads.worst: The shipped transaction verifier accepts any successful transaction without matching recipient, amount or deliverable, while the remote trust-service implementation and tests are absent.

plugins.name: expatslist
plugins.author: aitrainingdatabroker
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a public ExpatsList MCP endpoint and supplies a skill for city listings and relocation reference lookups.

reads.best: The small package clearly discloses remote calls, needs no credentials and marks the server untrusted.
reads.worst: There is no pinned server implementation or test suite, and the PR explicitly says the package has not been tested in Hermes.

plugins.name: exchangerebel
plugins.author: DataRebelHQ
plugins.does: Adds an ExchangeRebel remote MCP connection and a skill for free discovery and paid x402 API calls.

reads.best: A minimal credential-free connector marks its server untrusted and explains paid-call prices and approval expectations.
reads.worst: The package supplies no payment implementation or end-to-end tests, and its README still describes header/query payment retries while the pinned skill specifies MCP payment metadata.

plugins.name: aurora-design-system
plugins.author: Ntizar
plugins.does: Adds Aurora design-system skills, bundled component lookup and an offline HTML class and CSS-pack validator.

reads.best: Bundled canonical markup and census-backed class checks help agents avoid inventing design-system components without a service or API key.
reads.worst: The validator only recognizes double-quoted lowercase class attributes and style blocks, misses equivalent HTML and inline CSS, and ships no tests; the README also incorrectly calls it skills-only.

plugins.name: evaluation-ledger
plugins.author: 1anter
plugins.does: Stores immutable artifact text in a local SQLite ledger with SHA-256/JSON checks, and (opt-in) records allowlisted usage metadata from API-request and tool-call hooks for per-session usage reports.

reads.best: Privacy-minded design: usage collection is off unless observe_usage is exactly true, observers keep only an allowlist of ids and counters, and artifacts are insert-only.
reads.worst: Narrow audience and rough finish: the README still says no public repository is claimed and mentions a 'routing plugin' from its sibling listings, the code is written in dense one-line style, and its tests live outside the pinned plugin folder.

plugins.name: postsider
plugins.author: lumizone
plugins.does: Packages a hosted PostSider MCP connection and workflow skill for social-media drafts, scheduling, publishing, and analytics.

reads.best: Marks the MCP server untrusted and clearly discloses publishing effects, costs, remote tool changes, and draft-first workflows.
reads.worst: The submission contains configuration and a skill rather than server code or tests, and its bundled mcp-remote path stores OAuth tokens outside Hermes under ~/.mcp-auth.

plugins.name: emailfig
plugins.author: desheikh
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to EmailFig’s hosted MCP server for contact management, campaign analytics, and campaign drafts.

reads.best: The untrusted MCP declaration preserves write approvals, and the documentation clearly discloses contact changes that can trigger emails or automations.
reads.worst: Only two configuration files are submitted, without server code or tests, and the bundled bridge keeps OAuth tokens in ~/.mcp-auth rather than Hermes’s secret store.

plugins.name: tupliq-launchpad
plugins.author: muhammadsalihu
plugins.does: Fetches RevenueCat subscription and revenue metrics and returns git commits for release-note drafting.

reads.best: Four focused read-only tools use Hermes secret lookup and bounded HTTP and git calls without extra dependencies.
reads.worst: No tests ship, multi-project discovery silently chooses the first project, and invalid arguments or subprocess failures can escape despite the README's never-raise claim.

plugins.name: apphitlist
plugins.author: mmdincer
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted App Store research MCP service with a skill explaining its nine advertised research tools. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mmdincer/apphitlist-mcp/a7ef3444bd7b6821f34908e802a71a2fdde06e50/README.md)

reads.best: The documentation clearly distinguishes estimated revenue ranges, paid tools and quotas, and openly discloses the remote-only implementation. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mmdincer/apphitlist-mcp/a7ef3444bd7b6821f34908e802a71a2fdde06e50/README.md)
reads.worst: At this pin mcp.json supplies no Authorization header and the setup examples target other clients, leaving a Hermes catalog install unable to authenticate; server code and tests are also absent. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mmdincer/apphitlist-mcp/a7ef3444bd7b6821f34908e802a71a2fdde06e50/mcp.json)

plugins.name: thott-bot
plugins.author: sunfishposting
plugins.does: Adds a remote MCP connection to thott.bot for World of Warcraft game-data questions. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thott-bot/plugin/af8439ac4c4560aba5303ee7578d921a33c7b5da/hermes/README.md)

reads.best: A minimal Hermes-specific README gives an explicit OAuth setup command and discloses that service queries are recorded. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thott-bot/plugin/af8439ac4c4560aba5303ee7578d921a33c7b5da/hermes/README.md)
reads.worst: Only connector manifests and documentation are pinned, with no server source or tests to substantiate freshness or coverage, and no documented opt-in for query recording. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thott-bot/plugin/af8439ac4c4560aba5303ee7578d921a33c7b5da/hermes/README.md)

plugins.name: hermes-persona-stickers
plugins.author: EricBlack47
plugins.does: Creates captioned character-reaction images from bundled assets or a Pillow fallback through a tool and slash command.

reads.best: Local rendering, emotion and size validation, bundled assets and rendering tests make the narrow feature tangible.
reads.worst: Imports Pillow unconditionally without declaring a Python dependency, and the claimed automatic emotional reactions have no registered detection hook.

plugins.name: adwave
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Adwave’s hosted advertising MCP server with a skill for campaign creation, management and reporting.

reads.best: Documents a coherent advertising workflow, prepaid spending and user confirmation before spending operations.
reads.worst: The pinned source is manifests and a skill: spending confirmation is instructed in prose, while server-side enforcement and campaign behavior are unavailable for review.

plugins.name: smart-automation
plugins.author: buttercode101
plugins.does: Tracks manually advanced cron dependency chains in local SQLite and displays their status and graph in Desktop.

reads.best: The code honestly keeps cron execution separate and tests dependency gating, duplicate triggers and concurrent advancement.
reads.worst: The calendar check is skipped when after_iso is omitted, and every session-start hook resets all running jobs to ready even if another session is still working.

plugins.name: project-feed
plugins.author: Tezenari
plugins.does: Packages a hosted Project Feed MCP connection and four skills for task execution, planning, status reporting and backlog triage.

reads.best: A small readable package documents Hermes OAuth setup, untrusted write approvals and workspace selection without handling credentials itself.
reads.worst: The pinned submission contains no server implementation; tool behavior changes remotely, access requires a Pro workspace, and the PR reports no live Hermes OAuth/tool-call verification.

plugins.name: remoet
plugins.author: ugglr
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted tech-job search and account-management MCP server.

reads.best: Public job search needs no account and the documentation clearly discloses public profile data and application side effects.
reads.worst: The documented OAuth setup replaces the package trust setting and permits write tools without approval unless users manually restore untrusted; server implementation is not pinned.

plugins.name: inboxapp
plugins.author: PicchiKevin
plugins.does: Configuration-only package that points Hermes at Inboxapp's hosted MCP server for X, LinkedIn and WhatsApp DMs, plus four skills for triage, replies and pipeline work.

reads.best: Tidy multi-client packaging with a consistency check script, the server marked untrusted, and skills that tell the agent never to ask for or print a token.
reads.worst: No code of its own, needs an Inboxapp team with API v2 (private rollout, 404 otherwise), and sending or deleting is left to the remote server and skill wording.

plugins.name: screenscene
plugins.author: solocreativeone
plugins.does: Turns a screenshot and narrated beats into a zooming explainer MP4 using ElevenLabs, Manim and ffmpeg.

reads.best: The pipeline is a practical combination of narration, timed camera motion and video rendering for demos.
reads.worst: It has no tests, depends on several external executables/services, writes to a fixed home directory and sends model-supplied narration to ElevenLabs.

plugins.name: kaption-whatsapp
plugins.author: kshmir
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Kaption's hosted WhatsApp MCP server and adds a workflow skill for personal messages and contacts. [PR and pinned-package review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/151331)

reads.best: The package declares an untrusted server and the skill asks the user to confirm message recipients and contents. [PR and pinned-package review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/151331)
reads.worst: The required OAuth setup creates an overriding server entry without the untrusted flag, dropping enforced approval for send and scheduling tools, as the catalog review identifies. [PR and pinned-package review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/151331)

plugins.name: fiscalisto
plugins.author: RVP97
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Fiscalisto’s hosted Mexican invoicing and tax MCP service with thirteen Spanish workflow skills and an English overview.

reads.best: The invoice and cancellation workflows explicitly require previews and confirmation tokens, and the manifest marks the remote server untrusted.
reads.worst: No server implementation or automated tests are pinned, and the npx OAuth bridge stores tokens in ~/.mcp-auth rather than Hermes’s own store.

plugins.name: rhythm-reaper
plugins.author: D0xedDevi0
plugins.does: Builds and checks pasteable Suno production frames from a local catalog of 41 hip-hop styles, including section plans and pronunciation substitutions.

reads.best: The local deterministic builder, complete lane sweep tests and reproducible demo make a narrow music-production workflow unusually well documented.
reads.worst: check_lyrics collects contradictory dynamic tags but never adds them to issues, so a contradictory draft can still return ok=true.

plugins.name: 990tax
plugins.author: ivanku
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to the hosted 990.tax nonprofit lookup service and adds skills for IRS record research and filing guidance.

reads.best: No-key access to nonprofit records has a clear research use, and the skills distinguish missing public data from zero values.
reads.worst: Only client configuration and skills are pinned: the server implementation, data processing and tool behavior cannot be inspected or tested from this repository.

plugins.name: botsee
plugins.author: sidekickjanet
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to BotSee hosted MCP for AI-visibility research with a skill guiding bounded retrieval and approval for paid operations.

reads.best: The connector tests real Hermes loading and scoped-secret substitution and clearly discloses that paid-operation limits are guidance.
reads.worst: No authenticated product discovery or operation is demonstrated in the pinned package, and spend controls depend on skill compliance and remote tool annotations.

plugins.name: hermes-secret-gate
plugins.author: MSAbhishek22
plugins.does: Scans supplied text and tool results for credential patterns and returns masked findings and advisory gate receipts.

reads.best: Deterministic offline scans and bounded receipts provide a small, readable auditing tool with tests for common credential formats.
reads.worst: The advertised fail-closed gate only returns a BLOCK label; its post-tool hook logs after execution and neither prevents outbound sends nor changes results.

plugins.name: everything-nothing
plugins.author: dmkjr
plugins.does: Provides Desktop draft templates and design-brief generators plus configurable fixed reply-concision guidance.

reads.best: Local template editing, field previews, clipboard export, and illustrated setup make the small writing workflow approachable.
reads.worst: The agent-side feature only injects fixed style text, and the repository contains no tests for the Desktop template and brief workflows.

plugins.name: better-analyst
plugins.author: excelformulabot
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted PDF-to-Excel MCP service through a pinned mcp-remote bridge and an extraction workflow skill.

reads.best: The package explicitly marks its server untrusted so write-capable conversion calls require approval, and documents credits, uploads and sign-in limits.
reads.worst: Converter code and tests are absent from the pin, the server supplies tools dynamically, and OAuth uses the bridge token cache in ~/.mcp-auth instead of Hermes-managed authentication.

plugins.name: tripwire
plugins.author: percyhendrux123-prog
plugins.does: Hooks that append refused tool calls and approval denials to a private local events file with minimal metadata.

reads.best: Careful privacy-minimal logging (O_NOFOLLOW, 0600, no args stored).
reads.worst: No README and no tests in the plugin folder; ~140 lines with narrow value.

plugins.name: besthumanizer
plugins.author: shagghiesuperstar
plugins.does: Tools that score and rewrite text for AI-likeness via besthumanizer.app's MCP API, plus a hook on outgoing post/send tool results.

reads.best: Deterministic before/after scoring keeps the rewrite checkable.
reads.worst: Thin client for a metered paid service; no tests, and the transform_tool_result hook touches every post-like tool result.

plugins.name: hacmdn
plugins.author: Jpalmer95
plugins.does: Proposes a decentralized mesh of micro-specialist models with routing, bidding and attribution, exposed as Hermes tools, a GUI and a Desktop pane.

reads.best: Ambitious vision with docs, a dashboard and HF token from the secret store.
reads.worst: Specialist outputs are mostly hard-coded canned strings (e.g. a fixed SQL query) despite claims of a live network, so it claims more than the code does.

plugins.name: birta
plugins.author: mkrou
plugins.does: Sixteen SKILL.md files plus an MCP entry for Birta's hosted commercial service for publishing, sharing and reviewing pages.

reads.best: Well-written design and writing guidance across its skills.
reads.worst: No code or tests, the shipped MCP entry cannot sign in so the user must run 'hermes mcp add' by hand, and a skill tells the agent to use Birta even when the user does not name it.

plugins.name: bsc-mint-guard
plugins.author: Fuma2514
plugins.does: Reads BSC contract metadata, mint conditions and wallet balances to produce free-mint preview checks and price quotes.

reads.best: Read-only standard-library tools avoid private keys and spending, with mocked tests for verdicts, quantities and RPC fallback.
reads.worst: Fixed selector guesses cannot establish mint safety, failed wallet reads still return already_minted=false, and sequential RPC fallback has no overall deadline.

plugins.name: tap-giving
plugins.author: RyanShook
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted MCP workflow for NFC artwork, quotes, orders and human-paid invoice links ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tap-Giving/tap-giving-mcp/76350a5b4c4d46848aca238b39d3f1dd3db5e83f/README.md)).

reads.best: The source implements artwork previews, organization-scoped orders and recap checks while leaving payment and final design approval to people.
reads.worst: The repository bundles resvg.wasm, an executable payload covered by catalog rule 17, and its hosted MCP runtime is not fixed by the catalog commit pin ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tap-Giving/tap-giving-mcp/76350a5b4c4d46848aca238b39d3f1dd3db5e83f/src/preview.ts)).

plugins.name: printwatch
plugins.author: clawsyndicate
plugins.does: Implements LAN status, file upload, print control and camera tools for Anycubic, Bambu and Moonraker printers.

reads.best: The clean-room Anycubic handshake and firmware-specific G-code packaging address a concrete own-hardware workflow.
reads.worst: register stores PluginContext as _agent, but credential lookup expects its nonexistent secret_scope attribute and returns empty configuration; there are no tests or enforced print-start approval hooks.

plugins.name: webtwizz
plugins.author: ahmedwab
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted website-building MCP service through a pinned mcp-remote launcher and browser OAuth.

reads.best: The package explicitly marks the remote server untrusted and clearly discloses credit use, browser sign-in and user-confirmed publishing.
reads.worst: The pinned tree contains only configuration and docs, leaving server behavior and tests unreviewable, while OAuth tokens are stored by mcp-remote outside Hermes.

plugins.name: ambassly
plugins.author: MelMayssonOwen
plugins.does: Packages Ambassly's hosted affiliate-program MCP server (Bearer key) with one workflow skill for creating programs, links and reviewing commissions.

reads.best: Honest disclosure: it marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before write calls, and its skill tells the agent to get a person's decision on each commission.
reads.worst: There is no plugin code, only an MCP config and a skill for one commercial SaaS with UTM-tagged links. The tool list comes from the vendor's server and the pinned commit does not cover it.

plugins.name: mentionagent
plugins.author: BuildsbyMatt
plugins.does: Skill plus remote-MCP config for MentionAgent's hosted link-building outreach service, with sending behind approval.

reads.best: Skill marks which tools send email or spend credits and the server is untrusted.
reads.worst: No code of its own, a Claude skill repackaged for a paid third-party service.

plugins.name: hypotize
plugins.author: viluca94
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to the hosted Hypotize growth-experiment MCP server with three skills.

reads.best: Clear README and OAuth sign-in without pasting keys.
reads.worst: No plugin code at all, just an MCP config and skills for a vendor's hosted service.

plugins.name: dyscalculia
plugins.author: cms-be
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted, read-only MCP server for cited dyscalculia statistics and screening-test information, with a matching research skill.

reads.best: The six narrowly scoped read-only tools make it easier to retrieve topic-specific statistics with citations and explain the limits of a screening test.
reads.worst: The catalog package contains only connector metadata and a skill; the runtime service and its tools are remote and not pinned or covered by local tests.

plugins.name: thefaceanalysis
plugins.author: cms-be
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted read-only face-measurement and reference-data MCP service with a usage skill.

reads.best: The small keyless connector clearly discloses remote processing and the limits of its reference dataset.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no service implementation or tests; its seven remotely supplied tools can change outside the reviewed commit.

plugins.name: kareverse
plugins.author: digitalmanager-commits
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Kareverse service information and consent-based callback enquiries for elder care in Bangalore.

reads.best: The manifest marks remote tools untrusted, and the documentation clearly distinguishes browsing from an enquiry that shares contact details.
reads.worst: All business logic and consent enforcement are in an unpinned hosted server, with no local implementation or tests and a single-city service audience.

plugins.name: fudge
plugins.author: jacques-blom
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted Shopify store analysis and draft-management tools through MCP and six skills.

reads.best: The skills describe a useful merchant workflow that keeps publication on the human-reviewed Fudge page.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no implementation or tests of the hosted tools, and authenticated setup requires a separate manual MCP OAuth command disclosed in the PR.

plugins.name: details
plugins.author: koppkvn
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to the hosted Details MCP service for design reference searches and reusable components.

reads.best: The package gives design work a curated reference catalog and an explicit untrusted MCP connection.
reads.worst: The repository has only a bridge and skill; hosted tool behavior is unpinned, and the PR says an authenticated Hermes call was not tested.

plugins.name: saascity
plugins.author: nyyhao
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to SaaSCity's hosted MCP tools and supplies a guided product-launch skill.

reads.best: It exposes a launch directory service through a simple untrusted MCP connection with no local credentials.
reads.worst: The pinned plugin has no implementation or tests for its hosted tools, whose behavior can change independently of the repository.

plugins.name: peakflo-spaces
plugins.author: dimavedenyapin
plugins.does: A config-only package that registers Peakflo's hosted Spaces MCP server (via npx mcp-remote, marked untrusted) and a skill for finance and ops workflows.

reads.best: Honest and minimal: it says it ships no code, pins mcp-remote and marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before write tools.
reads.worst: No engineering of its own; all value sits in a closed commercial hosted service and Hermes can already add an MCP server without a plugin.

plugins.name: account-switcher
plugins.author: hendkai
plugins.does: Lists and reprioritizes existing provider credential-pool accounts through Hermes authentication CLI commands.

reads.best: It has a useful dry-run and post-switch verification path and avoids reading credential values.
reads.worst: There are no tests, and the custom process runner neither reports exit status nor terminates a timed-out child.

plugins.name: evm-token-inspector
plugins.author: sawi57003-ops
plugins.does: Reads token metadata, ownership, EIP-1967 proxy state, and a V2 liquidity pair on four EVM chains.

reads.best: The single read-only tool validates addresses and provides a compact set of on-chain facts without signing or keys.
reads.worst: A nonstandard token string can abort the whole inspection rather than leave optional metadata unknown; serial public-RPC fallbacks can make a check very slow.

plugins.name: sequenzy
plugins.author: polnikale
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Sequenzy's hosted email-marketing MCP service and bundles operating instructions.

reads.best: It uses OAuth, labels the remote server untrusted, and documents that writes and sends need approval.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no implementation or tests; it downloads an npx bridge and delegates its changing tool set to a hosted service outside the commit.

plugins.name: openseo
plugins.author: carterwsmith
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted OpenSEO data and project tools through mcp-remote, with twelve skills for SEO research, audits and reports ([pinned source](https://github.com/every-app/open-seo/tree/7d89cfb3ca30b2819356c57c5b746a1048b9743f/plugins/openseo)).

reads.best: Detailed workflows distinguish observed rankings from estimates and describe credit costs, reusable project context and approval before starting paid tracking.
reads.worst: The default connection delegates OAuth storage to mcp-remote in ~/.mcp-auth instead of Hermes, and the deployed server/tool set is not fixed by the plugin commit ([plugins/openseo/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/every-app/open-seo/7d89cfb3ca30b2819356c57c5b746a1048b9743f/plugins/openseo/README.md)).

plugins.name: mahj-trainer
plugins.author: jackwallner
plugins.does: An Agent Plugins v1 package (plugin.json, mcp.json, one skill) that points Hermes at a hosted Mahj Trainer MCP server for American mah jongg lessons, quizzes and rack reading.

reads.best: Clear, honest README, read-only tools with no account or key, and careful handling of the copyrighted NMJL card.
reads.worst: The plugin folder contains no code, just a pointer to a closed remote server, for a very narrow audience; it reads more like a funnel to the author's app.

plugins.name: tuneviva
plugins.author: omercelik
plugins.does: An Agent Plugins package that points Hermes at TuneViva's keyless read-only MCP server for sheet-music search and practice-score links, plus two guidance skills.

reads.best: No account or key needed and the endpoint is read-only.
reads.worst: No code at all: a remote MCP URL and two skills, with a README of a few lines, a narrow audience, and no tests.

plugins.name: shelldrop
plugins.author: danielbilsborough
plugins.does: A skill that has the agent set up SSH, tmux, Tailscale and keep-awake on a Mac or Linux box for an iPhone SSH app, plus a remote MCP server that returns fixed help text.

reads.best: A small, stateless, readable MCP worker with vitest tests and read-only annotations.
reads.worst: The remote tools repeat the skill's static text, the live server was never checked, and the skill performs sudo, curl|sh and authorized_keys changes guided only by prompt text.

plugins.name: fixmyscan
plugins.author: fightme-cmd
plugins.does: A manifest/connector pointing Hermes at an externally hosted MCP server and REST API (mcp.fixmyscan.com) that OCRs and cleans scanned book PDFs/DjVu files for e-readers; no implementation code exists in this repo.

reads.best: Clear, professional manifests (openapi.json, mcp.json, SKILL.md) describing a real external service with its own useful function.
reads.worst: There is no local implementation to judge at all (only manifests and a SKILL.md) and the plugin itself marks the remote server as 'untrusted', with no test suite and no code a skill plus a remote MCP tool call couldn't also achieve.

plugins.name: frontend-sensei
plugins.author: daniels-martins
plugins.does: Provides six PHP MCP tools for static frontend audits, contrast calculations, and stored audit-score history, plus frontend skills.

reads.best: The contrast calculator and persisted audit history provide deterministic functionality beyond frontend advice alone.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains an obfuscated init payload invoked by npm build/dev scripts, undermining code review and catalog trust; audit tests are only scaffold examples.

plugins.name: toolfound
plugins.author: MelMayssonOwen
plugins.does: Configures a hosted Toolfound MCP server and bundles a skill for software discovery and product launch submissions.

reads.best: The server is explicitly untrusted and the launch workflow asks for confirmation of the exact submission fields.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no server implementation or tests; its tool list and behavior are supplied by an unpinned remote service.

plugins.name: agentpass
plugins.author: shagghiesuperstar
plugins.does: Calls a hosted website-readiness scanner and turns its reports into ranked remediation prompts. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shagghiesuperstar/agentpass-plugin/c091db23bf8fe5f8773dfd29d6bf5127a1de9ec4/README.md)

reads.best: Its standard-library MCP client and stub tests cover handshakes, JSON/SSE replies, retries and structured failures. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shagghiesuperstar/agentpass-plugin/c091db23bf8fe5f8773dfd29d6bf5127a1de9ec4/README.md)
reads.worst: The optional API key is read directly from process environment rather than Hermes scoped secrets, and host-only caching conflates distinct URLs. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shagghiesuperstar/agentpass-plugin/c091db23bf8fe5f8773dfd29d6bf5127a1de9ec4/tools.py) [Credential source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shagghiesuperstar/agentpass-plugin/c091db23bf8fe5f8773dfd29d6bf5127a1de9ec4/mcp_client.py)

plugins.name: lexicon-seo
plugins.author: NK2-arch
plugins.does: Manifest pointing at Lexicon SEO's hosted MCP server for paid technical SEO audits.

reads.best: Honest README about plan limits and heuristic scores.
reads.worst: No code; requires a paid account and is a thin connector to a commercial service.

plugins.name: evidence-history
plugins.author: 1anter
plugins.does: Five tools that store caller-supplied evidence passages in a local append-only SQLite store and answer what was known or published as of a given time.

reads.best: A clear, honest idea of point-in-time evidence (observation versus publication cutoffs) with no network calls and stdlib-only storage.
reads.worst: About 140 lines of densely packed code with a 36-line test, and a README with placeholder install steps that says no public repository is claimed yet.

plugins.name: clef-music-tools
plugins.author: MelMayssonOwen
plugins.does: Configuration-only package pointing Hermes at Clef's hosted no-auth music MCP (transpose chords, spell piano chords, tab to piano notes) plus a skill and an offline transpose script.

reads.best: Honest disclosure of what is sent to clefdrills.com and a small offline transposition helper.
reads.worst: No plugin code of its own; the tools live on a remote server outside the pinned commit, and the README and skill are laced with UTM marketing links.

plugins.name: workout-tracker
plugins.author: hamidzr
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted workout-planning MCP servers for exercise lookup, plan analysis and account edits.

reads.best: The package cleanly separates public catalog tools from token-gated account tools.
reads.worst: The checked-in package contains no server implementation or tests, so its remote tool behavior cannot be judged at the pin.

plugins.name: lovedone-family
plugins.author: tera-sarah
plugins.does: Config-only MCP connector to the LovedOne Family Inbox for coordinating an aging parent's messages.

reads.best: Marks the server untrusted and takes the key from an env variable, with a skill that asks before writes.
reads.worst: About three tiny files, no README, tests or setup docs; works only with a paid third-party service.

plugins.name: agenttrust-seal
plugins.author: SyrupLabsAI
plugins.does: Writes a <file>.seal.json with the file's sha256, size, author and time, and later checks the file against it, as a tool and a slash command.

reads.best: Tiny, readable, local-only stdlib code with an honest three-way result (holds, broken, no seal) and a selftest.
reads.worst: The seal is an unkeyed hash stored next to the file, so whoever edits the file can simply re-seal it: it catches accidents, not tampering, which is less than the README's claim to 'prove' a handoff was not changed, and sha256sum in a skill would do the same.

plugins.name: onda
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Manifest plus mcp.json pointing Hermes at Onda's paid hosted MCP server for Instagram/YouTube/TikTok creator analytics.

reads.best: Honest README with OAuth through Hermes and no stored credentials.
reads.worst: No code at all; a niche paid Russian-language service and a manual mcp add step.

plugins.name: nanlmind-hermes
plugins.author: shemshallah
plugins.does: Bridges Hermes to a local NaNLMind '256-head universe' for training, chat and NANNET/CLOCKED operations through about twenty tools.

reads.best: Ambitious local training and runner integration with many tools.
reads.worst: Opaque, hard-to-read code with large unverifiable claims, a self_modify tool and a sprawling scripts tree; no clear user.

plugins.name: whoop-mcp
plugins.author: davidmosiah
plugins.does: Packages an MCP server and workflow skill for reading WHOOP recovery, HRV, sleep, strain, and workout data through OAuth.

reads.best: The workflow is clear about consent, local setup, synthetic demo data, and the limitations of health guidance.
reads.worst: The pinned plugin contains only manifests and a skill: its npx command downloads the actual server at runtime, which is outside the reviewed commit, and its PR flags an unresolved credential-policy question.

plugins.name: operate-hermes-plugin
plugins.author: rxdha1
plugins.does: A thin REST wrapper around the commercial operate.center gig marketplace that lets the agent list, sell, hire and fulfil paid gigs, release escrow and download deliveries, with a 15-minute unattended automation.

reads.best: Covers the marketplace's full buy/sell loop, and the API key comes from Hermes's secret store first.
reads.worst: It moves money (hire_gig, approve releases escrow) with no approval gate in the plugin, can upload any local file, and /operate demo writes a fake +$68 that /operate status then shows as Net Earned; there are no tests.

plugins.name: timetopost
plugins.author: MelMayssonOwen
plugins.does: Agent Plugins package with skills and an MCP config for TimeToPost's hosted social-scheduling server.

reads.best: Honest disclosure, OAuth through Hermes, server marked untrusted with human approval for writes.
reads.worst: Essentially skills plus a hosted-service MCP URL; the tool list is not in the pinned code.

plugins.name: midi-bridge
plugins.author: james-see
plugins.does: Exposes local MIDI notes, chords, patterns, and controller messages for a connected DAW.

reads.best: The [MIDI backend](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/james-see/midi-bridge/5c94d270116454795f644e2118f1f42e057da808/midi_utils.py) opens local virtual or existing ports, giving Hermes a concrete way to play a user's instruments.
reads.worst: The [sequence player](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/james-see/midi-bridge/5c94d270116454795f644e2118f1f42e057da808/pattern_player.py) sleeps each absolute start time plus each preceding note duration, so timing drifts and notes cannot overlap.

plugins.name: task-navigator
plugins.author: Guinevere1991
plugins.does: Validates caller-supplied evidence and 5W1H task cards, with a per-turn reminder to prepare them ([pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Guinevere1991/token-housekeeper-hackathon/e1b5d954131e3a44faef2ff3422ab6c430e0040e/plugin/README.md)).

reads.best: Bounded, side-effect-free validation checks exact source quotations, input limits and localization without claiming semantic proof.
reads.worst: Most value is structured prompting: the model supplies the analysis, and the near-universal reminder can add calls without demonstrated token savings ([reminder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Guinevere1991/token-housekeeper-hackathon/e1b5d954131e3a44faef2ff3422ab6c430e0040e/plugin/__init__.py)).

plugins.name: qqq-ai-visibility
plugins.author: meelis545
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to QQQ’s hosted MCP service for website AI-crawler readiness and existing public visibility reports.

reads.best: A no-key connector documents its read-only tools, privacy boundaries and public-report limitations clearly.
reads.worst: The pinned tree contains client configuration and documentation only, with no server code or tests to substantiate behavior and a shared 300-check daily ceiling.

plugins.name: phishnoo-sandbox
plugins.author: PangPang83
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted synthetic security-awareness metrics and example threat reporting through MCP.

reads.best: The small package uses profile secrets and marks its write-capable remote MCP server untrusted.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains only a skill and remote configuration, with no server implementation or tests to assess the advertised reporting behavior.

plugins.name: crosodo
plugins.author: tera-sarah
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted MCP service advertised for US cottage-food law, county requirements and certification lookups.

reads.best: A simple untrusted remote MCP declaration provides a focused data service without local keys or a local runtime.
reads.worst: The pin contains connector configuration and a skill only, with no server implementation or tests to verify the live legal dataset or checkout behavior.

plugins.name: faxforagents
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted fax MCP service for document preparation, quotes, sending, status, and inbox reads.

reads.best: It exposes a full fax workflow with an untrusted MCP declaration and an approval-oriented skill.
reads.worst: The actual service code is remote; portable use invokes an npm package at runtime, and live stdio loading was not tested.

plugins.name: synento
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Adds a portable MCP connection and skill for a hosted live-video session and recording service.

reads.best: The package declares the remote server untrusted and documents the separate OAuth setup and verification step.
reads.worst: All functional tools run on a changeable remote server; OAuth needs manual native configuration, and local tests mostly check packaging and mocked responses.

plugins.name: audit-lens
plugins.author: Luecria
plugins.does: Offers Solidity pattern checks, Sourcify source retrieval, public issue-class matching and formatted finding drafts through four tools.

reads.best: Returns source lines and remediation suggestions without dependencies and repeatedly warns that heuristic findings need manual verification.
reads.worst: The delegatecall check examines calldata arguments rather than the target expression, and regex-based parsing cannot substantiate several semantic security labels; source fetching selects the largest file.

plugins.name: wavegrain
plugins.author: destination
plugins.does: Declares a hosted Wavegrain MCP connection and a skill for social carousel creation, editing, scheduling and export.

reads.best: A small readable connector marks the server untrusted, while the skill describes spending limits and idempotent paid-call retries.
reads.worst: The pinned package has no server implementation or tests and its README supplies other-client setup rather than a Hermes authentication flow; the Hermes MCP entry includes neither OAuth configuration nor access-key wiring.

plugins.name: job-hunt-tracker
plugins.author: muhadilaga
plugins.does: Stores job applications locally and exposes duplicate checks, status updates, follow-up queries and summary counts as six chat tools.

reads.best: A small dependency-free implementation validates dates and statuses, rejects duplicate applications and atomically replaces its JSON store.
reads.worst: There are only manual test instructions, and its process-local lock cannot prevent lost updates when separate Hermes processes write the same JSON store.

plugins.name: hostinger
plugins.author: J182Razor
plugins.does: Ten tools wrapping the Hostinger API for VPS, snapshots, firewall, DNS, domains, SSL and billing.

reads.best: Uses get_secret for the token and asks for confirm on rebuild, restore and DNS changes.
reads.worst: The deploy tool does nothing yet returns success saying deployment executed, firewall apply and ssl provision are unconfirmed, and compiled .pyc files are committed.

plugins.name: aitrainingdatabroker
plugins.author: aitrainingdatabroker
plugins.does: Adds a read-only remote MCP blog server and one skill for questions about licensing company data for AI training.

reads.best: The package is transparent, small and safe by scope: remote read-only access, no key, no local execution and links back to source articles.
reads.worst: It is mostly a remote blog connector plus instructional skill, so a prompt/skill and ordinary web access cover much of the same value and there is little pinned implementation to test.

plugins.name: consequence-map
plugins.author: BitSempre
plugins.does: Provides a decision-audit library and Hermes hooks for correlating approval requests and outcomes, with a separate prototype authorization guard.

reads.best: The library separates host authorization from agent decisions and includes substantial lifecycle, audit and authorization tests.
reads.worst: The pinned plugin subdirectory imports a sibling implementation package absent from that install layout, catches registration failure, and supplies no active Guard service; the PR explicitly confirms zero registered hooks for that layout.

plugins.name: dyslexiasteps
plugins.author: cms-be
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to hosted read-only phonics and sight-word lists, with a skill for grade, pattern and provenance queries.

reads.best: The keyless, read-only connector has clear setup and emphasizes cited grade placement rather than diagnosing a child.
reads.worst: The entry is only remote MCP configuration and a skill, with no pinned word data, server implementation or tests and little Hermes-specific behavior.

plugins.name: bnb-airdrop-autopilot
plugins.author: sawi57003-ops
plugins.does: Finds new BSC token profiles, reads contract risk indicators and gas prices, and previews claim calls through the baw CLI ([Pinned source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sawi57003-ops/bnb-airdrop-autopilot/dbb3b2c36d994c9d1bd93b8cd3e3e308fd90b9e4/README.md)).

reads.best: The execution module only invokes transaction preview and implements no broadcast or signing operation.
reads.worst: The contract checker can leave risk at LOW when source verification is unknown and liquidity is absent, while discovery identifies new tokens rather than actual airdrops ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sawi57003-ops/bnb-airdrop-autopilot/dbb3b2c36d994c9d1bd93b8cd3e3e308fd90b9e4/safety.py)).

plugins.name: kaggle-competitions
plugins.author: landenjackson
plugins.does: Tracks Kaggle submission snapshots, score history, completed-result changes and leaderboards through CLI-backed tools and a Desktop board.

reads.best: A baseline-aware watch distinguishes pending submissions that finish from old results on first installation.
reads.worst: Credential fallback permits the Kaggle CLI to read its own token file, violating catalog policy; there are no tests, CLI failures are ignored, and best score always means maximum.

plugins.name: fledly
plugins.author: synthentica
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Fledly's hosted MCP server for iOS App Store market data and keyword research, plus a routing skill.

reads.best: Clear multi-client install docs with OAuth through a pinned mcp-remote version.
reads.worst: For Hermes it is only an mcp.json that runs npx (needing Node) and a skill, a niche data service with no Hermes-specific code or tests.

plugins.name: momentic
plugins.author: wuweiweiwu
plugins.does: A vendor skills bundle (five SKILL.md files plus an MCP config) for writing, running and repairing Momentic browser and mobile tests and running Mo bug bashes on Momentic's paid service.

reads.best: Well-written, detailed skills from the vendor, including careful guidance on keeping credentials out of commands.
reads.worst: It contains no Hermes plugin code at all (no plugin.yaml or register), its README never mentions Hermes, the MCP servers run unpinned `npx -y` packages, and a skill would do the same because it is only skills.

plugins.name: arena-skill
plugins.author: J182Razor
plugins.does: A skill plus a bracket.py bookkeeping script that runs a single-elimination tournament of up to 100 delegate_task sub-agents, each with a different strategy card, to find the best answer to one task.

reads.best: bracket.py is a real 1,235-line state machine that deals strategy cards, pairs matches and tracks verdicts under .arena/.
reads.worst: It is a skill bundle whose manifest says it was "generated from" another author's repo, with a 13-line README, no tests, no Hermes plugin code and a default of 100 agents (hundreds of sub-agent calls).

plugins.name: asyntai
plugins.author: asyntai
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Asyntai's hosted customer-support MCP service through a version-pinned npm stdio bridge ([pinned source](https://github.com/asyntai/mcp-bridge/tree/75680ed683534aea4e158b49a7ad629c656e10a5/hermes)).

reads.best: The readable bridge includes tests for stream framing, authentication retries and protocol errors, and the Hermes manifest explicitly marks the remote server untrusted.
reads.worst: The bridge reads and refreshes OAuth tokens in its own credential file instead of Hermes's credential route, and its browser authorization wait has no local timeout or unattended guard ([src/oauth.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asyntai/mcp-bridge/75680ed683534aea4e158b49a7ad629c656e10a5/src/oauth.js)).

plugins.name: onboard-me
plugins.author: skeptical-agency
plugins.does: A resumable getting-to-know-you interview offered on the first turn that compiles answers into memory-ready facts, plus a read-only setup advisor.

reads.best: The first-turn hook plus a persisted interview state gives new users a guided start, and the setup advisor reports key names, never values.
reads.worst: No tests; the README's promise that 'one no ends it forever' isn't implemented, delete matches profiles by prefix, the data path differs from the README, and it is mostly a question bank a skill could hold.

plugins.name: mood-engine
plugins.author: NiceStackApple
plugins.does: Persists four mood axes and injects adaptive tone directives after heuristic or background model evaluation.

reads.best: Uses Hermes state and auxiliary model routing with a bounded evaluator and a no-extra-model heuristic mode.
reads.worst: Its main effect is prompt-style steering, including deliberate reluctance to help at low patience, and background evaluations share one mood state across sessions.

plugins.name: reliability-desk
plugins.author: jonathan-kellerai
plugins.does: Bundles eight Markdown skills for evidence-based release polls, incident reviews, FMEA, readbacks and change-control checklists.

reads.best: Detailed worksheets, named decision owners and evidence requirements make the reliability practices clear and usable.
reads.worst: The pinned package is entirely skills and Markdown references, with no tools, hooks, executable enforcement or capability beyond prompting.

plugins.name: lovedone-soft
plugins.author: tera-sarah
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to LovedOne Soft’s hosted home-care agency MCP service for client, visit, note, invoice and scheduling workflows.

reads.best: The portable package marks its remote server untrusted and the skill asks for confirmation before mutations, giving existing agency users a straightforward connector ([manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Terahertz-Inc/lovedone-mcp/a1d55a218bf6e817cc950d423f19535f9a2760cf/hermes/lovedone-soft/plugin.json)).
reads.worst: The pin contains connector metadata and a skill, with no backend source or tests and no plugin-folder README, so the advertised live tools and their reliability cannot be verified from this commit ([repository disclosure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Terahertz-Inc/lovedone-mcp/a1d55a218bf6e817cc950d423f19535f9a2760cf/README.md)).

plugins.name: github-to-hermes
plugins.author: J182Razor
plugins.does: Detects repository types and attempts to generate and validate Hermes plugin scaffolds for MCP servers, APIs, CLIs, Python packages and skills. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/J182Razor/hermes-github-to-plugin/324fc0134dda32a0e11d74397e5148de77054994/tools.py)

reads.best: It returns detection, validation and doctor reports alongside generated file lists, making scaffold failures inspectable. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/J182Razor/hermes-github-to-plugin/324fc0134dda32a0e11d74397e5148de77054994/tools.py)
reads.worst: Committed bytecode violates catalog rules, model-selected paths and names permit arbitrary writes, and validation installs dependencies without approval; the pin also lacks a README. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/J182Razor/hermes-github-to-plugin/324fc0134dda32a0e11d74397e5148de77054994/tools.py) [Pinned file list](https://api.github.com/repos/J182Razor/hermes-github-to-plugin/git/trees/324fc0134dda32a0e11d74397e5148de77054994?recursive=1)

plugins.name: ghostbox
plugins.author: arjunbagga-xyz
plugins.does: Creates shadow worktrees or directory copies, reports change statistics, and offers tools to apply or discard those changes.

reads.best: The worktree-and-diff workflow could make agent edits reviewable, and basic copy, apply and discard lifecycle tests are present.
reads.worst: The claimed sandbox is not enforced: middleware only rewrites existing cwd fields, leak/egress counts are hardcoded zero, and commit can report success and discard a shadow after git apply fails.

plugins.name: trendswap
plugins.author: GptsApp
plugins.does: Connects a portable plugin to TrendSwap’s hosted video-template MCP service and bundles portrait-advice instructions plus a local API proxy.

reads.best: The public template catalog is reachable through a simple remote MCP declaration without a local service or account setup.
reads.worst: The read-only manifest and skill contradict the README and bundled proxy’s account and generation operations, and the proxy has no request timeout or shipped automated tests.

plugins.name: internet-outage-checker
plugins.author: AdeJol
plugins.does: Config-only MCP pointer to FindBroadband's hosted UK broadband outage checker.

reads.best: Simple, keyless and marked untrusted.
reads.worst: No code; a UK-only remote MCP tied to a commercial deals site.

plugins.name: twingraph-instagram
plugins.author: dalroot
plugins.does: Registers nine Instagram inspection, analytics and messaging tools that invoke a separately installed TwinGraph CLI.

reads.best: A consistent bridge exposes public profile research and authenticated inbox operations through ordinary Hermes tool schemas.
reads.worst: The required engine is absent from the pinned repository, has no bundled tests, and receives an Instagram session-file path instead of Hermes-managed credentials.

plugins.name: publora
plugins.author: publora-team
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to Publora social publishing through hosted MCP and nine platform-specific skills.

reads.best: Documents OAuth setup, outbound post-content disclosure and untrusted-server approval configuration without storing credentials locally.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no publishing implementation or automated tests; almost all functionality is hosted MCP plus skills, and native OAuth setup requires manually restoring untrusted status.

plugins.name: hook-desk
plugins.author: jonathan-kellerai
plugins.does: Packages two skills for analyzing pasted social-post openings and drafting sourced hooks using conversation-local voice rules.

reads.best: The skills clearly distinguish supplied metrics from verified facts and keep source links attached to reusable hook formulas.
reads.worst: It consists entirely of prompts, with no tools, automation or durable formula storage beyond text the user copies between conversations.

plugins.name: tenderlead-agent-plugin
plugins.author: jlucwright
plugins.does: A portable agent-plugin package holding one skill that reviews UK tender documents against a supplier profile to suggest BID or SKIP.

reads.best: Honest about scope: no install scripts, hooks, dependencies or credentials, and a clear vendor-published manifest.
reads.worst: It is a single skill with no code, tools or tests, and is aimed at a vendor product, so it adds nothing a prompt could not do.

plugins.name: hornlib
plugins.author: AbigailDavised
plugins.does: Manifest pointing Hermes at HornLib's hosted French horn fingering/transposition MCP server plus skills.

reads.best: Polished README and a hosted, keyless MCP endpoint.
reads.worst: No code in the repo; a thin marketing wrapper around a remote server for a very small niche.

plugins.name: transducer
plugins.author: arjunbagga-xyz
plugins.does: Uses laptop audio for chirp-based ranging and microphone spectrum analysis, with random-byte generation and a Desktop telemetry pane.

reads.best: Actual sounddevice capture and SciPy matched filtering demonstrate a creative way to expose physical sensing to an agent.
reads.worst: Claims exceed the implementation: entropy uses os.urandom, RT60 is fixed at 245 ms, Desktop readings include fabricated constants, and the sole test only asserts True.

plugins.name: selaeron-paperclip-sel9
plugins.author: nebout2011-debug
plugins.does: Posts a comment to an operator-allowlisted Paperclip issue after looking up its single current live run.

reads.best: The registered handler obtains run identity from a read-only lookup and refuses missing or ambiguous runs, with scoped credentials and comment-only writes.
