reads.worst: The duplicate key includes summary text and exists only in memory, so changing the summary or restarting permits another comment for the same run despite the one-comment claim.

plugins.name: marsell
plugins.author: Thisisily
plugins.does: Agent Plugins package pointing Hermes at Marsell's hosted marketing/sales MCP server.

reads.best: Marked untrusted with OAuth so Hermes asks before write calls.
reads.worst: No plugin code at all: a generic MCP connection manifest for a private SaaS backend, repo is cross-client registry metadata.

plugins.name: ndaa
plugins.author: tera-sarah
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted MCP service advertising FY2027 NDAA status, legislative text, comparisons and news.

reads.best: A credential-free endpoint offers a focused public-legislation workflow with source links.
reads.worst: The pinned tree contains connector metadata and a skill but no server implementation or tests, so advertised tools and their read-only behavior cannot be verified from the submission.

plugins.name: mayar
plugins.author: julianromli
plugins.does: Configuration-only MCP package pointing Hermes at Mayar's hosted payments MCP server for invoices, payment links and QRIS.

reads.best: Simple config for an official hosted MCP server with clear disclosure.
reads.worst: No code at all: reads the key from ~/.hermes/.env and gives the agent payment write actions with only a skill's advice to confirm first.

plugins.name: business-agent-os
plugins.author: danielbilsborough
plugins.does: Skill plus a read-only MCP server of templates that sets up a plain-text business memory and session commands, mainly for Claude Code.

reads.best: Careful skill with ask-before-each-step rules and an MCP test.
reads.worst: It is essentially a skill and static templates, not a Hermes plugin that changes what Hermes can do.

plugins.name: agentstatus-alabama+99-more
plugins.author: dulrajnr
plugins.does: Config-only package connecting Hermes to a public hosted Alabama DMV MCP server.

reads.best: Marks the server untrusted and needs no key.
reads.worst: No code, minimal docs, one of 100 templated near-identical entries.

plugins.name: boxcompute
plugins.author: farhan-helmy
plugins.does: Bundles a workflow skill for separately connected BoxCompute cloud-VM tools. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boxcompute/hermes-plugin/de27f5719372905686474f8a7650c591c63e899c/README.md)

reads.best: The skill explains deferred tool discovery, preserving VM disks on stop, public previews and cost-aware cleanup. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boxcompute/hermes-plugin/de27f5719372905686474f8a7650c591c63e899c/README.md)
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no VM backend or MCP declaration, so the working capability and its enforcement reside in an unpinned hosted service. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boxcompute/hermes-plugin/de27f5719372905686474f8a7650c591c63e899c/README.md)

plugins.name: penthera
plugins.author: danoszz
plugins.does: Packages a skill that guides Hermes through the Penthera CLI for local repository, dependency, URL and agent-configuration security scans.

reads.best: The skill provides detailed workflows, pinned CLI commands and approval guidance backed by an extensive standalone scanner repository.
reads.worst: The pinned plugin folder registers no tools, hooks or MCP server and is entirely a CLI-backed skill, with installation documentation still aimed at Claude Code.

plugins.name: mood
plugins.author: huy-sec
plugins.does: Maintains a keyword-driven mood and rapport state and appends a short tone cue to each user turn.

reads.best: It is compact, local-only, and persists state without model calls or prompt-cache changes.
reads.worst: Its keyword rules are a shallow personality prompt and the delivered test is an assertion script rather than a comprehensive suite.

plugins.name: agentic-kingdoms
plugins.author: agenticgameshq
plugins.does: A thin bundle (MCP server pointer plus a skill document) that lets the agent play a third-party-hosted browser MMO via a hosted MCP server, with no plugin-authored code at all.

reads.best: The underlying game concept (agents playing a persistent MMO, 'Humans vs AI war') is a creative idea, and the README is transparent about its limited scope and risks.
reads.worst: By its own admission ('There is no executable code and nothing that downloads or updates itself') this is just an MCP passthrough plus a skill file — all logic lives on a third party's server, so a skill/MCP config alone could reproduce it, and it runs game actions including attacks on other players without per-action approval by default.

plugins.name: interview-prep-coach
plugins.author: jonathan-kellerai
plugins.does: Packages nine skills for public-source interviewer research, tailored answers, mock interviews and follow-up drafts.

reads.best: Clear candidate-focused workflows require cited research and answers grounded in the user’s actual experience.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains only Markdown skills and a manifest, adding no executable tools, hooks or service integration.

plugins.name: cospark
plugins.author: teknium1
plugins.does: Installs a workflow skill that directs ad research and media creation through a separately configured hosted Cospark MCP connection.

reads.best: Clear native OAuth setup and candid privacy, credit-spending and remote-service disclosures.
reads.worst: The pinned Hermes package is skill text and metadata with no executable integration or automatically registered MCP server, so a skill does the same job and remote behavior is outside the reviewed code.

plugins.name: sovereign-plus
plugins.author: Sovereignplus
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a hosted service for UK contractor CIS estimates and right-to-work guidance.

reads.best: A small readable connector declares untrusted server access, requires no key and documents its narrow contractor audience.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains only configuration and a skill, with no server implementation or tests to verify its calculations and legal guidance.

plugins.name: nektar
plugins.author: kryptokrates
plugins.does: Supplies a Node installer intended to register an external nektar MCP memory-market server from a local JavaScript path or Docker image.

reads.best: The installer offers both local-server and Docker registration paths, and the README distinguishes test coins from real BSV.
reads.worst: No native entrypoint or portable MCP package is shipped, the setup key is not executed by Hermes, and manual installation defaults to an unpinned latest image without a declared untrusted spending gate.

plugins.name: qrblox
plugins.author: tera-sarah
plugins.does: A README-only bundle pointing Hermes at the vendor's hosted MCP server for QR codes, menus and loyalty campaigns.

reads.best: Simple MCP config marked untrusted, with a no-key sandbox.
reads.worst: There is no code; the endpoint in mcp.json (api.qrblox.com/mcp/v1) differs from the one in the README (app.qrblox.com/api/mcp), and it is a vendor advert.

plugins.name: qeemah-zatca
plugins.author: mosmn
plugins.does: Two tools that compute Saudi 15% VAT and run four simple format/arithmetic checks on invoice fields for ZATCA Phase 2.

reads.best: Deterministic, dependency-free VAT math with tool_error handling for bad amounts.
reads.worst: Claims ZATCA Phase 2 compliance validation 'against Schematron rules' but the code checks only a UUID regex, VAT-number shape, ICV>=1 and totals, ignores issue_date/time, has no tests, and its passed_checks count can go negative.

plugins.name: axiom
plugins.author: arjunbagga-xyz
plugins.does: Registers four SymPy/SciPy tools to check equation/inequality systems, SI dimensional homogeneity, conservation in ledgers and datasets, plus hooks and middleware that claim to self-repair numeric hallucinations.

reads.best: The constraint parser walks the AST into SymPy instead of calling eval, and the dimensional and conservation checks are real code.
reads.worst: Claims more than the code does: the PR advertises Z3/dReal SMT certificates but the code only runs SciPy SLSQP, the 'self-repair' middleware only acts on an axiom_claim field a model never emits, and the only test is assert True.

plugins.name: project_content
plugins.author: mikemonty
plugins.does: Experimental local project-content store: 13 tools to initialize a chosen folder, organize sections and units, append version-checked edit events, register media references and edit blocks, plus a separate Desktop organizer.

reads.best: Careful file handling: exclusive metadata creation with O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW, dir-fd operations and optimistic version conflicts instead of overwrites.
reads.worst: By its own README the Desktop workspace and the agent tools use different stores and do not interoperate, media playback is not implemented, the code is packed into dense one-line statements that are hard to review, and there are only two tests.

plugins.name: research-notes
plugins.author: Adebisi1111
plugins.does: Fetches public web pages and stores, searches, lists and deletes local tagged JSON notes.

reads.best: URL access fails closed without Hermes SSRF protection and note writes use atomic replacement.
reads.worst: No tests are shipped, concurrent note updates can overwrite each other, and the response-size check happens after the HTTP client has buffered the body.

plugins.name: money-magnet
plugins.author: Whydiriki700
plugins.does: Local JSON income/expense/budget tracker with crypto portfolio P&L and a CoinGecko-vs-Binance price-gap 'arbitrage' check, all read-only.

reads.best: It never trades or needs keys; it only reads public prices with 10s timeouts.
reads.worst: No tests, a 28-line README, the promised 'budget alerts' only report status, the 'arbitrage' just compares an aggregate price with one exchange, and bad /money add input raises an uncaught ValueError.

plugins.name: scrapeio
plugins.author: xhoantran
plugins.does: Skill library and MCP/plugin manifests pointing Hermes at ScrapeIO's hosted social-media data server.

reads.best: Wide platform coverage with key in a secret-typed config field.
reads.worst: Mostly skills plus a remote MCP URL, no plugin code or tests; pinned commit was not fetchable so it was scored from main.

plugins.name: reframe-proceed
plugins.author: bernardo9999
plugins.does: Stores personal visions, weekly plans, daily check-ins and reviews in profile-scoped SQLite and retrieves recent context.

reads.best: Simple local persistence uses Hermes-managed profile storage and has no network, credentials or third-party dependencies.
reads.worst: Only registration is tested; storage updates lack a uniqueness constraint and input/error handling is thin, while most planning value comes from the bundled skill.

plugins.name: zolva
plugins.author: zolvaagent
plugins.does: Configures a remote Zolva MCP server and two skills for querying public paper-trading agents and scheduling trade alerts.

reads.best: The manifest marks the remote server untrusted, and the skills clearly distinguish paper trades and require evidence for reported figures.
reads.worst: The pinned entry contains only skills and MCP configuration, with no server implementation or automated tests, and its remote tool list can change independently of the pin.

plugins.name: tala
plugins.author: domsilvestre
plugins.does: Configuration-only plugin declaring Tala's remote read-only MCP server and a skill to read Tala phone-agent calls.

reads.best: Honest, read-only, OAuth via Hermes's MCP flow.
reads.worst: No code: an MCP entry and a skill that a user could add in one command, serving only paying Tala customers.

plugins.name: cortex-zero-adaptive
plugins.author: TheRealBrofessor
plugins.does: Claims a local 1B-model loop that plans, executes and recovers browser automation steps through an external 'BAF' server.

reads.best: The observe-reason-act-adapt loop with domain/operation allowlists and failure classification is a reasonable idea for small local models.
reads.worst: It cannot run: __init__.py has no register(ctx), and engine.py imports czengine from a hard-coded /home/professor/cortexzero-engine that the repo does not include. There are no unit tests, and the README speaks of 'proof of compromise' and web-hacking packs.

plugins.name: fashion-design
plugins.author: priticolours
plugins.does: Ten local tools producing design briefs, tech packs, size sheets, BOMs and cost sheets from static tables.

reads.best: Runs fully offline with no keys.
reads.worst: Mostly templated text and hard-coded measurement tables a skill could produce; no tests.

plugins.name: developh
plugins.author: developh-co
plugins.does: Connects a hosted website-audit MCP service and a skill that turns PageSpeed findings into ranked fixes, with optional studio inquiries.

reads.best: The README clearly explains installation, the audit workflow, data destinations, and consent for inquiries, and the manifest marks the remote server untrusted.
reads.worst: The package contains no audit implementation or tests, and its own skill already calls the same service directly over HTTP without the plugin.

plugins.name: sapiens-sinteticos
plugins.author: inhabitants
plugins.does: Bundles eighteen skills for using a separately connected, hosted Sapiens creative-service account. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inhabitants/sapiens-mcp/03a000b2ca7f355d717204bf2f215250ce08054c/hermes/README.md)

reads.best: The setup documents OAuth ownership, prepaid generation costs and an untrusted-server setting for write approvals. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inhabitants/sapiens-mcp/03a000b2ca7f355d717204bf2f215250ce08054c/hermes/README.md)
reads.worst: The pinned Hermes folder contains skills and a manifest but no implementation or MCP declaration, so its added behavior can be supplied by skills alone. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inhabitants/sapiens-mcp/03a000b2ca7f355d717204bf2f215250ce08054c/hermes/README.md)

plugins.name: ceo-pack
plugins.author: tradersurfer
plugins.does: Returns business-role briefs, assignments, decision records, model suggestions and advisory tool-call validation plans.

reads.best: The envelope validator rejects nested credential material and the result verifier distinguishes a proposed call from completed work, with focused offline tests.
reads.worst: Despite the orchestration branding, tools return templates and flags without dispatching work, persisting decisions or creating agents, so a skill covers most of the value.

plugins.name: heycai-clinic-skills
plugins.author: notyourtechguru
plugins.does: Bundles instruction-only skills for estimating clinic front-desk revenue losses and auditing clinic websites for search visibility.

reads.best: Detailed workflows demand clinic-provided figures and site evidence, distinguish uncertainty, and avoid needing patient data.
reads.worst: The package adds only two Markdown skills with no executable integration, so a prompt or skill can provide its entire capability.

plugins.name: courierpr
plugins.author: aitrainingdatabroker
plugins.does: Connects Hermes to a public remote MCP server for browsing and searching CourierPR company press releases.

reads.best: The small read-only package needs no credentials and clearly labels releases as company statements.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains only configuration and a skill, with no server implementation or tests and no completed Hermes testing reported in the PR.

plugins.name: jalancost
plugins.author: Apihpih96
plugins.does: Calculates Malaysian road-trip fuel costs, optional toll totals, and per-passenger shares from supplied values.

reads.best: Decimal arithmetic, explicit fuel-only results, and input-validation tests make the narrow calculation easy to understand.
reads.worst: It performs only user-supplied arithmetic, with no route, price, service, or Hermes capability that a calculator skill could not provide.

plugins.name: reservegauge-agent-plugin
plugins.author: jlucwright
plugins.does: A skill-only package that tells the model how to review a user-supplied ReserveGauge usage CSV for coverage, reset boundaries and observed changes.

reads.best: Careful, honest instructions with no code, network or credentials, and it explicitly treats CSV cells as data.
reads.worst: It is just one SKILL.md for one vendor's export format, which a prompt does equally well, and it has no code or tests.

plugins.name: linkzoid
plugins.author: edkdev
plugins.does: Bundles instructions for using a separately configured hosted LinkZoid MCP service to audit and approve website internal links.

reads.best: Clear setup and troubleshooting documentation explains OAuth, analysis-credit costs and confirmation before live-site changes.
reads.worst: The pinned entry is just a manifest and skill, with no connector implementation or tests; its claimed functionality and approval enforcement depend on an external service and model instructions.

plugins.name: wever-labs
plugins.author: CodeWever
plugins.does: Registers two remote Wever Labs MCP endpoints, one paid and one free, for runtime tool discovery.

reads.best: The small manifest marks both remote MCP connections untrusted.
reads.worst: The submission is only declarative connector metadata, leaving the claimed hosted tools, payment path, and reliability outside reviewable code.

plugins.name: frosh
plugins.author: tera-sarah
plugins.does: Configures a public read-only remote MCP server for searching and reading Frosh documentation and blog content.

reads.best: It is a clearly documented, read-only connector with a simple public-data scope.
reads.worst: The README says the hosted endpoint is still launching and may not answer, and the pinned package has no implementation or tests.

plugins.name: listing-automater
plugins.author: Summertimechi
plugins.does: Skill-only plugin that registers one SKILL.md describing a commercial Facebook Marketplace posting app for real-estate agents and giving listing-writing tips.

reads.best: Honest and harmless: the PR and manifest say it is skill only, with no tools, hooks, network or env.
reads.worst: It is a product advertisement for a paid third-party app delivered as a skill; a prompt or skill does exactly the same and there is no code doing work.

plugins.name: daygauge-agent-plugin
plugins.author: jlucwright
plugins.does: Provides a skill that asks for manually supplied sleep times and instructs the model to calculate sleep duration and midpoint.

reads.best: The skill clearly handles midnight, equal times, invalid inputs and daylight-saving ambiguity without requesting health records ([skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jlucwright/daygauge-agent-plugin/b1f9ef5844cb03f87a38a86cdf0dc05d70e182e0/skills/daygauge-sleep-midpoint/SKILL.md)).
reads.worst: The entire capability is arithmetic instructions for the model, with no executable calculator, app integration or outcome tests ([skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jlucwright/daygauge-agent-plugin/b1f9ef5844cb03f87a38a86cdf0dc05d70e182e0/skills/daygauge-sleep-midpoint/SKILL.md)).

plugins.name: boardroomlist
plugins.author: aitrainingdatabroker
plugins.does: Configures a public remote MCP server and a skill for searching senior job listings and reading individual roles.

reads.best: A credential-free read-only connection makes a focused job dataset available with simple filtering guidance.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains only configuration and a skill, no server implementation or tests; runtime tools are remote and the PR reports no Hermes installation test.

plugins.name: fleetkeep-agent-plugin
plugins.author: jlucwright
plugins.does: Supplies a skill for preparing and reviewing user-provided vehicle CSVs before manual Fleetkeep import.

reads.best: The concise workflow preserves unknown dates, flags duplicate registrations and formula cells, and keeps imports under user control.
reads.worst: It contains only instructions and metadata, with no executable CSV validator, Hermes-specific tool, or live Fleetkeep integration.

plugins.name: custom-song-gift
plugins.author: GptsApp
plugins.does: Manifest connecting to a commercial site's MCP server that lists song occasions, styles, guidance and pricing.

reads.best: Keyless, read-only hosted endpoint.
reads.worst: Essentially a sales funnel for a paid service that a prompt could replicate; no code.

plugins.name: site-skills
plugins.author: imamalkan-hub
plugins.does: Twelve SKILL.md files that each describe and link to one of the author's own health-directory, home-improvement or yacht-charter websites.

reads.best: Harmless and includes a not-medical-advice note.
reads.worst: No code at all: it is site promotion packaged as skills, which a skill already is.

plugins.name: omnisight
plugins.author: arjunbagga-xyz
plugins.does: Registers four layout-inspection tools that claim to read live pages over Chrome DevTools, but every call returns the same hard-coded synthetic scene.

reads.best: Declares its tools, a Desktop entry and settings cleanly in a full manifest.
reads.worst: Claims more than the code does: inspect_surface ignores target_url and always returns mock_surface_scene data, and there is no CDP connection at all, so the agent gets invented defects and source lines.

plugins.name: riskpulse
plugins.author: Oko300
plugins.does: Fetches recent SEC filing inventories and assigns simple filing-volume risk labels ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Oko300/RiskPulse/fd812147886fcfac5d7e024410a7dfcef255ed16/tools/eight_k.py)).

reads.best: It provides dated primary-filing links and explicitly labels its output as an estimate requiring verification ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Oko300/RiskPulse/fd812147886fcfac5d7e024410a7dfcef255ed16/tools/eight_k.py)).
reads.worst: The 8-K item list is never populated, so the advertised material-event analysis is a filing-count heuristic rather than examination of the disclosed events ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Oko300/RiskPulse/fd812147886fcfac5d7e024410a7dfcef255ed16/tools/eight_k.py)).

plugins.name: hermes-wrm-pro
plugins.author: vedranius
plugins.does: A 28-line skill telling Hermes how to use an existing WRM Pro MCP server safely.

reads.best: Sensible safety guidance for remote server operations.
reads.worst: It is only a skill, exactly what the judges say a plugin should do more than.

plugins.name: awskills
plugins.author: aither-wzns
plugins.does: Packages a large cross-agent collection of instruction files, scripts, and optional Claude-oriented hooks for operating Aitherium tools.

reads.best: The skill collection is broad and its documentation is extensive.
reads.worst: The submitted manifest itself says it is instructions only; it does not implement a native Hermes plugin capability and is largely exactly the kind of skill the contest excludes.
